description: Key debates in the art of Africa and the African diaspora. Credit will be granted for only one of AFST_V 410 or ARTH_V 410. Equivalency: AFST_V 410.

name: The Artist in the World
description: Critical approach to the figure of the artist in art, film and texts, from the Early Modern period to the present.

name: Inferential Statistics and Research Methodology for Biotechnology
description: Credit limited to students in the Joint Degree Program in Biotechnology. Same as BCIT MATH 4442.

name: Is Art History Queer?
description: Issues in the history of art through the lens of queer theory.

name: Arts of the Northwest Coast Peoples: The South
description: The histories, historiography and cultural diversity of the Southern Northwest Coast region; persistence and innovation in the arts in communities, and in cross-cultural and market spheres.

name: Maya Public Ritual Arts
description: Architecture, sculpture, costume, and visual productions associated with Maya public ritual, including the ancient ball game and modern cofrada dances.

name: Molecular Genetics I
description: Credit limited to students in the Joint Degree Program in Biotechnology. Same as BCIT BIOT 5220.

name: Seminar in the Art of the Middle Ages
description: Credit will be granted for only one of ARTH_V 432, ARTH_V 431, ARTH_V 433.

name: Introduction to Medical Anthropology
description: An examination of health and illness, in their social and cultural contexts.

name: Sport in Society and Culture
description: Sport within the context of historic and contemporary society.

name: Introduction to Museums and Museology
description: The critical study of anthropology museums as social institutions and material culture research and classification from the late 19th century to the present day.

name: Anthropology of Gender & Sexuality
description: Ethnographic and theoretical approaches to gender and sexuality, in cross-cultural context.

name: Ethnography of Eurasia
description: Eurasia, including the Russian Federation, Central Asia, and Mongolia, with an emphasis on issues of power, identities, and transnational mobility in the region.

name: Ethnography of the Middle East
description: Critical analysis of colonial experience and cultural representations of the Middle East, particularly visions of orientalism and geopolitical discourses. Draws on ethnographic literature to consider contemporary life and subjectivities.

name: Visions of the Sacred: Introduction to the Anthropology of Religion
description: Comparative, cross-cultural approach to human engagement with the sacred. Examines religions as complex systems that share certain fundamental common features.

name: Ethnography of the Himalaya: Diversity & Development
description: Ethnographic engagement with lives of people in and from the Himalayan region: including parts of Bhutan, China, India, Nepal, Pakistan; Tibetan cultural zones traversing these countries; and diasporas.

name: Contemporary Anthropological Theory
description: Contemporary approaches to society and culture in anthropology. Prerequisite: ANTH 200 is recommended.

name: Ethnography of Korea
description: An exploration of ethnographic, topical, and theoretical issues.

name: Ethnography of Special Areas
description: A specialized study of ethnographic and theoretical problems in one area. Different culture areas or regions may be selected each term. Consult the Department for this year's offerings.

name: Ethnography of South Asia
description: A specialized study of ethnographic and theoretical problems relating to South Asia.

name: India in the Age of Empire and Revolution
description: History of India from the rise of the British East India Company to the beginnings of Indian nationalism and anti-colonial rebellion in the 19thcentury.

name: Film in South Asia
description: Social and cultural history of South Asian film.

name: Ethnography of the Northwest Coast
description: Specialized study of ethnographic and theoretical problems of the region.

name: Migration and (Im)mobilities: Anthropological Perspectives
description: Introduction to foundational topics in the anthropological study of migration, asylum, border-crossing, and (im)mobilities. Recommended: At least one 100-level or 200-level social science course (e.g. ANTH, SOCI, GEOG, POLI).

name: Topics in Japanese Cultural History I: Aristocrats and Warriors
description: Focuses each year on a specific topic related to the courtly or warrior culture of Japan.

name: Ethnography of Sub-Saharan Africa
description: An exploration of ethnographic, topical, and theoretical issues.

name: History of Later Imperial China
description: History of China from the end of Tang to the eve of its modern transformation. Students will acquire the analytical skills and tools to understand the political, socio-economic, and cultural changes in imperial China. Credit will be granted for only one of ASIA_V 340 or HIST_V 379. Equivalency: HIST_V 379.

name: Ecoculture and Literature in Japan
description: Ecocultural approach to reading, analyzing, and writing about narratives written in Japan from premodern times to the present.

name: Chinese Literature in Translation: The Vernacular Tradition
description: Readings in drama and fiction, 800 to 1800 AD. The emergence of vernacular genres as distinct from and sometimes opposed to the existing classical genres.

name: Classical Chinese Literature in Translation
description: Poetry, historical and philosophic prose writings and the earliest genres of fiction in classical Chinese (ca. 1100 BC ca. 750 AD).

name: The Construction of South Asian Communities in the Diaspora
description: An examination of contemporary South Asian communities in the diaspora. Topics of particular importance are family life, religious life, notions of space, communal memory, literary and visual representation.

name: Topics in Japanese Cultural History II: The Early Modern Age
description: Focuses each year on a specific topic related to the culture of early modern Japan.

name: Chinese Film Classics
description: Introduction to and analysis of artistically significant films made in mainland China during the first half century of Chinese film history.

name: Guided Case Study in Agricultural Real Estate
description: An agriculturally-focused version of BUSI 499. Prerequisite: All of BUSI 330, BUSI 331, BUSI 442, BUSI 452.

name: Modern Chinese Fiction in Translation
description: Reading of selected novels and stories written between 1750 and the present.

name: Topics in Traditional Chinese Vernacular Literature
description: Traditional Chinese culture as seen through reading and discussion of exemplary literary works in the vernacular language.

name: Asian Literature in Translation: A Comparative Approach
description: A comparative approach to the literatures of East, South and Southeast Asia focusing on a specific theme.

name: Poetic Life in Classical India
description: Cultural explorations in the poetry, theatre, and ornate prose writings of India in the classical period (c. 300-1300 CE).

name: Income Property Guided Case Study
description: The income property appraisal process, focusing both on valuation techniques as well as general research and report writing skills. Prerequisite: All of BUSI 330, BUSI 331, BUSI 442, BUSI 452.

name: Intermediate Managerial Accounting: Decision Making and Performance Evaluation
Foundations in  Accounting
description: Same as HCEC 502; credit will not be given for both.

name: Traditional Korean Literature in Translation
description: An introduction to Korean literature from ancient times to 1900.

name: International Business Management
description: Development of general environmental framework for international business studies by drawing on international and development economics, research into government-business relations and studies in comparative socio-cultural systems and political systems. Prerequisite: BUSI 293 and either(a) all of ECON 101, ECON 102 or (b) ECON 309. Corequisite: Two of BUSI 294, BUSI 329, BUSI 370, BUSI 465.

name: Introduction to Problems in Method and Theory in Anthropology
description: A survey of basic concepts and procedures in the cross-cultural study of human societies.

name: Anthropology of Drugs
description: Illicit and/or licit drugs through historical, political, cultural and societal examples.

name: Contemporary Social Problems
description: Cultural background to contemporary events; problems of nationalism and regional conflicts, economic and social development, gender, religion and social change. Course may stress a different region of the world in different years.

name: Witches, Vampires, and Zombies: Anthropology of the Supernatural
description: Anthropological approaches to supernatural beliefs in both traditional and contemporary societies.

name: Introduction to Cultural Anthropology
description: Basic concepts and methods of anthropology; culture and race; comparative study of social systems, religion, symbolism, art, and other institutions. Examples are drawn from a variety of cultures.

name: Culture, Race and Inequality
description: Anthropological critiques of racism, colonialism and ongoing structural inequalities.

name: Culture Through the Animal Body: Fundamentals of Zooarchaeology
description: Methods to study animal bones and shell remains to understand the ways that people acquired food, negotiated their social status, and contributed to ceremonial practices. Prerequisite: ARCL 103.

name: Eating Culture
description: An anthropological exploration of how the collection, cultivation and consumption of food shapes human society and culture.

name: Japanese Popular Culture
description: Television shows, dramas, movies, advertising, marketing, manga (Japanese style comics), anime (Japanese animation), theatrical forms, popular literature, popular music, fashion fads, tourism, toys, and sports.

name: The Anthropology of Insurrections and Revolution
description: Analysis of insurrections and revolutions from a comparative perspective.

name: The Family in Cross-Cultural Perspective
description: A cross-cultural comparison of family and kinship to provide an understanding of variations in the structure and meaning of marriage relations; forms of domestic organization; and the sexual division of labour, property, and inheritance.

name: Culture and Communication
description: The study of communication; the relation between communication and its cultural context with emphasis on verbal and non-verbal communication, cross-cultural communication, and cultural differences in the use of oral, literate, and electronic media.

name: Sex, Gender, and Culture
description: An anthropological exploration of how understandings of sex and gender are culturally and historically shaped.

name: Contemporary Indigenous Cultural Expressions
description: Forms and styles of indigenous expressive arts, and their current place in the lives of Indigenous Peoples. Prerequisite: ANTH 220 is recommended.

name: Studies in the History of a Major Asian Civilization
description: Study of an Asian culture area different from those covered in existing courses. Not given every year. Consult Department for details. May be taken multiple times on different subjects for credit.

name: South Asian Beyond South Asia
description: A history of South Asian peoples and communities that emigrated overseas, including Indo-Canadians.

name: Japan from Feudal to Modern State
description: Japanese history from 1600 to the Meiji Restoration. Political, economic, social and cultural forces which were involved in transforming Japan.

name: Tibetan and Himalayan Culture and Society
description: History and culture of the Himalayan regions, including India, China, Tibet, Nepal, and Bhutan.

name: Race and Ethnicity in Japanese Literature and Film
description: Examines relations between majority and minority groups in Japanese society and changing definitions of Japan through literature and film from Japan.

name: Contemporary Indigenous Issues in British Columbia
description: Anthropological perspectives on contemporary Indigenous issues in British Columbia.

name: Myth, Ritual and Epic in Ancient India
description: Myths of creation Gods and goddesses of the Vedic pantheon. Connections with myths in other parts of the world, particularly in the Indo-European tradition. Literary representations of the myths.

name: Introduction to Archaeology:  Past perspectives and Future Promise
description: A critical introductory overview to the discipline of archaeology, its functions and entanglements, and potential contributions and transformations for the future.

name: Tibetan Buddhism
description: Religious terrain of the Tibetan cultural realm, looking at the history and development of Tibetan Buddhism and key ideas of the four main Tibetan Buddhist traditions.

name: Premodern Japan
description: Japanese history (political, economic, social and cultural) to 1600.

name: Buddhism in Korea
description: Historical, cultural and philosophical development of Korean Buddhism.

name: Great Archaeological Discoveries
description: An examination of some momentous discoveries in archaeology that have shaped our knowledge of the ancient world and the history of humanity.

name: Ancient North America
description: Introductory survey of North American archaeology comparing the ancient cultures from all major regions of Canada and the US.

name: Bones: The Origins of Humanity
description: The origin and evolution of the human lineage and the emergence of human biological and cultural traits with emphasis on the fossil record before the Pleistocene.

name: Premodern India
description: A survey of the history and culture of India from the earliest historic period to 1200 and the coming of Islam, with emphasis on the evolution of classical Hindu civilization.

name: Korean Language and Writing in Culture and Society
description: An examination of Korean language and writing using approaches from sociolinguistics, the sociology of language, and linguistic anthropology.

name: The Rise of Korean Civilization
description: The evolution of a distinctive Korean civilization within the East Asian cultural sphere. Primary focus on cultural, social and political development from the earliest times to the sixteenth century.

name: Taming the Wild: Animals, Alcohol and Agriculture
description: How, when and why humans became dependent on cultivated foods and domestic animals and the methods used to document plant and animal domestication.

name: Doctoral Dissertation
description: Equivalency: CNRS_V 649.

name: Master's Thesis
description: Credit will be granted for only one of CNRS_V 549 or AMNE_V 599. Equivalency: CNRS_V 549.

name: Archaeological Methods
description: Introduces the methods and principles applied in anthropological archaeology and cultural-historical research.

name: History of Early China
description: History of China from the earliest times to the disintegration of the Tang empire. Students will acquire the analytical skills and tools to understand the origins and foundations of Chinese society. Credit will be granted for only one of ASIA_V 320 or HIST_V 378. Equivalency: HIST_V 378.

name: Contemporary Chinese Popular Cultures
description: Chinese popular cultures of the late twentieth and early twenty-first centuries, in relation to social changes, national policies, individual choices, everyday experience, and globalization.

name: Archaeological Interpretation
description: Current theoretical developments explored through the practice of archaeology. Examples drawn from a range of times and places focusing on emerging technologies, food production, colonial encounters and culture contact, materiality and symbolic systems, social inequality and complexity, and human-environmental interactions.

name: Japanese Culture and Society
description: Japanese culture and society: patterns of organization, value systems, family, education, work, minorities and diversity, harmony and conflict, urban/rural differences, gender, sexuality, youth, tradition, continuity, change, and future prospects.

name: Ancient Latin America
description: The archaeology of ancient Mexico, Central and South America, highlighting recent discoveries about the emergence and growth of civilizations such as the Aztecs, Maya, Zapotec, Inca, Chimor and their ancestors.

name: Summer Field Training in Archaeology
description: Intensive training in excavation techniques and interpretation, including mapping procedures, recording, preliminary analysis, and reporting. Students will participate in an excavation for the Summer Session and will use this excavation as a basis for lectures, discussions and reports. Additional Field Trip Fees are charged for this course.

name: Celebrity Culture in Chinese Societies
description: Histories, controversies, and implications of celebrity culture in Chinese societies, with a focus on the entanglement of author, audience, and media across different sociopolitical contexts.

name: The Emergence of Complex Societies in Eurasia and Africa
description: Archaeological evidence and theories for the origins and spread of settled village life, food production systems, and complex social and political organization: Early Neolithic period through to the appearance of the old world civilizations.

name: The Archaeology of Collapse and Sustainability
description: An evaluation of the issues of sustainability and collapse of ecological and social systems through the archaeological study of the past.

name: Forensic Anthropology
description: The application of methods from biological anthropology and archaeology to the identification, recovery, and analysis of skeletal remains from crime scenes, mass disasters, and unexplained deaths.

name: Archaeology of Hunter-Gatherer-Forager-Societies
description: Early hunter-gatherer-forager societies, spanning the period from the emergence of the first tool-using hominins to the origins of agriculture.

name: Contemporary Indigenous Issues in a Global Perspective
description: Anthropological perspectives on contemporary issues of public policy, law, and political activity, as they affect Indigenous Peoples in Canada and globally. Prerequisite: ANTH 220 is recommended.

name: Anthropology of Rural Peoples and the Global Economy
description: A comparative study of rural peoples (such as small-scale horticulturists, artisans and craft workers, peasants, fisherfolk, or industrial/manufacturing workers) in the global economy.

name: Art, Aesthetics and Anthropology
description: Anthropological perspectives on art, aesthetics, and expressive culture.

name: Anthropology of Childhood
description: Examines the life stage of childhood through various anthropological perspectives, and the evolutionary and social factors that shape human childhood. Explores childhood activities and culture to critically engage with reasons behind distinct patterns in human upbringing.

name: Ethnography of the Pacific Islands: Polynesia and Micronesia
description: Major cultural groupings in Polynesia and Micronesia, emphasizing both traditional cultures and the incorporation of the region into modern international institutions.

name: Understanding Asian Diasporic Health and Well-Being
description: Social issues that impact the health of Asian Canadian communities, with emphasis on race, colonialism, migration, community diversity, and intersectional identities.

name: The Anthropology of Social and Cultural Relationships
description: A survey of the social and cultural bases of relationships including changing family, kinship, social networks, groups, and organizations, based on theoretical analysis and case studies.

name: Culture, Power & Politics
description: Topics in political anthropology; ethnographic and theoretical approaches to nationalism, globalization, political systems, international movements and organizations; anthropology of the state.

name: Linguistic Anthropology
description: A survey of the ethnographic uses of language data and the techniques of linguistic analysis.

name: Ethnography of Latin America
description: Indigenous peoples of Latin America, emphasizing both pre-Columbian cultural traditions and socioeconomic and cultural changes from the Colonial period to the present.

name: Museums, Heritage and Memory
description: Museums, galleries, monuments, and other cultural institutions' relations to our perception of history and geography.

name: Oral Tradition
description: An ethnographic perspective on the dynamics of oral tradition in various oral and literate cultures; the characteristics and roles of oral genres including folktale, genealogy, oral history, autobiography, and myth in these societies; and the relationship between orality and literacy.

name: Ethnography of the Pacific Islands: Melanesia
description: Major cultural groupings in Melanesia, emphasizing both traditional cultures and the incorporation of the region into modern international institutions.

name: Asian Canadian Community-Based Media
description: Digital media production in the context of community engagement. Includes critical media literacy, community-based research ethics, project design, training in media forms such audio, video, photography, and web publishing.

name: Asian Migrations in a Global Context
description: Transpacific, migratory and socio-cultural connections of Asian migrations in a global context. Prerequisite: Minimum 2nd year standing, 3rd year standing recommended.

name: Studies in an Asian Language (Basic Course)
description: Introduction to the fundamentals of an Asian language not normally taught in the Department. Not given every year. Consult the Department for details.

name: Studies in an Asian Language (Intermediate Course)
description: Recommended pre-requisite: ASLA 300, permission of the instructor is also acceptable.

name: Introduction to Modern Asia
description: A survey of the emergence of modern Asia. Aims at an understanding of how the various peoples of Asia have maintained distinctive cultural identities despite centuries of political, economic, social and cultural change.

name: Language and Power
description: A sociolinguistic examination of the role of language in articulating, maintaining, and subverting power relations in society.

name: Directed Studies in Asian Canadian and Asian Migration
description: General reading and/or a research undertaking within the scope of Asian Canadian and Asian Migration. Prerequisite: Permission of the Chair of the ACAM program.

name: Introduction to Religions in Asia
description: A survey of religious traditions of Asia, including communities, professionals, practices and beliefs of small-scale and large-scale societies. Approaches and theories drawn from the field of religious studies.

name: Introduction to Ecological Anthropology
description: Analysis of the relations between human societies and the ecological aspects of their environment (including technology, society, and ideology). Previously ANTH 460.

name: Introduction to Traditional Asia
description: A survey of the histories and cultures of Asia before 1600 and the coming of the Europeans. Emphasis will be given to parallel themes in the development of the civilizations of South, Southeast and East Asia.

name: Cultural Foundations of South Asia
description: A survey of South Asian cultures, including language and literature, art, religion, polity and society, as they developed in the past and have been transformed in the modern period.

name: Traditions of Yoga
description: Philosophical, religious, and cultural development of yoga in classical and medieval South Asia and its relation to contemporary globalized practice.

name: Conservation of Organic Materials
description: Conservation of organic materials within a museum environment; the nature of materials, mechanisms of deterioration and principles of preventive conservation. Recommended for students intending to work with cultural materials. Prerequisite: Permission of instructor required.

name: Honours Tutorial
description: Will usually require the presentation of at least one research paper.

name: Anthropology Horizons: Navigating Careers and Shaping Research Futures
description: Essential research and writing skills for graduate school preparation and anthropology career paths. Restricted to students in Anthropology honours, major, and minor programs with 3rd year standing or higher (or permission of instructor).

name: Cultural Foundations of East Asia
description: A comparative survey of the beliefs, assumptions and values which have shaped the civilizations of East Asia in both traditional and modern times.

name: History of Anthropological Thought
description: Various approaches to anthropology, from classical to contemporary.

name: Topics in Contemporary Theory
description: Selected topics in contemporary social and cultural theory which contribute to anthropological analyses. Topics may include Marxist anthropology, critical theory, theories of culture, phenomenology, behavioural ecology, structuralism, hermeneutics, formal theory and examination of specific social theorists.

name: High-Energy Astrophysics
description: Radiative processes. White dwarfs, neutron stars, and black holes. Accreting systems. Gamma-ray bursts.

name: Asian Internets
description: The cultures of contemporary Asia through an exploration of the uses, form, and content of online media from and about Asia.

name: Principles of Modern Astronomy
description: An introduction to the physical processes occurring in the stars, the interstellar medium, and in our own and other galaxies (fourth-year Honours students in the Physics and Astronomy Department may elect this course with special permission of the Department Head).

name: Advanced Studies in Anthropology
description: An intensive examination of selected topics in Anthropology. Consult the Department for this year's offerings.

name: Sex, Sexual Ethics, and Asian Religions
description: Sex and sexual ethics in the scriptures, monastic rules, rituals, and narratives of Asian religions, such as Sikhism, Hinduism, Buddhism, and Confucianism.

name: Conservation of Inorganic Materials
description: Conservation of inorganic materials within a museum environment; the nature of materials, mechanisms of deterioration and principles of preventive conservation. Recommended for students intending to work with cultural materials. Prerequisite: Permission of instructor is required.

name: Astronomical Laboratory
description: Experiments in the use of astronomical instrumentation and data analysis. Use of the 40-cm reflector, spectrograph and electronic detectors. Photometric and spectroscopic analysis of digital data.

name: Racial and Sexual Politics of (Im)mobility
description: Combined anthropological approaches with interdisciplinary theories to understand experiences of mobilities and immobilities shaped by race, gender, sexuality, citizenship and class. Recommended: ANTH 375 or 376, or other upper-level courses focused on migration, gender and sexuality, or social inequality.

name: Anthropology of Law
description: Cross-cultural study of the operation of law within contested systems of meaning, the social organization of law, and forms of consciousness of the participants in legal/justice practices.

name: Special Topics in Ecological Anthropology
description: May include environmental discourse and social movements, anthropological contributions to ecological management systems, or examination of emerging issues in the field. ANTH 360 is recommended as background.

name: Cultural Foundations of Southeast Asia
description: A comparative survey of the different cultures found in the communities of Southeast Asia. Focus will be on language and literature, arts, religion, society and polity, ideologies and belief systems in the past as well as in modern times.

name: Anthropological Study of Social Inequality
description: An anthropological perspective on the historical origins and theoretical explanations of social inequality.

name: Urban Ethnographic Field School (UEFS)
description: Volunteering and fieldwork based in community organizations with theoretical approaches to urban spaces. Students will engage in collaborative research while considering a range of theoretical and methodological approaches. Students may earn a maximum of 6 credits from ANTH 480 and SOCI 480.

name: Cosmology
description: Introduction to the study of the Universe as a whole. Foundations of the Hot Big Bang model, the early Universe, nucleosynthesis, the cosmic microwave background, large-scale structure, galaxy formation and quasars. Credit will be granted for only one of ASTR 403 or PHYS 571.

name: Galactic Astronomy
description: The study of the structure, content and evolution of our own and other galaxies, including the study of the physical processes occurring in the interstellar medium and galactic nuclei.

name: Anthropological Study of Local Ecological Knowledge
description: Analysis of the concepts of ecological anthropology via the medium of local ecological knowledge. ANTH 360 is recommended as background.

name: Astronomical and Astrophysical Measurements
description: Astronomical instrumentation and techniques for ground and space-based observations. Theory of measurement, imaging, interferometry and spectroscopy of electromagnetic radiation at optical, radio, infrared, and X-ray wavelengths. Astronomical data analysis.

name: Honours Thesis in Astronomy
description: A research project in astronomy, undertaken under the direction of a faculty member, culminating in a thesis.

name: Architectural Design Abroad
description: Design studio component of term-long study abroad offering. Prerequisite: All of ARCH 500, ARCH 501.

name: Ethnographic Film Methods
description: Ethnographic digital video production, including methods of ethnographic fieldwork, creation of field notes, and research design; basics of digital video planning, production, and editing. Production fees are charged for this course. Prerequisite: ANTH 378 is recommended.

name: Planetary Science
description: Structure of planetary systems, planetary interiors, planet formation, planetary atmospheres, meteoritics, impact cratering.

name: Graduate Project Part I
description: Preparation of a graduation design project including literature review. Prerequisite: All of ARCH 521, ARCH 523, ARCH 531, ARCH 532, ARCH 533.

name: Seminar in Architecture
description: An in-depth study of a selected topic in architecture.

name: Graduate Project Part II
description: Design component, completion, and defense of the graduation design project. Honours/Pass/Fail. Prerequisite: [ARCH548] and no more than 18 credits outstanding beyond ARCH 549

name: Directed Studies in Architecture
description: Directed research and exploration of selected topics in architecture.

name: Seminar: Technology and Analysis
description: Topics across a range of building material and construction technology-based subject matter. Prerequisite: All of ARCH 511, ARCH 512.

name: Professional Practice
description: Ethical, legal and business context of professional practice, including contracts, project management.

name: Communicating Construction
description: Understanding the role, composition, organization, and conventions of the formal documentation necessary for communication of an architectural design to those undertaking the construction. Prerequisite: All of ARCH 511, ARCH 512.

name: Seminar: Contemporary Practice
description: Topics across a range of practice related subject matter.

name: Seminar: History and Theory
description: Topics across a range of history/theory-based subject matter.

name: Architectural Design Studio V
description: Prerequisite: ARCH 521.

name: Green Building Contemporary Practice
description: Enhanced building environmental performance and the integration of green building principles, strategies and technologies. Equivalency: HPB501

name: Co-operative Education
description: Approved and supervised work experience in an established company or organization for a minimum of one academic term. Technical report required.

name: Seminar: Environmental Studies
description: An investigation of specialized environmental topics concerning theory and the practice of architecture. Prerequisite: [ARCH513]

name: Research Seminar: Advanced Structure and Generative Methods
description: Structural principles and corresponding mathematical representation as three- and four-dimensional digital models using structural analysis software. Prerequisite: [ARCH512]

name: Professional Experience
description: Prerequisite: All of ARST_V 500, ARST_V 510, ARST_V 520, ARST_V 515, ARST_V 516, ARST_V 555, and ARST_V 573

name: World Art and Architecture Before 1800
description: Introduction to the histories of art and the built environment in a global context.

name: Thesis
description: Prerequisite: ARST 591.

name: Art, Patrons, and Audiences in the Middle Ages
description: A thematic study of the relationship between patrons and audiences in painting, sculpture, and architecture through the 15th century.

name: Art & Feminism(s): Histories, Lineages, Legacies
description: Feminist art and visual culture, from the political activism of the feminist first wave to its intersections with present-day social justice movements.

name: What is Modern Art?
description: Select issues in 20th-century art and the visual and built environment.

name: Byzantium: Arts of an Empire
description: Art, architecture, and material culture of the Byzantine Empire situated in the eastern Mediterranean (c. 300-1453); focus on social and cultural contexts of artistic production, including interactions with neighboring cultures. Credit will only be granted for one of ARTH 210, CNRS 207 or AMNE 279. Equivalency: AMNE 279

name: Indigenous Arts of North America
description: A survey of the artistic production by Indigenous peoples of North America from pre-contact times to the present.

name: Asian Arts: From Chinese Warriors to Bollywood Posters
description: A thematic examination of Asian arts, such as historic, religious, and secular painting and sculpture to contemporary visual culture.

name: Pre-Hispanic Arts of Central and South America
description: The relevance of various arts to social institutions in ancient societies of Peru and Mesoamerica.

name: Applied Ethics
description: Credit limited to students in the Joint Degree Program in Biochemistry and Forensic Science. Same as BCIT LIBS 7002.

name: Ways of Seeing: Introduction to Visual Studies
description: Drawing on examples from across history and around the world, this course deals with the role of the visual in society, culture, and everyday experience.

name: Asian Architecture: Sacred and Urban Spaces
description: Select built forms in Asia, such as temples, tombs, palaces, cities and gardens, and their relations to cultural, social and political systems.

name: Research Methodology and Measurement Models
description: Credit limited to students in the Joint Degree Program in Biochemistry and Forensic Science. Same as BCIT FSCT 7910.

name: Intermediate Forensic Science I
description: Block registration for the forensic biology: DNA typing theory, quality assurance, and business management for forensic science courses taken in the Joint BCIT/UBC Degree in Biochemistry and Forensic Science. Registration is limited to students in the Joint Degree Program.

name: Forensic Biology; DNA Typing Theory
description: Credit limited to students in the Joint Degree Program in Biochemistry and Forensic Science. Same as BCIT FSCT 8150.

name: Quality Assurance for Forensic Science
description: Credit limited to students in the Joint Degree Program in Biochemistry and Forensic Science. Same as BCIT FSCT 8370.

name: Introductory Forensic Science II
description: Block registration for the applied ethics and report writing and communication for forensic investigation courses taken in the Joint BCIT/UBC Degree in Biochemistry and Forensic Science. Registration is limited to students in the Joint Degree Program.

name: Art, Colonialism, and Indigeneity
description: Tensions and conflicts resulting from the expansion of trade and encounters among cultures, ethnicities, and religious practices, explored in visual art and architecture from the sixteenth century to the advent of the modern era.

name: Report Writing and Communication for Forensic Investigation
description: Credit limited to students in the Joint Degree Program in Biochemistry and Forensic Science. Same as BCIT COMM 7200.

name: Introductory Forensic Science I
description: Block registration for the introduction to forensic science course taken in the Joint BCIT/UBC Degree in Biochemistry and Forensic Science. Registration is limited to students in the Joint Degree Program.

name: Intermediate Forensic Science II
description: Block registration for the forensic biology: evidence recovery, research methodology, and elective courses taken in the Joint BCIT/UBC Degree in Biochemistry and Forensic Science. Registration is limited to students in the Joint Degree Program.

name: The Science of Fingerprints - Theory
description: Credit limited to students in the Joint Degree Program in Biochemistry and Forensic Science. Same as BCIT FSCT 8320.

name: Forensic Toxicology
description: Credit limited to students in the Joint Degree Program in Biochemistry and Forensic Science. Same as BCIT FSCT 8240.

name: Business Management for Forensic Science
description: Credit limited to students in the Joint Degree Program in Biochemistry and Forensic Science. Same as BCIT FSCT 8371.

name: Medico-Legal Aspects of Alcohol
description: Credit limited to students in the Joint Degree Program in Biochemistry and Forensic Science. Same as BCIT FSCT 8230.

name: Forensic Biology: DNA Typing Applications
description: Credit limited to students in the Joint Degree Program in Biochemistry and Forensic Science. Same as BCIT FSCT 8160.

name: Law for Forensic Science
description: Credit limited to students in the Joint Degree Program in Biochemistry and Forensic Science. Same as BCIT FSCT 7009.

name: The Expert Witness - Prepared for Court
description: Credit limited to students in the Joint Degree Program in Biochemistry and Forensic Science. Same as BCIT FSCT 7010.

name: Co-op Work Placement I
description: Approved and supervised technical work experience in either an industrial, public, or academic laboratory or a law enforcement agency for a minimum of 14 weeks. Technical report required. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-op Program in Biochemistry and Forensic Science. Prerequisite: Completion of academic third year in Biochemistry and Forensic Science Honours program is required.
prerequisites: Completion of academic third year in Biochemistry and Forensic Science Honours program

name: Instrumental Analysis for Forensic Chemistry
description: Credit limited to students in the Joint Degree Program in Biochemistry and Forensic Science. Same as BCIT FSCT 8156.

name: Co-op Work Placement IV
description: Approved and supervised technical work experience in either an industrial, public, or academic laboratory or a law enforcement agency for a minimum of 14 weeks. Technical report required. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-op Program in Biochemistry and Forensic Science. Prerequisite: FSCT 498.

name: Problem-Based Learning In Bioinformatics
description: Develops the student's ability to exchange ideas in small groups focused on real but simplified problems in bioinformatics. Problems are carefully selected to cover all aspects of Bioinformatics research. Required of students in the Bioinformatics graduate program. Students not registered in the Bioinformatics graduate program must get permission to register in this course.

name: Co-op Work Placement II
description: Approved and supervised technical work experience in either an industrial, public, or academic laboratory or a law enforcement agency for a minimum of 14 weeks. Technical report required. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-op Program in Biochemistry and Forensic Science. Prerequisite: FSCT 398.

name: Forensic Biology: Evidence Recovery
description: Credit limited to students in the Joint Degree Program in Biochemistry and Forensic Science. Same as BCIT FSCT 8155.

name: Co-op Work Placement III
description: Approved and supervised technical work experience in either an industrial, public, or academic laboratory or a law enforcement agency for a minimum of 14 weeks. Technical report required. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-op Program in Biochemistry and Forensic Science. Prerequisite: FSCT 399.

name: Refugees, Resistance, and Activism
description: Examines the movements around refugee and immigrant rights in various geographic contexts, through the lens of ethnographic texts and media. Explores how migrants and refugees are taking an active role in transforming the global system of borders. Recommended pre-requisite: at least one 200-level social science course (e.g. ANTH, SOCI, GEOG, POLI)

name: Advanced Forensic Science I
description: Block registration for the forensic biology: DNA typing applications, law and forensic science courses taken in the Joint BCIT/UBC Degree in Biochemistry and Forensic Science. Registration is limited to students in the Joint Degree Program.

name: Advanced Forensic Science II
description: Block registration for the expert witness testimony instrumental analysis for forensic chemistry and forensic toxicology courses taken in the Joint BCIT/UBC Degree in Biochemistry and Forensic Science. Registration is limited to students in the Joint Degree Program.

name: Ethnography of China
description: Advanced studies in the ethnography of China, premodern and contemporary. Topics may include kinship, rural and urban social structure, stratification and mobility, religion, national power structures, and social change in Chinese society.

name: First Peoples of North America
description: Anthropological perspectives of indigenous cultures and societies of North America. Prerequisite: ANTH 329 is recommended.

name: The Anthropology of Energy and Sustainability
description: Human dimensions of energy resource extraction, production and consumption, emphasizing ethnographic case studies. Critical debates around alternative energy transitions in the context of changing climates, with attention to cultural and historical settings, community perspectives and social justice.

name: Principles of Field Work
description: An examination of field work as the basic setting for ethnographic research. Research design; relationships with study participants, field techniques, and data analysis and presentation.

name: Ethnography in Circumpolar North: Comparative Perspectives.
description: An examination of relationships between indigenous people and nation states in Greenland, Canada, Alaska and Siberia, using ethnographic methods.

name: Statistical Methods for High Dimensional Biology
description: Equivalency: STAT540, GSAT540

name: Directed Studies
description: Advanced study under the direction of a faculty member composed of laboratory sessions and directed readings related to selected areas of bioinformatics. Students must get permission to register in this course.

name: Ethnography of Special Areas
description: An advanced study of ethnographic and theoretical problems. A different region may be studied each term.

name: Advanced Topics in the Anthropology of Gender
description: Contemporary theory employed in the anthropological study of gender.

name: History of Anthropology
description: The development of anthropological theory and practice in institutional contexts.

name: Anthropology of Media
description: Analysis of contemporary mass media and of the anthropological use of media (photography, film, digital audio and video, etc.).

name: Diasporas and Belonging: Anthropological Perspectives
description: Examines how multiple generations of migrants find, build, and reimagine what community and belonging are beyond the confines of the nation-state. Centres ethnographies of diasporic identity and personhood. Recommended: at least one 200-level social science course (e.g. ANTH, SOCI, GEOG, POLI).

name: Topics in Applied Anthropology
description: Advanced study of the theory and practice of applied, action, and consultancy anthropology. Topics may include the application of anthropology to questions of aboriginal rights and title, education, medicine, development, women and development, tourism, and other social issues.

name: Field Methods
description: Intensive examination and application of selected methods of ethnographic data-collection, e.g., visual anthropology, anthropological interviewing, genealogies, ethnographic semantics, life histories, oral traditions. Consult department for current description.

name: Anthropology of Globalization
description: Theories on the global flow of people, commodities, images, and ideas with critical ethnographic attention to the different ways people respond to globalization.

name: Business Economics
description: Introduction to microeconomics and macroeconomics principles with applications to accounting and business decision making.

name: Religion and Society
description: Comparative study of religious beliefs, practices, and movements; relations between religious, social, and political institutions; religion as a force for stability and change; anthropological/sociological theories of religion.

name: Introduction to Quantitative Decision Analysis
description: Introduction to decision models in business, including basic optimization, linear programming, probability, decision analysis, random variables, simulation, and solving decision problems using spreadsheet tools.

name: Application of Statistics in Business
description: Methods and applications of statistics in business; data analysis, descriptive regression; data generation; sampling distributions; hypothesis testing; confidence intervals; two sample problems; inference in regression.

name: Real Estate Finance in a Canadian Context
description: History, function and mechanics of Canadian mortgage markets.

name: Business Communications
description: Basic communication theory, communications in organizations. Includes written and oral practice in lab sessions.

name: Topics in Architectural History II (1900-Present)
description: History of architecture in the post-1900 time period. Technological, political, social, and economic changes which have influenced architecture and related fields.

name: Introductory Financial Accounting
description: Introduction to the construction and interpretation of financial reports prepared primarily for external use.

name: Principles of Organizational Behaviour
description: An introductory examination of work organizations and the behaviour of individuals within them. Phenomena to be studied include organizational structure, environments, group processes, motivation and leadership.

name: Urban and Real Estate Economics
description: Comprehensive treatment of urban and real estate economics; introduction to study of cities and real estate market; analytical microeconomic principles. Prerequisite: All of BUSI_V 100, BUSI_V 101.

name: Information Systems
description: Introduction to information technology related to business use: design, implementation, and application of information systems.

name: Introductory Management Accounting
description: Introduction to the development and use of accounting information for management planning and control, and the development of cost information for financial reports. Prerequisite: BUSI293 or equivalent. Corequisite: BUSI293 or equivalent.

name: Intermediate Financial Accounting I
description: An examination of accounting as a means of measurement and as an information system for external reporting purposes. Prerequisite: BUSI293 or equivalent.

name: Case Studies in Residential Valuation
description: Examines common issues that affect the practice of residential real estate valuation. Credit will be granted for only one of BUSI 352 or both BUSI 442 and BUSI 452. Prerequisite: BUSI 330. BUSI 121, BUSI 344 recommended.

name: Real Estate Investment Analysis and Advanced Income Appraisal
description: Valuation techniques for income real estate, including income method of appraisal, tax consequences of real property ownership, and portfolio analysis methodology. Prerequisite: All of BUSI 121, BUSI 330.

name: Design Media I
description: Foundations of manual and digital skills and concepts employing a variety of subjects, techniques and software. Credit will be granted for only one of ARCH 515, DES 211 or ENDS 320.

name: Architectural Technology I
description: Architectural technology, including materials and methods, construction types, and building system integration. Strong emphasis on enclosure performance with focus on smaller buildings and light wood framing construction.

name: Foundations of Real Estate Appraisal
description: Introduction to concepts and techniques for appraising the value of real estate. Recommended pre-requisite: BUSI 121.

name: Statistical and Computer Applications in Valuation
description: Explores creative, practical uses of statistical and computer applications in determining and analyzing real estate value. Through case studies and hands-on computer work, students will learn the fundamentals of exploratory data analysis and appraisal valuation modelling.

name: Design Media II
description: Intermediate manual and digital skills and concepts employing a variety of subjects, techniques and software. Credit will be granted for only one of ARCH 517, ARCH 437 or DES 212. Prerequisite: ARCH 515.

name: Architectural Design Studio IV
description: Prerequisite: All of ARCH 511, ARCH 512, ARCH 513, ARCH 520. Corequisite: All of ARCH 531, ARCH 533.

name: Environmental Systems and Controls I
description: Building form and fabric considerations to assure appropriate thermal, luminous, sonic, and atmospheric conditions within buildings.

name: Current Issues in Architecture
description: A seminar examining current issues in Architecture, based on reading assignments, papers and presentations. Enrolment is limited to facilitate discussion.

name: International Exchange in Architecture
description: Pass/Fail. Pre-approved studies in architecture in an international context.

name: Contemporary Theories in Architecture
description: Theoretical propositions and their built manifestations. Prerequisite: 6 credits of ARCH 504, ARCH 505.

name: Architectural Design Studio III
description: Prerequisite: ARCH 501.

name: Environmental Systems and Controls II
description: Mechanical and electrical services of buildings and their integration with architectural form and fabric. Prerequisite: [ARCH513]

name: Structures I
description: Quantitative and qualitative means for understanding of statics, materials and flow of force through a structure.

name: Architectural Structures II
description: Complex multi-span and continuous systems: effective material configuration, approximate methods of analysis, selection of appropriate structural systems, earthquake configuration and high rises. Prerequisite: [ARCH512]

name: Forest-fire Weather and Climate
description: Synoptic and mesoscale meteorology and weather forecasting applied to wildfires. Effect of weather on fire behaviour, danger, smoke, climate and sustainability at the urban-forest interface.  Prerequisite: One of ATSC 201, GEOS 200.

name: Honours Project
description: Honours students must submit a graduating report based on a project undertaken with the approval of the Associate Chair of the Atmospheric Science Program.

name: Co-operative Work Placement IV
description: Approved and supervised technical work experience in an industrial, university or government setting for a minimum of 14 weeks. Normally taken in Winter Session (Term 1) of the fifth year. Technical report required. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-operative Education Program in Atmospheric Science. Prerequisite: [ATSC498]

name: Architectural Technology II
description: Analysis and design of advanced assemblies. Integration of multiple building systems within a wide range of construction types, and more complex enclosures in a variety of climatic conditions. Emphasis on technical performance, durability and sustainability. Prerequisite: [ARCH511]

name: Numerical Techniques for Ocean, Atmosphere and Earth Scientists
description: Credit will be granted for only one of ATSC 409 or ATSC 506/EOSC 511. Equivalency: EOSC511

name: Numerical Weather Prediction
description: Prerequisite: All of a fluid-dynamics course, a numerical-methods course, as well as computer-programming skills.

name: Directed Studies
description: Investigation of a topic to be agreed upon by a member of the faculty and the student. Permission of the undergraduate advisor and of the supervising faculty member is required before registration.

name: Study of Architecture Abroad
description: More than one section may be taken concurrently.

name: Co-operative Work Placement II
description: Restricted to students admitted to the M.Sc. Co-operative Education Option in Atmospheric Science. Prerequisite: ATSC 597.

name: Co-operative Work Placement I
description: Restricted to students admitted to the M.Sc. Co-operative Education Option in Atmospheric Science.

name: Institutions of Adult Education
description: The history, roles, and activities of institutions in the field of adult education. Institutions in Canada, Great Britain, and the United States are emphasized, and some experiences in other countries are examined.

name: Co-operative Work Placement III
description: Approved and supervised technical work experience in an industrial, university or government setting for a minimum of 14 weeks. Normally taken in the Summer Session (Terms 1 and 2) after fourth year. Technical report required. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-operative Education Program in Atmospheric Science. Prerequisite: ATSC 399 and one of ATSC 303, GEOB 304, GEOS 304.

name: The Community Practice of Adult Education
description: Community based adult education with particular emphasis on the application of knowledge of the social, economic, cultural and political environment in developing and conducting adult education programs with an for individuals and groups.

name: Student Directed Seminars in Atmospheric Science
description: Self-directed, collaborative studies in atmospheric science, in a group-learning environment, initiated and coordinated by senior undergraduate students with the supervision of a faculty advisor. Course structure, enrolment, and delivery methods will comply with the Handbook for Student Directed Seminars. Prerequisite: Prerequisite: Third-year standing.

name: Diploma Seminar and Internship in Adult Education
Introduction to African Studies
description: Cultural, historical, and geographical issues of African Studies.

name: Developing Short Courses, Workshops and Seminars
description: Organization and administration of adult education events such as short courses, seminars, workshops, conferences and institutes.

name: Boundary-Layer Meteorology
description: Theoretical and empirical analysis of the atmospheric boundary layer with particular emphasis on energy and mass exchanges near the Earth's surface.

name: Southern Africa
description: Pre-colonial, colonial, and contemporary, emphasizing South Africa. Credit will be granted for only one of AFST 312 or HIST 312. Equivalency: HIST 312

name: Arts of Africa and the African Diasporas
description: Comparative exploration of art practices and their relationship to colonial and postcolonial histories. Credit will be granted for only one of AFST 309 or ARTH 309. Equivalency: ARTH 309

name: Teaching Adults
description: Planning, conducting and evaluating instruction for adults. Consideration is given to different beliefs and ways of thinking about teaching.

name: An Overview of Adult Education
description: Survey of adult education theory and practice in Canada and the world. The focus is on the purpose and participation in, adult education, characteristics of learners, and the training of adult educators.

name: History of Africa
description: An introduction to selected themes and historical approaches in African history. These may include African geography and identities, sources and methodology, pre-modern state formation, gender relations, world religions, labour systems, colonialism, and post-colonialism. Credit will be granted for only one of AFST 256 or HIST 256. Equivalency: HIST 256

name: Writing About Japan
description: Literary, historiographic, religious, and feminist approaches to Japanese myths, legal tracts, religious tales, fiction, and poetry.

name: Introduction to Buddhism
description: Origins, basic teachings, development of Theravada, Mahayana, and Tantric traditions, historical spread first through Asia and later the world, and Buddhism in contemporary societies.

name: Topics in African Studies
description: Topics will vary from year to year. Consult the program website (https://africanstudies.arts.ubc.ca) for further details.

name: Perspectives in African Studies: Literary and Theoretical Approaches
description: Major issues and theoretical approaches.

name: Perspectives in African Studies: A Social Science Approach
description: Major issues and theoretical approaches.

name: Encountering Asia
description: Introduction to the literary, religious, and philosophical traditions of at least two Asian cultures using foundational texts. Students will learn about these traditions by encountering them historically as well as through the lenses of their own diverse identities and contexts.

name: Myth, Literature, and Film in North India
description: Indian literary and mythological texts, in genres from epic to lyric, as recast in contemporary Hindi film.

name: Religion in South Asia
description: The major religious traditions of South Asia, including Hinduism, Islam, Sikhism, and Buddhism; the significance of religious thought and practice in premodern India, as well as the continuing impact of religion in today's globalized South Asia.

name: Buddhism in the Modern Era
description: Buddhism from the nineteenth century to present day with special emphasis on its history and character in local settings, including specific traditions such as Tibetan Nyingma and Japanese Zen, as well as the development of a modern and global Buddhism.

name: Survey of South and Southeast Asian Performing Arts
description: An historical perspective of the performing arts of South and Southeast Asia, highlighting the role of music, dance, and the dramatic arts in the lives of actors and audiences. Option to complete a practicum performance.

name: Modern Africa
description: Africa in the 19th and 20th Centuries: Islamic revolutions, the end of the slave trades, colonial conquest, labour struggles, Christianity’s new appeal, PanAfricanism, nationalist resistance, and decolonization. Post-independence challenges of nation-building and economic development. Cultural renaissances and the politics of tradition. Credit will be granted for only one of AFST_V 313 or HIST_V 313. Equivalency: HIST_V 313

name: The Languages of Africa
description: Linguistic survey of the languages of Africa, including typological and historical connections between languages, individual and comparative surveys of sound systems, word structures, sentence structures, semantics, and sociolinguistic properties of a representative selection of languages. Credit will be granted for only one of AFST 308 or LING 308 Equivalency: LING 308

name: Mahayana Buddhism
description: Historical and philosophical development of Mahayana Buddhism.

name: Sex, Gender, and Sexuality in Japanese Literature and Film
description: The integral role that sex, gender, and sexuality play in literary and cinematic works from Japan. Literary works will be read in translation, movies will be subtitled.

name: Asian Horror Cinema: National Nightmares and Specters of Trauma
description: Engaging with the ideologies, industrial histories, socio-cultural contexts, and aesthetics of horror films - and the genre itself - from various Asian cinemas.

name: History of Cantonese Worlds
description: The history, culture, languages, and identities of the multi-faceted Cantonese worlds, in the context of Chinese history and the Cantonese diaspora. Credit will be granted for only one of ASIA_V 323 or HIST_V 377. Equivalency: HIST_V 377.

name: Writing and Culture in East Asia
description: Practical, aesthetic, historical, technological and political issues pertaining to the use of Chinese characters - hanzi (Chinese), kanji (Japanese), or hanccha (Korean) - throughout the region.

name: Esoteric Buddhism
description: Overview of Buddhism's rich and complex esoteric traditions in the Himalayan region and South, Southeast, and East Asia, with particular emphasis on texts, commentaries, and practices from a variety of traditions, locales and time periods.

name: Critical Approaches to Manga and Anime
description: A critical introduction to Japanese manga and anime in the 20th and 21st centuries.

name: Writing Asia
description: This writing-intensive course is to be taken concurrently with ASIA 222. The seminar builds on the materials of ASIA 222. Students must have knowledge of or be enrolled in the study of one of the languages offered in Asian Studies.

name: Muslims in Modern South Asia
description: The history of Muslims in modern South Asia from colonialism to the present.

name: Korean Popular Music in Context
description: History, contexts, and the genres of Korean popular music. Students will analyze specific artists and songs using a range of approaches. While an understanding of basic concepts of music will be helpful, no previous exposure to ethnomusicology or music performance is required.

name: China in World History
description: The history of China in a global context, from the earliest times to the most recent past; how China has changed the world and how engagement with the world has changed China. Credit will be granted for only one of ASIA_V 270 or HIST_V 270. Equivalency: HIST_V 270.

name: Islam in South Asia (750-1750)
description: The history of Islam in South Asia beginning with the first Indo-Islamic interactions, the crystallization of Sufi traditions and sultanates, through the rise of European colonialism.

name: Literature of Hong Kong
description: A survey of the literature of Hong Kong, from classical times to the present. Important periods in literary history (imperial, colonial, post-colonial), major authors (locals, visitors, and writers elsewhere), and important genres, including poetry, essays, and fiction.

name: Theravada Buddhism
description: History, story, and culture of the major form of Buddhism primarily focused on the regions of Sri Lanka, and mainland Southeast Asia, including southern Vietnam, parts of southern China, spread to Nepal, and modern global diffusion.

name: Modern Islam
description: History, culture, values, and sociopolitical movements of the Islamic world from 1500 to the modern day; interconnections between power, politics, gender, and the arts in modern Islamic societies. Recommended as a basis for all other Islamic studies courses.

name: Hong Kong Cinema
description: A survey of the cinema of Hong Kong from the post-war period to the present. The influence of Hong Kong on global cinema, and the forces (artists, studios, audiences, etc.) that have given rise to filmmaking styles and genres perceived as distinctively Hong Kong.

name: Gender in South and Southeast Asia
description: A critical examination of what it means to be a woman or a man within the social and cultural context of South and Southeast Asia. What masculinity and femininity signify in these societies; how these concepts are reaffirmed or challenged.

name: Cantonese Music
description: A history of musical genres with Cantonese lyrics from the nineteenth century to the present. Topics include music and text relationships, major singers, major genres (narrative songs, Cantonese opera, Cantopop). Credit will be granted for only one of ASIA_V 335 or MUSC_V 327. Equivalency: MUSC_V 327.

name: Writing Women in Premodern East Asia
description: The construction of gender in literary writings by and about women in select areas of premodern East Asia.

name: Confucianism in China and Beyond: Reinventions of Tradition
description: Key ideas and trends in Confucian thought and practice from its origins to modern times through primary sources in translation and secondary scholarship.

name: Sufi and Bhakti Devotional Literatures
description: Sufi and Bhakti thought and tradition in South Asia through literary works in translation.

name: Contemporary South Asian Gender and Sexuality Studies
description: Main theories and key concepts with a particular focus on the changing status of women, and gender and sexual minorities.

name: Human Anatomy
description: A correlated course of study for medical and dental students of the structure of the human body including gross and radiological anatomy and embryology. Clinics are held in cooperation with the Departments of Medicine, Orthopaedics, Surgery and Family Practice. Both terms.

name: Study of Sociolinguistics of a Selected African Language
description: Selected African language with emphasis on major syntactic structures, vocabulary, conversation patterns, reading short texts, and the cultural and historical contexts of language use.

name: American Sign Language and Deaf Culture I
description: An introduction to understanding and producing American Sign Language. Emphasizes core grammar and vocabulary, contextual use, connection between language and Deaf culture. For students new to ASL.

name: Seminar in African Art
description: Key debates in the art of Africa and the African diaspora. Credit will be granted for only one of AFST 410 or ARTH 410. Equivalency: ARTH 410

name: Topics in Ancient Mediterranean and Near Eastern History and Culture
description: Selected topics in the history and culture of the ancient Mediterranean, Near East and/or Egypt.

name: African Diasporic Culture in African Canadian Communities
description: African diasporic culture in Canadian society, fostering dialogue with members of African Canadian communities on cultural values, traditions, memory, adaptation and change.

name: Microscopic Human Anatomy
description: A survey course for medical and dental students of the microscopic structure of the human body as studied by light and electron microscopy. Lectures and laboratory sessions. Both terms.

name: The Korean People in Modern Times (1600 to the present)
description: The transformation of Korea from a Confucian state into an industrial nation. The rise of nationalism and modern ideologies in Korea. Cultural, social and economic changes Korea has undergone as it has entered the modern world.

name: Literatures and Cultures of Africa and/or the Middle East
description: Literary and cultural works from Africa; some sections include Africa and the Middle East. Multiple perspectives on local, national, and global issues including colonialism, migration, transnationalism, education, art and politics. May include fiction, poetry, drama, digital media, and other forms. Consult department website for current year's offerings. Credit will be granted for only one of AFST 370 or ENGL 370. Prerequisite: For ENGL courses at the 200- or 300- level, prior completion of at least one 100- level ENGL course is recommended. Equivalency: ENGL 370

name: Gross Anatomy of the Limbs and Trunk
description: Lectures and laboratory sessions on the human gross and functional anatomy of the limbs and trunk. The course includes the study of predissected specimens. For credit only in the Department of Physical Therapy.

name: American Sign Language and Deaf Culture II
description: Skills in using ASL in a range of social contexts. Training in grammar and vocabulary that builds fluency, and in using the language appropriately for meaningful interactions with members of the Deaf community. For students with basic ASL conversational ability. Prerequisite: ASL 100. or by placement.

name: Ancient Greek Warfare
description: Ancient Greek methods and tactics of war plus underlying social, religious and philosophical concepts relating to warfare, through sources in translation. Equivalency: CLST_V 329.

name: Gross Human Anatomy
description: An advanced laboratory course in the structure of the human body.

name: Directed Studies in Anatomy
description: Permission of the Head and supervisor required.

name: Women in the Roman World of Republican and Imperial Times
description: Women in the Roman world in the culture of the Republic and the Empire. Literary, artistic, and mythological sources are compared and contrasted to historical, legal, and archaeological records. Equivalency: CLST_V 312.

name: Women in the Bronze Age, Classical Greek and Hellenistic Cultures
description: The images projected in mythology, literature, and art are compared with realities of women's lives insofar as they can be reconstructed from historical, legal, and archaeological records. Equivalency: CLST_V 311.

name: Slavery in the Ancient Greek and Roman World
description: The study and history of slavery in the Greek and Roman worlds as a political, legal, economic, social, and cultural phenomenon. Equivalency: CLST_V 320.

name: Roman Law
description: The development of Roman private law during the classical period with special attention to family law, contract and delict. Equivalency: CLST_V 308.

name: The Early Roman Empire
description: Roman imperial history during the Julio-Claudian and Flavian periods (30 BC-96 AD).  Prerequisite: One of CLST_V 232, AMNE_V 216. Equivalency: CLST_V 353.

name: Translating the Bible
description: Key issues involved in translating the Bible, with attention to gender, sexuality, race, ethnicity, religion, and colonialism.

name: Elements of Neuroanatomy
description: An introduction to the structure of the human nervous system. Given only in conjunction with PHYL 425. (Open to Medical and Dental students only.)

name: The Roman Army
description: Rome's military from the early Republic to the Imperial period. Topics range from those of a military nature such as equipment and strategy to social topics such as policing and marriage of soldiers. Equivalency: CLST_V 319.

name: Human Anatomy for Physical Therapy Students
description: Microscopic systems anatomy and regional anatomy of the nervous system.  Prerequisite: Registration in Rehabilitation Sciences (RSPT) is required.

name: Jewish Law
description: History, sources, theoretical issues and current state of research about early Jewish legal traditions, focusing on close readings of classic primary texts in English translations. Equivalency: RELG_V 335.

name: Greek Law
description: The study of Greek legal theory, practice, and institutions from their origin in self-help, through the early lawgivers and their codes, to the developed system of Athens in the fifth and fourth centuries. A variety of test cases from the works of the Greek orators will be explored. Equivalency: CLST_V 307.

name: Latin Epic
description: The development of the epic genre in Latin, with detailed study of Vergil's Aeneid, Ovid's Metamorphoses, and Lucan's Civil War, in translation.  Prerequisite: Second-year standing or above. Equivalency: CLST_V 314.

name: Topics in Ancient Mediterranean and Near Eastern Literature and Ideas
description: Selected topics in the literature, ideas, and arts of the ancient Mediterranean, Near East and/or Egypt.

name: Greek Epic
description: Homer's Iliad and Odyssey, in translation.  Prerequisite: Second-year standing or above. Equivalency: CLST_V 313.

name: Sex, Lies, and Violence in the Hebrew Bible
description: An exploration of the Bible's dark side, with emphasis on texts that center on sex, deceit, and murder. Equivalency: RELG_V 307.

name: Introduction to Income Tax
description: A study of income tax from the standpoint of the individual and business enterprise. Prerequisite: BUSI293 or equivalent.

name: Cost Accounting
description: The provision and analysis of cost accounting information that will assist management in making operating decisions and in evaluating operational performance. Prerequisite: All of BUSI_V 294, BUSI_V 370.

name: Residential Property Guided Case Study
description: The residential property appraisal process, focusing both on valuation techniques as well as general research and report writing skills.

name: Business Finance
description: An introduction to the basic principles of financial valuation and an examination of corporate enterprise decisions including working capital management; capital budgeting; capital structures and dividend policy. Prerequisite: BUSI293 or equivalent.

name: Introduction to Management Information Systems
description: Overview of computer technology and terminology; use of computers as managerial and administrative tools; the management of computer resources and the influence of information technology within the organization.

name: Logistics and Operations Management
description: The design and management of systems to make products, provide services and deliver them to the end user. Prerequisite: All of BUSI 290, BUSI 291. or equivalents.

name: Commercial Property Analysis
description: Underlying theory and techniques used in the design and construction of commercial properties.

name: Real Estate Management I
description: Examines the day-to-day issues which affect the practice of property management. Prerequisite: BUSI 330. BUSI 331 recommended.

name: Introduction to Business Law
description: Introduction to the law of contracts, with particular reference to contracts for sale of goods and related law of personal property, principles of agency, partnership, and company law.

name: Modern Literatures of South Asia in Translation
description: Fiction, drama, and/or poetry of modern India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, and/or Sri Lanka, including works in translation and/or originally written in English.

name: Residential Property Analysis
description: Underlying theory and techniques used in design, construction, and inspection of residential properties.

name: Real Estate Business
description: General business skills for real estate practitioners.

name: Foundations of Chinese Thought
description: Early (pre 221 BCE) Chinese thought (Confucianism, Daoism, Mohism, Legalism), its contemporary implications, and the role of philosophy and religion in human flourishing./Credit will only be granted for one of PHIL 371 or ASIA 371. Equivalency: PHIL371

name: Computer Aided Mass Property Assessment
description: This course develops and applies the major techniques for valuing real property. Recommended pre-requisites: all of BUSI 121, BUSI 330, BUSI 443.

name: The Sanskrit Cosmopolis: India and the World, 200-1500 CE
description: Languages, religions, art forms, and political structures of Asian societies shaped by creative encounters with Sanskrit.

name: History of Hong Kong
description: History, culture, and identities of Hong Kong from the early 1800s to the present. Credit will be granted for only one of ASIA_V 373 or HIST_V 373. Equivalency: HIST_V 373.

name: Global Chinese Cinemas
description: A survey of Chinese cinemas in global perspective, covering films, filmmakers, producers, audiences, markets, industries, and critical discourse since the early twentieth century. Covers both cinematic culture and filmmaking technique.

name: Imagining Punjab
description: The cultural and linguistic region of Punjab as it has been imagined in different times and places, in South Asia and beyond, in literature, scholarship, film, and popular culture.

name: Case Studies in Appraisal I
description: Examines the day-to day issues that affect the practice of real estate appraisal. Prerequisite: All of BUSI 121, BUSI 330, BUSI 331.

name: Assessment Administration
description: Introduces the practice of real property assessment, including the nature of the techniques used, the required duties of assessors, and how an assessment office is administrated. Recommended pre-requisite: BUSI 330

name: Data Visualization and Business Analytics
description: Builds critical thinking and data skills by identifying statistical pitfalls, cleaning data with Power Query, creating financial models, and crafting impactful visualizations using Power BI and Excel to support decision-making through practical applications. Prerequisite: All of BUSI_V 291, BUSI_V 335.

name: History of Korean Thought
description: An examination of Korean religious, philosophical, and scientific thought from the earliest written records to the present day, with particular focus on the interaction of Shamanism, Buddhism, Confucianism, and, in the present century, Christianity.

name: The Persian Book of Kings
description: The Persian Shahnameh (the Book of Kings) and its context in Iranian myth and history. Analysis of the poem through lenses of gender and sexuality, race/ethnicity, and religion.

name: Asian Folklore
description: A survey of oral and expressive traditions in Asia, including jokes, superstitions, fairy tales, myths, music, and foodways; practical training in collecting and archiving folklore.

name: Development of Traditional Chinese Thought
description: Chinese thought from the Han dynasty (206 BCE to 220 CE) to Wang Yangming (1472-1529) in its historical and cultural contexts.

name: Roman Art and Architecture
description: Visual culture of the ancient Roman world from the 8th century BCE to the 4th century CE. Credit will only be granted for one of ARTH 332, CLST 332, or AMNE 377. Equivalency: AMNE 377

name: Buddhism in China
description: History, thought, and practices of Chinese Buddhism from its beginnings until the twentieth century.

name: 20th Century Art and Culture: The Postmodern
description: A critical examination of international visual art and culture from the 1950s to the present; the role of art in consumerist society and the emergence of postmodernism.

name: The Sikhs: Formations, Contexts, and Historical Development
description: Introduction to the historical development of Sikh traditions in India and Diaspora, from the 15th century to the present, with attention to broader historical contexts.

name: Visual Culture in the Age of Enlightenment and Revolution (1715-1830)
description: Art, architecture, and social space in Europe and America: redefining gender, identity and nation in the era of industrialization and political change.

name: 19th-Century Art and Social Space
description: Ideologies of gender, class, race, ethnicity, and economics in 19th-century European and American visual culture.

name: Inventing Canada Through Art
description: The institutions and art movements that constructed a view to the country now known as Canada, from colonial contact, to Confederation, through the mid-1900s. Emphasis on the significance of locality and situated approaches to understanding the land.

name: Archaeological Foundations of East and Southeast Asia
description: Survey of the archaeology of East and Southeast Asia, with an emphasis on the beginnings of the economic, social, political, and artistic traditions and systems of the great civilizations, and the conditions in which they arose.
