Assessment in Mathematics Education
description: Recommended pre-requisites: one of EDCP 340, EDCP 342.

name: Founding Principles in Chemical and Biological Engineering II
description: Introduction to Chemical and Biological Engineering profession with emphasis on the biological sciences that form the founding principles of the discipline. Prerequisite: CHBE 220.

name: Chemistry for Teaching: Topics and Pedagogical Approaches - Secondary
description: Teacher Education Office approval is required. Open only to secondary students admitted with an academic deficiency. Not for credit toward graduate degree or for undergraduate credit in an academic subject.

name: Special Study in Social Studies: Geography
Teaching Earth and Space Science Beyond the Textbook
Conceptions of the Natural World: Implications for Science Education
Biology for Teaching: Topics and Pedagogical Approaches - Secondary
description: Teacher Education Office approval is required. Open only to secondary students admitted with an academic deficiency. Not for credit towards a graduate degree or for undergraduate credit in an academic subject.

name: Material and Energy Balances
description: Introduction to Chemical and Biological Engineering; units; stoichiometry; phase equilibria; material balances; energy balances. Prerequisite: All of CHEM 154, MATH 152.

name: Teaching Life Science Beyond the Textbook
Introduction to Unit Operations
description: Foundational concepts and design equations for basic unit operations such as: comminution, screening, filtration, centrifugal separations, evaporation and crystallization. Prerequisite: Either (a) all of CHBE 241, CHBE 244 or (b) CIVL 215 or (c) third-year or higher standing in BASc. Not for credit for CHBE students.

name: Chemical and Biological Engineering Laboratory
description: Laboratory experiment in 2nd year Chemical and Biological Engineering Prerequisite: CHBE 263. Corequisite: All of CHBE 244, CHBE 251.

name: Forest Education
description: Transportation and living costs for required field experiences will be borne by the student.

name: Teaching Physical Science Beyond the Textbook
Introduction to Chemical and Biological Engineering Process and Technology
description: Processes used in chemical and biological industries, which emphasize underlying physical, chemical, and biological principles.

name: Unit Operations
description: Stage-wise mass transfer operations; extraction and absorption; single and stage-wise binary and multi-component distillation; principles and equipment design for continuous contact mass transfer operations including absorption, binary distillation and others such as extraction, drying, and humidification. Prerequisite: All of CHBE 346, CHBE 352.

name: Transport Phenomena I
description: Fluid Mechanics. Momentum-transfer in fluids in laminar and turbulent flow; microscopic and macroscopic material; momentum and energy balances; rheology; dimensional analysis; flow in conduits; pumps; fluid metering. Prerequisite: [PHYS170] Corequisite: One of MATH 255, MATH 256.

name: Introduction to Chemical and Biological Engineering Laboratory Practice
description: Introduction to Chemical and Biological Engineering laboratory practice with topics in physical, inorganic and organic chemistry. Corequisite: All of CHBE 220, CHBE 241, CHEM 250, CHEM 260.

name: Computational Methods
description: Mathematical formulation of chemical and biological engineering problems; standard techniques of numerical analysis and their application to chemical, environmental and biotechnological systems; program development; use of commercial numerical analysis software. Prerequisite: APSC 160. Corequisite: MATH 256.

name: Mass Transfer Bridge Module
description: Mass transfer; molecular diffusion; convective transfer; analogies among heat, mass and momentum transfer; mass transfer coefficients; interphase mass transfer. Prerequisite: All of CHBE 251, CHBE 351, MATH 253.

name: Physics - Secondary: Curriculum and Pedagogy
description: Pass/Fail. Prerequisite: A completed concentration in physics or permission of the Head.

name: Kinetics and Reactor Design
description: Kinetics of homogeneous chemical and biological reactions, isothermal ideal reactor design, analysis of non-ideal reactors using residence time distribution and mixing models. Prerequisite: All of CHBE 230, CHBE 346, CHBE 352.

name: Earth and Space Science - Secondary: Curriculum and Pedagogy
description: Pass/Fail. Prerequisite: A completed concentration in earth and space science or permission of the Head.

name: General Science - Secondary: Curriculum and Pedagogy
description: Pass/Fail. Prerequisite: A completed concentration in agricultural sciences, biological sciences, chemistry, earth and space science, or physics, or permission of the Head.

name: Chemical and Biological Engineering Thermodynamics I
description: Energy and the first law; second law of thermodynamics; entropy; availability (energy) analysis; thermodynamic properties of fluids, application to power generation, refrigeration, and liquefaction, as well as biological, environmental, and electrochemical systems. Prerequisite: CHBE 241.

name: Chemical Engineering and Applied Chemistry Laboratory
description: Experiments chosen to illustrate and use material presented in 200-level CHBE and CHEM courses. Corequisite: All of CHBE 201, CHBE 241, CHBE 251, CHEM 250, CHEM 251, CHEM 260.

name: Chemical and Biological Engineering Thermodynamics II
description: Volumetric and thermodynamic properties of fluids; equations of state; heat effects; ideal and non-ideal mixtures; fugacities and activity coefficients; vapor-liquid and liquid-liquid phase equilibrium; solubility of gases and solids in liquids; chemical reaction equilibrium; equilibrium partitioning of pollutants. Recommended prerequisite: MATH 256. Prerequisite: All of CHBE 220, CHBE 241, CHBE 244, MATH 253.

name: Transport Phenomena II
description: Heat and mass transfer; conduction and molecular diffusion; convective transfer; analogies among heat, mass and momentum transfer; heat exchanger design; mass transfer coefficients; interphase mass transfer. Prerequisite: One of CHBE 251, CIVL 215, MECH 280 and MATH 256. or third-year standing in ENVE.

name: Elementary and Middle Years: Curriculum and Pedagogy
description: Pass/Fail.

name: Chemistry - Secondary: Curriculum and Pedagogy
description: Pass/Fail. Prerequisite: A completed concentration in chemistry or permission of the Head.

name: Agricultural Sciences - Secondary: Curriculum and Pedagogy
description: Pass/Fail. Prerequisite: A completed concentration in Agricultural Sciences or permission of the Head.

name: Integrating Business Applications across the Curriculum: Elementary and Middle Years
description: Pass/Fail.

name: Logistics Services Management
description: Overview of the characteristics and commercial environment of logistics and transportation services; service operations planning and design, costing, pricing and quality management.

name: Design and Technology I - Secondary: Curriculum and Pedagogy
description: Pass/Fail.

name: Financial Accounting: Intermediate I
description: An examination of accounting as a means of measurement and as an information system for external reporting purposes.

name: Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics (STEM) Education I: Curriculum and Pedagogy
Curriculum Design and Evaluation: Practical and Theoretical Issues
Consumer Behaviour
description: The use of consumer research and theory in marketing and policy decisions. Psychological, sociological and economic theory and research relevant to consumer behaviour are considered.

name: Income Taxation
description: A study of income tax from the standpoint of the individual and of business enterprise.

name: Cost Accounting
description: The provision and analysis of cost accounting information that will assist management in making operating decisions and in evaluating operational performance. The utilization of statistical analysis and linear models is included.

name: Corporate Finance
description: Examination of corporate enterprise decisions including capital budgeting; capital structure choice, and financial policies, tools, and valuation. Credit will be granted for only one of COMM_V 370 or COEC_V 370. Equivalency: COEC_V 370

name: Biological Sciences - Secondary: Curriculum and Pedagogy
description: Pass/Fail. Prerequisite: A completed concentration in biological sciences or permission of the Head.

name: Integrating Design and Technology Across the Curriculum: Elementary and Middle Years
description: Pass/Fail.

name: Information and Communication Technologies I - Secondary: Curriculum and Pedagogy
description: Pass/Fail.

name: Integrating ICT Across the Curriculum: Elementary and Middle Years
Behavioural Finance
description: The psychological processes that give rise to decision-making biases in investment settings and counter-strategies to minimize their negative effects on financial decisions.

name: Marketing Analysis
description: Analytical methods applicable to marketing management decision making; attention to strategic considerations linking analysis of consumer data, corporate data, environmental factors, and competitive response. The course makes extensive use of strategy simulations.

name: Investment Theory
description: Basic concepts of finance, including security valuation, security markets, and financial decisions concerning risk and return. Credit will be granted for only one of COMM_V 371 or COEC_V 371. Equivalency: COEC_V 371

name: Market Research
description: The process of marketing research including topics such as problem/opportunity formulation, research objectives, data sources, research instrument design, sampling, data collection and processing and methods of data analysis.

name: Applied Financial Markets
description: Introduction to methodologies and evidence concerning the structure and operation of security markets and the valuation of financial securities including stocks, bonds, options and futures contracts; portfolio management, corporate finance and investment decisions.

name: Advanced Organic Chemistry for the Life Sciences
description: Chemistry of organic substances having particular relevance to the life sciences.  Prerequisite: CHEM 213.

name: Biophysical Chemistry
description: Diffusion and transport phenomena; interaction of radiation and matter. Methods for determining molecular weight, size, and shape of molecules in solution.  Prerequisite: One of MATH 200, MATH 217, MATH 226, MATH 253 and either (a) a score of 76% or higher in CHEM 205 or (b) CHEM 304 or (c) PHYS 203.

name: Introduction to Quantum Mechanics and Spectroscopy
description: Principles of quantum mechanics; atomic wavefunctions; angular momentum; spin; atomic term symbols.  Prerequisite: One of CHEM 123, SCIE 001 and one of MATH 200, MATH 217, MATH 226, MATH 253.

name: Introduction to Pensions and Insurance
description: Financial dimensions and institutional structure of the pension and insurance industry; calculation of annuities and other aspects of actuarial science based on probability distributions and asset returns. Suitable for students in mathematics who have taken basic finance and for commerce students in finance, accounting and related areas.

name: Fundamentals of Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics
description: Principles of chemical thermodynamics; introduction to statistical mechanics; phase equilibria; electrochemistry.  Prerequisite: One of CHEM 123, CHEM 130 and one of MATH 200, MATH 217, MATH 226, MATH 253.

name: Research Ethics and Data Analysis Skills
description: Research ethics; data analysis skills for chemical research. Restricted to Honours students with third year standing and, with permission of the department Head, to Major students with satisfactory third year standing.

name: Financial Institutions I
description: The roles and operation of financial institutions, including banks, and the financial systems and markets in which they function, including those involving payments processes and the creation and use of fiat and digital money including cryptocurrencies.

name: International Financial Markets and Institutions
description: Structure, nature and institutions of foreign exchange markets, including spot, forward, futures, options, and offshore currency markets. Factors affecting exchange rates are also discussed. Credit will be granted for only one of ECON_V 456, COMM_V 377, or COEC_V 377. Equivalency: COEC_V 377

name: Co-operative Work Placement I
description: Approved and supervised work experience for a minimum of 3.5 months. Normally taken during the winter term of the third year. Technical report required. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-operative Education Program in Commerce. Option-specific prerequisites apply.

name: Advanced Organic Chemistry
description: Application of carbonyl group chemistry, cyclization reactions, conformational analysis and rearrangement reactions in organic synthesis.  Prerequisite: CHEM 213.

name: Chemistry Integrated Laboratory II
description: Further development of principles and techniques of modern chemistry applied by integrating experiments chosen from organic, inorganic, physical, and analytical chemistry.  Prerequisite: CHEM 315.

name: Instrumental Analytical Chemistry
description: Theory, design, and application of instrumental methods of chemical analysis including spectroscopy, mass spectrometry, electroanalysis, and chemical separations.  Prerequisite: One of CHEM 210, CHEM 211.

name: Introduction to Trans* Studies
description: How race, citizenship, gender, sexuality, culture and dis/ability are materially and socially constructed together to give meaning to the category trans*. (Trans*: transgender, transsexual, gender variant and other articulations.) Recommended pre-requisite: GRSJ 101.

name: Practical Skills for Chemical Research
description: The nature of scientific research; practical skills for chemical research; communicating science. Restricted to Honours students with third year standing and, with permission of the department Head, to Major students with satisfactory third year standing.

name: Chemistry Integrated Laboratory I
description: Principles and techniques of modern chemistry applied by integrating experiments chosen from organic, inorganic, physical, and analytical chemistry.  Prerequisite: One of CHEM 211, CHEM 215 and all of CHEM 213, CHEM 245.

name: Integrated Chemistry Laboratory II
description: Further development of principles and techniques of modern chemistry applied by integrating experiments chosen from organic, inorganic, physical, and analytical chemistry.  Open only to students in Chemistry Major or Honours specializations.  Prerequisite: CHEM 325.

name: Introduction to Materials Chemistry
description: Basic principles of materials chemistry: classification; nomenclature; synthetic methods; characterization.  Prerequisite: One of CHEM 208, CHEM 250 and one of CHEM 203, CHEM 223, CHEM 233, CHEM 260.

name: Introduction to Critical Studies in Sexuality
description: A multi-disciplinary course which provides an introduction to the study of sexuality, including lesbian, gay, bisexual, heterosexual, and transgender issues and related topics.

name: Principles of Catalysis
description: Fundamental aspects of chemical catalysis: kinetic models; catalytic processes in biochemistry and industry; emerging topics in catalysis.  Prerequisite: One of CHEM 218, CHEM 250.

name: Topics in Critical Studies in Sexuality
description: A thematic course, which explores current questions and issues in relation to the study of sexuality. Topics may vary from year to year.

name: Directed Topics
description: Designed to allow a student to develop an individual course of study in a specific area as approved by a faculty member affiliated with the CSIS program.

name: Integrated Chemistry Laboratory I
description: Principles and techniques of modern chemistry applied by integrating experiments chosen from organic, inorganic, physical, and analytical chemistry. Open only to students in Chemistry specializations.  Prerequisite: One of CHEM 211, CHEM 215 and all of CHEM 208, CHEM 213, CHEM 245.

name: Global Challenges: A Chemical Perspective
description: Importance of chemistry in society. Detailed case studies drawn from modern chemistry: human health, energy, commodity chemicals, materials, green chemistry, agriculture.  Prerequisite: one of CHEM 203, CHEM 211, CHEM 223, CHEM 233, CHEM 260.

name: Ceramic Design and Pedagogical Approaches: Art Education
description: Prerequisite: 6 credits of introductory art studio or art history courses.
prerequisites: 6 credits of introductory art studio or art history courses

Digital Media in Arts Education: Introduction
Critical Studies in Sexuality: Multi-disciplinary Approaches

name: Intermediate Business Statistics
description: Statistical techniques useful in business environments. Includes regression analysis, analysis of variance, forecasting, and logit and probit analysis. Credit may be obtained for only one of STAT_V 300, STAT_V 306, and COMM_V 411. Prerequisite: One of COMM_V 191, COMM_V 291. Equivalency: STAT_V 300

name: Marketing
description: Basic considerations affecting the domestic and international marketing of goods and services. Analytical frameworks and techniques that are used to guide marketing strategy decisions. For Master of Management - Dual Degree Option students only.

name: Art - Elementary: Curriculum and Pedagogy
description: Pass/Fail.

name: Textile Design and Pedagogical Approaches: Art Education
description: Prerequisite: 6 credits of introductory art studio or art history courses.
prerequisites: 6 credits of introductory art studio or art history courses

name: Data Visualization and Business Analytics
description: Descriptive analytics including data analysis and visualization. Predictive analytics including forecasting and various statistical techniques. Predictive analytics including optimization, Monte Carlo simulation, decision trees, and discrete event simulation. Prerequisite: COMM_V 204.

name: Introductory Finance
description: Introduces the basic principles of financial valuation, including the time-value of money and the risk/return tradeoff. Develops tools for the quantitative analysis of corporate and/or individual financing and saving decisions, and of capital budgeting decisions. For Master of Management - Dual Degree Option students only.

name: Research Methods for Human Resource Management
description: Techniques for collection and analysis of data in organizations to support adoption and administration of human resource management. Prerequisite: COMM_V 327 and one of COMM_V 191, COMM_V 291 and one of COMM_V 192, COMM_V 292.

name: Introduction to Music Education
description: Role of music education in schools and society, including historical, philosophical, psychological, and sociological perspectives. Includes guided class observations and practice music teaching in elementary and secondary schools. Criminal Record Check required.

name: Operations and Climate
description: Quantitative and qualitative evaluation of public policies and corporate strategies using statistical evaluation methods, cost benefit analysis, and other modelling tools, with a focus on the impacts of climate change on operations and vice versa. Industries including service provision, manufacturing, and infrastructure investment are assessed based on pricing, operating costs, emissions, and other environmental and societal impacts. Prerequisite: COMM_V 204.

name: Co-operative Work Placement II
description: Approved and supervised work experience for a minimum of 3.5 months. Normally taken during the summer term of the third year. Technical report required. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-operative Education Program in Commerce. Prerequisite: COMM_V 380

name: Information Systems Analysis and Design
description: The process of information systems development; modern techniques and tools for systems analysis and design. Prerequisite: One of COMM_V 335, CPSC_V 310.

name: CIO Strategies
description: Common issues faced by Chief Information Officers (CIO): Cost and value of information technology (IT), IT priorities, IT and the Board of Directors, Business-IT alignment, IT governance, IT talent management, standardization vs. innovation, project and vendor management/partnering, and managing security and risks. Prerequisite: COMM_V 205.

name: Negotiation
description: Negotiation simulations to provide experience and confidence in the negotiation process and to develop effective skills for achieving objectives.

name: Land Law
description: Legal principles and concepts relating to real estate and land development. Prerequisite: COMM_V 393

name: Economics of Entrepreneurship and Innovation
description: Fundamental economic issues faced by entrepreneurs who want to commercialize innovations within start-ups and established firms. Credit will be granted for only one of COMM_V 382 and COMR_V 382. Equivalency: COMR_V 382

name: Law of Business Organizations and Corporate Governance
description: Statutory provisions and case law that regulate the creation and governance of sole proprietorships, partnerships, corporations, joint ventures, and franchises in British Columbia. Fiduciary duties of partners, directors and officers are also examined. Prerequisite: COMM_V 393

name: Creativity in Business
description: The role and importance of creativity in developing successful business solutions. Credit will be granted for only one of COMM_V 389 and COMR_V 389. Equivalency: COMR_V 389

name: Database Technology
description: Theory and technology of database management from an applications perspective; database design; database administration. Credit will be granted for only one of COMM_V 437, COEC_V 437, CSPC_V 304 or CPSC_V 368. Prerequisite: COMM_V 335.

name: Innovation Leadership
description: Social science frameworks useful for understanding organizational innovation processes and application of these frameworks to innovation. Diagnosing and solving a broad range of organizational innovation challenges from the perspective of an innovation leader.

name: Management of Information Systems
description: Managerial issues in the administration of computerized information systems. Prerequisite: COMM_V 205.

name: Business Data Communications
description: Basic data communications concepts and technology; local area, wide area, and enterprise networks; the Internet; wireless networking; network development life cycle; network security and management. Credit will be granted for only one of COMM_V 439 or CPSC_V 317, and COMM_V 439 or CPSC_V 417. Prerequisite: COMM_V 335

name: Topics in Business III
description: Equivalency: COMR_V 386

name: Selected Topics in Human Resource Management
description: Prerequisite: COMM_V 327, COMM_V 425

name: Entrepreneurial Finance and Private Equity
description: Financial issues encountered by entrepreneurs and those active on the investing side of entrepreneurship, such as working for banks, venture capital firms, or corporate venture organizations, or anyone interacting with entrepreneurs and private equity investors. Credit will be granted for only one of COMM_V 387, COEC_V 387, or COMR_V 387. Equivalency: COEC_V 387, COMR_V 387

name: Business Communications
description: Understanding non-written communications in day-to-day business.

name: Intermediate Creative Nonfiction Workshop
description: An intermediate level workshop class in writing of creative nonfiction. Manuscript submission is not required for admission. Prerequisite: CRWR 305.

name: Real Estate Economics
description: The economics of real estate markets. Topics include real estate cycles and bubbles, search models and vacancy, the relationship between real estate and the economy, housing demand, and models of housing supply. Prerequisite: One of COMM_V 295, ECON_V 201, ECON_V 301.

name: Design Methods for Business Innovation
description: Studio-based experience in thinking strategies and design processes applied to business innovation in the private, public, and social sectors. Emphasis on problem solving, co-creation, and innovation for external clients in a collaborative environment. Credit will be granted for only one of COMM_V 388 and COMR_V 388. Equivalency: COMR_V 388

name: Capstone Experience
description: Prepares students to transition to career and life after BCom. Integrates and leverages BCom learning towards meeting future challenges personally, at work and in society. Pass/Fail. Corequisite: COMM_V 491.

name: Business Communications II
description: An activity-focused course providing the opportunity to study and practice forms of written communication needed in business. Credit will be granted for only one COMM_V 396, COMM_V 390, COMM_V 220, or ENGL_V 301. Prerequisite: COMM_V 196. Equivalency: COMM_V 390

name: Intermediate Graphic Forms Workshop
description: An intermediate level workshop class in writing for graphic forms. The ability to draw is not required. Manuscript submission is not required for admission. Prerequisite: CRWR 308.

name: Commercial Law
description: Introduction to the law of contracts, with particular reference to contracts for sale of goods and related law of personal property; principles of agency, partnerships and company law.

name: Writing Poetry I
description: A workshop class in the writing of poetry. Prerequisite: Restricted to Majors in Creative Writing.

name: Environment, Society, and Government
description: Roles of government and business in the Canadian economy, emphasizing interactions with the environment and society, including Indigenous communities. Ethical foundations of government, business and personal decision-making. Credit will be granted for only one of COEC_V 394 or COMM_V 394. Prerequisite: One of COMM_V 295, ECON_V 201, ECON_V 301. Equivalency: COEC_V 394

name: Real Estate Finance
description: The role of mortgage markets, mathematical analysis of return and valuation issue and methods of dealing with lender and borrower risk exposure. Prerequisite: One of COMM_V 297, COMM_V 298.

name: Intermediate Children and Young Adult Writing Workshop
description: An intermediate level workshop class in writing for children and young adults. Manuscript submission is not required for admission. Prerequisite: CRWR 303.

name: Writing for New Media I
description: An advanced workshop class in writing for new media. Restricted to Majors in Creative Writing.

name: Intermediate Screenplay Workshop
description: An intermediate level workshop class in writing for the screen. Manuscript submission is not required for admission. Prerequisite: CRWR 306.

name: Real Estate Development
description: The development process from theories of development, market analysis, site selection, project design, land use regulation and financial analysis. Prerequisite: One of COMM_V 307, COMM_V 405.

name: Writing for Graphic Forms I
description: A workshop class in the writing of graphic novel, manga, and other forms of illustrated writing. The ability to draw is not required. Prerequisite: Restricted to Majors in Creative Writing.

name: Intermediate Fiction Workshop
description: An intermediate level workshop class in writing of fiction. Manuscript submission is not required for admission. Prerequisite: CRWR 309.

name: Video Game Writing
description: A workshop class on writing for video games. Restricted to Creative Writing majors.

name: Writing of Drama for the Stage I
description: A workshop class in writing of drama for the stage. Studio work is required, and some plays may be given a live stage production in Brave New Play Rites (adjudication process involved). Prerequisite: Restricted to Majors in Creative Writing.

name: Writing for the Screen I
description: A workshop class in writing for the screen. Prerequisite: Restricted to Majors in Creative Writing.

name: Writing Creative Nonfiction I
description: A workshop class in writing creative nonfiction, focused on some of the more popular forms of creative nonfiction: autobiography, rhetoric (commentary), literary journalism, and the personal essay. Prerequisite: Restricted to Majors in Creative Writing.

name: New Venture Design
description: Teams comprising students in COMM_V 466 and APSC_V 486 propose a new product, produce a viable prototype, and develop a business plan for the marketplace. Credit will be granted for only one of COMM_V 466, COMM_V 497, COEC_V 497, COMR_V 497, APSC_V 486, or APSC_V 496E.

name: Venture Capital
description: Theory and evidence concerning venture capital markets. Contracting, fundraising, and financing choice covered in depth, with the aim of catering to students looking to raise money for entrepreneurial ventures or to invest in entrepreneurial ventures. Prerequisite: One of COMM_V 370, COMM_V 387.

name: Writing for Radio I
description: A workshop class in writing for the radio. Prerequisite: Restricted to Majors in Creative Writing.

name: Digital Marketing
description: Investigation of Internet-based marketing, emphasizing customer-focused perspectives, competitive situations and analysis of the effectiveness of business websites using marketing principles and practices. Prerequisite: COMM_V 296.

name: Public Relations
description: Managing an organization's strategic communications and relationships with diverse publics to handle issues, strengthen reputation, fulfill social responsibilities, and build trust. Topics include stakeholder engagement, issues management, crisis communications, and events and sponsorship.

name: Risk Management and Financial Engineering
description: Principles of financial engineering and risk management. Use of derivatives in risk management. Valuation and hedging models for contingent claims. Prerequisite: COMM_V 374.

name: Writing for Children and Young Adults I
description: A workshop class in writing for Children and Young Adults. Prerequisite: Restricted to Majors in Creative Writing.

name: Writing Fiction I
description: A workshop class in the writing of fiction. Prerequisite: Restricted to Majors in Creative Writing.

name: Integrated Marketing Communication
description: Marketing communication campaign strategy, conceptual framework, and practical application for integrated marketing communications, including advertising. Prerequisite: COMM_V 362

name: Investment Policy
description: The management of security portfolios for individual and institutional investors; relation of investment policy to money markets and business fluctuations. Prerequisite: COMM_V 371.

name: Advanced Topics in Investment Management
description: Applications of contemporary research, innovations, and technologies in the allocation of capital across asset classes, portfolios of assets, and individual securities. Empirical analyses of current market data using software and quantitative tools to implement potential investment and trading strategies. Prerequisite: All of COMM_V 370, COMM_V 371.

name: Mergers and Acquisitions
description: Mergers and acquisitions as a focal point in making important corporate decisions deduced from careful study of relevant business cases. Prerequisite: COMM_V 370.

name: International Marketing
description: An analysis of the scope and significance of contemporary international business operations with particular reference to the marketing management problems encountered by firms with multinational branches and subsidiaries. Prerequisite: COMM_V 296.

name: Marketing Applications
description: A capstone marketing course where student teams develop comprehensive marketing plans for corporate clients by conducting industry analyses and crafting creative marketing strategies. Prerequisite: All of COMM_V 362, COMM_V 363, COMM_V 365.

name: Brand Management
description: Issues and challenges commonly faced by brand managers, including: assessing brand meaning, evaluating brand health, assessing a brand's leverage potential, evaluating brand extensions, managing brands through a crisis, and assessing brand value. Prerequisite: COMM_V 296.

name: Organic Chemistry
description: Spectroscopy of organic compounds. Mechanistic analysis of chemical reactivity of common functional groups with a focus on carbon-carbon bond formation; functional group interconversion. Preference will be given to students in Chemistry or Biochemistry specializations. Prerequisite: Either (a) one of CHEM 203, CHEM 223 or (b) a score of 76% or higher in CHEM 233.

name: Introductory Synthetic Chemical Laboratory
description: An introduction to the principles and techniques in the synthetic organic and inorganic chemistry laboratory. Prerequisite: One of CHEM 123, CHEM 135.

name: Fundamentals of Reactivity in Inorganic Chemistry
description: Chemical reactivity of inorganic systems: oxidation/reduction chemistry; multiply-bonded systems; main group chemistry. Prerequisite: CHEM 208.

name: Fixed Income Markets and Management
description: Fixed income instruments and derivatives. Risk profiles and their use in establishing fixed income investment portfolios. Performance attribution techniques. Corequisite: COMM_V 374.

name: Advanced Topics on Corporate Finance
description: Corporate Finance is the process by which corporations raise money, allocate funds to real assets, and manage the flow of funds back to the investors. Topics will vary according to interests of students, instructors, and developments in the field. Corequisite: All of COMM_V 370, COMM_V 371.

name: Introduction to Chemical Analysis
description: Quantitative chemical analysis; chemical and physical principles of spectrophotometry, potentiometry, and chromatography. Prerequisite: Either (a) CHEM 123 or (b) all of CHEM 130, CHEM 135 or (c) SCIE 001.

name: Intermediate Synthetic Chemistry Laboratory
description: Techniques in synthetic organic and inorganic chemistry. Open only to students in Chemistry or Biochemistry specializations. Prerequisite: Either (a) CHEM 203 or (b) all of CHEM 223, CHEM 225 or (c) all of CHEM 233, CHEM 235. Corequisite: CHEM 213.

name: Organic Chemistry for the Biological Sciences
description: Reactions and properties of carbonyl compounds, carbohydrates, amino acids, nucleic acids. Credit will be granted for only one of CHEM 233 or CHEM 203 or CHEM 223. Prerequisite: One of CHEM 123, CHEM 130, SCIE 001.

name: Introduction to Organic Chemistry (Lecture)
description: Structure, bonding and physical properties of aliphatic and aromatic compounds; mechanistic analysis of chemical reactivity of common functional groups with a focus on carbon-heteroatom bond formation; functional group interconversion and oxidation/reduction reactions. Only open to students in Chemistry or Biochemistry specializations. Students should consult the Credit Exclusion List for credit exclusions relating to second-year organic chemistry courses. Prerequisite: One of CHEM 123, CHEM 130, SCIE 001.

name: Physical Chemistry for Engineers
description: States of matter, properties of gases, phase diagrams. Elementary chemical thermodynamics and kinetics. Reaction equilibria. Prerequisite: One of CHEM 123, CHEM 130, CHEM 154, SCIE 001.

name: Introductory Analytical Chemical Laboratory
description: An introduction to the principles and techniques in the analytical chemistry laboratory. Prerequisite: CHEM 210 and one of CHEM 123, CHEM 135.

name: Co-operative Work Placement III
description: Approved and supervised work experience for a minimum of 35 months. Normally taken during the summer term of the fourth year. Technical report required. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-operative. Education Program in Commerce. Prerequisite: COMM_V 381

name: Atmospheric Environmental Chemistry
description: Introduction to structure, composition and chemical processes occurring in Earth's atmosphere, including interactions with solar radiation, stratospheric ozone layer, photochemical smog and acid rain. Prerequisite: One of CHEM 123, CHEM 130, CHBE 220. and Third year standing.

name: Aqueous Environmental Chemistry
description: Properties and composition of natural waters, including gas and solid equilibria, pH and acidification, redox chemistry, complexation, corrosion, ion exchange, colloids and microbial transformations. Prerequisite: One of CHEM 123, CHEM 130, CHBE 220. and Third year standing.

name: Inorganic Chemistry for Engineers
description: Chemistry of selected groups of inorganic compounds, considered in relation to industrial processes. Prerequisite: One of CHEM 123, CHEM 130, CHEM 154, SCIE 001.

name: Organic Chemistry for Engineers
description: A description of the properties and reactions of organic compounds. Prerequisite: One of CHEM 123, CHEM 130, CHEM 154, SCIE 001.

name: Communicating Chemistry
description: Effective argumentation and communication skills in chemistry. Only open to students in a Chemistry specialization. Prerequisite: Third year standing

name: Organic Chemistry Laboratory
description: Techniques of organic chemistry. To be taken in conjunction with, or in the term following, CHEM 233. Credit will be granted for only one of CHEM 235 or CHEM 203. Prerequisite: One of CHEM 123, CHEM 135, SCIE 001. Corequisite: [CHEM233]

name: Co-operative Work Placement IV
description: Approved and supervised work experience for a minimum of 35 months. Normally taken during the fall term of the fourth year. Technical report required. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-operative Education Program in Commerce. Prerequisite: COMM_V 480

name: Social Entrepreneurship

Credit will be granted for only one of COMM_V 485 or COMR_V 485. Equivalency: COMR_V 485

name: Leadership and General Management

name: New Product Development

name: Applied Methods in Technology Start-ups at CDL
description: Students work with the Creative Destruction Lab team to help start-ups that are focused on science and emerging technology. Students support real companies with market analysis, customer development, financial analysis, and will see how investors make decisions.

name: Management Simulation
description: Student teams manage hypothetical firms in a complex simulation, coordinating production, finance, marketing and strategic planning in competition with other teams. Prerequisite: Fourth-year standing. Either (a) COMM_V 390, COMM_V 395 or (b) COMM_V 396.

name: Directed Studies in Commerce
description: An investigation and report on a topic to be agreed upon by a member of the faculty and a senior student.

name: Sustainability Marketing
description: Role of marketing in creating social value. Integration of marketing fundamentals with core social, environmental, and economic principles of sustainability. Analysis of current sustainability trends. Development of strategic and practical marketing recommendations for for-profit enterprises. Potential and pitfalls of sustainability marketing.

Credit will be granted for only one of COMM_V 498 or COEC_V 498. Prerequisite: Either (a) all of COMM_V 390, COMM_V 395 or (b) COMM_V 396.

description: Computation as a tool for systematic problem solving in non-computer-science disciplines. Introductory programming skills. Not for credit for students who have credit for, or exemption from, or are concurrently taking CPSC 110 or APSC 160. No programming experience expected.

name: Models of Computation
description: Physical and mathematical structures of computation. Boolean algebra and combinations logic circuits; proof techniques; functions and sequential circuits; sets and relations; finite state machines; sequential instruction execution. Prerequisite: Principles of Mathematics 12 or Pre-calculus 12. Corequisite: One of CPSC 107, CPSC 110.

name: Computational Thinking
description: Meaning and impact of computational thinking. Solving problems using computational thinking, testing, debugging. How computers work. No prior computing experience required. Not for students with existing credit for or exemption from CPSC 107, CPSC 110 or APSC 160.

name: Special Projects in Writing Drama for the Stage
description: For students who receive departmental permission to do advanced work in this genre.

name: Systematic Program Design

name: Cybersecurity Research Seminar
description: Prerequisite: by permission of the instructor.

name: Basic Algorithms and Data Structures
description: Design and analysis of basic algorithms and data structures; algorithm analysis methods, searching and sorting algorithms, basic data structures, graphs and concurrency. Prerequisite: One of CPSC 210, CPEN 221 and either (a) one of CPSC 121, MATH 220 or (b) a score of 68% or higher in MATH 226.

name: Computation, Programs, and Programming
description: Fundamental program and computation structures. Introductory programming skills. Computation as a tool for information processing, simulation and modelling, and interacting with the world.

name: Entrepreneurial Finance
description: Financial issues encountered by those active on the investing side of entrepreneurship, such as working for banks, venture capital firms, or corporate venture organizations, or anyone interacting with entrepreneurs and private equity investors. name: Cybersecurity

description: Software architecture, operating systems, and I/O architectures. Prerequisite: All of CPSC 121, CPSC 210.

name: Error Resilient Computing Systems
description: Credit will only be given for one of CPEN 533 or EECE 513.

description: Analysis of increasingly complex algorithmic problems, using a modern programming language and a variety of approaches. Problem decomposition and abstraction guide explorations of topics from applied algorithms, for example Voronoi Diagrams, Markov Chains, Bin Packing, and Graph Search. Not for students with credit for, or currently enrolled in, CPSC 210 or CPEN 221. Prerequisite: One of CPSC 103, CPSC 110, APSC 160, EOSC 211, MATH 210, PHYS 210, COMM 337.

name: International Financial Markets and Institutions
description: Structure, nature and institutions of foreign exchange markets, including spot, forward, futures, options, and offshore currency markets. Factors affecting exchange rates are also discussed. Credit will be granted for only one of ECON 456, COEC 377, or COMM 377. Prerequisite: COEC 371. Equivalency: COMM377

name: Strategic Management
description: Concepts and processes for the strategic management of single- and multi-business unit private sector enterprises, analyzed using the case method. name: International Business Management

name: Strategic Compensation
description: Employee compensation, including pay systems, benefits systems, and rewards and recognition programs. Examination of the motivational underpinnings of compensation administration and the application of compensation principles to the achievement of employer strategic objectives.

name: Strategic Staffing
description: Processes of workforce recruitment, selection, retention, and renewal. Includes human resources planning, development of an effective staffing strategy and employer brand, job analysis and descriptions, cost-benefit analysis of various recruiting methods, analysis and evaluation of selection methods.

name: Introduction to Organizational Consulting
description: Frameworks from the social sciences useful for understanding organizational processes and how to apply these frameworks to particular organizational consulting challenges.

name: New Enterprise Development

name: Training, Development, and Performance Management
description: Employee training, development and performance management in a variety of employment settings. Application of various training methods to performance enhancement, performance appraisal, feedback, and empirical evaluation of training investments.

name: Labour Relations

name: Career Fundamentals
description: Fundamentals of career management including effective resume and cover letter writing, performing well in interviews and learning about the recruiting cycles, networking and resources available at the Hari B. Varshney Business Career Centre.

name: Introduction to Management Information Systems
description: Overview of computer technology and terminology; use of computers as managerial and administrative tools; the management of computer resources and the influence of information technology within the organization.

name: Managing the Employment Relationship
description: The role of employment relations in enterprise performance. Managing employees under statutory law, collective bargaining, and progressive human resource management. Key issues in forming, developing, and maintaining a work force. Prerequisite: One of COMM_V 192, COMM_V 292 and either (a) all of ECON_V 101, ECON_V 102 or (b) ECON_V 100.

name: Logistics and Operations Management
description: The design and management of systems to make products, provide services and deliver them to the end user. Credit will be granted for only one of COMM_V 204, COMM_V 398, or COMR_V 398. Prerequisite: One of COMM_V 190, COMM_V 290 and one of COMM_V 191, COMM_V 291. Equivalency: MGMT_O 355.

name: Introduction to Quantitative Decision Making
description: Introduction to decision models in business, including basic optimization, linear programming, probability, decision analysis, random variables, simulation, and solving decision problems using spreadsheet tools. Credit will be granted for only one of COMM_V 190, COMM_V 290, ECON_V 325, ECON_V 327, PSYC_V 366, STAT_V 241, or STAT_V 251. Strongly recommended as corequisite: One of MATH_V 100, MATH_V 102, MATH_V 104, MATH_V 110, MATH_V 120, MATH_V 180, MATH_V 184. Equivalency: COMM_V 290.

name: Business Communications

name: Intermediate Writing Poetry
description: The writing of poetry in various forms using a combination of workshopping and online modules. Manuscript submission not required for admission. Prerequisite: CRWR 201.

description: Roles of capital market institutions and participants. Skill development for basic financial principles in the quantitative and qualitative evaluation of bond and stock investments.

description: Techniques of and practice in writing for lyric forms, including song lyrics, lyrical narratives, and libretti. Manuscript submission is not required for admission.

name: Intermediate Writing Fiction
description: An exploration of the writing of fiction, focusing on how a writer employs the technical elements of the craft of fiction. Manuscript submission not required for admission. Prerequisite: CRWR 209.

Credit will be granted for only one of COMM_V 280 or COMR_V 280. Equivalency: COMR_V 280.

name: Intermediate Writing for Children and Young Adults
description: The writing of work for children and young adults in various forms using a combination of workshopping and online modules. Manuscript submission not required for admission. Prerequisite: CRWR 203.

name: Intermediate Writing for the Stage
description: An exploration of practice in the writing of the one-act stage play, focusing on how a writer employs the technical elements of the craft of this genre. Manuscript submission is not required for admission. Prerequisite: CRWR 200.

name: Intermediate Writing for Graphic Forms
description: The writing of graphica (comics, manga and graphic novels), using a combination of workshopping and online modules. Manuscript submission not required for admission. Prerequisite: CRWR 208.

name: Intermediate Writing for Television
description: Elements of episodic and serialized comedic and dramatic television writing with writing practice applied to primary formats and genres. Prerequisite: CRWR 206.

name: Interactive Storytelling
description: Origin, theory and practice of interactive story forms. Exploring structural links between interactive theatre, gaming, and extended (virtual, mixed, and augmented) reality. Prerequisite: One of CRWR 213 or B.M.S. student with 3rd year standing or higher.

name: Intermediate Writing of Creative Nonfiction
description: An exploration of and practice in the writing of creative non-fiction, covering four of the more basic forms of this genre: memoir, profile, commentary, and exposition. Manuscript submission is not required for admission. Prerequisite: CRWR 205.

name: Intermediate Writing for the Screen
description: An exploration of and practice in writing for the screen, focusing on how a writer employs the technical elements of the craft of screenwriting. Manuscript submission is not required for admission. Prerequisite: CRWR 206.

name: Study Abroad, Non-Commerce
description: A study abroad program developed in cooperation between UBC Faculty of Commerce and another institution offering a set of courses tailored to a particular field of study.

name: Managerial Economics
description: Economic foundations of managerial decision-making. Demand theory, cost and production, market structure, competitive strategy, organization of the firm, welfare-economic foundations of business regulation. Credit will be granted for only one of ECON 201, ECON 206, ECON 301, ECON 304, FRE 295, or COMM 295. Prerequisite: Either (a) ECON 100 or (b) all of ECON 101, ECON 102.

name: Intermediate Poetry Workshop

name: Research Theory for Commerce Scholars
