name: Evolution and the Sciences of Mind, Brain, and Behaviour
description: Examines how Darwin's theory of evolution changed the investigation of human nature. Questions will be historical and scientific, but will also concern the social, ethical, and existential stakes raised by the human mind as a product of evolution.

name: History and Social Relations of Modern Sciences.
description: Science and society in the 19th to 21st Centuries.

name: Vegetation Dynamics: Disturbance, Climate and Human Impacts
description: Investigation of vegetation dynamics integrating theory and research to address contemporary issues of global environmental change. Students will conduct fieldwork and learn to analyze data and interpret results.

name: Rivers and Landforms: Fluvial Geomorphology
description: Introduction to open channel flow and sediment transport. River morphology and channel types. Palaeohydrology. The development of channel networks.

name: Catchment Hydrology
description: Hydrometeorology; runoff processes; streamwater chemistry in relation to runoff processes; effects of climate variations and land cover change on streamflow regimes; models of catchment hydrology.

name: Science and the Enlightenment
description: Examines the relationship between science and society in the long eighteenth century. Topics include empiricism, classification, academies, print culture, and voyages of exploration.

name: The Changing Cryosphere: Snow, Ice and Climate Change
description: Formation of ice masses and their evolution including snowpacks, glaciers, and ice sheets. Relationships between ice and climate including records of climate change, glacier dynamics and ice-related hazards.

name: Research in Cartography
description: Use of cartography in primary research applications. Discussion of contemporary topics in cognitive, social, and technical cartography and data visualization.

name: Advanced Field Studies in Geographical Sciences
description: Advanced research design, field sampling methods, instrumentation, surveying, mapping techniques, data analysis and management; self-directed field-based research.

name: Cultural Histories of Media: From Writing to Tweeting
description: The history of different forms of media in global perspective, with particular attention to audiovisual electronic media.

name: Urban Meteorology
description: The impact of urbanization upon atmospheric processes and climates. The energy and water balances of cities. Meteorological effects (urban heat island, precipitation modification, etc.) and their significance. Models of the urban atmosphere.

name: Asia and the World
description: The political, economic, social, cultural, and human interactions between Asia and the world, inter-Asian relations, Asian diaspora, colonialism, war and the social consequences of conflict, decolonization, industrial growth, and developing world issues.

name: Air Pollution Meteorology
description: The nature of atmospheric pollutants. The ability of the atmosphere to disperse, transform, and remove pollutants. Air pollution dispersion models. Air quality monitoring, criteria, and standards.

name: Directed Studies in Geographical Sciences
description: For fourth-year students in Geography to permit investigation of a topic to be agreed upon by a member of the faculty and the student. Permission of the department head and of a supervisory faculty member is required. .

name: Watershed Dynamics and Morphology
description: Hillslope and stream channel processes and their rates of operation. Analysis and modelling geomorphic processes and associated hazards at the watershed scale. Applications in geoscience and engineering.

name: Global History Since 1900
description: Historical survey of the 20th and 21st centuries. Includes international relations, colonialism, decolonization, and political ideologies. Application of historical sources and methods to examine the dynamics of change in a global context.

name: History Through Video Games
description: Exploration of global histories through video games and uses of video games for research by historians.

name: Undergraduate Thesis
description: Original research on an approved topic, developed under the guidance of a faculty member. Open to 4th year students in Geographical Sciences with appropriate background courses related to the research topic, and permission of the directing faculty member. The 3-credit option is only available to students who complete GEOS_V 449 in tandem with GEOS_V 409.

name: River Restoration: Science and Society
description: Projects designed to give students research development and design experience. Projects are provided by research faculty in Science and Engineering and from local industry.

name: Research in Geographic Information Science
description: Students use GIS in primary research applications in conservation biology, crime analysis, and health geography; theoretical and practical aspects considered in a hands-on environment.

name: The Global War on Terror
description: Critically examines the origins, impacts, and legacies of the nebulous “Global War on Terror”.

name: Magic, Miracles, and Witchcraft: The Supernatural in Medieval Europe
description: Social, religious, and political functions of the supernatural in late antique, early medieval, and medieval European society (400-1400 CE). Emphasis on the different roles and impacts of magic, witchcraft, and the occult in pre-modern European conceptions of the cosmos.

name: Global History from the 15th to 20th Century
description: Survey of global history from the 15th to the 20th century, a transformative period marked by profound social, political, economic and environmental changes.

name: Global Environmental History
description: The impact humans have had on the environment, and the ways in which the physical environment has shaped human history: climate, agriculture, energy use, and urbanization. Credit will only be granted for one of HIST 207 or HIST 106. Equivalency: HIST 106

name: Theory and Practice of Research in Geographical Sciences
description: Restricted to M.A.GEOG, M.Sc. GEOG, or PhD GEOG.

name: Gateway to the Middle Ages
description: Problems and themes of medieval European History through the close study of the people and cultures that produced them.

name: Global Indigenous Histories
description: An introduction to the experiences of Indigenous peoples and the nature of colonialisms around the world since 1500, and an introduction to historical practices and perspectives. Credit will only be granted for one of HIST 208 or HIST 107. Equivalency: HIST 107

name: History Through Photographs
description: The discipline of history through the study of photographs. Explores themes such as colonialism, orientalism, the mass media, representations of gender and sexuality, and protest through photographic evidence.

name: Student Directed Seminar in Geographical Sciences
description: Self-directed, collaborative studies in physical geography, in a group-learning environment, initiated and coordinated by senior undergraduate students with the supervision of a faculty advisor. Course structure, enrolment, and delivery methods will comply with the Handbook for Student Directed Seminars. This course carries science credit.

name: Global History of Capitalism
description: The history of capitalism in its global dimension from the beginnings to the age of industrialization. An investigation of economies - in both their practices and cultures - around the world and across the ages from ancient times to the modern era. Credit will only be granted for one of HIST 209 or HIST 108. Equivalency: HIST 108

name: History of Global Migration
description: Explores the mass migration of people in the modern world through a global perspective. Industrial and export-oriented economies in the mid-nineteenth century to contemporary issues of border regulation and refugees. Credit will be granted for only one of HIST 211 or HIST 110. Equivalency: HIST 110.

name: History Through Film
description: Explores films as a powerful medium for making history. Analyze visual arguments and historical representations, claims, and narratives made in films.

name: Re-Storying History: Indigenous Perspective
description: Exploration of the diversity of Indigenous peoples of British Columbia and Canada and their unique histories, beginning with origin stories and oral histories and moving on to the histories and relationships that Indigenous groups have with the federal, provincial and territorial governments.

name: Introduction to Resilience Theory in Community
description: Theory of social-ecological resilience as applied to cross-cultural community settings, using case studies from communities on Haida Gwaii and other exceptional cases of community resilience.

name: Introduction to Historical Archaeology
description: An introduction to the study of medieval and modern material culture, with special emphasis on Canada, using archaeological evidence to illustrate the principles, aims, and techniques of historical archaeology and related disciplines.

name: Systems Thinking and Social-Ecological Change
description: Theories of systems change, including complex systems thinking, resilience/transformation, transition management and other social science-based change theories. Corequisite: All of HGSE 382, HGSE 383, HGSE 384.

name: Ecological Economics
description: Underlying philosophy and principles of ecological economics, including the cascading effects of change, unintended consequences of change, and why it might be difficult to separate our ecological goals from our political realities.

name: Ocean Governance
description: Introduction to key marine conservation and management issues, pairing broad topics with examples on Haida Gwaii to bring theory into practice.

name: Community Resilience Seminar
description: The application of theory, concepts, stories, and histories of community resilience through focused readings, group discussions and engagement with local speakers to provide the opportunity to engage deeply and work at the theory-practice interface.

name: Language and Cultural Continuity
description: An exploration of language as a means of looking at culture, and cultural continuity. Using Xaad Kilthe Haida language as a framing device, students will explore the integral connections between language, culture, history, land, health and resilience.

name: Political and Legal Aspects of Systems Change
description: An examination of the emergence of Aboriginal Law in Canada, with a focus on the development of Aboriginal law as an innovation in shaping new contexts for Federal-, Provincial- and Corporate-Indigenous relations and its implications for systems transformation. Corequisite: All of HGSE 380, HGSE 383, HGSE 384.

name: Case Studies in Social-Ecological Change
description: An exploration of complex issues of social-ecological change in the current social-economic-political context of reconciliation initiatives and Indigenous governance, highlighting the Haida worldview and Haida ways of knowing and being with western understandings of social-ecological systems. Corequisite: All of HGSE 380, HGSE 382, HGSE 383.

name: Marine Conservation in British Columbia
description: Perspectives and methodologies applied to the conservation of marine environments in British Columbia.

name: Community Planning and Development for Resilience
description: An examination of the challenges and opportunities of developing and diversifying resilient resource dependent cross-cultural, rural communities using Haida Gwaii's comprehensive community planning as a case study.

name: Social Innovation and Entrepreneurship
description: An examination of the relationships between culture, ingenuity, creativity, entrepreneurship and innovation required to understand and foster systems change through Indigenous and cross-cultural examples. Corequisite: All of HGSE 380, HGSE 382, HGSE 384.

name: Beginning Biblical Hebrew I
description: Biblical Hebrew, with an introduction to vocabulary and grammar, and the reading of simple biblical texts in the original.

name: Advances in Food Theory and Applications
description: Restricted to students in the Master of Nutrition and Dietetics graduate program. Corequisite: All of HUNU 545, HUNU 573.

name: Food Provision and Management in Dietetics
description: Restricted to students in the Master of Nutrition and Dietetics graduate program. Prerequisite: All of HUNU 540, HUNU 573, HUNU 575.

name: Research Methods in Human Nutrition
description: Experimental design, methods of survey research, nutritional epidemiology, clinical research, and laboratory animal research. Issues such as animal models, ethics in animal and human research, statistical methods, and preparation of written reports and manuscripts, etc., will be addressed. Required of all M.Sc. and Ph.D. students in Human Nutrition.

name: Sociocultural Determinants of Health
description: Methods for analyzing population health data and medical research reporting.

name: Current Issues in Nutrition and Metabolism
Counselling Skills in Dietetics
description: Restricted to students in the Master of Nutrition and Dietetics graduate program. Prerequisite: HUNU 510.

name: Korea Since 1860
description: An examination of the political, economic, social, and cultural transformations of Korea since the late nineteenth century. Topics include the end of the Choson Dynasty, the history of Japanese colonial rule, the Korean war, and the two Koreas in the international system.

name: India from Raj to Republic
description: Exploration of the rise of the East India Company as territorial power, the formation of a colonial society in India, competing responses to British rule, the struggle for independence, and the legacies of partition.

name: The Making of Modern Sikhism
description: Historical, social, and cultural forces that shaped Sikh religious beliefs, practices, institutions, and thought in the modern period, including both colonial and post-colonial contexts and the transnational Sikh community.

name: Introduction to History and Philosophy of Science
description: An examination of historical, conceptual, and methodological conditions of scientific knowledge through detailed consideration of important episodes in the history of science. Credit will be granted for only one of HIST 393 or PHIL 360. Equivalency: PHIL 360

name: Topics in History
description: Topics will vary from year to year. Consult the program websitehttps://history.ubc.ca/courses/for more information.

name: Foundations of Sikh Traditions
description: Sikh religious beliefs, practices, institutions, and thought. Emphasis on the history of the Sikh Gurus and their writings, and the larger social and cultural forces within which the tradition developed.

name: Human Rights in World History
description: Changing ideas about humanity and rights. Considers the relationship between human rights and the nation-state, imperialism, and capitalism. Assesses the efforts to end large-scale human rights violations and the role of the United Nations.

name: Dietetics Practice Education Placement III.I Management
description: Practice education placement in management and leadership settings across British Columbia. Restricted to students in the Master of Nutrition and Dietetics program. Pass/fail. Prerequisite: All of HUNU_V 541, HUNU_V 578, HUNU_V 580, HUNU_V 581.

name: Environmental History of North America
description: Overview of land use and environmental change in Canada and the United States; examines ideas and practices that shaped indigenous and non-indigenous resource exploitation, management, and activism to the end of the twentieth century.

name: Directed Studies
description: In special cases, directed studies on certain aspects of nutrition may be arranged for graduate students in attendance.

name: Asian Cities
description: Urban, environmental, and cultural history through Asian Cities.

name: India in the Early Modern World: Kings, Courtesans, and Saints
description: History of India during the period of Mughal rule (roughly 1500-1750). Studies the role of India and the Mughals within the global dynamics of the early modern world.

name: Selected Issues in German-speaking Culture
description: In depth study of one topic from German-speaking cultural history, varying from year to year. Find out which topic/s will be explored in the current or coming year athttps://cenes.ubc.ca/courses/. Credit will be granted for only one of GERM 408 or GMST 424. Equivalency: GERM408

name: Major Controversies in German-speaking Culture
description: Selected debates and controversies in the German-speaking societies. Find out more athttps://cenes.ubc.ca/courses/. Credit will be granted for only one of GERM 411 or GMST 427. Equivalency: GERM411

name: Germanophone Representations of the Holocaust
description: The Holocaust in German literature and film. Find out more athttps://cenes.ubc.ca/courses/. Credit will be granted for only one of GERM 426 or GMST 433. Prerequisite: Restricted to students with Second Year Standing or above. Equivalency: GERM426

name: Special Topics in Germanophone Cinema
description: Themes, traditions, and techniques specific to cinema from German-speaking societies. Find out more athttps://cenes.ubc.ca/courses/. Credit will be granted for only one of GERM 409 or GMST 436. Equivalency: GERM409

name: Scientific Revolution: Circulation of Knowledge in the Early Modern World
description: The profound transformation of knowledge about the world in the context of the first global encounter of civilizations between 1450 and 1800. Explores the foundations for modern science.

name: Selected topics in Germanophone Literature
description: Topics of special interest, varying from year to year. Find out which topic/s will be explored in the current or coming year athttps://cenes.ubc.ca/courses/. A maximum of 6 credits will be granted for GERM 406 or GMST 440. Equivalency: GERM406

name: Voices from Medieval India
description: History of medieval India explored through different stories from and about India's pre-modern past. Studies trends in society, religion, politics, and material life to reveal the dynamism of this period and to challenge simplified narratives of Hindu-Muslim confrontation.

name: Studies in Modern German-speaking Culture
description: Topics of special interest, varying from year to year. Find out more athttps://cenes.ubc.ca/courses/. A maximum of 6 credits will be granted for GERM 403 or GMST 420. Equivalency: GERM403

name: German Media Studies
description: Major themes and methods in German media studies. Find out which themes will be explored in the current or coming year athttps://cenes.ubc.ca/courses/. Credit will be granted for only one of GERM 412 or GMST 475. Equivalency: GERM412

name: The Nuclear Century: Scientists, Atoms, and the World Order Since 1900
description: Science and the military-industrial complex; quantum and relativistic revolutions in physics; nuclear energy and weapons of mass destruction; international tensions, environmental damage, and global perils.

name: Directed Studies
description: Advanced research undertaking topics of German Studies, with the agreement and under the supervision, of a faculty member with relevant expertise. Restricted to German Studies students with approval from the Director of Undergraduate Studies.

name: Words and Music in Germanophone Literature
description: Individual works and genres in which words and music together form a whole. Possible topics include the Lutheran Hymn, the Volkslied, the Romantic Lied and Brecht songs, operas by Mozart, Wagner and Strauss, and music and the musician as a subject in literature. No musical training is necessary. Find out more athttps://cenes.ubc.ca/courses/. Credit will be granted for only one of GERM 402 or GMST 445. Equivalency: GERM402

name: Religion and Germanophone Literature
description: Religion and literature in German-speaking cultural history. Find out more athttps://cenes.ubc.ca/courses/. Credit will be granted for only one of GERM 404 or GMST 448. Equivalency: GERM404

name: Darwin, Evolution, and Modern History
description: Darwin and the science of evolution in nineteenth and early twentieth century. Credit will be granted for only one of HIST 394 or PHIL 364. Equivalency: PHIL 364.

name: Environmental History of the Modern World
description: Major themes in global environmental history and historiography since 1500, with a particular focus on the nineteenth through twenty-first centuries.

name: Honours Research Capstone
description: Conception and execution of research study with the goal of publication, peer-review, and application to graduate study in relevant field. Find out more athttps://cenes.ubc.ca/courses/. Credit be granted for only one of GERM 449 or GMST 492. Equivalency: GERM449

name: Literary Theories
description: A maximum of 6 credits will be granted for GERM 501 or GMST 501. Equivalency: GERM 501

name: German Studies Research Methods
description: A maximum of 6 credits will be granted for GERM 500 or GMST 500. Equivalency: GERM 500

name: History of Canada: Moments that Matter
description: An introduction to major turning points in Canadian history. Exploration of the social, political, cultural, and environmental transformations/revolutions that have shaped Canada from early European colonialism to the twenty-first century.

name: The Acquisition of German as an Additional Language
description: Credit will be granted for only one of GERM 505 or GMST 505. Equivalency: GERM 505

name: Introduction to Public History in Canada: Confronting the Canadian Past
description: An introduction to public history in Canada that explores the politics and practice of representing the past in a variety of sites, such as museums, monuments, and films, and examines questions of historical interpretation, memory, and audience.

name: Honours Seminar
description: Credit will be granted for only one of GERM 439 or GMST 490. Equivalency: GERM439

name: History of the United States
description: Survey from colonial period to present examining political system, slavery, Civil War, race relations and civil rights, westward expansion, industrialization, feminism, expanding international presence, Cold War, and modern culture.

name: Health, Illness and Medicine I: From the Ancient World to the Early Modern Period
description: History of western medicine, from the Ancient World to the Enlightenment, with a focus on social and cultural ideas surrounding the body, health, and disease, and the development of medical institutions.

name: Science and Society in the Contemporary World
description: An introduction to the historical development, conceptual foundations, and cultural significance of contemporary science. Themes will vary from year to year. Credit will be granted for only one of HIST_V 260 or PHIL_V 260. Equivalency: PHIL_V 260.

name: Science, Medicine, and Technology in the Ancient and Medieval Worlds
description: The history of science, medicine, and technology, emphasizing networks, exchanges, and encounters in a global context.

name: Modern Caribbean History
description: A survey of social, cultural and political history of Anglophone, Francophone and Spanish Caribbean from the Haitian Revolution to the present.

name: History of Africa
description: An introduction to selected themes and historical approaches in African history. These may include African geography and identities, sources and methodology, pre-modern state formation, gender relations, world religions, labour systems, colonialism, and post-colonialism. Credit will be granted for only one of AFST_V 256 or HIST_V 256. Equivalency: AFST_V 256

name: History of Europe
description: Selected themes and historical approaches in European history; may include Europe's history of religious conflict, state formation, colonialism, nationalism, industrialization, revolution, total war, globalization, genocide, or environmental change.

name: Latin American History
description: Exploring themes of colonialism, indigenous life, national imaginaries, dictatorships and transitions to democracy through different forms of telling Latin American history. Includes epistolary writing, maps, eyewitness accounts, chronicles, actions, novels, films, built environment and city plans, testimonios, and plays.

name: China in World History
description: The history of China in a global context, from the earliest times to the most recent past; how China has changed the world and how engagement with the world has changed China. Credit will be granted for only one of HIST_V 270 or ASIA_V 270. Equivalency: ASIA_V 270.

name: Islamic World History
description: The history of the Islamic world in its global dimensions from its origins to the present day through the themes of religion, law, politics, culture, and modernity.

name: Quebec from the End of the 18th Century to the Present
description: Relations between the English and the Canadians prior to the Rebellions of 1837-38, the emergence of French Canadian nationalism after 1840, the impact of State formation and industrialization in Quebec, the Quiet Revolution, and the independence movement.

name: History of British Columbia
description: The social, political, cultural, environmental, and economic transformations that have made British Columbia. Topics include the histories of Indigenous and settler peoples, the modern state, migration, activism, and identity.

name: History of India
description: Societies, cultures, and politics of the Indian subcontinent from its ancient civilizations to the formation of the modern nation-states of South Asia.

name: Health, Illness and Medicine II: The Modern World from 1700 to the Present
description: Western medicine from 1700 to the present, with a focus on social and cultural ideas surrounding the body, health and disease, and the development of medical institutions.

name: Global Medieval Heritage and Policy
description: Examination of cultural heritage work and policy based on contemporary international case studies that engage the global medieval past.

name: Steppe Empires in World History
description: Powerful empires that flourished over the Eurasian Steppe, from the earliest to modern times, and how regimes and cultures associated with these empires have changed the world.

name: Researching Local History from the Ground Up
description: Sources and methods for reconstructing local history that can be used by Social Studies teachers in B.C. The aim is to develop an appreciation of the formative processes and past experiences that created one's familiar community.

name: History of Vancouver
description: Selected themes in the history of Vancouver, exploring how the study of the past illuminates or explains major debates in the city today. Credit will be granted for only one of HIST_V 316 or HIST_V 415 Equivalency: HIST_V 415.

name: The State of the Earth
description: The demographic, economic, ecological, and technological factors that underlie current environmental challenges, considering their effects to date and their possible impact in the future. Recommended: Second-year standing. Equivalency: ENST 211

name: Modern Africa
description: Africa in the 19th and 20th Centuries: Islamic revolutions, the end of the slave trades, colonial conquest, labour struggles, Christianity’s new appeal, PanAfricanism, nationalist resistance, and decolonization. Post-independence challenges of nation-building and economic development. Cultural renaissances and the politics of tradition. Credit will be granted for only one of AFST_V 313 or HIST_V 313. Equivalency: AFST_V 313

name: History of the Indigenous Peoples of North America
description: Indigenous peoples from pre-contact to the present in Canada and the U.S. Topics may include colonial frontiers, disease, fur trade, government policies, environment, gender, religion, oral narratives, activism, urbanization, and identity.

name: Cities
description: An interdisciplinary introduction to the city in the context of contemporary globalization. Analysis of urban patterns and processes from the theoretical perspectives of various disciplines and methodologies. Equivalency: URST_V 200.

name: The British Empire after 1850
description: Transformation of the British imperial system from the mid-nineteenth century to de-colonization and neo-colonialism after the second World War.

name: Japan and Global History, 1550 - 1900
description: Thematic study of comparisons and relations between Japan and the world outside (primarily Europe and China). Commercial expansion, systems of world order, social institutions, religious and ideological expression, and state organization.

name: Vikings: Then and Now
description: Historical and archaeological study of Viking-Age and premodern Scandinavia and the Vikings complex legacies in contemporary cultural heritage.

name: Geopolitics
description: Introduction to the political geographic perspectives on today's interdependent world through three themes: borders, regions, and flows.

name: People, Places & Landscapes
description: Relationships among individuals, social groups, and place, with a focus on everyday spaces. Examines how social identities are intertwined with the places we live.

name: Southern Africa
description: Pre-colonial, colonial, and contemporary, emphasizing South Africa. Credit will be granted for only one of AFST_V 312 or HIST_V 312. Equivalency: AFST_V 312

name: Environmental Justice and Social Change
description: Economic, social, political and cultural structures and institutions that shape contemporary socioecological challenges. Recommended pre-requisite: GEOG_V 121. Equivalency: ENST_V 313

name: Human and Environmental Geography Field Course
description: Engage in primary field-based research in British Columbia on important issues concerning intercultural understanding, engagement with local communities and sustainability. Focus will shift on a bi-annual basis in accordance with location and available community partners. Special fees and liability insurance are required. Third year standing is recommended. Prerequisite: Permission of the instructor.

name: Urban Environments
description: The impact of urban development on the natural environment and vice versa. Study of the ecology and metabolism of cities and green urban design, using global and local case studies. Equivalency: ENST311

name: Constitutions in Canadian History: From Pre-Contact to the Charter of Rights
description: European precedents, Colonial self-government, Canadian Confederation, and issues such as gay rights, abortion, and First Nations land rights. Credit will be granted for only one of HIST_V 320 or HIST_V 414. Equivalency: HIST_V 414.

name: Introduction to the Geography of Canada
description: Selected topics in human geography focusing on the regional distribution of natural resources, population, urban systems, and economic activities.

name: Britain, 1945 to the Present
description: Survey of recent British history, with emphasis on de-colonization, emergence of the welfare state, new social movements and patterns of immigration, and Britain's changing relationship with Europe.

name: Early Modern Britain
description: The social, economic, political, religious, cultural, and intellectual history of Britain between the Reformation and the Industrial Revolution, emphasizing the rise of modern industrial society.

name: Analysing Environmental Problems
description: Concepts and techniques employed in environmental research; challenges in the areas of climate change, water use, knowledge translation and natural hazards. Restricted to students with at least third-year standing. Prerequisite: One of GEOG_V 211, GEOB_V 102, GEOB_V 103, GEOS_V 102, GEOS_V 103, EOSC_V 110 or EOSC_V 112. Equivalency: ENST_V 314.

name: Britain, 1850-1918
description: Britain from the Great Exhibition to the Great War: the creation of a mass electorate, the New Imperialism, the New Woman, and the ways that class, race, gender, and sexuality shaped modern Britain.

name: Geography of Natural Hazards
description: The role of geophysical events, human ecology, environmental perception, world social and political order in explaining the risk of natural disasters. Assessment of acceptable risk, disaster relief and reconstruction and contrasts between developed and developing nations. Recommended pre-requisites: one of GEOB 102, GEOS 102 and one of GEOB 103, GEOS 103. Equivalency: ENST 316

name: Geography of the Pacific Rim
description: An introduction to changing geographies (social, economic, and political) of the Pacific Rim, with special emphasis on the relationships between Canada and Japan.

name: Climate Change: Science and Society
description: Climates over the geological, historical and instrument periods. Theories of climatic change. Monitoring and modelling the climate system. Impacts of change on environmental and socio-economic systems. Recommended pre-requisites: one of GEOS 102, GEOB 102, GEOS 200, GEOB 200, GEOS 204, GEOB 204, ATSC 201, EOSC 112. Third-year standing. Equivalency: ENST312

name: Environment and Sustainability
description: Concepts of environment, resources and sustainability; the roles of physical and human geography in understanding the interaction of humans and the environment; introduction to management of environment-resource systems. Equivalency: ENST310

name: Sustainability in a Changing Environment
description: Biophysical and human causes of short- and long-term environmental change at various spatial scales, including measurement, interpretation, and policy. Recommended pre-requisite: GEOG 310. Equivalency: ENST 318

name: Climate Justice
description: Concepts and debates in the interdisciplinary field and practice of climate justice; the role of systemic processes and patterns underlying climate change and climate injustices. Recommended: Second-year standing. Equivalency: ENST 302

name: Advanced Hindi-Urdu
description: Further study of the grammar of Hindi and Urdu; advanced conversation; literary readings in Hindi and Urdu; Hindi film. Recommended pre-requisites: one of HINU 200, HINU 202.

name: Intermediate Hindi-Urdu II
description: Continuation of HINU 201. Recommended pre-requisite: HINU 201.

name: Introduction to the Devanagari Script
description: The writing system of Hindi for those with some background in the spoken language. May be taken at the same time as HINU 200.

name: Intermediate Hindi-Urdu I
description: Conversation and grammar; an introduction to Hindi literature; an introduction to the Urdu script. Recommended pre-requisite: HINU 101.

name: What is History?
description: The discipline of history through the study of questions, sources, methods, and controversies. Includes case studies of key turning points in world history to examine what historians do and why it matters.

name: Global History to 1500 CE
description: Introduction to premodern human societies of Asia, Africa, Europe, and the Americas and cultural, political, social, economic, and religious exchanges from a global history perspective and introduction to historical practices.

name: Advanced Hindi-Urdu I
description: Further study of the grammar of Hindi and Urdu; advanced conversation; literary readings in Hindi and Urdu; Hindi film. Recommended pre-requisite: HINU 202.

name: Advanced Hindi-Urdu II
description: Continuation of HINU 301. Recommended pre-requisite: HINU 301.

name: Hindi Film
description: Regional, religious, and historical dialects of Hindi and Urdu as represented in films. Recommended pre-requisite: HINU 200 or fluency in Hindi.

name: Introduction to Hindi and Urdu Literature
description: Readings of various literary genres in Hindi, Urdu and their medieval equivalents. Modern fiction from India and Pakistan; the Urdu ghazal; medieval Hindi bhakti poetry; readings from the Adi Granth of the Sikhs Hindi film. Discussion in Hindi-Urdu of all materials. Recommended pre-requisite: HINU 300.

name: World History Since 1900
description: International relations; changes in the nation-state system; the emergence and impact of major political ideologies; genocide; decolonization; the globalization of trade; and the dynamics of economic, social, cultural, and environmental change in a global context.

name: World History from 1500 to the Twentieth Century
description: The civilizations of Asia, Europe, Africa and the Americas, with emphasis on the political, economic, ecological and cultural links among them, and the impact of oceanic contact, imperialism, warfare, migration, and globalization.

name: Canada 1896-1945: Boom, Bust and War
description: Includes Aboriginal policy, immigration and national identity; Canada, Britain and the US; World Wars; economic modernization; the Great Depression; regionalism; political and social movements; and the creation of 'Canadian' culture. Credit will only be granted for one of HIST_V 325 or HIST_V 426.

name: Empires, Wars, and Revolutions in Europe and the Americas,1763-1838
description: Political, social, cultural, and intellectual transformations that reshaped the Atlantic world between 1763 and 1838; special attention will be given to the American, French, and Haitian Revolutions, the Latin American Wars of Independence and Canadian rebellions.

name: Contemporary Global Issues in Historical Perspective
description: Places issues and problems of current relevance such as disease, terrorism, drugs, or ethnic conflict in historical perspective. Each section will explore a single theme. Check with department for course offerings.

name: Heroes, Rebels, Villains, Folks: The People Who Shaped Canada
description: Canadian history through the lens of individual people's lives and their social impact. Themes include race, class, gender, sexuality, indigeneity, colonialism, slavery, immigration, moral regulation, and activism.

name: Inventing Canada, 1840-1896
description: An examination of political, cultural and national developments within the British North American colonies in the second half of the nineteenth century. Credit will not be granted for both HIST 324 or 326, if 326 was taken before 2007W.

name: Rebels in America: Revolution to Civil War, 1763 - 1865
description: Issues in U.S. history from the colonial era through the Civil War, including the causes of the American Revolution; slavery; aboriginal peoples; labour, gender, and industrialization.

name: Introduction to the Perso-Arabic (Urdu) Script
description: The writing system of Urdu for those with some background in the spoken language. Corequisite: One of HINU 300, HINU 400.

name: Canada Since 1945: Affluence and Anxiety in the Atomic Age
description: Includes immigration policy; the welfare state; Aboriginal peoples; the Cold War; resource economies and national politics; continentalism and free trade; constitutional crises; conflicting nationalisms; and new social movements. Credit will only be granted for one of HIST 326 or HIST 426.

name: Colonial America: Encounter and Settlement, 1607 - 1763
description: Encounters between European, African, and Indigenous North American peoples as well as the history of the colonies within the Atlantic world, from the late sixteenth century to the eve of the American Revolution.

name: The United States, 1865-1900: Labour, Race, Gender, and Empire
description: The complicated political, economic and social history of the United States in the three decades following the Civil War.

name: Gaming the System: Digital Media, Social Justice, and Video Games
description: Emerging technology in the areas of digital affect theory, cyborg feminism, critical digital humanities, critical race studies, surveillance studies, and queer game studies.

name: History of the Global Financial Order
description: Origins and transformation of the global financial order (18th century onward) in relation to war, state-building, international political economy, and colonialism.

name: Slave Societies in the Americas
description: A comparative analysis of the institution of chattel slavery, its growth, its effects on slaves and masters, its relation to the larger society, and the causes of its decline, in the various cultures of the Americas. Credit will be granted for only one of HIST 332 or HIST 444. Equivalency: HIST 444.

name: Creativity from the Margins
description: Critical engagement with the creative process of marginalized peoples and the intersection of creative writing, social justice, and anti-racist feminism. Emphasis on how historical and social context are crucial to acts of creative writing and reading. Recommended pre-requisites: all of GRSJ 101, GRSJ 102, or third-year standing.

name: Topics in World History
description: Thematically-organized topics will explore global aspects of human experience across time. Each section will examine a single theme. Check with the department for course offerings.

name: African-American History, 1850 to the Present
description: The history of African-Americans from the Civil War and emancipation through the present. Topics include the Jim Crow system; the Harlem Renaissance; the Civil Rights Movement; and the current economic and political status of Americans of African ancestry.

name: Gender, Race, Sexuality, and Popular Culture
description: Critical examination of mainstream and alternative media images of gender, race, and sexuality in the context of networked social media, film, music, and television. Recommended pre-requisites: either all of GRSJ 101, GRSJ 102 or third-year standing.

name: Gender, Race, Social Justice and Health
description: Interdisciplinary introduction to gender and health issues using selected theoretical frameworks. Recommended pre-requisites: either all of GRSJ 101, GRSJ 102 or third-year standing.

name: African-American History, 1450 - 1850
description: The history of African Americans from the beginnings of the African slave trade in the 15th Century through the mid-1800s and the coming of the U.S. Civil War.

name: Social Justice Issues in Community and International Organizing
description: Critical examination and practical applications of concepts, theories, methods, and strategies of gender-aware organizing at the community and international levels. Recommended pre-requisites: either all of GRSJ 101, GRSJ 102 or third-year standing.

name: Critical Racial Theories
description: Critical theories of racial and cultural difference. Initial formulations of theses against scientific racism and their later transformation by historical, social, and global-historical accounts of racial subjugation.

name: Pedagogies of Social Justice
description: The intersections of gender, education, and work using sociological and economic frameworks. Recommended pre-requisites: either all of GRSJ 101, GRSJ 102 or third-year standing.

name: Gender, Race, Social Justice and the Law
description: A survey of feminist legal thought and recent developments in feminism and law, with a focus on Canada. Recommended pre-requisites: either all of GRSJ 101, GRSJ 102 or third-year standing.

name: Imperial and Colonial Archaeology and Museums
description: The impact of imperialism and colonialism on archaeological practice, museum collecting, and the telling of historical narratives.

name: Feminist Anti-Racist Pedagogies
description: Feminist pedagogies and feminist debates about pedagogy in formal, nonformal, and informal educational settings. Recommended pre-requisites: either all of GRSJ 101, GRSJ 102 or third-year standing.

name: African/Black Women in the Americas
description: An interdisciplinary survey of gender studies and histories of African/Black women in the Americas from the beginning of the slave trade to the present. Recommended pre-requisites: either all of GRSJ 101, GRSJ 102 or third-year standing.

name: Theories of Representation and Difference
description: Feminist scholarship emphasizing languages and processes of representation and the construction of difference in cultural discourses and institutions. Recommended pre-requisites: all of GRSJ 101, GRSJ 102. Restricted to GRSJ Majors and Minors in third-year standing or above.

name: Globalization and Social Justice: Gender, Race, and Sexuality in International Politics
description: Critical examination of the gender dimension of globalization and the theories, discourse, and practices in international politics using gender analysis. Recommended pre-requisites: either all of GRSJ 101, GRSJ 102 or third-year standing.

name: Anti-colonial and Feminist Qualitative Methodologies
description: Data collection techniques, the politics of interpretation, and the formulation of a research proposal using a feminist, anti-racist framework. Recommended pre-requisites: all of GRSJ 101, GRSJ 102. Restricted to GRSJ Majors and Minors in third-year standing or above.

name: French Digital Culture
description: Contemporary issues and debates on how media and digital technologies have impacted French culture and society. Examines how text, language, and writing are used in digital media.

name: The Politics of Gender, Families, and Nation-Building
description: Investigation of historical and contemporary scholarship on the diversity of families, focusing on differences of gender, sexuality, race/ethnicity, and social class within and across national borders. Recommended pre-requisites: all of GRSJ 101, GRSJ 102. Restricted to GRSJ Majors and Minors in third-year standing or above.

name: Ancients and Moderns: Studies in 17th-century French Literature
description: Aesthetic and ideological trends of seventeenth-century French literature in their historical context.

name: Renaissance: Studies in 16th-century French Literature
description: Aesthetic and ideological trends of sixteenth-century French literature in their historical context.

name: Queer and Trans of Colour Theorizing
description: The intellectual and political interventions of queer of colour theorizing in the gender and sexual politics of racial and imperial projects, including its engagements with women of colour feminisms, settler colonial and indigenous studies, and immigration and diaspora studies.

name: Contemporary French Literature and Culture
description: Aesthetic and ideological trends of twentieth- and twenty-first century French literature in their historical context.

name: Popular Fiction
description: Popular genres in modern French fiction, including science fiction, crime, romance, fantasy and historical fiction. Aesthetic characteristics, historical context and cultural relevance.

name: Women's Writing
description: Representative women's writings from the Middle Ages to the present; contemporary women's writings in the Francophone world.

name: The Modern and Contemporary French Novel
description: Major historical, social and artistic movements reflected in representative novels published in France from the 19th Century to the present.

name: Introduction to Literature in French
description: Critical reading of foundational literary texts in French from genres of prose fiction, non-fiction, poetry, and theatre. Prerequisite: One of FREN 123, FREN 302.

name: Selected Topics in French Literature and Culture
description: Study of a literary or cultural topic that extends beyond one chronological period and/or place proper. Consult the Department for this year's offerings.

name: Enlightenment and Revolution: Studies in 18th-century French Literature
description: Aesthetic and ideological trends of eighteenth-century French literature in their historical context.

name: Intermediate French II
description: A continuation of FREN_V 301. This course is aligned with level B1 objectives of the CEFR. Recommended prerequisites: one of FREN_V 122, FREN_V 301, or assignment based on placement. Credit will be granted for only one of FREN_V 302 or FREN_V 123. Equivalency: FREN_V 123.

name: Critical Writing
description: Practical tools for university-level writing in French. Apply stylistic devices and rhetorical structures to form questions and arguments, analyse literary and cultural objects, and produce a variety of essay genres. Prerequisite: One of FREN 123, FREN 302.

name: Tradition and Modernity: Studies in 19th-century French Literature
description: Aesthetic and ideological trends of nineteenth-century French literature in their historical context.

name: French Cinema
description: Study of major past and contemporary French film productions.

name: Quebec Literature and Culture
description: Study of representative aspects of Quebec literature and culture through the study of literary texts, films, and artistic productions in their historical context.

name: Introduction to Quebec Literature
description: Survey of representative literary texts from Quebec viewed in their historical, social, and cultural contexts. Prerequisite: One of FREN 220, FREN 221, FREN 311, FREN 321 and one of FREN 224, FREN 401.

name: Francophone Cinema
description: Study of major past and contemporary film productions from around the Francophone world.

name: African and Caribbean Francophone Literatures
description: Representative and contemporary writings from African and Caribbean francophone cultures.

name: Indigenous Literatures of Francophone Canada
description: Study of the literature and cinema of First Nations, Inuit and Métis creators working in French and in Francophone spaces in Canada. Recommendation: One of FREN 321, FREN 328, FREN 329 and one of FREN 225, FREN 402.

name: French at Work
description: Communicative French for students preparing for a career in the francophone world. This course is aligned with the B1 objectives of the CEFR. Recommended pre-requisites: one of FREN 123, FREN 302.

name: Arts, Cultures and Society from Romanticism to the Present Day
description: Exploration of modern and contemporary French culture and literature from the early 19th century to the present day; the impact of society on the arts and vice versa. Prerequisite: One of FREN 311, FREN 321 and one of FREN 224, FREN 401.

name: French Grammar
description: Principles of grammar theory and contextualized French grammatical concepts. Emphasis on terminology and analysis of grammatical issues. Aligned with CEFR level B2 objectives. Recommended pre-requisite: FREN 401, FREN 402. Prerequisite: One of FREN 123, FREN 302.

name: Upper-Intermediate French I
description: Communicative proficiency at an autonomous level: vocabulary enrichment, pronunciation practice, grammatical analysis and development of efficient reading and writing techniques. This course is aligned with level B2 objectives of the CEFR. Recommended prerequisites: one of FREN_V 123, FREN_V 302, or French Immersion 12, or assignment based on placement test. Credit will be granted for only one of FREN_V 401 or FREN_V 224. Equivalency: FREN _V 224.

name: Introduction to French Linguistics
description: A survey of basic terminology, methods, problems, and theoretical trends in French linguistics, specifically designed to provide students with a foundation for advanced language study in French. Prerequisite: Either (a) FREN 223 or (b) all of FREN 352, FREN 401.

name: Arts, Cultures and Society from the Middle Ages to the Revolution
description: Exploration of early French culture and literature from the Middle Ages to the close of the Early Modern period and the French Revolution; the impact of society on the arts and vice versa. Prerequisite: One of FREN 311, FREN 321 and one of FREN 224, FREN 401.

name: Upper-Intermediate French II
description: A continuation of FREN_V 401. This course is aligned with level B2 objectives of the CEFR. Recommended prerequisites: one of FREN_V 224, FREN_V 401, or assignment based on placement test. Credit will be granted for only one of FREN_V 402 or FREN_V 225. Equivalency: FREN _V 225.

name: Advanced French Grammar
description: Advanced grammar theory and critical analysis of difficult French grammatical structures. Emphasis on autonomous examination of complex grammatical issues. Recommended pre-requisite: FREN 401, FREN 402. Prerequisite: One of FREN 223, FREN 352.

name: Special Topics Abroad
description: Study of Francophone literature, history, culture, or communities in an authentic context. Topics and locations may vary. Consult Department for current offerings. Recommendation: CEFR A2 French proficiency level.

name: Topics in Indigenous History of the United States
description: Interdisciplinary topics in the history of the United States' Indigenous peoples from before European contact. HIST 302 or other background in the field is recommended.

name: Medieval French Literature
description: Aesthetic and ideological trends of French-language literature of the Middle Ages (11th-15th centuries) in their historical context Prerequisite: Either (a) all of FREN 311, FREN 321 or (b) all of FREN 328, FREN 329 and one of FREN 225, FREN 402.

name: Seminar in Medieval History
description: Annually changing topics of medieval studies with special attention to research methods on primary sources.

name: Aboriginal Title in British Columbia: History and Legacy
description: Colonial land policy, Indigenous resistance and organizing, treaties, and court decisions. Some previous knowledge of Indigenous history is strongly recommended.

name: First Contacts in the Pacific
description: An interdisciplinary history of early European contact with the Indigenous peoples of the northwest coast of North America and the Pacific Islands.

name: Imagining the Middle Ages
description: Influence of nostalgia for the history, literature, arts, architecture, and traditions of medieval European centuries on modern intellectual, artistic, and nationalist and racist political movements in Europe and North America. Restricted to students with third-year standing or higher.

name: Ideas and Religions of the Middle Ages
description: A survey and exploration of the development, interpenetration, conflict, and transformation of various intellectual and religious traditions during the Middle Ages.

name: Documenting Punjabi Canada
description: Exploration of the history of the Punjabi Canadian community through traditional text-based methods and oral history collection. Credit will be granted for only one of HIST_V 475 or ASIA_V 475. Equivalency: ASIA_V 475.

name: Topics in Indigenous History of Canada
description: Selected interdisciplinary topics in the history of Canada's Indigenous peoples after European contact, including historical demography, economic interdependency, missionary encounters, gender relations, and interactions with colonial powers and the nation state. Recommended: HIST 302 or other background in the field.

name: Women in the Middle Ages
description: A study of women's roles in the family, society, law, religion, the economy, and literature from about 500 to 1500 CE.

name: Translation
description: Principles, practical strategies and methods of translation from French to English and English to French. Overview of the main challenges involved in intercultural communication. Recommended pre-requisite: FREN 353. Prerequisite: One of FREN 225, FREN 402.

name: Topics in Comparative Indigenous History
description: Comparative interdisciplinary analysis of selected topics in Indigenous history in North America and beyond. HIST 302 or other background in the field is recommended.

name: Constitutional History of Medieval Europe
description: The evolution of political institutions, the emergence of royal governments as well as representative assemblies and urban republic and conflicts within and among them leading to the emergence of modern structures.

name: Histories of the American West
description: Frontier ideologies in relation to race, gender, class, sexuality. Place-making and historical narrative in and about the western part of the United States.

name: Law and Society in the Middle Ages
description: The history of law in the Middle Ages, including English common law, civil (Roman) law, and canon law, and how changes in both medieval law and society affected the development of each.

name: The United States Since 1945: The Limits of Power
description: American military and geo-political power during and after Cold War; wars in Korea, Vietnam, and Middle East; domestic issues including McCarthyism, social movements (blacks, women, youth, gays and lesbians, and Native Americans), consumerism, immigration, and rise of New Right.

name: Medieval Portraits and Personalities
description: The lives of leading and controversial figures in the Middle Ages and the means by which they have portrayed themselves and been portrayed by others.

name: Social History of Modern China
description: Changes and continuities in Chinese society and culture from the late imperial period to the present. Topics may include rural and urban life, social stratification, social movements and ideology, family and community, popular beliefs and cultural values.

name: Medieval and Imperial Russian History, 998 to 1800
description: Russian politics, society, culture, and empire, beginning with the medieval period extending through the era of Peter the Great's modernization efforts and the Enlightenment.

name: Cultural History of Imperial China
description: An in-depth examination of the construction, transmission, and transformation of Chinese culture(s) prior to 1800. A maximum of 6 credits will be granted for only one of HIST_V 479 or ASIA_V 440. Equivalency: ASIA_V 479.

name: American Modernity: The United States, 1890-1945
description: U.S. emergence as an industrial powerhouse and, eventually, a global superpower; responses to industrial society, meaning of modern times, economic upheaval and social change, U.S.'s role as a world power, and politics of race, ethnicity, and gender.

name: Crime and Punishment in Canadian History
description: The relationship between law and society; the development of legal institutions and the evolving character of crime in Canada. Credit will be granted for only one of HIST_V 345 or HIST_V 419. Equivalency: HIST_V 419.

name: Medieval Jewish History
description: A survey of the political, social, economic, and cultural history of the Jews from the time of the Christianization of the Roman Empire to the expulsion of professing Jews from Spain and Portugal at the end of the fifteenth century.

name: History of Modern France
description: The political, social, and cultural history of France from the Revolution of 1789 to the present. Topics may include: France's journey toward democracy and republicanism, the country’s many revolutions over the course of the nineteenth century; the country’s unique model of demographic and industrial modernization.

name: The 1960s in Global Perspective
description: The history of the 1960s from a transnational perspective: culture, social change, student activism, and global conflict. Credit will be granted for only one of HIST_V 337 or HIST_V 418. Equivalency: HIST_V 418.

name: Master's Thesis
description: A maximum of 9 credits will be granted for GERM 549 or GMST 549. Equivalency: GERM 549

name: Major Essay
description: Credit will be granted for only one of GERM 548 or GMST 548. Equivalency: GERM 548

name: Epidemiology and Biostatistics in Global Health
description: Fundamental principles and methods of epidemiology and biostatistics and their application to global health challenges. This course is restricted to students registered in the MGH program. Other Students must contact the department for permission to register.

name: Critical Evidence Appraisal in Global Health
description: Trends and variations in health; evidence appraisal in global health; global heath data sets, the role observational studies and clinical trials. This course is restricted to students registered in the MGH program. Other Students must contact the department for permission to register. Prerequisite: All of GLBH 501, GLBH 503

name: Global Environmental Health
description: Major environmental factors that impact health on a global scale; climate change, air pollution, water quality; measures to address these challenges in local and global contexts This course is restricted to students registered in the MGH program. Other Students must contact the department for permission to register.

name: Imperial Russian History, 1800 to 1917
description: History of Russia from the time of Catherine the Great to the Russian Revolution with particular focus on social and cultural history.

name: The Soviet Union
description: History of the Soviet Union. Topics may include the political, social, and cultural history of the Soviet Union and post-Soviet successor states from 1900 to the present.

name: Ancient Regime France
description: The political, social and/or cultural history of early modern France before the Revolution. Topics may include: the changing significance of the monarchy; the Enlightenment critique of the Catholic Church and religion; the 'pre-revolution'. Credit will only be granted for one of HIST_V 344 or HIST_V 406.

name: Program Planning and Evaluation in Global Health
description: Theory, approaches and methods for conducting global health programs among populations in various low resource contexts. Key concepts, ethical approaches and practices, intersectional considerations, case studies and practical skills development. This course is restricted to students registered in the MGH program. Other Students must contact the department for permission to register. Prerequisites: All of GLBH 501, GLBH 503, SPPH 581H, GLBH 505

name: Foundations of Global Health II
description: Central competencies and system-level concepts required for effective global health practice. This course is restricted to students registered in the MGH program. Prerequisite: GLBH 501

name: Colonialism and Global Health
description: Impacts of distinct types of colonialism on global health. Emphasis on case studies of colonialism and health of Indigenous and non-Indigenous populations both locally and internationally. Explores contextual measures that can improve health and respect for rights of Indigenous Peoples. This course is restricted to students registered in the MGH program. Other Students must contact the department for permission to register. Prerequisite: All of GLBH 501, GLBH 505

name: Global Health Practicum
description: Applied worked-integrated global health experiential learning in a professional setting. Pass/Fail. This course is restricted to students registered in the MGH program. Prerequisites: All of GLBH 501, GLBH 502, GLBH 503, GLBH 505

name: Modern Jewish History
description: A survey of the political, social, economic, and cultural history of the Jews from the beginning of the sixteenth century to the present with special emphasis on changing attitudes to Jews and Judaism, social and cultural transformations.

name: Beginning Biblical Hebrew II
description: Biblical Hebrew, with further introduction to vocabulary and grammar, and the reading of biblical texts in the original. Credit will be granted for only one of HEBR_V 102 or HEBR_V 205. Prerequisite: HEBR_V 101. Equivalency: HEBR_V 102.

name: History of the Holocaust
description: A study of the systematic attempt to destroy European Jewry during the Nazi regime, 1933- 1945. Topics of special importance include: the motivations and behaviour of the perpetrators; the reactions of the victims; the roles of bystanders. Credit will be granted for only one of HIST_V 348 or HIST_V 441. Equivalency: HIST_V 441.

name: Medieval Gender, Christianity, and the Body
description: Medieval representations and treatments of gendered bodies through disciplines of history, religion, and archaeology. Implications of a dominant male standard in early Christian thought.

name: Global Water and Energy Nexus
description: Energy water nexus for sustaining ecological goods and services, and food security; significance in global resource systems. Prerequisite: One of CHEM 111, CHEM 121 and one of BIOL 112, BIOL 121, BIOL 140.

name: Intermediate Biblical Hebrew I
description: Biblical Hebrew. Devised to enrich vocabulary and grammar and enhance fluency in reading and interpreting a range of biblical texts. Credit will be granted for only one of HEBR_V 201 or HEBR_V 301. Prerequisite: One of HEBR_V 102, HEBR_V 205. Equivalency: HEBR_V 201.

name: Global Issues in Cultural Context
description: Students interact face-to-face and online as a community of learners to discuss global issues in agriculture, food, and natural resources in cultural context. Typically taken prior to studying abroad.  Prerequisite: Open only to students in the B.Sc. (GRS) program.

name: East Central Europe in the 19th and 20th Centuries
description: Covers the region between Germany and Russia as well as Southeast Europe. Emphasis on comparisons with Western Europe and features that make the area significant to Europe as a whole.

name: Foundations of Global Health I
description: Key institutions and initiatives related to Global Health; global burden of disease, global social and environmental determinants of health, global health challenges, sustainable development goals, and major actors. This course is restricted to students registered in the MGH program. Other Students must contact the department for permission to register.

name: Supervised Study in Classical Hebrew
description: Prerequisite: One of HEBR 202, HEBR 302.

name: Global Health Ethics
description: Central ethical theories and issues in global health effects of global socioeconomic inequities, recruitment from low to high-resource settings, cultural relativity versus universal human rights This course is restricted to students registered in the MGH program. Other Students must contact the department for permission to register.

name: Global Health Economics and Financing
description: Mobilization, accumulation, and allocation of economic resources to meet the health needs of populations in global health contexts.

name: Whole Building Energy Modelling and Simulation
description: Modelling energy in a high performance building. Introduction to indoor space requirements. Heat and mass transfer through building envelopes. Climate. Fenestration, daylighting, solar energy. Introduction to major energy models. Modelling project.

name: Intermediate Biblical Hebrew II
description: Biblical Hebrew. Devised to further enrich vocabulary and grammar and to enhance fluency in reading and interpreting a range of biblical texts. Credit will be granted for only one of HEBR_V 202 or HEBR_V 302. Prerequisite: One of HEBR_V 201, HEBR_V 301. Equivalency: HEBR_V 202.

name: Building Energy Systems Design
description: Designing the energy system for a high performance building. Heating, cooling and ventilation load estimation. Heating and cooling using solar, electrical and chemical energy. Air, water, and refrigerant distribution systems. Energy storage. System design project. Design performance assessment.

name: Green Building Contemporary Practice
description: Enhanced building environmental performance and the integration of green building principles, strategies and technologies. Equivalency: ARCH574

name: Capstone: Greening Existing Buildings
description: Students will analyze the performance and design data of an existing building and propose design changes that will improve performance, considering the real priorities of the client, a building owner or operator.

name: Regenerative Development
description: The relationship between human and natural systems in the context of regenerative design. Provides an understanding of how regenerative approaches differ from green design and how they can offer new insights and directions for design. Equivalency: ARCH575

name: Capstone: New Building Energy Systems Design
description: Students will take a building under design and work with the designers towards a high performance energy system. The project will be a proposed high performance building with a client, a design team, and energy performance objectives.

name: Advanced Readings in Classical Hebrew
description: Credit will not be given for both HEBR 479 and HEBR 509.

name: Introductory Hindi-Urdu II
description: Continuation of HINU 100. Credit will be granted for only one of HINU 101 or 102. Recommended pre-requisite: HINU 100.

name: Introductory Hindi-Urdu I
description: Spoken Hindi and Urdu, and written Hindi. Credit will be granted for only one of HINU 100 or 102.

name: Networks, Crowds, and Communities
description: Introduces network concepts and methods for exploring social and organizational connectivity for work, socializing, and knowledge production. Examines impact of social media on connections that span space and place; peer production on authority structures; ubiquitous mobile connectivity on daily life.

name: (De)coding Information and Why it Matters
description: Information and data as concepts and aspects of everyday experience. Creation, sharing, authorization, and valuing of information with implications for society. Critical perspectives and practices to engage with data, information, and technologies for personal productivity, scholarly inquiry, and civic engagement.

name: Intermediate Hindi-Urdu
description: Conversation and grammar; an introduction to Hindi literature; an introduction to the Urdu script. As of 2011W, credit will be granted for only one of HINU 201/202 or HINU 200. Recommended pre-requisites: one of HINU 101, HINU 102.

name: Sociotechnical Perspectives for Information Systems Design
description: Interdisciplinary approaches to theorizing, evaluating, envisioning, and designing information systems as assemblages of society and technology that can favor historically, persistently, or systemically marginalized groups and communities.

name: Introductory Hindi-Urdu
description: Spoken and written Hindi and Urdu. As of 2011W, credit will be granted for only one of HINU 100/101 or HINU 102.

name: Information Visualization
description: Basic theory and practice required to visually represent information. Introduces design principles and practical skills to create effective information visualizations. Examines effect of different visual representations on understanding and meaning.

name: Foundations of Informatics
description: Theory, methods, and approaches for the analysis, design, and evaluation of information objects, activities, systems, and infrastructures in contemporary societies.

name: Digital Cultural Collections
description: Design, construction and critique of digital collections from a cultural informatics perspective.

name: Information and Data Design
description: Design of interactive information systems informed by human capabilities and behavior. Application of contemporary information design principles and practices to the conceptualization, creation, and testing of real-world prototypes of information objects and applications. Recommended pre-requisite: INFO 100. Prerequisite: INFO 200.

name: The First World War
description: WWI as a global war; cultural history and legacy; impact of imperialism on the war; military technology. Credit will be granted for only one of HIST_V 374 or HIST_V 404. Equivalency: HIST_V 404.

name: U.S. Foreign Relations from Independence to World War II
description: U.S. foreign policy and international history. Examines the American rise to power and political, economic, and cultural relationships between the United States and other peoples, organizations, and states worldwide. Credit will be granted for only one of HIST_V 371 or HIST_V 408. Equivalency: HIST_V 408.

name: Intermediate Indonesian II
description: Continuation of INDO 201. Credit will be granted for only one of INDO 202 or INDO 200. Recommended pre-requisite: INDO 201.

name: U.S. Foreign Relations since 1945
description: U.S. foreign policy and international history. Political, economic, and cultural relationships between the United States and other peoples, organizations, and states worldwide. Credit will be granted for only one of HIST_V 372 or HIST_V 409. Equivalency: HIST_V 409.

name: Europe Since 1950
description: Europe since the middle of the twentieth century. Themes include the Cold War, the development of separate social and political systems in Western and Eastern Europe, the emergence of the welfare state, and the problems of European integration.

name: Europe, 1900-1950
description: Europe in the first half of the twentieth century. Themes include the imperialist system, two world wars and their aftermaths, political and social movements of the interwar years, the Depression, and the crisis of liberal democracy. Credit will be granted for only one of HIST_V 369 or HIST_V 462. Equivalency: HIST_V 462.

name: The Second World War
description: Precursors and consequences of the war; military, political, cultural, social, and economic histories of how the war shaped and reflected its global context. Themes include totalitarianism, genocide, and imperialism and decolonization. Credit will be granted for only one of HIST_V 375 or HIST_V 406. Equivalency: HIST_V 406.

name: Information Policy and Society
description: Develops capabilities required to assess the need for information policies in professional contexts, evaluate relevant socio-technical dimensions and envision likely implications for specific communities and practice settings.

name: Memory and Identity in the Digital Age
description: Personal and collective constructions of the past from collections of digital artefacts. Emphasis on history, social movements, lived experience, and public life.

name: Europe in the 19th Century
description: An investigation of main themes in European history from the French Revolution to the beginning of the 20th century. Topics of particular importance are: domestic politics; the interaction of states; the formation of new states; social and economic transformations affecting the whole civilization; major cultural expressions of the century.

name: Search Engines and Society
description: Aspects of technical implementation and societal impact of search engines. Explores how Google and other Internet search engines are powerful, global, and non-neutral tools that drive economies and shape our views of the world. Recommended pre-requisite: INFO 200.

name: Perspectives and Methods in Asia Pacific Policy Studies
History of Later Imperial China
description: History of China from the end of Tang to the eve of its modern transformation. Students will acquire the analytical skills and tools to understand the political, socio-economic, and cultural changes in imperial China. Credit will be granted for only one of HIST_V 379 or ASIA_V 340. Equivalency: ASIA_V 340.

name: History of Cantonese Worlds
description: The history, culture, languages, and identities of the multi-faceted Cantonese worlds, in the context of Chinese history and the Cantonese diaspora. Credit will be granted for only one of HIST_V 377 or ASIA_V 323. Equivalency: ASIA_V 323.

name: Media Design for Contemporary Childhood
description: Cultural narratives, values, and practices promoted by media technologies designed for children/youth and the tensions they create.

name: Modern Japanese History Since 1830
description: Meanings of modernity, from the establishment of a nation-state to the creation of a colonial empire, postwar occupation, modern politics and global influence. Social change, including civil protest, mass culture, censorship and expression, and gender, sexuality, ethnicity and race.

name: History of Hong Kong
description: History, culture, and identities of Hong Kong from the early 1800s to the present. Credit will be granted for only one of HIST_V 373 or ASIA_V 373. Equivalency: ASIA_V 373.

name: History of Early China
description: History of China from the earliest times to the disintegration of the Tang Empire. Students will acquire the analytical skills and tools to understand the origins and foundations of Chinese society. Credit will be granted for only one of HIST_V 378 or ASIA_V 320. Equivalency: ASIA_V 320.

name: Topics in Asia Pacific Policy Studies
The City and the National Imagination
description: Examines relations between the idea of the nation and its embodiment in the spaces of the city through visual, spatial, and architectural representations.

name: East Asian Organizations in Comparative Perspective
description: Contemporary theories of organizational behavior applied to economic organizations in Japan, with some comparisons to South Korean, Taiwanese and Chinese firms. Historical and theoretical conceptualizations of business organizations with empirical applications as applied to East Asian firms.

name: Practicum in Asia Pacific Policy Studies
Multinational Firms and Policy Issues in Asia-Pacific
Post-Colonial Southeast Asia
description: The history of the Japanese occupation, wars of independence, international relations of the independent nation-states, and internal armed conflicts. Special attention will be paid to the wars in Vietnam, Indonesia, and East Timor.

name: Advanced Engineering Design Projects
description: Projects involving all material in the curriculum of the Integrated Engineering Program. Students will be expected to propose a project and complete the design and construction of a prototype. Restricted to students in the fourth year of the Integrated Engineering program.

name: Introduction to Engineering Design
description: Introduction to engineering design methods, problem solving, working individually and in teams, and methods of communication of results. Engineering design projects will be assigned. Restricted to students in the second year of the Integrated Engineering program.

name: Integrated Technical Communication
description: Written and oral communication in business correspondence, engineering design methods, report preparation, and oral presentations of technical material. Restricted to students in second year of the Integrated Engineering Program.

name: Cross-National Comparisons in the Social Sciences
description: The methodological and epistemological underpinnings of cross-national comparative research across the social sciences. Focused on but not limited to Northeast Asia. Credit will be granted for only one of IAR_V 511 or SOCI_V 511. Equivalency: SOCI_V 511.

name: The Making of Modern China: Nationalism, War, Revolution
description: The history of China from 1800 to the present including the decline of the Qing empire, the rise of modern nationalism, foreign invasion, and China's multiple revolutions.

name: Introduction to Biodiversity
description: Geographical ecology emphasizing contemporary species distributions at local to global spatial scales, population and community dynamics, and human impacts. Labs emphasize collecting data (sometimes outdoors) and interpreting results.

name: Pipeline Systems and Infrastructure
description: Energy infrastructure; pipe flows; equipment and facilities including compressors, pumping stations, coolers, and controls; terminals; pipeline integrity; corrosion control.

name: Landscapes: Introduction to Geomorphology
description: Earth surface processes shaping the landscape; identification of hazards and hazardous areas associated with these processes; introduction to techniques for measurement and analysis at various spatial and time scales; field trips are required.  This course is recommended for students with credit in one of GEOB 103, GEOS 103, EOSC 110, PHYS 101, PHYS 106, PHYS 107, PHYS 117, PHYS 131, PHYS 157, SCIE 001.

name: Imperialism and Nationalism in Southeast Asia
