Inquiry-Based Pedagogy in School Library Programs
description: Principles and practices of teachers and teacher-librarians designing and teaching curriculum using inquiry-based pedagogy. LLED 469 is a core course for the Teacher Librarian Diploma.

name: Instructional Skills Workshop
description: Introduction to concepts and practice in higher education instruction; emphasis on lesson planning, student participation and instructional aides; includes video-taped practice teacher/peer feedback 28 classroom hours.

name: Exploring Imaging in the Twenty-First Century
description: Interdisciplinary course that covers a wide range of topics regarding not only the scientific and technological basis of medical imaging, but also its origins and impact on society and the individual.

name: Water Infrastructure Capstone
description: Delivery of major water infrastructure projects from policies to planning and implementation, including schedule, cost, scope, impacts, performance and risk management, indigenous participation and innovative project financing and delivery approaches. Credit will be granted for only one of: IWME 506 or CIVL 523.

name: Directed Studies
description: A series of directed readings related to student's area of interdisciplinary studies. This advanced course may be taken upon approval of the Program head.

name: Interdisciplinary Studies: Thematic Seminars
description: Seminars, lectures, and discussions of topics involving several faculties. Contact the Interdisciplinary Studies Program for specific topics (http://www.isgp.ubc.ca).

name: Beginners' Italian I
description: Introduction to the essentials of Italian vocabulary, expressions, grammar and cultural life. Focus on listening, reading, speaking and writing skills in everyday situations in the present tense. Aligned with CEFR level A1 objectives. Credits will be only granted for ITAL_V 103 or both ITAL_V 101, ITAL_V 102.

name: Elementary Italian I
description: Introduction to complex language structures used to communicate in a variety of situations by using different tenses and modes. Enhanced ability to comprehend, interact and express wishes or feelings in common personal and social contexts. Aligned with CEFR level A2 objectives. Recommended pre-requisite: ITAL 102 or successful completion of CEFR Level A1.

name: Italian for Singers
description: The study of the Italian language with the study of Italian lyric diction and musical culture; practice in translation, phonetic transcription and the performance of vocal music. Recommended pre-requisite: ITAL 101.

name: Elementary Italian II
description: Expansion of fundamental notions and presentation of elaborate structures, present, past and future tenses and different modes. Enriched opportunities to explore Italian culture and develop intercultural skills. Aligned with CEFR level A2 objectives. Recommended pre-requisite: ITAL 201.

name: Interdisciplinary Honours Thesis
description: Original research work under the guidance of a faculty member. Registration by approval of the Integrated Sciences Director.

name: Comparative Field Research Course: Systems Approaches to Regional Sustainability
description: Systems science approaches encompassing geological, hydrological, ecological, atmospheric sciences, and energy systems to investigate, analyze and research two unique regions of the world. Course location may vary; course location must be different than ISCI 361; fee payable prior to field course. Prerequisite: ISCI 361.

name: Intensive Beginners' Italian
description: Fundamentals of the Italian language. Aligned with CEFR level A1 objectives. Recommended: Expertise in another Romance language. Credit will be granted for ITAL 103 or both ITAL 101, ITAL 102. Prerequisite: Language placement test.

name: Intermediate Italian I
description: Advanced grammar structures in context, lexical repertoire and cultural elements to further increase learners' ability to communicate in most situations, including complex conversations. Aligned with CEFR level B1 objectives. Recommended pre-requisites: Second-year standing or higher and one of ITAL 202, ITAL 203, ITAL 206, or successful completion of CEFR level A2.

name: Beginners' Italian II
description: Continuation of foundational elements of Italian language. Development of listening, reading, speaking and writing skills in the context of everyday situations in the present and past tenses. Aligned with CEFR level A1 objectives. Credits will be only granted for ITAL_V 103 or both ITAL_V 101, ITAL_V 102. Recommended prerequisite: ITAL_V 101.

name: Integrated Sciences Graduating Seminar
description: Reflection of Integrated Sciences degree experience, development of professional skills, and a showcase of degree integrations to the community. Pass/Fail. Prerequisite: Fourth-year standing in the Integrated Sciences specialization.
prerequisites: Fourth-year standing in the Integrated Sciences specialization

name: Co-operative Work Placement III
description: Industrial or academic work experience for a minimum of 4 months. Technical report required. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-op Program in ISP. Prerequisite: ISCI 399.

name: Non-Animal Methods in Biomedical Science
description: Interdisciplinary non-animal methods (e.g., organoids, organ-on-a-chip, 3D bioprinting) for research, testing, and education; the regulatory landscape. Prerequisite: Third-year standing.

name: Student Directed Seminars
description: Self-directed, collaborative studies, in a group-learning environment, initiated and coordinated by senior undergraduate students with the supervision of a faculty advisor. Course structure, enrolment and delivery methods will comply with the Handbook for Student Directed Seminars. Prerequisite: Third-year standing in the Faculty of Science.
prerequisites: Third-year standing in the Faculty of Science

name: Ethical Issues in Science
description: Theoretical and practical consideration of ethics in the practice, reporting, public impact and accountability of science. Prerequisite: Third-year standing in any faculty.

name: Directed Studies
description: Permission of the Director is required.

name: Conversational Italian for Elementary Learners
description: Develop oral and intercultural proficiency while reviewing fundamental grammar structures and expanding vocabulary. Communicate to explore Italian culture. Aligned with CEFR level A2 objectives. Recommended pre-requisite: ITAL 201.

name: Discourse Analysis in Education Research
description: Pass/Fail. Permission of instructor required.

name: Qualitative Research Interviewing in Education: Theories and Methods
Models in Science
description: Meaning, nature, use, strengths and limitations of models as investigative tools in all scientific disciplines. Detailed investigation of selected model systems from different scientific disciplines. Priority to students in the Integrated Sciences Program. Prerequisite: Third-year standing in the Faculty of Science.
prerequisites: Third-year standing in the Faculty of Science

name: Environmental Fluid Mechanics
description: Governing equations for incompressible, non-rotating flows of variable density; equations of motion for stratified fluids; selective withdrawal; flow over topography; estuarine and exchange flows; hydrodynamic stability.

name: Chemical and Biological Industrial Water Treatment Design
description: Fundamental principles of process design for chemical and biological systems to treat water used in and effluents generated from industrial processes. Industry application examples: mining, oil sands, oil and gas, pulp and paper, agriculture, food and beverage.

name: Water Resources Systems Planning and Management
description: Art and science of modelling for integrated water resources planning and management; practice of developing and deploying simulation and optimization models to solve water problems; risk informed decision making frameworks and stakeholder processes for analysis of water resources systems.

name: Analyzing Discourse and Talk: An Overview of Methods
description: Credit will be granted for only one of LLED 501 or EPSE 586. Equivalency: EPSE586

name: Engineering Hydrology
description: Water cycle and role of water in the environment and environmental engineering. Physical and statistical prediction methods for design related to hydrologic systems; precipitation; evaporation; snow hydrology; infiltration and base flow; surface runoff; channel and storage routing; unit hydrograph methods.

name: Analyzing Discourse in Education: Descriptive and Critical Approaches
description: Credit will be granted for only one of LLED 502 or EPSE 587. Equivalency: EPSE587

name: Water and Wastewater Management Strategies
description: Chemical and microbiological quality and contaminations, techniques and analytical procedures for assessing and monitoring chemical and microbiological water quality; water and wastewater quality standards, pollution prevention strategies and policies; risk analysis; asset management.

name: Teacher Action Research in Language and Literacy Education
description: Taught in French. Understanding of the literature and methods associated with teacher (action) research in language and literacy.

name: Co-Operative Work Placement IV
description: Industrial or academic work experience for a minimum of 4 months. Technical report required. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-op Program in ISP. Prerequisite: ISCI 498.

name: Theory and Research in Teaching Written Composition
Theory and Research in Teaching of Modern Languages
Theory and Research in Drama in Education
Supervised Study in Modern Languages Education
Child Language in Education
description: Language development in preschool and early school years: influence in education, heritage language, English as an Additional Language and multilingual contexts for development are explored across multiple theoretical approaches.

name: Drama, Literacies and Literature in Education
Introduction to Research in the Teaching of Literature
Theoretical Foundations of ESL/EL Reading Pedagogy
Introduction to Literacies Across the Lifespan: Theories and Practices
Second Language Assessment: Conceptual and Empirical Approaches
MATERIALS DEVELOPMENT FOR INDIGENOUS LANGUAGE LEARNING & TEACHING
description: Conceptual understanding and practical experience in designing and developing language print materials and interactive multimedia. Overview of production, publication, dissemination, and accessibility of language resources, and pedagogical approaches for language revitalization and education efforts using multimodal resources.

name: Asia-Pacific Narratives as Inquiry on Intercultural Aspects of Language Education
Assessment in Reading and Other Language Arts
Critical Intercultural Studies in Language Education
Theories and Perspectives in Teaching Literature
Practicum in Teaching English as a Second Language
Theory and Practice in Reading Instruction
description: Credit may be obtained for only one of LLED 310, 391, 300.

name: Theoretical Foundations of Reading Research and Practice
Supervision of Reading
description: Curriculum analysis and planning. Implications for the administrator, the consultant and supervisor of reading.

name: Theory and Research in Early Literacy
Family and Community Literacy: Issues and Perspectives
description: Literacy learning, teaching, policy and research across the lifespan.

name: Using Canadian Children's Literature in the French Education Classroom
description: Taught in French. Credit will be given for one of LLED 440, LLED 420.

name: Applied Linguistics for Teachers of French
Language Assessment in the French as a Second/Additional Language Classroom
Physical Activity and Disability
description: Physical activity counselling, education programming principles, exercise considerations, and strategies for promoting inclusive physical activity for people with disabilities.

name: Drama in Education: Community, Inquiry, and Performance
Gramligne: Learning and Teaching Grammar in Text for the Second Language Classroom
description: Taught in French.

name: Principles and Practice of French Program Development
description: Taught in French. The development and implementation of French Immersion, Program Cadre, and French as a Second language Programs for preschool, elementary, secondary, or adult.

name: Living Language: Science and Society
description: Multi-disciplinary course in which students, individually and in groups, examine, integrate and apply subject-specific knowledge through the lens of language and the framework of the language sciences, with a focus on themes of real-world importance. Prerequisite: Fourth-year standing or permission of the instructor. Equivalency: APSC402, ASTU402, FRST402, LFS 402, PHAR402

name: Current Topics in Exercise and Health Psychology
description: Exploring concepts, principles, and theories as they relate to the practice of promoting and supporting recommended physical activity for individuals and population groups. Particular attention will be directed at contemporary issues, controversies, evidence informed initiatives, and innovative new approaches.

name: Advanced Studies in Modern Language Education
description: Credit will be given for only 6 credits of LLED 480 and LLED 429.

name: Drama in Education: Creative Approaches and Strategies
description: Drama-based activities relevant to a wide range of classroom contexts; involves reading about, practicing, and discussing various creative drama approaches and strategies developed by contemporary scholars and practitioners.

name: Sport, Peace, and Conflict
description: Relationships that sport and leisure have with peace, conflict, and social inequality in Canada and internationally.

name: Movement Experiences for Young Children
description: The design and implementation of movement experiences for children in early childhood years.

name: Foundations of Coaching
description: Methods of athletic conditioning, planning the program, psychology of training and coaching, athletic evaluation.

name: Indigenous Sport and Physical Culture in Settler Canada
description: Historical and contemporary issues in Canada that shape Indigenous sport and physical activity, health programs, and policies.

name: Leisure Services for Persons with a Disability
description: Policy issues relating to leisure opportunities for persons with disabilities.

name: Leisure, Sport and Popular Culture
description: Selected aspects of leisure and sport examined in relation to modern social structures and cultures.

name: The Modern Olympics: Power, Politics, and Performance
description: Examination of the Modern Olympic Games as an event with important political, economic, environmental, and cultural ramifications.

name: Laboratory Investigations in Neuromechanical Kinesiology
description: Integration and application of laboratory principles and techniques for experimental investigations of topics in neuromechanical kinesiology, including biomechanics, motor behaviour, and neurophysiology.

name: Drama in Education: Cross-Curricular Learning and Story
Medical Aspects of Sport and Exercise
description: Training and safety strategies for the management and prevention of disorders of internal organs and central nervous system. Topics include environmental and nutritional factors in conditioning and pre-event preparation.

name: Interdisciplinary Seminar
description: Critical analysis of recent scientific literature that combines disciplines that students are integrating in their Integrated Sciences Curriculum.

name: Research Development Project
description: Retreat to develop skills in writing scientific research proposals. Emphasis on formulating and testing hypotheses to explain observations. Course location will vary; fee payable prior to retreat. Prerequisite: Third-year standing in the Faculty of Science.
prerequisites: Third-year standing in the Faculty of Science

name: Sensori-motor Neuroplasticity in Movement and Exercise
description: Concepts in neuroplasticity related to sensori-motor control of movement and exercise. The focus will be on plasticity (both adaptive and maladaptive) that arises because of either training or injury/non-use as it relates to movement control and exercise.

name: Integrative Bioinformatics
description: Storage and processing of information in biological systems. Computational methods for recovering and interpreting stored genetic information. Priority to students in the Integrated Sciences Program. Prerequisite: Third-year standing in the Faculty of Science.
prerequisites: Third-year standing in the Faculty of Science

name: Sensori-Motor Control of Human Balance
description: Examining the sensory, motor, and biomechanical factors that contribute to human balance control during quiet standing and postural reactions to internal and external perturbations. Emphasis on understanding the characteristics of healthy balance control and changes associated with age and disease.

name: Darwinian Medicine
description: Using the Darwinian theory of natural selection to explore explanations of infectious diseases, allergies, cancer, mental illness, and other human diseases. Priority to students in the Integrated Sciences Program. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion Lists:http://www.vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/faculty-science/bachelor-science/credit-exclusion-listsPrerequisite: Third-year standing in the Faculty of Science. Equivalency: BIOL 350
prerequisites: Third-year standing in the Faculty of Science

name: Prevention of Sports Injuries
description: Training and safety strategies for the prevention of injuries to the musculoskeletal system and sense organs.

name: Theory and Practice of Games in Economics and Evolution
description: Exploration of human and animal interactions: integrating evolutionary and economic perspectives to investigate individual and social behaviour. Credit will be granted for only one of ECON 221 or ISCI 344. Prerequisite: Third-year standing.

name: Topics in Integrated Sciences
description: Interactive examination of a theme common to all areas of science. Themes will change from year to year. Priority to students in the Integrated Sciences Program. Prerequisite: Third-year standing in the Faculty of Science
prerequisites: Third-year standing in the Faculty of Science

name: Neuroanatomy of Human Movement
description: Neuroanatomy of human motion in healthy and clinical populations.

name: Pipeline Design
description: Pipeline and pipeline system design reflecting technical, regulatory, environmental, societal, professional, and economic aspects; pipeline design project.

name: Co-operative Work Placement I
description: Industrial or academic work experience for a minimum of 4 months. Normally taken in Winter Session of third year or Summer Session after third year. Technical report required. Restricted to students in the ISP Co-op program. Prerequisite: One term in ISP.

name: The Size of Things
description: Scaling as a general approach to laws governing the geometry, kinematics and dynamics of systems. Dimensional analysis, isometry and allometry applied to topics from Biology, Physics, Earth Science and Economics. Priority to students in the Integrated Sciences Program. Prerequisite: Third-year standing in the Faculty of Science.
prerequisites: Third-year standing in the Faculty of Science

name: Picturebooks and Literacy Development
description: Explore, analyze and critique recent developments in picturebooks, ways of engaging with these texts and bridging picturebook forms and innovations with theories of literacy development in children.

name: Symmetry
description: Recognizing symmetry; point groups in 2D and 3D; plane groups in 2D; space groups in 3D; the role of symmetry in the natural and human world. Prerequisite: Third-year standing in the Faculty of Science.
prerequisites: Third-year standing in the Faculty of Science

name: Science of Measurement and Instrumentation
description: Interactive course integrating diverse aspects of science: semi-quantitative overview of physical principles underlying modern measurement technology; philosophy of measurement; accuracy and limits to measurement, and resultant scientific, sociological and economic consequences. Priority to students in the Integrated Sciences Program. Prerequisite: Third-year standing in the Faculty of Science.
prerequisites: Third-year standing in the Faculty of Science

name: Systems Approaches to Regional Sustainability
description: Application of systems science encompassing geological, hydrological, ecological, atmospheric sciences, and energy systems approaches to study regional sustainability. Prerequisite: Third-year or higher standing in the Faculty of Science.
prerequisites: Third-year or higher standing in the Faculty of Science

name: Field Course: Systems Approaches to Regional Sustainability
description: Systems science approaches encompassing geological, hydrological, ecological, atmospheric sciences, and energy systems to investigate a selected region of the world. Course location will vary; fee payable prior to field course.

name: Co-operative Work Placement II
description: Industrial or academic work experience for a minimum of 4 months. Technical report required. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-op Program in ISP. Prerequisite: ISCI 398.

name: Why the Big Brain? The Evolution of Human Cognition
description: Evolutionary causes, consequences and constraints of human cognition; enhanced encephalization and mentalizing capabilities throughout the Primate Order, and the emergence of cognitive faculties that define the human species. Prerequisite: Third-year or higher standing in the Faculty of Science.
prerequisites: Third-year or higher standing in the Faculty of Science

name: Practicum in Assessment in Reading and Other Language Arts
description: Pass/Fail.

name: Special Course in Subject Matter Field
description: Courses in various subject matter fields designed to bring teachers up to date in recent findings in each field.

name: Graduating PROJECT
description: Demonstration of students' theoretical and applied knowledge as acquired during their M.Ed. program. Pass/Fail.

name: Research in Language Curriculum: Social Practice Perspectives
Theory and Research in English Language Education: Discourse Perspectives
Problems in Education
description: Investigation and report of a problem.

name: Theory and Research in Teaching English as a Second Language
Culture and Politics in Second Language Education
Theory and Research in Teaching Second Language Writing
Topics in Philosophy of Law and Theoretical Perspectives
description: Not offered each year, consult Faculty.

name: Marine Resources Law
description: Legal regimes governing the protection and exploitation of ocean resources. Not offered each year, consult Faculty.

name: International Human Rights
description: The recognition and protection of human rights in international law. Not offered each year, consult Faculty.

name: Legal History
description: The relationship between law, society and historical change, normally emphasizing 19th and 20th century issues. Not offered each year, consult Faculty.

name: Economic Analysis of Law
description: Economic analysis used to explore, describe, evaluate and offer prescriptive suggestions for legal decision-making. Not offered each year, consult Faculty.

name: Law of Armed Conflict
description: The legal basis for armed conflict or military operations; the rights and obligations of combatants and civilians in a region of armed conflict; war crimes.

name: Field Experiences
description: For those on master's, doctoral, and diploma programs.

name: Topics in Legal History
description: Not offered each year, consult Faculty.

name: Indigenous Peoples in Comparative and International Law
description: The legal situation of indigenous peoples in various states and in modern international law. Not offered each year, consult Faculty.

name: International Law
description: The history, sources and evidence of international law and its relation to municipal law; international personality; state jurisdiction; and treaties. Credit will be granted for only one of LAW 316 or POLI 376.

name: International Commercial Disputes
description: International commercial arbitration and other means for resolving legal disputes relating to international commercial transactions. Not offered each year, consult Faculty.

name: Conflict of Laws
description: A study of the private legal problems arising in cases in which the relevant facts cut across provincial or national boundaries. Recommended to be taken in third year. Credit will only be granted for one of LAW 325 or LAW 592.

name: International Business Transactions
description: Legal problems in international financial and commercial transactions. Not offered each year, consult Faculty.

name: Topics in International Law and Transactions
description: Not offered each year, consult Faculty.

name: Introduction to Asian Legal Systems
description: Introduction to the comparative study of legal systems of East and South-East Asia, including those of China and Japan.

name: Property Law and Theory
description: The idea of property, its origins, its justifications, its uses, its effects, and the rules that surround and create it.

name: Maritime Law
description: Canadian maritime law and admiralty practice.

name: International Law Problems
description: Selected issues in international law. Not offered each year, consult Faculty.

name: Cultural Law
description: Relationship of law to cultural activities and phenomena. International, national, and indigenous laws as they apply to various forms of tangible and intangible cultural expression.

name: Japanese Law
description: Constitutional foundation and protection of human rights under Japanese law.

name: International Environmental Law
description: Customary international law and treaties relating to the environment; institutional structures. Not offered each year, consult Faculty.

name: Innovation, Law, and Regulation
description: Examines and applies interdisciplinary research on regulation, governance, and institutional and legal design under conditions of change and uncertainty.

name: European Union Law
description: The legal system of the European Union as created by the treaties establishing the Union and by the Union's institutions. Not offered each year, consult Faculty.

name: Intensive Seminar I
description: Honours/Pass/Fail grading.

name: International Trade Law
description: Rules and regulatory systems that govern the international movement of capital, goods and services.

name: Topics in Public Law - Seminar
description: Not offered each year, consult Faculty. Credit will only be granted for one of LAW 343 or LAW 543.

name: Chinese Law: Implications for Canada-China Relations
description: Overview of the laws and legal system in the People's Republic of China with some introduction to Taiwan law. Legal interpretation of implications for Canada-China relations.

name: Human Motor Behaviour I
description: Processes underlying human movement and learning motor skills and factors influencing acquisition, performance, and movement control.  Prerequisite: All of KIN 110, KIN 131.

name: Comparative Law
description: Basic theory of comparative law and the differences between the civil law tradition and the common law tradition.

name: Topics in Comparative Law
description: Not offered each year, consult Faculty.

name: Human Rights in Asia
description: Legal issues relating to civil, political, social and cultural rights in particular areas in Asia. Not offered each year, consult Faculty.

name: Topics in Public Law - Lecture
description: Not offered each year, consult Faculty.

name: Biomechanical Properties of Tissues
description: Mechanics of muscular contraction and how the mechanical properties of the muscle, ligaments, tendons, and bone work synergistically.  Prerequisite: All of KIN 110, KIN 131, KIN 211, KIN 216.

name: Introduction to Statistics in Kinesiology
description: Basic concepts and principles of descriptive and inferential statistics, and distribution-free statistical techniques. Please consult the School of Kinesiology Credit Exclusion Lists:https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/faculty-science/bachelor-science/credit-exclusion-lists Prerequisite: Second-year standing or higher.

name: Biomechanics I
description: Application of elementary principles of physics and math to a quantitative analysis of movement. Analysis will also focus on the development of forces within muscles and their effect on initiating and controlling human movement.  Prerequisite: All of KIN 110, KIN 131.

name: Human Functional Musculoskeletal Anatomy
description: The musculoskeletal structures and neural innervations involved in the control of human movement. Attention will be given to the practical application of human anatomy as it pertains to clinical, athletic, or everyday situations. Prerequisite: Third-year standing. Restricted to students in the BHK and BKIN programs.

name: Human Athletic Performance
description: An exploration of human movement and related issues pertaining to sports and athletic performance. Restricted to non-B.Kin. students only. Not for credit in the B.Kin. Program. Prerequisite: Second-year standing.

name: Research Methods in Kinesiology
description: Critical evaluation of research studies and methods with emphasis on the physical activity context. Please consult the School of Kinesiology Credit Exclusion Lists:https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/faculty-science/bachelor-science/credit-exclusion-lists Prerequisite: Second-year standing or higher.

name: Basic Korean Grammar
description: Emphasis on grammar, writing, and reading. For heritage learners and students with prior background in spoken Korean.

name: Exercise Testing and Prescription
description: Conditioning methods, exercise techniques and appraisal methods for fitness in physical activity and sport.  Prerequisite: All of KIN 110, KIN 120, KIN 205, KIN 206.

name: Nutrition, Physical Activity, and Health
description: Study of nutrition and its application to physical activity and health. Macro- and micronutrient classification and recommended daily intakes, their digestion, functions in the body and their role in supporting physical activity and health will be discussed.  Prerequisite: All of KIN 131, KIN 132.

name: Intermediate Korean II
description: Continuation of KORN 201. Credit will be granted for only one of KORN 202 or KORN 200. Recommended pre-requisite: KORN 201.

name: Health Policy and Society
description: Health policy and the social context in relation to active health.  Prerequisite: KIN 160.

name: Exercise Physiology I
description: Acute and chronic effects of exercise on body systems; basic concepts of cardiovascular, respiratory and muscular responses to physical activity.  Prerequisite: All of KIN 110, KIN 120, KIN 131, KIN 132.

name: Sensorimotor Control of Human Movement
description: Processes and mechanisms involved in the sensory, perceptual, and cognitive contributions to human movements.  Prerequisite: All of KIN 110, KIN 131, KIN 211, KIN 216.

name: Readings in Korean Topics
description: Readings in intermediate-level Korean on aspects of Korean culture, customs, and contemporary life, along with structured conversations based on those readings. As of 2011W, credit will be granted for only one of KORN 301/302 or KORN 300. Recommended pre-requisites: one of KORN 200, KORN 202.

name: Neuromuscular Integration of Human Movement
description: The neurophysiological and functional neuroanatomical processes involved in the sensory and motor control of movement, posture and balance in the human. Peripheral and central sensorimotor structures, and neurological diseases that affect human movement and balance control will be discussed.  Prerequisite: All of KIN 110, KIN 131.

name: Creating Effective, Developmentally Appropriate, Physical Activity Learning Environments
description: The pedagogical skills and knowledge required to design, and implement, developmentally appropriate physical activities learning environments in a variety of settings.  Prerequisite: One of KIN 140.

name: Advanced Applications of Exercise Physiology
description: Explore how the cardiovascular and respiratory systems are regulated and integrated during exercise.  Prerequisite: All of KIN 110, KIN 120, KIN 131, KIN 132, KIN 235.

name: Intermediate Korean I
description: Reading and writing of modern colloquial Korean at an intermediate level. Credit will be granted for only one of KORN 201 or KORN 200. Recommended pre-requisite: KORN 101.

name: Readings in Korean Topics II
description: Continuation of KORN 301. As of 2011W, credit will be granted for only one of KORN 301/302 or KORN 300. Recommended pre-requisite: KORN 301 or permission of instructor.

name: Readings in Korean Topics I
description: Readings in intermediate-level Korean on aspects of Korean culture, customs, and contemporary life, along with structured conversations based on those readings. As of 2011W, credit will be granted for only one of KORN 301/302 or KORN 300. Recommended pre-requisite: KORN 202 or permission of instructor.

name: Enriched Summer Intensive Beginning
description: An integrated language course developing communicative competence in speaking, listening to, reading, and writing modern Korean.

name: Introduction to Hancha: Sinographs and Sino-Korean Vocabulary II
description: Continuation of KORN 351. Students learn an additional 250 sinographs and related sinographic vocabulary. Prerequisite: KORN 351. or placement approval.

name: Intermediate Korean
description: Reading and writing of modern colloquial Korean at an intermediate level. As of 2011W, credit will be granted for only one of KORN 201/202 or KORN 200. Recommended pre-requisites: one of KORN 101, KORN 102.

name: Introduction to Hancha: Sinographs and Sino-Korean Vocabulary I
description: Chinese characters in their Korean pronunciations and shapes. Students learn approximately 250 sinographs, related sinographic vocabulary, and do structured readings in mixed scripts on aspects of Korean culture and contemporary life. Prerequisite: One of KORN 200, KORN 202. or placement approval.

name: Korean Conversation and Composition
description: Structured conversation practice and weekly composition assignments based on viewing one designated Korean television program per week. Recommended pre-requisite: KORN 300.

name: Korean-to-English Translation
description: Translation into English of Korean writing in various literary genres, including short story, poetry, personal essay, and academic essay. Supplementary readings in translation studies and translation theory.

name: Modern Korean Short Fiction
description: Reading and translating twentieth-century Korean short fiction. Recommended pre-requisites: either (a) KORN 300 or (b) all of KORN 301, KORN 302.

name: Readings in Middle and Early Modern Korean
description: History and structure of the Korean language through targeted close readings in different editions of an illustrated text from the 15th and 18th centuries. Prerequisite: Non-heritage speakers should have completed KORN 410 or be taking it concurrently. Heritage and native speakers of Korean welcome.

name: Newspaper Japanese I
description: Developing fluency in reading contemporary Japanese newspapers; concentration on current and emerging vocabulary, evolving grammatical features, and style of presentation. Credit will be granted for only one of JAPN 456 or JAPN 416. Recommended pre-requisites: one of JAPN 301, JAPN 401 and one of JAPN 302, JAPN 402, JAPN 314, JAPN 424.

name: Readings in Modern Japanese Literature
description: An advanced course in the reading and analysis of literary texts in modern Japanese. Advanced conversation, translation into English and practice in the use of standard reference tools as preparation for advanced research in Japanese. Credit will be granted for only one of JAPN 453 or JAPN 408. Recommended pre-requisites: one of JAPN 301, JAPN 401.

name: Advanced Readings in Korean Non-Fiction
description: Guided readings on contemporary affairs from the Korean press and/or selected readings in Korean academic prose. Recommended pre-requisite: KORN 300.

name: Supervised Study in the Japanese Language
description: Primarily for graduate students. Credit will be granted for only one of JAPN 470 or JAPN 440.

name: Japanese Media and Translation
description: Emphasizing the development of translingual and transcultural literacies in Japanese popular media with a primary focus on film. This course is recommended for students with credit for JAPN_V 401 and JAPN_V 402, or placement with native or near-native proficiency in Japanese.

name: Topics in Japanese Language, Culture, and Society
description: Advanced Japanese language course combined with analysis of various media in literary, journalistic, and popular genres drawn from history, sociology, cultural studies, etc. Practice in the use of standard reference tools prepares students for independent research in Japanese. Students are recommended to complete JAPN 403 prior to JAPN 459. Credit will be granted for only one of JAPN 459 or JAPN 419. Recommended pre-requisites: one of JAPN 301, JAPN 401; and permission from instructor.

name: Grammatical Analysis of Japanese II
description: A continuation of JAPN 460. Credit will be granted for only one of JAPN 461 or JAPN 421. Recommended pre-requisites: one of JAPN 420, JAPN 460.

name: Newspaper Japanese II
description: A continuation of JAPN 456. Credit will be granted for only one of JAPN 457 or JAPN 417. Recommended pre-requisites: one of JAPN 416, JAPN 456.

name: New Media and Society
description: Development of new media technologies, their applications, and their cultural, political, and social impacts.

name: Antisemitism and the Jewish Experience
description: Examines antisemitism, discrimination against or hostility towards Jews. Impacts of antisemitism on Jews and the development of Judaism from antiquity to the present.

name: Grammatical Analysis of Japanese I
description: Analysis of the grammatical structure of modern Japanese. Contrastive analysis of Japanese and English as well as error analysis. Credit will be granted for only one of JAPN 460 or JAPN 420. Recommended pre-requisites: one of JAPN 301, JAPN 401 and one of JAPN 303, JAPN 403.

name: Tutorial in Japanese for Honours Students
description: This course will require the presentation of at least one research paper. Credit will be granted for only one of JAPN 472 or JAPN 442.

name: Italian Language and Literature
description: A maximum of 6 credits is available in any one topic.

name: Journalism Here and Now
description: Examines the technologies and trends that are changing the profession of journalism. Explore the dynamic, changing, and sometimes problematic world of journalism through critical analysis and creating works of journalism.

name: Researching Modern Japanese Religions
description: Research tools and approaches to the interdisciplinary study of modern Japanese religions (nineteenth century to the present) including state-of-the-field works in English, and locating primary and secondary materials in Japanese. Credit will be granted for only one of JAPN 462 or JAPN 452. Prerequisite: 6 credits of 200- or 300-level courses in Asian religions; 3 credit writing-intensive course in Asian Studies; ability to read modern Japanese or 18 credits of Japanese language courses and permission of instructor.

name: Multimedia Journalism
description: Principles of multimedia storytelling with hands-on journalistic methods in information gathering, fact-checking, and ethical decision making. Prerequisite: One of JRNL 200, JRNL 201.

name: Intensive Beginning Japanese I
description: An introduction to modern spoken and written Japanese with emphasis on both form (grammar and syntax) and functions. Offered in Term 1. Not available for credit to students with JAPN 12. Students are recommended to complete JAPN 160 and 260 in the same year. Credit will be granted for only one of JAPN 160 or JAPN 150 or both JAPN 100, JAPN 101.

name: Intermediate Japanese I A
description: Integrated coverage of topics on culture and cross-cultural communication designed to develop competencies in speaking, listening, reading, and writing. It is strongly recommended that JAPN 320 and JAPN 321 be taken in the same year. Credit will be granted for only one of JAPN 320 or JAPN 210 or JAPN 360. Recommended pre-requisites: one of JAPN 103, JAPN 151, JAPN 201, JAPN 260.

name: Beginning Japanese IA
description: An introduction to modern spoken and written Japanese with emphasis on both form (grammar and syntax) and functions (Non-intensive). Not available for credit to students with JAPN 11 and/or JAPN 12. Credit will be granted for only one of JAPN 100 or JAPN 160.

name: Introduction to News Audiences
description: The evolution of news audiences and their relationships with journalists. Examines different approaches to audience engagement and various forms of such engagement.

name: Beginning Japanese IB
description: Continuation of JAPN 100 (Non-intensive). Not available for credit to students with JAPN 12. Credit will be granted for only one of JAPN 101 or JAPN 160. Recommended pre-requisite: JAPN 100.

name: Intermediate Japanese I B
description: Continuation of JAPN 320. It is strongly recommended that JAPN 320 and JAPN 321 be taken in the same year. Credit will be granted for only one of JAPN 321 or JAPN 211 or JAPN 360. Recommended pre-requisites: one of JAPN 210, JAPN 320.

name: Basic Japanese Grammar
description: Emphasis on grammar, writing and reading Intended for students with a background in spoken Japanese. Credit will be granted for only one of JAPN 204 or JAPN 104.

name: Intensive Beginning Japanese II
description: Continuation of JAPN 160. Offered in Term 2. Students are recommended to complete JAPN 160 and 260 in the same year. Credit will be granted for only one of JAPN 260 or JAPN 151 or both JAPN 102, JAPN 103 or both JAPN 200, JAPN 201. Recommended pre-requisites: one of JAPN 101, JAPN 150, JAPN 160.

name: Law, Society and State
description: Theories of the relationship between the legal system, social relations and the state. Not offered each year, consult Faculty.

name: Torts
description: A study of the bases of civil liability for intentionally and accidentally caused harms.

name: Beginning Japanese II B
description: Continuation of JAPN 200 (Non-intensive). Credit will be granted for only one of JAPN 201 or JAPN 103 or JAPN 260. Recommended pre-requisites: one of JAPN 102, JAPN 200.

name: Aboriginal and Treaty Rights
description: An overview of the unique constitutional status and rights of Aboriginal Peoples in Canada.

name: Beginning Japanese II A
description: Continuation of JAPN 101 (Non-intensive). Credit will be granted for only one of JAPN 200 or JAPN 102 or JAPN 260. Recommended pre-requisite: one of JAPN 101, JAPN 150, JAPN 160.

name: Enriched Summer Intensive Beginning Japanese
description: An integrated language course developing communicative competence in speaking, listening to, reading, and writing modern Japanese. Credit will be granted for only one of JAPN 261 or JAPN 161.

name: Transnational Law
description: Introduction to principles of public and private international law and research methods for international legal materials.

name: Public Law
description: An overview of the constitutional and statutory law governing the legislative, executive, and judicial branches of government in Canada, including an introduction to statutory construction and analysis and the administration of law in Canada.

name: Legal Research and Writing
description: Introduction to legal research and writing skills and the use of legal databases.

name: Fundamental Concepts of Law
description: A study of some of the fundamental principles and ideas that cut across many areas of the substantive law, including such concepts as fault, intent, legal personality, possession, ownership, justice, and causation. Not offered each year, consult Faculty.

name: Feminist Legal Theory
description: Recent developments in feminist legal theory. Not offered each year, consult Faculty.

name: Intermediate Japanese II A
description: It is strongly recommended that students plan to complete both JAPN 322 and JAPN 323 within one year. Credit will be granted for only one of JAPN 322 or JAPN 212 or JAPN 361. Recommended pre-requisites: one of JAPN 211, JAPN 250, JAPN 321, JAPN 360.

name: Philosophy of Law
description: An examination of the principal schools of legal theory, such as legal positivism, legal realism, sociological jurisprudence, and contemporary rights theory. Not offered each year, consult Faculty.

name: Corporate Social Responsibility and the Law
Legal Traditions and Ideas of Law
description: Historical and comparative study of the evolution of legal systems from custom and proto law emphasizing influences and sharing ideas among traditions of the Ancient Near East, Athens, Roman Empire, Western Europe and China. Not offered each year, consult Faculty.

name: Women, Law and Social Change
description: A survey of feminist approaches to law, with reference to selected substantive areas of the law.

name: Introduction to Public Law and the Charter
description: An introduction to the structure, powers, duties of and relationships among the various institutions and actors that comprise the Canadian state, the principles of statutory interpretation, and the Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms.

name: Scholarly Writing and Argumentation in Land and Food Systems
description: Communicating concepts of food systems and links to human and environmental health through writing, elements of argumentation, evaluating evidence, and searching for and citing references to back up claims; small-class experience. Enrolment limited to LFS students with first year status. Credit will be granted for only one of NRES_V 150, FRST_V 150, or LFS_V 150. Equivalency: FRST_V 150, NRES_V 150.

name: International Field Studies in Policy Analysis for Agriculture and Natural Resources
description: Field studies carried out abroad under the direction of the instructor. Students will be guided to apply selected tools for analysis of agricultural and natural resource policy in developing countries with input from local policymakers. Participating students are assessed a fee. Prerequisite: One of ECON 101, LFS 101. Third-year standing and permission of instructor. 9 credits of upper level ECON, FRE or COMM courses are strongly recommended.

name: Land One: First-year Integrative Seminar
description: Current issues and cases in Forestry and Land and Food Systems are examined with a focus on integration of first-year subjects and exposure to both Indigenous and Western perspectives. Restricted to Faculty of Land and Food Systems students in the Land One option. Equivalency: FRST 110

name: Topics in Feminist Legal Studies
description: Not offered each year, consult Faculty.

name: Land, Food and Community I: Introduction to Food Systems and Sustainability
description: Managed systems and concepts of sustainability; economic, ecological and social components; managed landscapes, agri-food systems, and communities; urban and rural systems; the land, food, nutrition and human health continuum.

name: Supervised Study in the Korean Language
description: Seminar in Korean-to-English literary translation. Primarily for, but not limited to, students in Asian Studies and Linguistics. Recommended pre-requisite: KORN 410 or placement exam.

name: First Nations Health and the Traditional Role of Plants
description: This Interprofessional Health and Human Service (IHHS) course covers the First Nations medical systems and medicinal plants. Bridging the traditional with modern sciences. Credit will be granted for only one of LFS 340 or IHHS 301.

name: Introduction to Land, Food and Community
description: Orientation to the programs, learning environment and core values of the Faculty of Land and Food Systems; career programs; survey of professional opportunities and requirements.

name: Aquaculture Field Studies
description: An orientation to the aquaculture system in BC. Participating students are assessed a fee.

name: Co-operative Work Placement I
description: Work experience in relevant private and/or public sector settings. Work terms are normally four months long. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-op Program in Land and Food Systems. Pass/Fail. Prerequisite: Must attend all Co-op pre-employment workshops.

name: Jurisprudence and Critical Perspectives
description: Introduction to the basic principles of legal theory and critical perspectives on law.

name: Land, Food, and Community II: Principles and Practice of Community Food Security
description: Project-based application of the principles and processes of community food security. Emphasis on developing skills required to address economic, ecological, social, and technological components of managed landscapes, agri-food systems, and communities comprising the land, food, nutrition and health continuum. Prerequisite: LFS 250.

name: International Field Studies
description: Field studies carried out abroad under staff direction. Participating students are assessed a fee.

name: Co-operative Work Placement II
description: Work experience in relevant private and/or public sector settings. Work terms are normally four months long. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-op Program in Land and Food Systems. Pass/Fail. Prerequisite: LFS 398.

name: Land, Food, and Community: Quantitative Data Analysis
description: Introduction to tools needed for data analysis of the economic, ecological, health, and scientific components of land and food systems. Prerequisite: One of MATH 100, MATH 102, MATH 104, MATH 110, MATH 120, MATH 180, MATH 184.

name: Critical Analysis of Issues and Methodology in Language and Literacy Education
description: Prerequisite: Admission to the Ph.D. program in LLED.
prerequisites: Admission to the Ph.D. program in LLED

name: Theories for Language and Literacy Research
description: Prerequisite: Admission to the Ph.D. program in LLED.
prerequisites: Admission to the Ph.D. program in LLED

name: Principles of Microeconomics with Applications to Land and Food Systems
description: Microeconomic principles focused on private and social decision making related to the use of land, especially in agriculture, forestry, and conservation. Restricted to Faculty of Land and Food Systems students in Land One Option. Credit will be granted for only one of FRST 101, LFS 101, ECON 101, or ECON 310 Equivalency: FRST 101, ECON 101

name: Beginning Latin I
description: Classical Latin, Part I.

name: Beginning Latin II
description: Classical Latin, Part II. Prerequisite: LATN 101.

name: Advanced Latin: Readings
description: Readings in Latin. Prerequisite: One of LATN _V 301, LATN _V 202, LATN _V 200.

name: Audio Storytelling
description: Adopts a journalistic framework to communicate powerful stories and present academic content in new ways through the use of audio and podcasting technology. Prerequisite: Third-year standing or higher.

name: Master's Thesis
description: This course is restricted to students in Language and Literacy Education (LLED) MA programs.

name: Intermediate Latin II: Beginning Reading
description: Completion of the grammatical foundations of classical Latin, Part II; an introduction to the reading of unadapted passages of Latin literature and discussion of their cultural contexts. Credit will be granted for only one of LATN_V 202 or LATN _V 301. Pre-requisites: LATN _V 201. Equivalency: LATN _V 202.

name: Introduction to Latin American Studies
description: An overview of the culture and society of Latin America from ancient to contemporary times and from Argentina to Mexico.

name: Seminar in Latin American Studies
description: Topics will vary from year to year. Consult the program website (https://las.arts.ubc.ca/all-courses/) for further details./ Prerequisite: One of LAST 100, LAST 201, LAST 205, LAST 301, LAST 303, LAST 315.

name: Popular Culture in Latin America
description: The culture of everyday life, both rural and urban: issues of identity, popular memory, resistance, negotiation, as expressed through ritual, crafts, the body, social movements, films, music, and literature.

name: Issues of Development in Modern Latin America
description: Theory of development in the Latin American context: current problems and development alternatives.

name: Human and Civil Rights in Latin America
description: Focuses on human rights movements; state violence and impunity; reform of criminal justice systems; rights of indigenous peoples, women, and minorities; international protection of human rights; the UN and inter-American systems.

name: Intermediate Latin I
description: Completion of the grammatical foundations of classical Latin, Part I. Prerequisite: LATN 102.

name: Studies in Latin Prose and Verse
description: Thematic studies using both Latin prose and Latin verse. A maximum of 12 credits can be granted for either one of or any combination of LATN 403, LATN 503. Prerequisite: One of LATN 350, LATN 351.

name: Studies in Latin Prose and Verse
description: Advanced thematic studies using both Latin prose and Latin verse. A maximum of 12 credits can be granted for either one of or any combination of LATN 403, LATN 503.

name: Criminal Law and Procedure
description: Bases of criminal responsibility; principles and objectives of the criminal law and procedure; pre-trial procedure.

name: Climate Justice in Latin America
description: Survey of the geographic, colonial, racialized, and gendered underpinnings and materialities of the climate crisis in Latin America.

name: Advocacy
description: Introduction to principles of written and oral advocacy. Pass/Fail.

name: Sexuality and Law
description: Legal issues relating to sexual activity, orientation and identification. Not offered each year, consult Faculty.

name: Afro-Latin America
description: The Black experience and the diversity of the African diaspora in Latin America.

name: Indigenous Latin America
description: Historical and contemporary cultures, struggles, and experiences of Indigenous peoples in what is now Latin America. Different cultural areas or regions may be selected to illustrate the course's principal themes.

name: Topics in Race and Law
description: Not offered each year, consult Faculty.

name: Property Law
description: The legal concept of ownership and its changing nature and application, including equitable principles, the acquisition and transfer of interests, the regulation of use, Aboriginal title, and statute-based systems for registering interests in land.

name: Topics in Social Justice
description: Not offered every year; consult the Faculty.

name: Canadian Constitutional Law
description: Principles of Canadian constitutional law, including Canadian federalism, the Charter of Rights and Freedoms, and the unique constitutional status and rights of Aboriginal Peoples in Canada.

name: Women, Law and Family
description: Feminist and other critical perspectives on the relationship between unequal gender relations and laws embodying a concept of family. Not offered each year, consult Faculty.

name: Topics in Law and Social Relations
description: Not offered each year, consult Faculty.

name: Indigenous Settler Legal Relations
description: Critical examination of the history and legacy of colonial legal orders in Canada.

name: Topics in Latin American Studies
description: Topics will vary from year to year. Consult the program website (https://las.arts.ubc.ca/all-courses/) for further details.//

name: Topics in Municipal and Planning Law
description: Not offered each year, consult Faculty.

name: Administrative Law
description: Study of the external control of public actors exercising statutory authority. Introduction to general principles of procedural and substantive judicial review, delegated authority and subordinate legislation, remedies, and administrative processes. Credit will be granted for only one of LAW 372 or LAW 509.

name: Contracts
description: Historical development; formation and enforceability of contracts; parties; contractual terms; changes of circumstances; remedies for breach.

name: Topics in Administrative Law
description: Not offered each year, consult Faculty.

name: Refugee Law
description: International and Canadian refugee law; the Refugee Convention and its implementation in Canada; the practice of refugee law in Canadian courts and tribunals. Course content does not duplicate LAW 377. Credit will only be given to one of LAW 378 or LAW 578.

name: Land Use Planning
description: The legal and administrative aspects of the regulation of land use and development, especially at the local level. Not offered each year, consult Faculty.

name: Reproduction and Law
description: Legal issues relating to human reproduction. Not offered each year, consult Faculty.

name: Federalism
description: An examination of the principles of Canadian federalism.

name: Municipal Law
description: The municipality as a legal entity; its creation, operation and powers; by-laws and their validity; contractual liability; judicial review; business regulation; expropriation and land use control.

name: Topics in Constitutional Law
description: Not offered each year, consult Faculty. Credit will only be granted for one of LAW 349 or LAW 539.

name: Immigration Law
description: Admission of immigrants into Canada; refugee protection; practice and procedure before immigration tribunals and the courts. Credit will only be granted for one of LAW 377 or LAW 577.

name: Comparative Constitutional Law
description: Comparison of the constitutional history, government structure and powers, and protection of individual rights between the United States and Canada.

name: Topics in Human Rights
description: Not offered each year, consult Faculty.

name: Aboriginal Peoples and Canadian Law
description: Survey of the history and present status of the legal relationships between Canada's Aboriginal peoples and the state.

name: Externship Reflection
description: Structured reflective exercises on the LAW 379 Externship experience.

name: First Nations and Economic Development
description: Legal issues affecting land use and economic activity involving First Nations' resources. Not offered each year, consult Faculty.

name: First Nations and the Administration of Justice
description: The justice system and its operation in relation to First Nations people. Not offered each year, consult Faculty.

name: Externship
description: Students work for an approved organization, supervised by a Faculty-approved mentor and a faculty member. Consult the Faculty for full eligibility criteria.

name: Aboriginal and Treaty Rights
description: Rights of Aboriginal people stemming from their aboriginal status and from treaties. Not offered each year, consult Faculty.

name: First Nations Self-Government
description: Issues relating to First Nations' assumption of self-government powers. Not offered each year, consult Faculty.

name: Topics in Family Law
description: Not offered each year, consult Faculty.

name: Family Law
description: The law relating to family relationships, including the law of marriage, divorce, maintenance, custody, matrimonial property, and related matters. Credit will only be granted for one of LAW 359 or LAW 559.

name: Children and the Law
description: The civil and criminal law affecting juveniles; custody, guardianship and adoption.

name: Topics in First Nations Law - Seminar
description: Not offered each year, consult Faculty. Credit will only be granted for one of LAW 358 or LAW 558.

name: Advanced Criminal Procedure
description: Selected topics relating to procedural law and practice in criminal matters.

name: Topics in First Nations Law - Lecture
description: Not offered each year, consult Faculty. Credit will only be granted for one of LAW 357 or LAW 579.

name: Topics in Natural Resources
description: Not offered each year, consult Faculty.

name: Advanced Criminal Law
description: Selected topics in advanced substantive criminal law and related issues.

name: Racism and Law
description: Legal issues relating to race and racism, including related issues of gender, culture or identity. Not offered each year, consult Faculty.

name: Penal Policy
description: Selected legal policy issues relating to punishment for crime. Not offered each year, consult Faculty.

name: Oil and Gas Law
description: Legal regimes for the disposition of interests in petroleum; government regulation. Not offered each year, consult Faculty.

name: Topics in Criminal Justice
description: Not offered each year, consult Faculty.

name: International Taxation
description: The tax aspects of international transactions. Not offered each year; consult Faculty. Credit will be granted for only one of LAW 410 or LAW 565.

name: Advanced Seminar in Psychology of Movement
description: Topics examines the application of psychology to understanding and supporting healthy sport, physical activity, and health behaviors. Prerequisite: Restricted to students in the BKIN program with third- or fourth-year standing.

name: The Law of Sexual Offences
description: Criminal law relating to sexual offences, including non-consent, evidentiary and procedural rules, and sentencing. History of sexual offence laws and law reform movements.

name: Scientific Communication and Research Skills in Neuromechanical Kinesiology
description: Training in research methods, computational skills, and scientific dissemination related to neuromechanics research in Kinesiology. Students will learn the principles underlying scientific communication and apply these principles in the form of an oral dissemination of scientific results. Restricted to students in the BKIN program with third- or fourth-year standing. Pass/Fail. Prerequisites: Two of KIN_V 310, KIN_V 311, KIN_V 313, KIN_V 316, KIN_V 411, KIN_V 413, KIN_V 415, KIN_V 419.

name: Principles of Sentencing
description: This course is designed to teach students the law and policy involved in sentencing persons convicted of crimes. Students will develop an in-depth understanding of statutory and case law rules regarding sentencing and will be required to apply those rules to actual sentencing scenarios.

name: Advanced Seminar in Systems Biology, Exercise and Health
description: Topics examine the roles of physical activity and fitness on physiological systems and underlying cellular and metabolic mechanisms. Prerequisite: Two of KIN_V 320, KIN_V 335, KIN_V 420, KIN_V 424, KIN_V 432, KIN_V 434, KIN_V 435, KIN_V 438. Restricted to students in the BKIN program with fourth-year standing.

name: Taxation of Partnerships
description: Survey of statutory and judicial rules governing the taxation of income earned through partnerships. Credit will be granted for only one of LAW 409 or LAW 563.

name: Computational Methods for Data Acquisition and Signal Processing in Kinesiology
description: Hands-on laboratory course with an emphasis on developing critical computational research skills for the acquisition, processing and presentation of data related to human movements. Recommended prerequisite: Undergraduate degree in Kinesiology (or related field) including neuromechanical science courses.

name: Psychology of Leadership and Group Processes
description: Contemporary theory, research and application with regard to leadership and group processes in the context of sport and exercise.

name: Tax Policy
description: The policies underlying the creation and implementation of tax laws. Not offered each year, consult Faculty. Credit will be granted for only one of LAW 411 or LAW 566.

name: The Law of Homicide
description: Available in online distance education format only. Elements of sentencing for murder, manslaughter and infanticide; defences to homicide; parties to homicide; and corporate homicide.

name: Taxation of Corporations and Shareholders
description: Survey of statutory provisions and judicial decisions governing the taxation of corporations and shareholders. Credit will be granted for only one of LAW 408 or LAW 562.

name: Topics in Criminal Law
description: Not offered each year, consult Faculty.

name: Taxation
description: A survey of the law and practice of income and capital gains taxes. Credit will be granted for only one of LAW 407 or LAW 506.

name: Advanced Seminar in Leadership Education for Physical Activity
description: Topics consider health-related fitness, physical competence, cognitive understanding, and positive attitudes about physical activity. Prerequisite: Restricted to students in the BKIN program with third- or fourth-year standing.

name: Advanced Seminar in Indigenous Sport, Physical Activity and Health
description: Topics explore the relationship between Indigenous physical cultures, physical activity, health and wellbeing. Prerequisite: Restricted to students in the BKIN program with third- or fourth-year standing.

name: Gap Analysis
description: Using analytics to obtain, describe, and visualize data to create a sport profile. Determine optimal programming decisions for coached athletes based on their performance pathway and gold medal profile. Apply research methods and principles of scientific inquiry, performance analysis, descriptive, prescriptive, and predictive analytics to improve athlete development and performance.

name: Advanced Seminar in Sociocultural Studies
description: Topics explore the social, cultural and global context of sport, exercise, physical activity, health, and the body. Prerequisite: Two of KIN_V 360, KIN_V 363, KIN_V 368, KIN_V 460, KIN_V 464, KIN_V 465, KIN_V 468. Restricted to students in the BKIN program with fourth-year standing.

name: Health Law
description: Legal and policy issues relating to the health care system, including legal aspects of individual and public health decision-making.

name: Sustainable Development Law
description: The linkages, intersections, and tensions between the legal regulation of the environment and competing social and economic priorities. Credit will only be granted for one of LAW 386 or LAW 586.

name: Physical Activity Counselling and Prescription for People with Spinal Cord Injury
description: Gain hands-on experience working with members of the Physical Activity Research Centre at the Blusson Spinal Cord Centre. Apply skills in exercise testing, prescription, and physical activity counselling. Restricted to students in the BKIN program with third- or fourth-year standing. Pass/Fail. Prerequisite: KIN_V 320 (KIN_V 351 strongly recommended).

name: Mental Health Law
description: The law relating to commitment and treatment issues for persons with mental disabilities.

name: Selected Issues in Environmental Law and Policy
description: Case studies of leading problems in environmental law and regulation. Not offered each year, consult Faculty.

name: Advanced Seminar in Neuromechanics
description: Topics consider how neurological, cognitive, sensory, mechanical and muscular systems interact to control human motion and its response to the physical environment. Prerequisite: Two of KIN_V 311, KIN_V 313, KIN_V 316, KIN_V 411, 413, 415, KIN_V 419. Restricted to students in the BKIN program with fourth-year standing

name: Environmental Law in Practice
description: Jurisdiction, remedies and administrative schemes as they apply in practice to selected environmental law problems. Not offered each year, consult Faculty.

name: Directed Studies in Kinesiology
description: Opportunity for students to conduct an independent study in a subject area of interest to them, under the direction of a KIN faculty member. Prerequisite: Third-year standing and permission of the Associate Director, Undergraduate Program.

name: Undergraduate Research Experience in Kinesiology
description: Opportunity for independent study that includes original data collection, under the direction of a KIN faculty member. Prerequisite: Third-year standing and permission of the Associate Director, Undergraduate Program.

name: Environmental Law Workshop
description: Legal research and writing for environmental agency or NGO under supervision of faculty member and lawyer. Not offered every year, consult Faculty. Credit will only be granted for one of LAW 390 or LAW 591.

name: Topics in Environmental Law
description: Not offered each year, consult Faculty.

name: Environmental Law
description: A foundation course dealing with the regulatory and policy framework for the protection of the environment in Canada, such as pollution control and biodiversity conservation. Credit will only be granted for one of LAW 387 LAW 587.

name: Natural Resources Law
description: A foundation course dealing with legal problems common to the management of natural resources such as fisheries, mines and minerals, petroleum, forests, and water resources.

name: Social Welfare Law
description: Aspects of the law structuring the provision of welfare and other social services in Canada. Not offered each year, consult Faculty.

name: Disabilities and Law
description: Legal issues relating to people with disabilities. Not offered each year, consult Faculty.

name: Advanced Seminar in Interdisciplinary Research in Kinesiology
description: Topics will be approached from multiple perspectives in a course designed to explore the interdisciplinarity of the field of kinesiology. Prerequisite: Restricted to students in the BKIN program with fourth-year standing.

name: Green Rights and Warrior Lawyers
description: Explore the human right to a healthy environment and the rights of nature through the stories of environmental lawyers and defenders worldwide who struggle for environmental justice through law. No pre- or co-requisites.

name: Fisheries Law
description: Legal regimes for the exploitation and regulation of fisheries. Not offered each year, consult Faculty.

name: Forest Law
description: Acquisition of timber interests; development, financing and organization of timber companies; regulation of exploitation industry interests; management taxation. Not offered each year; consult Faculty. Credit will only be granted for one of LAW 395 or LAW 595.

name: Mining Law
description: Acquisition of mineral interests; development, financing and organization of mining companies; regulation of exploitation industry interests; management taxation. Not offered each year, consult Faculty.

name: Literature and Other Materials for Young Adults
Services for Families and Early Literacy in the Preschool Years
Canadian Literature and other Materials for Children
Illustrated Literature and Other Materials for Children
Science and Technology Information Sources and Services
Writing, Publishing and the Book Trade for Children
Corporate Transactions
description: Legal aspects of selected transactions relating to public corporations and corporate governance. Not offered each year, consult Faculty.

name: Competition Policy
description: The law and policy relating to the regulation of competition in Canada and other jurisdictions. Not offered each year, consult Faculty.

name: Close Corporations
description: The corporation, taxation, accounting, insurance and estate planning aspects of the close corporation. Not offered each year, consult Faculty.

name: Securities Regulation
description: The law relating to the distribution of securities. Continuous and timely disclosure requirements and civil liability. Credit will only be granted for one of LAW 463 or LAW 576.

name: Preventing Wrongful Convictions
description: Substantive legal principles and rules of evidence that can cause or help to prevent wrongful convictions or other miscarriages of justice. Roles of the participants in the criminal justice system. Not offered each year; consult Faculty.

name: Advanced Trial Advocacy
description: Skills-training in all aspects of civil and criminal trial advocacy.

name: Trial Advocacy
description: Techniques of advocacy in civil and criminal cases including interviewing, pre-trial preparation, tactical analysis, development of facts, direct and cross examination and various ethical considerations.

name: Advanced Corporate Law
description: Selected topics such as the nature of shares, equity financing, corporate structure and reorganization, and shareholder squeezeouts.

name: Directed Research
description: Enrolment restricted.

name: Introduction to Corporate Finance
description: Interdisciplinary elements of corporate finance and law, in both theory and practice.

name: Directed Research
description: Students will be able to undertake advanced research into a topic approved by a faculty member, under the supervision of and in consultation with, that faculty member.

name: Taxation
description: Law and practice of income and capital gains taxes. Credit will be granted for only one of LAW 506 or LAW 407.

name: Topics in Corporate Law - Seminar
description: Not offered each year, consult Faculty. Credit will only be granted for one of LAW 467 or LAW 594.

name: Business Organizations
description: A conceptual overview of business organizations in Canada, including partnerships and corporations, and the rights and duties of shareholders and directors. Credit will be granted for only one of LAW 508 or LAW 459.

name: Innocence Project
description: Clinical program giving hands-on experience in reviewing claims of innocence post-conviction. Not offered every year; consult Faculty.

name: International Criminal Law
description: Analysis of topics such as jurisdiction, immunity from prosecution, mutual assistance in penal matters, recognition and enforcement of foreign penal laws, and international police cooperation; examination of selected offences such as war crimes, crimes against humanity, genocide, terrorism, illicit drug trafficking, and torture.

name: Administrative Law
description: Study of the external control of public actors exercising statutory authority. Introduction to general principles of procedural and substantive judicial review, delegated authority and subordinate legislation, remedies, and administrative processes. Credit will be granted for only one of LAW 372 or LAW 509.

name: Evidence

description: Prerequisite: All of LAIS 605, LAIS 607 and one of LAIS 608, LAIS 609.

name: Advanced Seminar in Library, Archival and Information Studies Topics
Introduction to Language and Linguistics
description: Study of language as a universal and uniquely human cognitive system: What universals do all languages share and how do languages differ? An investigation of sound systems, word-building, grammatical principles, language change, dialect variation, language acquisition, neurolinguistics. Recommended but not required for an honours, major, or minor in linguistics or speech sciences.

name: Directed Studies in Mathematics
description: Advanced study under the direction of a faculty member may be arranged in special situations.

name: Formal Foundations of Syntax & Semantics
description: Conceptual underpinnings of the study of sentence structure and meaning; core issues in syntax and semantics; the place of syntax and semantics in a model of grammar; interface issues. Prerequisite: LING 520 and 525 are recommended.

name: Language as a Social Instrument
description: Language as a tool that shapes and is shaped by technology, media, politics and power relations in society. Considers multiple levels of linguistic structure from a cross-linguistic perspective. Prerequisite: All of LING 200, LING 201.

name: Directed Studies
description: Supervisor and topic chosen by mutual agreement between student and Linguistics faculty member. Department Advisor approval is required.

name: Acquisition of Syntax
description: Central issues in the first language acquisition of syntax, including early lexical and semantic development, acquisition of morphology, and syntactic development (e.g., word order, questions). Prerequisite: All of LING 222, LING 300.

name: Native Languages of the Americas
description: Survey of the indigenous languages of the Americas. Study of the basis of genetic classification and areal similarities. The structure of representative languages will be presented and contrasted. The present status of American Indian languages will be considered. Note: this course is not necessarily offered every year.

name: Formal Foundations of Phonetics & Phonology
description: Conceptual underpinnings of the study of speech sounds; core issues in phonetics and phonology; the place of phonetics and phonology in a model of grammar; interface issues. Prerequisite: LING 508 and 510 are recommended.

name: Community-based Language Research
description: Research methods and partnerships, ethical paradigms, the social, cultural and historical context of language research, and the relation of language research to pedagogy, policy and planning.

name: Electronic Materials
description: Semiconductor materials, MOSFET structure, operation and applications in digital circuits, fabrication techniques, basic mask and fabrication flow design and semiconductor fabrication process theories at an entry level.

name: Materials for Aerostructures and Engines
description: Engineering theory of aerospace structural material mix: metal alloys, ceramics, and polymer composites. Material requirements for weight-, damage tolerant-, cost efficient-design. Overview of material characterization, including fracture and fatigue. Statistical variability, material allowables, structural certification.

name: Biomaterials
description: Engineered materials in medical applications with an emphasis on material properties, functionality, design, and material response in the biological environment.

name: Topics in Linguistics
description: A capstone course for Linguistics and Speech Sciences majors, normally taken after three years of study. Individual sections will differ substantially; see online Course List for detailed descriptions and prerequisites. May be repeated for credit when content is different.

name: Acquisition of Phonology
description: Development of the phonological system in typical first language acquisition from the perspective of diverse linguistic topics. Phonetic transcription of child speech. Prerequisite: All of LING 222, LING 311.

name: Failure of Materials
description: Failure by excess deformation, fracture, fatigue, and environmental effects. Failure theories and case studies of engineering failures.

name: Nondestructive Evaluation
description: Principles of test methods; inspection techniques and equipment; quantitative flaw evaluation; reliability analysis.

name: Material Optimization for the Manufacture of Structural Metallic Components
description: Phase transformations and strengthening of advanced engineering alloys (e.g. steels, aluminum, magnesium and titanium alloys) with particular emphasis on structure-property development relevant to the latest materials manufacturing technologies.

name: Clinical Topics in Speech, Language, and Hearing Sciences
description: Introduction to speech and hearing sciences with emphasis on the clinical perspectives of audiology and speech pathology.

name: Issues in Morphological Theory and Analysis
