description: Morphology from both historical and theoretical perspectives.

name: Advanced Simulation and Modelling Tools for Materials Manufacturing
description: Mathematical modelling of manufacturing processes; Computer Aided Engineering tools; application examples will be drawn from a range of manufacturing operations.

name: Composite Materials
description: Understanding the properties and the mechanical behaviour of composite materials with emphasis on analysis, design, and manufacturing.

name: Microstructure Engineering
description: Follows the production of metallurgical products, focusing on process design models used to describe solidification, recrystallization, and precipitation.

name: Materials Engineering Undergraduate Thesis
description: Materials-related academic research. Projects will be defined within materials engineering, involving design, experimental, and/or simulation work, as selected from topics provided by faculty members. Restricted to students with fourth year class standing.

name: Metallurgical Thermodynamics
description: Application of advanced thermodynamic principles in metallurgical processes.

name: Materials Sustainability
description: Concepts of life cycle analysis, circular economy and critical materials. Project-based introduction to key concepts, calculations, and design.

name: Phonological Theory and Analysis
description: Discussion and critical analysis of current issues in phonological theory.

name: Case Studies in Advanced Materials Manufacturing
description: The full spectrum of design encountered including the design of components, structures and processes used to manufacture materials.

name: Phonetic Theory & Analysis
description: Discussion and critical analysis of current issues in linguistic phonetics; instrumental analysis.

name: Modelling of Cell-Scale Biology
description: Concepts and techniques for modelling cellular and subcellular dynamics in biological systems. Topics may include complex biochemical systems, biopolymers in cell motility and division, continuum mechanics, and membrane dynamics.

name: Mathematical Biology
description: Mathematical methods in modelling biological processes, at levels from cell biochemistry to community ecology.

name: Linear and Nonlinear Waves
description: Classical and recent results in linear and nonlinear waves. Geometrical acoustics and kinematic waves; large amplitude waves in weakly stratified media; small amplitude waves in strongly stratified media. Dispersive waves; group velocity; applications. Recommended pre-requisites: MATH 400 and some knowledge of either fluid mechanics or elasticity.

name: Separation Science in Aqueous Metal Processing
description: The theory of solvent extraction and ion exchange, membrane separations, chemical precipitation, electrochemical separations and other techniques for aqueous metal processing, applications from the metal processing literature.

name: Mathematics of Infectious Diseases and Immunology
description: Mathematical models for disease spread in populations. Within-host infectious disease dynamics. Models of the immune system and immune cells.

name: Graduate Seminar
description: Presentation and discussion of recent results in the mathematical literature.

name: Transport Phenomena III - Mass Transport
description: Mass transfer fundamentals, gas interdiffusivity, Sievert's law, Fick's laws, solid-state diffusion, steady and non-steady state diffusion, mass transfer in quiescence fluids. The application examples are related to metallurgical processes, green technologies, and the semiconductor industry.

name: Evolutionary Dynamics
description: Mathematical models of evolution and evolutionary game theory. Stochastic dynamics in finite populations, dynamics in spatially structured populations, and adaptive dynamics. Applications include the origin of species and the problem of cooperation.

name: Mechanical Behaviour of Materials
description: Polycrystalline and single crystal deformation; dislocation theory; strengthening mechanisms; fracture mechanics; fatigue; high temperature deformation mechanisms.

name: Aerospace Materials and Manufacturing
description: Advanced materials and manufacturing in the framework of aerospace requirements and regulations, with a focus on processing of materials, including advanced metals and polymer composites, to produce aerospace structures and engine components.

name: Phase Transformations
description: Solidification and solid state transformations; nucleation and growth processes; segregation and structure in castings; phase changes in steel; transformation diagrams; diffusion equations.

name: Mathematical Electrophysiology
description: Formulation and analysis of models of excitable media. FitzHugh-Nagumo model, ionic models of membrane excitability (e.g., Hodgkin-Huxley), calcium excitability, bursting phenomena.

name: Structure and Properties Laboratory
description: Structure and properties of ferrous and non-ferrous metals; heat treatment; hardenability; metallography; age hardening. Corequisite: All of MTRL 365, MTRL 378.

name: Environmental Degradation of Materials
description: Fundamental aspects of environmental degradation of metals (corrosion), ceramics, and polymers, with an emphasis on aqueous environments.

name: Economic Aspects of Materials Engineering
description: Time value of money, cash flows, capital and operating cost estimation, financial decision making and relevant case studies.

name: Polymers
description: The structure and properties of polymeric materials and reinforced polymers with emphasis on their engineering properties and applications.

name: Casting Technology
description: Various casting technologies related to the automotive and aerospace sectors will be covered, including upstream liquid metal processing.

name: Engineering Project I
description: Design projects to illustrate the full spectrum of design encountered in Metals and Materials Engineering including the design of components, structures and processes used to manufacture materials.

name: Hydrometallurgy II
description: Leaching, purification, precipitation, regeneration; thermodynamics and kinetics of separation steps; electrochemical applications.

name: Microstructural Analysis Laboratory
description: Basic principles and techniques of microstructural analysis with particular reference to engineered materials including x-ray, SEM microprobe TEM and high energy electron analysis.

name: Welding and Joining of Materials
description: Case studies addressing temperature modelling in welding and joining, material selection for welds and joints, calculation of properties for welds and joints, mechanical analysis of joints, and design of welding and joining procedures.

name: Perturbation Methods for Differential Equations
description: Prerequisite: [MATH550] Ordinary and partial differential equations (MATH 400 or equivalent).

name: Engineering Project II
description: Design projects to illustrate the full spectrum of design encountered in Metals and Materials Engineering including the design of components, structures and processes used to manufacture materials.

name: Monitoring and Optimization of Materials Processing
description: Measurement systems for materials processing and evaluation, methods of data collection and analysis in materials engineering, materials processing monitoring and control, design of experiments for materials processing and optimization.

name: Continuous Time Stochastic Processes
description: Prerequisite: All of MATH 544, MATH 545.

name: Optimal Control Theory
description: Optimal control of systems governed by ordinary differential equations. The control problem will be carefully stated, and existence results and necessary conditions will be established. Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman theory will be introduced.

name: Finite Elements in Heat Transfer
description: Application of the finite element method to heat transfer and solidification; steady state and transient heat conduction; latent heat evolution and radiation.

name: Discrete Random Processes
description: Prerequisite: All of MATH 544, MATH 545.

name: Deformation of Crystalline Materials
description: Nature and properties of lattice imperfections; dislocation theory and its use to describe work hardening, creep, structure of grain boundaries and other phenomena.

name: Symmetries and Differential Equations
description: Dimensional analysis, modelling, and invariance. Lie groups of transformations, infinitesimal transformations. Applications to ordinary and partial differential equations. No knowledge of group theory will be assumed. Recommended pre-requisite: elementary courses in differential equations and linear algebra.

name: Topics in Fracture Mechanics
description: The equations and concepts of linear elastic fracture mechanics. Fracture toughness testing, statistical theories of fracture and proof testing, stress corrosion cracking and static fatigue. Acoustic emission and other nondestructive testing methods. Case studies of large scale fractures of pressure vessels and structures.

name: Corrosion
description: Modern theories relating to corrosion and corrosion protection of metals. Thermodynamic and kinetic phenomena, corrosion measurements, inhibition and passivation, design for corrosive environments, stress corrosion cracking theory.

name: Electrochemical Science, Engineering and Technology
description: Electrochemical interfaces; electrode reactions; thermodynamics; kinetics and transport processes in electrochemical systems; experimental techniques. Electrochemical reactors and processes; modelling, design and economics. Electrochemical technologies; electrosynthesis, batteries and fuel cells. Electro-metallurgy; electrowinning and refining of metals, corrosion, leaching and cementation. Equivalency: CHBE577, MMAT588

name: Advanced Phase Transformations
description: Thermodynamic and kinetic bases for the theory of phase transformations in the condensed state.

name: Advanced Topics in Materials Engineering
description: May be arranged on approval of the department head.

name: Physics of Microfabrication: Front End Processing
description: Practical aspects, physical models, and simulations of Si-based nanofabrication processes such as oxidation, diffusion, ion implantation, chemical vapor deposition, etching, stress techniques. Semiconductor device physic basics will also be discussed.

name: Microstructural Evolution of Deformed Materials
description: Physical mechanisms of microstructure evolution; structure, energy and mobilities of grain boundaries, grain boundary segregation, precipitation, recovery, recrystallization, grain growth; microstructure engineering of steels.

name: Hydrometallurgical Reactor Design and Analysis
description: Batch leaching kinetics, leaching mechanisms; statistical methods for design of multiparticle continuous leaching reactors; coupled heat and mass balances, mixing phenomena, redox and precipitation reactions, complex mineralogical feeds; heap and dump leaching.

name: Advanced Dynamical Systems
description: Topics from: hyperbolic invariant sets and symbolic dynamics, global bifurcations, local bifurations for partial differential equations, multiple bifurcations, bifurcations and symmetry, applications. Prerequisite: [MATH552]

name: Mathematical Modelling: Discrete Optimization Problems
description: Formulation of real-world optimization problems using techniques such as linear programming, network flows, integer programming, dynamic programming. Solution by appropriate software.

name: Advanced Composite Materials
description: Processing and properties of advanced polymer based composite materials with emphasis on analysis, design, and manufacturing.

name: M.Sc. Thesis
description: For M.Sc. Degree. Research studies in materials engineering. Honours/Pass/Fail.

name: Complex Analysis
description: The residue theorem, the argument principle, conformal mapping, the maximum modulus principle, harmonic functions, representation of functions by integrals, series, and products. Other topics at the discretion of the instructor.

name: Advanced Hydrometallurgy
description: Advanced thermochemical modelling of hydrometallurgical unit operations to include extraction, separation, and recovery of base metals. Application to flow-sheet analysis.

name: Introduction to Dynamical Systems
description: Ideas, methods and applications of bifurcation theory and dynamical systems: differential and difference equations, local bifurcations, perturbation methods, chaos. Recommended pre-requisites: one of MATH 215, MATH 255, MATH 256 and one of MATH 256, MATH 257, MATH 316.

name: Advanced Biomaterials
description: Formation and structure-function relations of biological materials, the interaction of tissue-synthetic biomaterials, advanced biomaterials design, biomimetic processing, and current progress in drug delivery systems and biomedical devices.

name: Mathematical Research and Writing
description: Current research topics in pure and applied mathematics are explored at the undergraduate level. Technical communication and research skills are developed.

name: Graphs and Networks
description: Graph theory, emphasizing trees, tree growing algorithms, and proof techniques. Other topics chosen from shortest paths, maximum flows, minimum cost flows, matchings, and graph colouring.

name: Topics in the History of Mathematics I
description: Historical development of concepts and techniques in areas chosen from Geometry, Number Theory, Algebra, Calculus, Probability, Analysis. The focus is on historically significant writings of important contributors and on famous problems of Mathematics.

name: Directed Studies in Mathematics
description: Introduction to the methods of mathematical research through an exploration of a mathematical topic under the supervision of a faculty member. Written report required.

name: Graph Theory
description: Introductory course in mostly non-algorithmic topics including: planarity and Kuratowski's theorem, graph colouring, graph minors, random graphs, cycles in graphs, Ramsey theory, extremal graph theory. Proofs emphasized. Intended for Honours students.

name: Co-operative Work Placement III
description: Approved and supervised technical work experience involving mathematics in industry for a minimum of 3 1/2 months. Technical report required. Restricted to students admitted to the Mathematics Co-operative Education Program.

name: Projects in Mathematical Biology
description: Development and analysis of mathematical models for complex systems in ecology, evolution, cell biology, neurophysiology, and other biological and medical disciplines.

name: Projects in Mathematical Modelling
description: Computational methods for mathematical modelling. Numerical methods for partial differential equations, stochastic processes, and data-driven models. Includes student-directed projects on current research and applications.

name: Honours Reading
description: Independent reading by Honours students in Mathematics under the direction of a faculty member. Written report required.

name: Co-operative Work Placement IV
description: Approved and supervised technical work experience involving mathematics in industry for a minimum of 3 1/2 months. Technical report required. Restricted to students admitted to the Mathematics Co-operative Education Program.

name: Managing and Preserving Linguistic Data
description: Theory and practice of research data management and preservation with an emphasis on linguistic and language data.

name: Directed Reading in Topics related to Linguistics
Asymptotic and Perturbation Methods
description: Asymptotic expansions. Asymptotic evaluation of integrals; WKBJ methods. Regular and singular expansions. Boundary layer theory; matched asymptotic expansions. Multiple scale techniques.

name: Introduction to Management Thought and Social Responsibility
description: Introduces management thought in business and organizations. Utilizes critical thinking in socially and ethically responsible decisions at a corporate and personal level. Includes managing responsibly through people, mass production, ethical and socially-responsible practices. Covers start-ups, entrepreneurs, family business, non-profit/for-profit organizations and governments in global regions. Credit will be granted for only one of MGMT 110 or MGMT 200. Equivalency: MGMT 200

name: Introduction to Management Thought and Social Responsibility
description: Introduces management thought in business and organizations. Utilizes critical thinking in socially and ethically responsible decisions at a corporate and personal level. Includes managing responsibly through people, mass production, ethical and socially-responsible practices. Covers start-ups, entrepreneurs, family business, non-profit/for-profit organizations and governments in global regions. Credit will be granted for only one of MGMT 200 or MGMT 110. Equivalency: MGMT 110

name: Manufacturing Engineering Laboratory
description: Theory, operational constraints, and problem solving in traditional manufacturing processes. Casting, heat treatment, bulk deformation (i.e. rolling, extrusion, drawing), machining, joining, and shaping of composites. Experiments in process and product characterization.

name: Production Systems Management I
description: Impact of operations in increasing productivity and reducing waste.

name: Machine Dynamics
description: Classifications of mechanisms, velocity, acceleration and force analysis, graphical and computer-oriented vector and matrix methods, balancing, flywheels, gears, gear trains, cams. Prerequisite: All of MATH 101, MATH 152, PHYS 170. Corequisite: MATH 255.

name: Biology of Marine Mammals
description: Survey course covering systematics and distribution of marine mammals, their sensory capabilities and physiology, with special emphasis on the Cetacea. The course will involve an independent field study. Prerequisite: Introductory vertebrate zoology.

name: Manufacturing Engineering Project I
description: Project-based, multi-step manufacturing engineering design and problem solving. Prerequisite: MANU 230.

name: Special Topics
description: 6 weeks. Offered, as opportunities arise, by distinguished scientists who are visiting at the Bamfield Marine Sciences Centre. The course will be of a specialized nature.

name: Thermodynamics
description: Thermodynamic system and properties, thermodynamic processes; work and heat interactions. Conservation of energy and First Law, internal energy and enthalpy, the Second Law and entropy, application to manufacturing processes. Prerequisite: All of MATH 101, MATH 152, PHYS 157. Corequisite: MATH 255.

name: Transport Phenomena I - Fluid Mechanics
description: Fluid statics; fluid mechanics; laminar and turbulent flow; equations of continuity and motion; boundary layers; flow in conduits and packed and fluidized beds; flow measurements.

name: Technical Communication
description: Written and oral communication in business correspondence, engineering design methods, report preparation, and oral presentations of technical material. Restricted to students in second year of the Materials Engineering Program. Prerequisite: One of APSC_V 176, ENGL_V 110, ENGL_V 111, ENGL_V 112, ENGL_V 120, ENGL_V 121, WRDS_V 150. Equivalency: APSC_V 201.

name: Transport Phenomena II - Heat Transport
description: Conduction, forced and natural convection, and radiation. Heat transfer with fluid flow, applications of heat exchange, and solidification of castings.

name: Thermodynamics of Materials II
description: Behaviour of solutions, phase diagrams, electrochemistry, chemical potential and free energy diagrams applied to materials processing and thermodynamic modelling. Prerequisite: MTRL 250.

name: Special Topics
description: 3 weeks. Offered, as opportunities arise, by distinguished scientists who are visiting at the Bamfield Marine Sciences Centre. The course will be of a specialized nature.

name: Modelling of Materials Processes
description: Mathematical and physical modelling of processes employed in the production of materials. The application of models to analyze, design and improve materials production.

name: Language in the Age of AI
description: Examines the impact of generative AI, large language models, and virtual assistants on human communication. Includes evolving language trends, ethics, and applications like speech recognition, text-to-speech, and machine translation. No computational or programming background required.

name: Technical Communication
description: Written and oral communication in business correspondence, engineering design methods, report preparation and oral presentations of technical material. Restricted to students in second year of the Manufacturing Engineering Program. Prerequisite: One of APSC 176, ENGL 110, ENGL 111, ENGL 112, ENGL 120, ENGL 121, WRDS 150. Equivalency: APSC 201

name: Introduction to Business
description: Introduction to the Faculty of Management and traditional areas of business including accounting, economics, finance, marketing, organizational behaviour, operations, business policy, information systems and entrepreneurship. Identifies the steps needed to build and manage successful local, national, and international competitive businesses and organizations. Introduces ethical and policy decisions faced by businesses, organizations and governments.

name: Challenging Language Myths
description: Critical consideration of a broad range of commonly held beliefs about language and its relation to the brain and cognition, learning, society, change and evolution. Note. This is an elective course that does not fulfill writing requirements in any faculty or the literature requirement in the Faculty of Arts. Credit will be granted for only one of LING_V 140 or ENGL_V 140. Equivalency: ENGL_V 140.

name: Seminars and Papers in Marine Science
description: Instruction in the critical analysis of published research papers and of oral seminars.  Prerequisite: Completion of second year in a biology program.
prerequisites: Completion of second year in a biology program

name: Materials in Design
description: The process of materials selection for different design criteria; the importance of shape and processing variables; the use of computer software in the selection process.

name: Introduction to How to Learn a Language
description: Skills and strategies for second language acquisition, through the foundations of pronunciation, vocabulary, grammar, and pragmatics, connected to the practical, social, and personal challenges of language learning.

name: Management of Engineering Design
description: Fundamental communication and inter- personal skills, as well as operational processes, that engineers require to effectively work in design teams. Concepts and best practices around project management tools and techniques, team dynamics, planning, and organization. Prerequisite: MTRL_V 201.

name: Clinical Topics in Speech, Language, and Hearing Sciences
description: Introduction to speech and hearing sciences, with emphasis on the clinical perspectives of audiology and speech pathology.

name: Computational Tools for Linguistic Analysis
description: Practical skills for analyzing language using the Python programming language and relevant packages. Prerequisite: One of LING 100, LING 101, LING 140, LING 170, LING 200, LING 201, ENGL 330, ENGL 331. Recommended: LING 201 and CPSC 103 or CPSC 110 (or other programming experience).

name: Manufacturing in Materials Engineering
description: Manufacturing processes from a materials perspective; metal casting, heat treating processes, forming processes, machining, and joining. Role of manufacturing in microstructure and material properties development and on component performance.

name: Thermodynamics of Materials I
description: Heat and mass balances applied to materials engineering; thermodynamic principles applied to materials processing: heat of reaction, free energy, activity, phase equilibrium, reactions involving gases, Ellingham diagrams.

name: Language Acquisition
description: Audition and speech perception, phonological organization, word learning, syntax, and pragmatics.

name: Linguistic Theory and Analysis II
description: Introduction to grammatical analysis; morphology, syntax, semantics; synchronic analysis and description with illustrations from various languages. Analytical practice and seminar discussion.

name: Hydrometallurgy I
description: Aqueous extraction of metals from ores and concentrates.

name: Languages of the World
description: A survey of the linguistic map of the world, examining how languages are genetically classified and how different languages evolve. Principles underlying different writing systems and the decipherment of historical documents. Issues of languages in contact, minority language endangerment, language death and the role of English as a world language. Recommended but not required for an honours, major, or minor in linguistics or speech sciences.

name: Hydrometallurgy I Laboratory
description: Laboratory exercises on aqueous extraction of metals from ores and concentrates. Corequisite: MTRL 358.

name: Introduction to Studies in Second Language Acquisition
description: Linguistic systems that learners of an additional language develop as they approximate towards the target language, and key questions about what this 'interlanguage' system reveals about how we learn languages. Prerequisite: One of LING 100, LING 101, LING 140, LING 170.

name: Studies in Grammar
description: Introduction to syntactic analysis and theory, with emphasis on description and analysis of data from a wide variety of languages. Prerequisite: LING 201.

name: Linguistic Theory and Analysis I
description: Introduction to phonetics and phonology; training in the identification and production of speech sounds; principles and methods for describing and writing the sound system of a language; phonological theory with reference to selected languages; the interface between phonology and morphology. Analytical practice and seminar discussion.

name: Instrumental Phonetics
description: Physiological and/or acoustic phonetics. Focus on experimental methods and analysis techniques. Topics may include: source-filter theory; spectral and temporal acoustic analysis, inter-articulator timing and motor coordination. Prerequisite: LING 200. Recommended: LING 313

name: Introduction to Linguistic Phonetics and Speech Science
description: The articulatory and acoustic properties of speech production and perception, including practice in phonetic transcription, instrumental recording, and the analysis of normal speech. Prerequisite: [LING200]

name: Directed Studies
description: A research project approved by the supervisor in the field of interest of the student designed to take advantage of the opportunities offered by the Bamfield Marine Sciences Centre. Note: the supervisor may be teaching at the Marine Centre; or a member of faculty of WCUMSS whether at the Marine Centre as a research investigator or as one of the members of WCUMSS.

name: The Languages of Africa
description: Linguistic survey of the languages of Africa, including typological and historical connections between languages, individual and comparative surveys of sound systems, word structures, sentence structures, semantics, and sociolinguistic properties of a representative selection of languages. Credit will only be granted for one of LING_V 308 or AFST_V 308. Equivalency: AFST_V 308.

name: Studies in Phonology
description: Introduction to phonological analysis and theory, with a strong emphasis on description and analysis of data from a wide variety of languages. Prerequisite: LING 200.

name: Machine and Part Metrology
description: Laser interferometer measurement of volumetric accuracy; error mapping, modelling and compensation of errors, rotation metrology, spindle accuracy. Part dimension and surface metrology. Metrology instruments: Coordinate measurement machine, surface profile meter, laser interferometer and ball bar.  Prerequisite: All of MANU 265, MATH 255, MECH 368. Corequisite: MANU 430.

name: Marine Invertebrate Zoology
description: A survey of the marine phyla, with emphasis on the benthic fauna in the vicinity of the Marine Station. The course includes lectures, laboratory periods, field collection, identification and observation. Emphasis is placed on the study of living specimens in the laboratory and in the field.

name: Population and Community Ecology of Marine Organisms
description: Emphasis on interactions among organisms and between organisms and their physiochemical environment, and on biological diversity.  Prerequisite: Completion of second year in a biology program.

name: Introduction to Biological Oceanography
description: An introduction to the biology of oceans, with supporting coverage of relevant physics and chemistry. Emphasis will be placed on plankton biology, community structure and life histories, and influencing environmental factors. Collections will be made from sheltered inlets, through Barkely Sound to offshore waters. The course will involve both field and laboratory. Prerequisite: All of BIOL_V 320, BIOL_V 205.

name: Special Topics in Manufacturing Engineering
description: Prerequisite: Fourth-year standing

name: Comparative Invertebrate Embryology
description: A comprehensive study of development of marine invertebrates available at the Bamfield Marine Sciences Centre, including all major phyla and most of the minor phyla. Prerequisite: course in invertebrates or embryology.

name: Special Topics in Marine Biology
description: This course will be offered, as opportunities arise, by distinguished scientists visiting at the Bamfield Marine Sciences Centre. It is expected that the course will generally be of a specialized nature and be at a level appropriate to graduate or senior undergraduate students.

name: Special Topics in Marine Biology
description: This course will be offered, as opportunities arise, by distinguished scientists visiting at the Bamfield Marine Sciences Centre. This course will be of a specialized nature and at a level appropriate to graduate or senior undergraduate students.

name: Biology of Marine Birds
description: Study of interrelationship of birds and the marine environment. Census techniques and observation of birds in the field will be emphasized. Prerequisite: Completion of a course in vertebrate zoology or permission of the instructor.

name: Linear FEA in Solids and Heat Transfer
description: Theory and element selection. Virtual work and weighted residual formulation. Linear elastic analysis. Heat transfer analysis. Isoparametic elements. Computer program development. Utilization of existing computer packages.

name: Control Sensors and Actuators
description: Review of control, instrumentation and design. Performance specification of control components, component matching, error analysis. Operating principles, analysis, modelling, design considerations of control sensors and actuators such as analog sensors for motion measurement, digital transducers, stepper motors, DC motors, induction motors, synchronous motors, and hydraulic actuators. Control techniques pertaining to actuators. Applications.

name: Software Development for Mechatronic Systems
description: Equivalency: EECE524

name: Instrumentation for Mechatronic Systems
description: Equivalency: EECE525

name: Marine Ecology
description: An analytical approach to biotic associations in the marine environment. Opportunities are provided for study of the intertidal realm in exposed and protected areas, and of beaches and estuaries in the vicinity of the Marine Centre; plankton studies and investigations of the subtidal and benthic environments by diving and dredging are envisaged.

name: Structure and Function in Marine Animals
description: Principles of classification, evolution, morphology, biomechanics, physiology and biochemistry will be illustrated in representatives from a variety of animal phyla.  Prerequisite: Completion of second year in a biology program.

name: Mechatronic System Design Project II
description: The full assembly, instrumentation, computer and electronic interfacing, and testing of a dynamic machine.

name: Biology of Fishes
description: Classification, physiology, ecology, behaviour and zoogeography of fishes with particular emphasis on those in the marine environment of the British Columbia coast. Prerequisite: A course in comparative vertebrate anatomy.

name: Ecological Adaptations of Seaweeds
description: Morphological, physiological, genetic and reproductive adaptations of seaweeds to their environments.  Prerequisite: Completion of second year in a biology program.

name: Mechatronic System Design Project I
description: The design, analysis, manufacturability, instrumentation and computer control of a selected dynamic machinery assembly will be studied.

name: Computer Control of Multi-Axis Machines
description: Digital control laws for servo drives; state space and transfer function models of feed drives; tracking errors; trajectory generation of multi-axis machines; contouring analysis of multi-axes servo drives; real time linear and circular interpolation methods supported by laboratory applications.

name: Biofluids
description: Principles, biorheology, circulatory biofluid mechanics, synovial fluid in joints, biofluid dynamics of the human brain, respiratory biofluid mechanics, flow and pressure measurement techniques in the human body.

name: Orthopaedic Biomechanics
description: Musculoskeletal anatomy. Static and dynamic analysis of the musculoskeletal system. Gait. Musculoskeletal tissue mechanics. Biomaterials. Advanced study of relevant problems in orthopaedics, including joint replacement, fracture fixation, and spinal disorders.

name: Manufacturing Processes I
description: Correlation between material properties and processibility for practical engineering manufacturing routes. Calculations and design. Application of heat/mass/fluid transport, mechanics and thermodynamics to manufacturing processes.  Prerequisite: All of APSC 278, APSC 279, MTRL 264, MECH 260 and one of MECH 280, MTRL 263. Corequisite: MANU 261.

name: Special Topics in Manufacturing Engineering
description: Prerequisite: Third-year standing.

name: Marine Phycology
description: A survey of the marine algae, with emphasis on the benthic forms in the vicinity of the Marine Centre. The course includes lectures, laboratory periods, field collection, identification and observation. Emphasis is placed on the study of living specimens in the laboratory and in the field.

name: Fundamentals of Microelectromechanical Systems
description: Micro-fabrication of MEMS: solid-state technology and other micromachining techniques. Engineering principles of various MEMS devices.

name: Modelling of Dynamic Systems
description: Advanced modelling of mechanical, electrical, fluid, thermal and multi-domain systems; inter-domain analogies; analytical models in time and frequency domains; modelling tools; response analysis; digital simulation; practical project. Recommended pre-requisite: prior undergraduate coursework in dynamics, vibration, or electrical circuits.

name: Additive Manufacturing Design
description: Design tools and methods for additive manufacturing, complex digital geometry creation, computer aided design tools, additive manufacturing workflow development, producibility analysis, analysis of 3D data sets for suitability to additive manufacturing processes.  Prerequisite: Third-year standing or greater.

name: Production Systems Management II
description: Functional area of production and operations management. Decision-making, capacity planning, aggregate planning, inventory management, distribution planning, materials requirements planning and quality control.  Prerequisite: MANU 270.

name: Probability
description: Probability spaces, random variables, distributions, expectation, conditional probabilities, convergence of random variables, generating and characteristic functions, weak and strong laws of large numbers, central limit theorem.

name: Engineering Materials II
description: Materials selection for different design criteria; importance of shape and processing variables; computer software in selection. Credit will be granted for only one of MTRL 280 or MANU 378.  Prerequisite: APSC 278.

name: Real Analysis I
description: Sigma-algebras, Lebesgue measure, Borel measures, measurable functions, integration, convergence theorems, Lp spaces, Holder and Minkowski inequalities, Lebesgue and/or Radon-Nikodym differentiation.

name: Industrial Automation
description: Principle components of manufacturing automation, modelling of sensors-actuators and control systems, robotic programming, programmable logical control (PLC) systems and development of PLC ladder diagrams.  Prerequisite: All of MANU 265, MATH 255. Corequisite: MANU 330.

name: Fundamentals of Injury Biomechanics
description: Introduction to injury biomechanics. Anatomy. Impact experiments. Multi-body dynamic simulation and finite element analysis. Skull, face, brain, eye, pelvis, abdomen, and extremity injury. Anthropomorphic test devices, seat belts, airbags, child restraints, and helmets.

name: Emerging Topics in Mechatronics, Manufacturing, Controls, and Automation
Manufacturing Design Capstone Project
description: Project-based, multi-step, multi-part Capstone design project involving manufacturing engineering design methods, problem solving.  Prerequisite: MANU 330.

name: Manufacturing Processes III
description: Integrating concepts of primary (casting), secondary (deformation), and tertiary (machining and surface treatment) processes and economic and environmental assessment.  Prerequisite: MANU 380.

name: Biomedical Manufacturing
description: Bulk and nanoscale manufacturing processes for biomedical devices, materials and therapeutics; drug delivery; host-tissue biomaterial interactions; surface modification of medical devices; sterilization techniques; good manufacturing processes; medical device regulation.  Prerequisite: Third-year standing or higher.

name: Stochastic Processes
description: Random walks, Markov chains, branching processes, Poisson processes, continuous time Markov chains, martingales, Brownian motion.

name: Metal Cutting and Machine Tool Vibrations
description: Metal cutting and grinding mechanics; prediction of force-torque-power in turning, drilling, milling and grinding operations. Machine tool vibrations, forced and self-excited vibrations in machining, experimental modal testing of machine tools, chatter, and stability. Credit will be granted for only one of MANU 485 or MECH 592.

name: Commutative Algebra
description: Commutative algebra; homological algebra or representation theory of finite groups.

name: Factory Planning
description: Resources planning, layout and logistics. Modular production and cyber-physical manufacturing systems in laboratory scale, virtual manufacturing and factory automation.

name: Classical Differential Geometry
description: The differential geometry of curves and surfaces in three-dimensional Euclidean space. Mean curvature and Gaussian curvature. Geodesics. Gauss's Theorema Egregium.

name: Manufacturing for Clean Energy
description: Manufacturing and the net-zero energy transition; renewable, low-carbon and sustainable energy and electricity generation; energy, electricity transport, storage and batteries; hydrogen economy; carbon capture utilization and storage (CCUS).  Prerequisite: Third-year standing or greater.

name: AI and Machine Learning Applications in Manufacturing
description: Artificial intelligence, machine learning techniques, Deep learning, Python libraries for machine learning, Basic signal processing techniques, Data Acquisition, Applications in Manufacturing, Use of sound to evaluate operation of CNC machinery, Use of AE sensor to evaluate metal 3D printing

name: Mathematical Demonstrations
description: Students will prepare material illustrating ideas and applications of mathematics and present it to audiences outside the University. Intended for third or fourth year Mathematics students and Math/Science Education students.

name: Fields and Galois Theory
description: Field extensions, the Galois correspondence, finite fields, insolvability in radicals, ruler and compass constructions, additional topics chosen by instructor.

name: Manufacturing Processes II
description: Numerical modelling of manufacturing processes, linkage between material, process, properties and product geometry, heat/mass transport, thermodynamics and design principles applied to practical engineering processes.  Prerequisite: MANU 380.

name: Real Analysis II
description: Banach spaces, linear operators, bounded and compact operators, strong, weak, and weak* topology. Hahn-Banach, open mapping, and closed graph theorems. Hilbert spaces, symmetric and self-adjoint operators, spectral theory for bounded operators.

name: Introduction to Modern Differential Geometry
description: Smooth manifolds, smooth maps, immersions and submersions, vector fields, vector bundles, tangent and cotangent bundles, tensors and differential forms, orientation of manifolds, integration of forms, and selected topics.

name: Introduction to Topology
description: General topology, combinatorial topology, fundamental group and covering spaces, topics chosen by the instructor.

name: Turbulent Shear Flow
description: The basic equations of fluid motion; introduction to hydro-dynamic stability; Reynolds' equations; energy equations for turbulent motion; intermittency; similarity near a solid boundary and in free turbulence; approximate methods for predicting the growth of turbulent boundary layers and free symmetrical shear flows.

name: Computational Fluid Dynamics
description: Analytical, computational, and experimental methods in fluid mechanics. Overview of CFD program development. Finite volume methods, spacial discretization and spatial accuracy analysis. Boundary conditions. Time advance methods, time accuracy, and stability. Application to model problems and to the incompressible laminar Navier-Stokes equations. Validation techniques for CFD codes.

name: Advanced Topics in Computational Fluid Dynamics
description: Selected advanced topics in CFD, typically chosen from: Finite volume methods on curvilinear meshes and structured mesh generation. Finite volume methods on unstructured meshes. Multigrid methods for elliptic PDE's. Reynolds-averaged form of the Navier-Stokes equations and turbulence modelling. Three-dimensional flows. Compressible flows. Prerequisite: One of MECH 510, MECH 587.

name: Mathematical Classical Mechanics I
description: Newton's equation, conservation laws, the Euler-Lagrange equation; Hamilton's principle of least action, Hamilton's equations, Lagrangian mechanics on manifolds.

name: Number Theory
description: Divisibility, congruences, Diophantine equations, arithmetic functions, quadratic reciprocity, advanced topics. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion List:https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/faculty-science/bachelor-science/credit-exclusion-lists.

name: Research Seminar
description: Current topics in mechanical engineering research for M.A.Sc. students. Pass/Fail.

name: Special Topics in Mechanical Engineering
description: Special advanced lecture courses may be arranged for graduate students upon the approval of the department head. There will not be more than 6 credits in any one such course.

name: Doctoral Dissertation
description: Pass/Fail

name: Special Topics in Analysis
description: The student should consult the Mathematics Department for the particular topics offered in a given year.

name: Special Topics in Algebra
description: The student should consult the Mathematics Department for the particular topics offered in a given year.

name: Topics in Topology
description: Homology theory, homotopy theory, manifolds, and other topics chosen by the instructor.

name: Introduction to Number Theory
description: Euclidean algorithm, congruences, Fermat's theorem, applications. Some diophantine equations. Distribution of the prime numbers.

name: Media Communities
description: Media engagement with community partners through data, narrative and visual processes. Prerequisite: Restricted to BMS students with 1st year standing.

name: AI and Media Creation
description: Investigation of media objects shaped by algorithms, through a balance of foundational concepts and hands-on experimentation. Examines perspectives on aesthetics, the impact of technology on media, and ethics.

name: Special Topics
description: Selected topics in media studies. Not offered every year. Restricted to BMS students.

name: Project for M.Eng. Studies
description: Project on assigned topic of specialization. For students registered in the M.Eng. program whose project is supervised by a faculty member in the department of Mechanical Engineering.

name: Collaborative Methods
description: Development and practice of media group production processes. Restricted to BMS students with 2nd year standing or above.

name: Probability with Physical Applications
description: Random variables, discrete and continuous distributions. Random walk, Markov chains, Monte Carlo methods. Characteristic functions, limit laws.

name: Real Variables I
description: The real number system; real Euclidean n-space; open, closed, compact, and connected sets; Bolzano-Weierstrass theorem; sequences and series. Continuity and uniform continuity. Differentiability and mean-value theorems.

name: Seminar
description: Current topics in mechanical engineering for doctoral students. Pass/Fail.

name: Elementary Differential Equations II
description: Power series methods (ordinary and regular singular points, Bessel's equation); boundary value problems and separation of variables (Fourier series and other orthogonal series), applications to the vibrating string, heat flow, potentials.

name: Calculus IV
description: Parametrizations, inverse and implicit functions, integrals with respect to length and area; grad, div, and curl, theorems of Green, Gauss, and Stokes.

name: Introduction to Group Theory
description: Groups, cosets, homomorphisms, group actions, p-groups, Sylow theorems, composition series, finitely generated Abelian groups.

name: Introduction to Real Analysis
description: Ideas and methods of real analysis and their application. Countability and topology of the reals; convergence, continuity and differentiability of functions; metric spaces.

name: Thesis
description: For M.A.Sc. Pass/fail.

name: Real Variables II
description: The Riemann or Riemann-Stieltjes integrals. Sequences and series of functions, uniform convergence. Approximation of continuous functions by polynomials. Fourier series. Functions from Rm to Rn , inverse and implicit function theorems.

name: Topics in Number Theory
description: Topics chosen by the instructor. These might include: division algorithms, group theory, continued fractions, primality testing, factoring.

name: Applied Variant Interpretation
description: Human genome-wide sequencing (GWS) variant interpretation, with an emphasis on determining variant pathogenicity and significance in a clinical and research setting. Online. Restricted to students in the Graduate Certificate in Genomic Counselling and Variant Interpretation or others with permission of instructor.

name: Introduction to Abstract Algebra
description: Ideas and methods of group theory and their applications. Groups, subgroups, and cosets; homomorphisms, isomorphisms, and associated theorems.

name: Doctoral Dissertation
description: Pass/Fail.

name: Introduction to Mathematics
description: Intensive course with required tutorial. Combinatorics, probability, geometry and elementary number theory. Not for credit in the Faculty of Science. Students who obtain credit at UBC for any other mathematics course cannot in the same or later years obtain credit for MATH 335.

name: Introduction to Linear Programming
description: Linear programming problems, dual problems, the simplex algorithm, solution of primal and dual problems, sensitivity analysis. Additional topics chosen from: Karmarkar's algorithm, non-linear programming, game theory, applications.

name: Introduction to Discrete Mathematics
description: Introduction to ideas and methods of discrete mathematics and their application.

name: Molecular and Cellular Biology of Experimental Medicine
description: Cell and molecular function in normal tissues and in specific disease processes, including, genetic, viral, bacterial, immune, and physiological disorders.

name: Research Seminar
description: Reviews of research in selected areas of experimental medicine, including presentation of student's own research results.

name: Emerging Genomic Topics
description: Utility, impacts, and ethical implications of developing genomic applications; multiomics, tumour genomics, pharmacogenomics, population genomics. Online. Restricted to students in the Graduate Certificate in Genomic Counselling and Variant Interpretation or others with permission of instructor.

name: Advanced Research Topics in Genetic and Genomic Counselling
description: Qualitative and quantitative methodology, models of decision making, patient-oriented research, applied ethics, clinical genomics, diversity, privacy, health services, health policy, health economics and practice-based implications.

name: Algebra and Coding Theory
description: Error-correcting codes via abstract and linear algebra. Emphasis on proofs and computation. Finite fields, Hamming distance and error-correction, upper and lower bounds on the size of a code, linear codes, groups and cosets, encoding and decoding schemes.

name: Nephrology
description: Mechanisms of regulation of acid-base balance, fluid and electrolyte content, excretion of proteins and organic substances in kidney disease; abnormal renal mechanisms in hypertension.

name: Gastroenterology
description: Pathogenesis and abnormal physiology in disease of the intestine and accessory organs; carcinogenesis; regulatory peptides; liver disease; inflammatory bowel disease; oesophageal dysfunction.

name: Introduction to Rings and Modules
description: Rings, ideals, unique factorization, Euclidean rings, fields, polynomial rings, modules; structure theory of modules over a principal ideal domain.

name: Advanced Topics in Visual Sciences
description: Fundamental principles of vision from basic physiology to clinical syndromes across the visual pathway spanning the globe, ocular structures including the retina, up to striate and extrastriate cortices.

name: Advances in Neurology
description: Pathogenesis and immunological mechanisms in acute and chronic virus infections of the central nervous system; immunologically induced non-infectious neurological disease.

name: Evidence-Based Genomic Counselling
description: Genomic counselling skills and clinical insights; obtaining informed consent, variant appraisal, incidental and secondary findings, informing results, family communication. Online. Restricted to students in the Graduate Certificate in Genomic Counselling and Variant Interpretation or others with permission of instructor.

name: Introduction to Clinical, Patient Oriented and Translational Research
description: Framing appropriate research questions, appropriate research designs, protocol development, key concepts in regulatory approval and human ethical oversight in Canada, privacy and knowledge translation. For students pursuing clinical, patient oriented and translational research. Prerequisite: Permission of Experimental Medicine Program Director

name: Experimental Medicine Methodology
description: Laboratory experience with experimental models of human disease; critical reviews of their relevance. Laboratory rotations, oral presentations and written reviews. Registration requires permission of the Department.

name: Emerging Topics in Experimental Medicine
description: Restricted to students in one of: Master of Science in Experimental Medicine or Doctor of Philosophy in Experimental Medicine.

name: Pulmonary Pathophysiology
description: Same as PATH 518.

name: Clinical Genetics Clinic
description: A rotation for three months through the Clinical Genetics Clinic dealing with the techniques of diagnosis and counselling, and of the prenatal diagnoses of genetic disease and genetic counselling relative to congenital malformations and failures of reproduction.

name: Molecular Regulation of Cell Growth and Differentiation
description: Receptors, kinases, phosphatases, G proteins, adapters, transcription factors and other regulatory proteins involved in eukaryotic cell activation, growth and differentiation; defective cell signalling in human diseases; methods to track actions of toxins and drugs in experimental model systems. Prerequisite: A third-year or higher Biochemistry course.

name: Cardiovascular Pathophysiology
description: Pathogenesis, abnormal physiology and therapeutic approaches in heart disease including cardiac arrhythmia, heart failure, myocardial infarction, hypertension, atherosclerosis. Equivalency: PATH570

name: Experimental Medicine: Infectious Diseases
description: Supervised individual program of directed studies in experimental aspects of pathogenesis, diagnosis and treatment of infectious diseases, and mechanisms of host defence against microbial infections.

name: European Literature from the 5th to the 14th Century
description: Selected works from the 5th to the 14th centuries in their cultural and social contexts. Recommended pre-requisites: Third-year standing or above in the Faculty of Arts. Credit will be granted for only one of RMST_V 321 or MDVL_V 301. Equivalency: RMST_V 321.

name: Introduction to Medieval Studies
description: A survey of the study of the medieval period in Western Europe (400-1550), integrating history, literature, and the arts; topics vary from year to year; interested students should consult the Medieval Studies Advisor.

name: Introductory Medical Microbiology and Immunology
description: Introduction to cellular and humoral immune responses, the properties of viruses and the principles of bacterial pathogenesis. (Consult the Credit Exclusion list within the Faculty of Science section of the Calendar.) Prerequisite: One of BIOL 112, BIOL 200, BMEG 245, MICB 201, SCIE 001.

name: Introductory Environmental Microbiology
description: Prokaryotic diversity and the impact and applications of bacterial and archaeal metabolic, genetic, and growth processes in environmental contexts.  Prerequisite: One of BIOL 112, BIOL 200, SCIE 001. For students with BIOL 112, CHEM 121 is recommended.

name: Research Seminar in Medieval Studies
description: An intensive research seminar in a specific period, area, or issue integrating topics in medieval history, literature, and the arts; topics vary from year to year; interested students should consult the Medieval Studies advisor.

name: Data Science Research in Microbiology and Immunology
description: A team-based data science research experience in microbiology and immunology.

name: Topics in Microbiology, Immunology and Virology
description: Selected topics in a specific area within Microbiology, Immunology and Virology. May be taken more than once for credit with permission of the department.

name: Advanced Immunogenetics
description: Consult the Credit Exclusion List in the Faculty of Science section of the Calendar.

name: Co-operative Work Placement III
description: Work experience. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-operative Education Program in the Biotechnology or Microbiology and Immunology specializations. Pass/Fail Prerequisite: Either (a) MICB 399 or (b) BIOT 380. and completion of two co-op work terms.

name: Research Problem
description: A laboratory investigation in the final year of the Honours program. The results are presented in a written report, to be reviewed by oral examination.

name: Topics in Medieval Studies
description: Interdisciplinary approaches to selected topics in medieval history, literature, and the arts; topics vary from year to year; interested students should consult the Medieval Studies advisor.

name: European Literature from the 14th to the 16th Century
description: Selected works of the Late Middle Ages and Renaissance in their cultural and social contexts. Recommended pre-requisites: Third-year standing or above in the Faculty of Arts.

name: Co-operative Work Placement IV
description: Work experience in an industrial research setting, taken during the Winter Session (Term 1) of fifth year. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-operative Education Program in the Biotechnology or Microbiology and Immunology specializations. Pass/Fail Prerequisite: MICB 498.

name: Microbiological and Immunological Research
description: Developing, discussing, and undertaking research projects. Oral communication skills, peer review skills, scientific ethics, and the ability to critically evaluate papers in the literature.

name: Ordinary Differential Equations
description: Review of linear systems; nonlinear equations and applications; phase plane analysis; Laplace transforms; numerical methods. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion List:https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/faculty-science/bachelor-science/credit-exclusion-lists

name: Student Seminars in Microbiology, Immunology and Virology
description: Student seminars on selected papers from the microbiology, immunology and virology literature.

name: Directed Studies on an Approved Problem
Laboratory Research in Microbiology and Immunology
description: A team-based laboratory research experience in microbiology and immunology.

name: Topics in Molecular Pathogenesis and Immunology
Introduction to Complex Variables
description: Functions of a complex variable, Cauchy-Riemann equations, elementary functions, Cauchy's theorem and contour integration, Laurent series, poles and residues. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion List:https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/faculty-science/bachelor-science/credit-exclusion-lists

name: Vector Calculus for Electrical Engineering
description: Divergence, gradient, curl, theorems of Gauss and Stokes. Applications to Electrostatics and Magnetostatics. MATH 264 content is strongly coupled to BMEG 220 and ELEC 211 with topics and student evaluations weighted accordingly.

name: Differential Equations
description: Linear ordinary differential equations, Laplace transforms, Fourier series and separation of variables for linear partial differential equations. Consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion List:https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/faculty-science/bachelor-science/credit-exclusion-lists.

name: Applied Complex Analysis
description: Functions of a complex variable, Cauchy-Riemann equations, contour integration, Laurent series, residues, integrals of multi-valued functions, Fourier transforms. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion List:https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/faculty-science/bachelor-science/credit-exclusion-lists

name: Multivariable and Vector Calculus for Mechanical Engineering
description: Partial differentiation, extreme values, multiple integration, vector fields, line and surface integrals, the divergence and Stokes' theorems; applications to fluid mechanics: buoyancy, hydrostatic force, pipe flow, drag; applications to thermodynamics: work, entropy, heat transfer; numerical methods. Emphasis on mechanical engineering applications.

name: Introduction to Probability
description: Basic notions of probability, random variables, expectation and conditional expectation, limit theorems.  Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion List:https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/faculty-science/bachelor-science/credit-exclusion-lists

name: Data Science Research in Microbiology and Immunology
description: A team-based data science research experience in microbiology and immunology. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion List:https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/faculty-science/bachelor-science/credit-exclusion-lists.

name: Interdisciplinary Capstone Design Project
description: An extension to projects in the New Venture Design Program that introduces additional technical design principles and requirements. Registration for this program is only permitted for Mechanical Engineering students who are in the New Venture Design Program. Credit will be granted for only one of MECH_V 453, MECH_V 454, MECH_V 455, MECH_V 456, MECH_V 457, MECH_V 458, MECH_V 459, or MECH_V 490.

name: Industrial Engineering
description: Organizational structure. Manufacturing systems and group technology. Classification and coding. Scheduling and sequencing of operations. Forecasting. Quality control for variables and attributes. Plant location. System reliability analysis. Advanced manufacturing automation concepts.

name: Abstract Linear Algebra
description: Linear spaces, duality, linear mappings, matrices, determinant and trace, spectral theory, Euclidean structure. Consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion List:https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/faculty-science/bachelor-science/credit-exclusion-lists

name: Applied Analysis
description: Integrals involving multi-valued functions, conformal mapping and applications, analytic continuation, Laplace and Fourier transforms.

name: Fluid Mechanics
description: Governing equations; viscous incompressible flow, incompressible potential flow; incompressible boundary layers, stability and turbulence; compressible potential flow.

name: Differential Equations for Mechanical Engineering
description: First-order equations; linear equations; linear systems; Laplace transforms; trajectory analysis of plane nonlinear systems; translational and rotational vibrations; applications to RLC circuit analysis; numerical and graphical methods. Emphasis on mechanical engineering applications.

name: Research Communication
description: Scholarly writing and communication in engineering. Standard research genres such as journal articles, conference posters, and grant proposals. Students will write on the topic of their CREATE-U research. Prerequisite: MECH 497.

name: Applied Linear Algebra
description: Applications of linear algebra to problems in science and engineering; use of computer algebra systems for solving problems in linear algebra.

name: Partial Differential Equations
description: Introduction to partial differential equations; Fourier series; the heat, wave and potential equations; boundary-value problems; numerical methods. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion List:https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/faculty-science/bachelor-science/credit-exclusion-lists

name: Euclidean Geometry
description: Classical plane geometry, solid geometry, spherical trigonometry, polyhedra, linear and affine transformations. Linear algebra proofs are used. It is suggested that MATH 307 be taken concurrently.

name: Introduction to Stochastic Processes
description: Discrete-time Markov chains, Poisson processes, continuous time Markov chains, renewal theory. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion List:https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/faculty-science/bachelor-science/credit-exclusion-lists

name: Engineering Management
description: Organization structures. Management styles. Cost systems and control. Financial statements; accounting procedures. Budgets and performance control. Project management. Human resources management.

name: Thermodynamics
description: Thermodynamic principles, Maxwell relations, availability, irreversibility, and equilibrium. Introduction to statistical mechanics.

name: Computer-Aided Manufacturing
description: NC programming and machining with interactive CAD/CAM systems. Curve and surface geometry for tool-path generation. Tool-path generation methodologies. Geometric modelling techniques for simulation and verification of manufacturing processes. Introduction to Computer-Aided Process Planning. Supplementary tutorial laboratory experiments. Recommended co-requisites: MECH 392 or MANU 380.

name: Introduction to Academic Research
description: Research project directed by a faculty member in Mechanical Engineering. Prerequisite: Fourth-year standing and at least 80% average in third-year courses and permission of instructor.

name: Topics in Geometry
description: Topics chosen by the instructor. These may include conic sections, projective configuration, convexity, non-Euclidean geometries, fractal geometry, combinatorial problems of points in the plane.

name: Analytical Dynamics
description: Newtonian mechanics; generalized co-ordinates and analytical mechanics; Lagrange equations; Hamilton's Principle; rotational motion and rigid body dynamics; Gyroscopic motion; phase space, equilibrium, and stability of motion; stability characteristics of autonomous systems; Hamilton-Jacobi method; applications.

name: Historical Linguistics
description: How and why languages change over time, and how languages can be grouped into families based on historical relationships. Methods of comparative and internal reconstruction of phonological, morphological, syntactic, semantic change. Social factors in language change. Not offered every year. Prerequisite: LING 200 and LING 201.

name: Experimental Methods in Mechanics
description: Operating principles of transducers for measuring typical quantities; the construction of transducers and factors controlling their measurement accuracy; electronic signal conditioning equipment and computerized data acquisition system.

name: Research Skills and Data Analysis
description: Research environment, funding and dissemination systems; literature reviews and critically evaluating papers; creating research questions; research ethics, data security and research records; equity, diversity, and inclusion in research. Recommended pre-requisite: Third-year standing.

name: Sociolinguistics
description: The systematic study of language as a social phenomenon. Credit will be granted for only one of LING 445 or 315. Prerequisite: All of LING 200, LING 201.

name: Linear Elasticity
description: Stress and strain in three dimensions, fundamental field equations of linear elasticity; equilibrium, compatibility, Hooke's law; Papkovitch-Neuber solution, plane stress and plane strain; torsion, torsion of thin-walled members with warping restraint; plate theory.

name: Research Methods for Linguistics
description: Research methods used in linguistics and speech science. Emphasis on scientific reasoning, critical thinking, experimental design, and the ethics and methods of linguistic data-collection. Prerequisite: All of LING 200, LING 201.

name: Linear Vibrations
description: Transient and steady state vibration analysis of continuous and discrete mechanical systems. Lagrange's equation and Hamilton's Principle. Measurement of vibration. Machinery health monitoring. Frequency domain analysis. Experimental modal analysis. Vibration of rotating machinery.

name: Computational Models of Language
description: A re-examination of major areas of linguistics from a computational perspective, including popular formalisms and algorithms associated with morphology, syntax, semantics, and discourse. Prerequisite: LING 242 and one of LING 201, ENGL 331 and one of STAT 200, STAT 203, STAT 251, STAT 302, MATH 302, PSYC 218.

name: Introduction to Semantics
description: The analysis and theory of linguistic meaning with emphasis on formal techniques for semantic analysis and their application to empirical phenomena in language, including pragmatics. Prerequisite: LING 201.

name: Controls
description: State space model; stability; controlability; observability; Kalman decomposition; state feedback; observer; linear quadratic regulator; Kalman filter. Credit will be granted for only one of MECH 468 or 509.

name: Pragmatics
description: Selected topics in pragmatics and information structure, including variations in their cross-linguistic expression and the corresponding influence of sentence form on context. Prerequisite: One of LING 201, ENGL 331, PHIL 220, PHIL 222.

name: Morphology
description: Analytic and theoretical consideration of the interrelation of word formation, sound patterning, and meaningful sentence structure. Not offered every year. Prerequisite: All of LING 300, LING 311.

name: Honours Seminar in Linguistics
description: Research papers on general linguistic topics to be read and discussed.

name: Advanced Semantics
description: Current issues in semantic theory. Prerequisite: One of LING 327, PHIL 220, PHIL 222. A basic introduction to syntax is recommended (e.g., LING 100, LING 201, or ENGL 331).

name: Advanced Phonology
description: Current issues in phonological theory. Prerequisite: LING 311.

name: Field Methods I
description: Elicitation, transcription, organization, and analysis of linguistic data from a native speaker of a language not commonly studied. Practical experience in the use of fieldwork equipment. Prerequisite: All of LING 300, LING 311.

name: Jazz Ensemble (Lower Years)
description: Performance techniques and repertoire. May be taken twice for credit.

name: Contemporary Players (Lower Years)
description: Performance of contemporary music. An ensemble of variable size, including both instrumentalists and singers, will be formed to present several concerts of 20th-century music during the academic year. May be taken twice for credit.

name: World Music Ensembles (Lower Years)
description: Training on traditional instruments and their techniques, with emphasis on ensemble performance. Different sections focus on the music of different cultures, e.g., Bali, China, Ghana, Korea. May be taken twice for credit.

name: Intensive Chamber Ensemble (Lower Years)
description: Intensive coaching in chamber ensemble for advanced players. Performance of works prepared is expected. May be taken twice for credit. Corequisite: Any small ensemble (MUSC 156-166) and permission of the instructor.

name: Introduction to Piano Chamber Music
description: A survey of repertoire and performance issues.

name: Field Methods II
description: Elicitation, transcription, organization, and analysis of linguistic data from a native speaker of a language not commonly studied. Practical experience in the use of fieldwork equipment. Prerequisite: LING 431.

name: Language Across Time, Geography, and Society
description: A cross-linguistic exploration of language change, discussing theories, data, and methods. Topics can include change across historical time periods, lifespan; change across regions, within areas; change due to language contact and other social and cultural factors. Prerequisite: One of LING 319, LING 315, LING 445, ENGL 318, ENGL 319, ENGL 324 and two of LING 300, LING 311, LING 313, LING 327.

name: Introduction to Linguistics
description: General background to linguistic studies; the different approaches to the analysis of languages; synchronic and diachronic linguistics; phonetics, phonology, morphology, syntax, and semantics. Not available for credit toward a Major or Honours program in Linguistics.

name: Piano Chamber Ensembles (Lower Years)
description: Open to students by audition, with credit, as stipulated by their faculties.

name: Wind and Percussion Chamber Ensembles (Lower Years)
description: May be taken twice for credit. Open to students by audition, with credit, as stipulated by their faculties.

name: Advanced Syntax
description: Current issues in syntactic theory. Prerequisite: LING 300.

name: Music Performance (Major)
description: Private instruction, vocal or instrumental.

name: Music Performance (Secondary)
description: Private instruction, vocal or instrumental.

name: Music Performance (Concentration)
description: Private instruction, vocal or instrumental.

name: Risk Assessment for Mine Waste Management
description: Risk assessment and management topics including risk assessment methodologies, risk management, and decision-making under risk.

name: Music Performance (Secondary)
description: Private instruction, vocal or instrumental.

name: Advanced Mine Waste Management
description: Advanced geotechnical, hydrological, and water management aspects of mine waste management.

name: Music Performance (Concentration)
description: Private instruction, vocal or instrumental.

name: Lyric Diction
description: A study of the basic phonetics and accepted principles of lyric diction of the four languages most commonly used in concert and operatic repertoire: French, German, Italian, and English.

name: Music Performance (Major)
description: Private instruction, vocal or instrumental.

name: Risk Management of Tailings Storage Facilities
description: Prerequisite: MINE 581.

name: Music Performance (Concentration)
description: Private instruction, vocal or instrumental.

name: Mine Waste Management Case Studies
description: Case study analysis including design, construction, operations and closure of mine waste facilities.

name: Seminar
description: Topics in mining, mineral processing and the environment for M.A.Sc. and M.Eng. students.

name: Introductory Modern Arabic I
description: Basic listening, speaking, reading and writing skills in Modern Standard Arabic at the Beginning Elementary level.

name: Advanced Mine Site Management
description: Advanced mine site management topics including site and corporate governance and responsibility for mine waste facilities, specifically tailings; the role and responsibilities of the Engineer of Record; geochemistry of mine waste and mine closure realities.

name: Communication Skills and Workplace Readiness
description: Preparation for mining and mineral processing engineering internships. The course includes workshops on the following topics: developing a synopsis of qualifications, written communication and interviewing skills for the engineering professional. Pass/fail.

name: Special Advanced Topics
description: A special advanced course may be arranged upon the approval of the department head. Prerequisite: Permission of instructor is required.

name: The Middle East: Critical Questions and Debates
description: Critical questions and debates in Middle East Studies that shape scholarly and public perception of the region.

name: Directed Studies Project
description: Projects that provide essential knowledge and skills for academic and/or community engagement in Middle East Studies. May include academic works or presentations, community projects, and/or digital initiatives. Prerequisite: MES 300. and permission of instructor.

name: Topics in Middle East Studies
description: Topics will vary from year to year. Consult the program website (https://mes.arts.ubc.ca/courses/) for further details.

name: Engineering Project
description: A project involving laboratory, pilot plant or field work is to be completed in close collaboration with an academic advisor. For M.Eng. students only.

name: Mining Industry Internship
description: Mining or mineral processing engineering internship in which concepts, theory and practice of mining and mineral processing engineering are applied by working with industry on appropriate technical projects. Pass/fail. Prerequisite: MINE 591.

name: Birth and its Meanings
description: An interdisciplinary study of pregnancy and childbirth drawing on and integrating the disciplines of psychology, sociology, philosophy of science, anthropology, women's studies, and cultural studies.

name: Applied Health Services for Maternity Providers
description: Introduction to diagnostics related to cellular and humoral immune responses in pregnant women and newborns, the properties of viruses, epidemiology, the principles of bacterial pathogenesis, and related physiologic responses.

name: Reproductive Anatomy and Physiology
description: Covers the anatomy and physiology of conception, fetal growth, pregnancy, labour, birth, transition to extra- uterine life, postpartum and lactation through lectures and lab sessions. Emphasizes anatomy and physiology as related to professional midwifery practice.

name: Counselling for Maternity Care Providers
description: Theory, knowledge, strategies, and skills of person-centered counselling including family systems, trauma theory, theory, grief counselling, motivational interviewing skills, self-awareness and mindfulness, interprofessional communication, and cultural competency in continuity of care.

name: Theoretical Foundations for Midwifery Practice
description: Scope of practice of a midwife, regulatory framework, skills for basic midwifery practice. A series of lectures and clinical lab sessions.

name: Lactation and Infant Feeding for Maternity Care Providers
description: Breastfeeding physiology, pathophysiology, and strategies for support of the dyad based on best-practice principles. Discussion of major Canadian and international initiatives for the support and protection of breastfeeding.

name: Introductory Modern Arabic II
description: Continued development of basic listening, speaking, reading and writing skills in Modern Standard Arabic. Introduction to various aspects of Arab and Islamic culture. Prerequisite: ARBM 101.

name: Midwifery and Social Justice
description: Social justice frameworks and issues as they pertain to individuals' engagement with health care systems. Draws on various disciplines, including sociology, anthropology, gender studies, and cultural studies.

name: Seminar
description: Topics in mining and mineral processing for Ph.D. students.

name: Political Economy of the Modern Middle East
description: Roles of material and political forces, economic policies, and ideologies in the transformation of the Middle East. Topics include oil, colonial finance, trade, hydropower, industrialization, land reform, social reproduction, and geo-economic warfare. Restricted to students with second year standing or above.

name: Research Methods for Midwives
description: Research designs used in midwifery research, types of studies reported in the midwifery and health care literature, research methodology and basic principles of epidemiology, biostatistics and social research.

name: Physical Assessment
description: Principles of physical and psychological  assessment of the mother and neonate. A series of lectures and clinical lab sessions.

name: Pharmacology for Maternity Care Providers
description: An overview of basic concepts in pharmacology, pharmacy, and therapeutics relevant to the practice of midwifery in Canada.

name: CAD/CAM Principles and Practice
description: 3D geometric modelling; parametric representation of curves and surfaces; CNC machine tool programming; milling operations and setup; tool path generation for three- and five-axis sculptured surface machining.

name: Machine Tool Structures and Vibrations
description: Review of metal cutting mechanics, milling, static deformations of machine tools. Machine tool vibrations, forced and self-excited vibrations in machining, chatter, stability. Sensors for machine tool monitoring and adaptive control. Sensor assisted intelligent machining techniques.
