name: Midwifery Clinical Care - Antepartum, Postpartum and Newborn
description: Clinical care of women experiencing normal pregnancy, labour, birth, and puerperium. Clinical education experiences in preventative and therapeutic midwifery care with emphasis on prenatal and postnatal midwifery care. Clinical practice education opportunities within the province.

name: Research Writing
description: Credit will be granted for only one of MECH 498 or MECH 556. Equivalency: MECH 500X, MECH 500A, MECH 550U

name: Experimental Fluid Mechanics
description: Modelling Test facilities. Wind tunnel force measurement. Theory of conventional and modern manometry. Classical velocimetry. Hotwire anemometry. Theory and application of laser Doppler velocimetry. Particle image velocimetry. Flow visualization techniques. Thermometry. Credit will only be granted for one of MECH 489 or MECH 582.

name: Internal Combustion Engines
description: Analysis of spark and compression ignition engines. Calculation of fuel economy, power and emission. Practical and regulatory considerations in engine design. Numerical engine modelling and analysis. Credit will be granted for only one of MECH 478 or MECH 578.

name: Readings in Orchestral Repertoire
description: Standard repertoire for orchestral instrumentalists.

name: Multivariable Feedback Control
description: Well-posedness and internal stability of feedback systems, performance limitations, uncertainty, LFT representations, robust stability and robust performance, model reduction, linear matrix inequalities, H- infinity control, multi-objective control, mu-analysis and synthesis, H-infinity gain- scheduling, control applications. Recommended prerequisite: MECH 466, MECH 468, ELEC 341 or equivalent. Credit will be granted for only one of MECH 562, EECE 508, or ELEC 572.

name: Topics in the History of Music Theory
Combustion
description: Thermodynamics of combustion, stoichiometry, heat of formation and reaction. Equilibrium composition and adiabatic flame temperature. Chemical kinetics of combustion. Flames in premixed gases; laminar and turbulent flame propagation. Diffusion flames, pollutant emissions and combustion in IC engines.

name: Aerodynamics of Aircraft
description: Analysis of airfoils and wings. Potential flow, thin airfoil theory, lifting line analysis of wings. Predicting viscous drag. Numerical methods for analysis and design of airfoils and wings. Subsonic, transonic, supersonic, and hypersonic flow. Credit will be granted for only one of MECH_V 581 or MECH_V 481.

name: Emerging Topics in Thermodynamics, Fluid Mechanics, and Heat Transfer
Fuel Cell Systems
description: Energy system architecture and electrochemical energy conversion; fuel cell thermodynamics and electrochemistry; Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cells (PMFCs) and Solid Oxide Fuel Cells (SOFCSs); hydrogen production, storage, and distribution. Credit will only be granted for one of MECH 445 or MECH 577.

name: Robotics: Kinematics, Dynamics and Control
description: Definitions and classification Kinematics: homogeneous transformations, manipulator kinematic equations, forward and inverse kinematic solution methods, differential kinematic equations, motion trajectories. Dynamics: Lagrange-Euler formulations, Newton-Euler formulation. Control: methods, robot control hierarchy, control of single joint and multiple link manipulators, advanced control methods. Credit will be granted for only one of ELEC 442, EECE 571R, EECE 589, MECH 464, or MECH 563.

name: Convection Heat Transfer
description: Governing equations for laminar and turbulent flow. Forced convection in internal and external flow. Free, and combined free and forced convection. Heat transfer at high velocities, in rarefied gases and in two-phase flow. Mass transfer.

name: Composition
description: The composition of original music for conventional instruments and/or electronic media.

name: Composition
description: A continuation of MUSC 507. Prerequisite: [MUSC507]

name: Introduction to Music Research
description: Principal resources of the research library.

name: Seminar in Performance Practices
description: Studies in the theoretical and practical problems of musical interpretation.

name: Seminar in Notation of Polyphonic Music
Topics for Engineers in the Mining Industry
description: Leading practices and technologies employed in the Canadian Mining Industry. Topics include: mining, mineral processing, mine finance and mining and the environment.

name: Rock Fragmentation
description: Theory and practice of drilling and blasting; explosive types and strengths. Blast pattern design for underground and surface operations. Permission of the instructor is required.

name: Directed Individual Studies
description: Approval by the Director, School of Music, is required.

name: Integrated Mining and Processing Systems
description: Methods and systems for integrated mining and processing, conceptual model development, simulation, economic and technical evaluation. Permission of the instructor is required.

name: Processing of Mineral Fines
description: Particulate systems. Role of particle size and interfacial phenomena in properties of disperse systems. Stability of colloids and suspensions DLVO (Dejaguin-Landau-Vervey-Overbeek). Credit will be granted for only one of MINE 522 or MINE 572.

name: Processing of Precious Metal Ores
description: Advances in science and technology for recovering gold, silver, and platinum group elements. Credit will be granted for only one of MINE 524 or MINE 577.

name: Mine Ventilation
description: Mine air conditioning, ventilation network analysis, radioactivity in mining, case studies in mine ventilation and control of dust, fumes and diesel exhausts.

name: Simulation and Optimization of Mineral Processes
description: Mineral process simulators including off-line optimization strategies; optimal flow sheet design. Credit will be granted for only one of MINE 527 or MINE 576. Prerequisite: One of MINE 526, MINE 575.

name: Advanced Topics in Rock Engineering
description: Rock mass properties and numerical modelling applied to rock engineering design with particular emphasis on applications in rock slopes and tunneling. Permission of the instructor is required.

name: Advanced Coal Preparation
description: Thermal and metallurgical coals. Desulphurization Theory of coal beneficiation. Dense media separation. Coal surface properties and their effect on fine coal processing by flotation and oil agglomeration; coal/water/slurries. Plant performance testing and instrumentation. Permission of the instructor is required.

name: Block Caving Systems
description: Mass mining (caving) methods, their design and operation, the value proposition and the key value drivers.

name: Large Instrumental Ensemble
description: Symphony Orchestra or Wind Ensemble. Open only to graduate students.

name: University Chamber Orchestra
description: Open only to graduate students.

name: Mining Methods
description: A more advanced study of some aspects of mining methods. Permission of the instructor is required.

name: Rheology of Mineral Suspensions
description: Rheological measurements, flow curve modelling, micro-rheology, control of rheological properties. Application to mineral processing unit operations. Credit will be granted for only one of MINE 529 or MINE 579.

name: University Choral Union
description: Open only to graduate students.

name: University Singers
description: Open only to graduate students.

name: Mathematical Modelling of Mineral Processes
description: Emphasis on crushing, grinding, screening, classification and flotation. Credit will be granted for only one of MINE 526 or MINE 575.

name: Jazz Ensemble
description: Open only to graduate students.

name: Vocal Chamber Ensemble
description: Open only to graduate students.

name: Wind and Percussion Chamber Ensembles
description: Open only to graduate students.

name: University Chamber Strings
description: Open only to graduate students.

name: University Chamber Singers
description: Open only to graduate students.

name: World Music Ensembles
description: Training on traditional instruments and their techniques, with emphasis on ensemble performance. Different sections focus on the music of different cultures, e.g., Bali, China, Ghana, Korea.

name: Contemporary Players
description: Open only to graduate students.

name: Piano Chamber Ensembles
description: Open only to graduate students.

name: Early Music Ensemble
description: Open only to graduate students.

name: Advanced Human Molecular Genetics
description: Gene structure and regulation, genetic and epigenetic variation, genome and epigenome analysis, stem cell genetics, personalized genetics, bioinformatics, pharmacogenetics and genomics. Recommended pre-requisite: BIOL 335.

name: String Chamber Ensembles
description: Open only to graduate students.

name: Molecular and Cell Biology of Cancer
description: Focuses on molecular and cell biology of cancer through a series of lectures, reviews, student presentations and discussion. Recommended pre-requisites: One of BIOL 234, BIOL 335, BIOC 303, or consent of instructor. Equivalency: PATH531

name: Human Genetics
description: Human Mendelian and non-Mendelian inheritance and clinical applications of genetics. Recommended pre-requisite: BIOL 335.

name: Genetics and Ethics
description: This course is intended to serve the diverse needs of genetic counselling students, research graduate students in genetics, genetic residents and clinical fellows, other health professional students, and graduate students from other sciences and humanities.

name: Data analysis in Medical Genetics and Genomics
description: Methodology in data analysis applicable to the study of human genes, traits or diseases. Includes computer programming, foundational biostatistics, and data science methods. Prerequisite: All of BIOL 335 and BIOL 300

name: Introductory Clinical and Laboratory Rotation
description: Clinical experience in prenatal procedures and counselling; teratogen counselling. Clinically relevant experience in cytogenetics, molecular, biochemical disease and embryopathology laboratories. Pass/Fail Prerequisite: Acceptance into M.Sc. Genetic Counselling program.
prerequisites: Acceptance into M.Sc. Genetic Counselling program.

name: Concepts in Clinical Genetics for Genetic Counselling
description: Practical applications, theories, and principles of medical genetics as they apply to genetic counselling. Prerequisite: Acceptance into M.Sc. Genetic Counselling program.
prerequisites: Acceptance into M.Sc. Genetic Counselling program.

name: Advanced Genetic Counselling Seminar
description: Patient attitudes toward genetic counselling; the grieving process in response to pregnancy loss, death, and disability; risk perception, attitudes toward prenatal testing, dealing with results of genetic testing, crisis counselling, giving bad news; ethical dilemmas; legal and professional issues. Prerequisite: MEDG 560. And acceptance into M.Sc. Genetic Counselling program.
prerequisites: Acceptance into M.Sc. Genetic Counselling program.

name: Directed Studies
description: Investigation of readings and research undertaking topics of media studies, with the agreement, and under the supervision, of a faculty member with relevant expertise. Restricted to BMS students with approval from the Program Chair.

name: Genetic Counselling Seminar
description: Medical and genetic interviewing and family history taking; decision making; family dynamics; impact of congenital defects, genetic disease, and chronic disease on individuals and families; support groups and other community resources; computer resources; cross-cultural issues. Prerequisite: Acceptance into M.Sc. Genetic Counselling program.
prerequisites: Acceptance into M.Sc. Genetic Counselling program.

name: Advanced Clinical Rotation
description: In-depth clinical experience in general and prenatal genetic counselling. Pass/Fail Prerequisite: MEDG 570. And acceptance into M.Sc. Genetic Counselling program.
prerequisites: Acceptance into M.Sc. Genetic Counselling program.

name: Directed Studies
description: A series of laboratory sessions, directed readings and directed counselling interviews related to selected areas of Medical Genetics. This advanced course may be taken upon approval of the department head.

name: M.Sc. Thesis
description: Pass/Fail.

name: Genomic Testing and Clinical Bioinformatics
description: Annotation, filtering, and candidate variant calling skill development with a clinical focus; yield, benefits, and limitations of genome-wide sequencing. Online. Restricted to students in the Graduate Certificate in Genomic Counselling and Variant Interpretation or others with permission of instructor.

name: Seminar
description: All seminars will be presented by graduate students in the Department of Medical Genetics. Although students will be encouraged to attend these seminars throughout their graduate studies, credit will only be available for one year.

name: Approaches to Writing for Media Studies
description: Interdisciplinary perspectives of thematic topics in contemporary media and related theory with focused attention on writing practices. Restricted to BMS students with 3rd year standing.

name: Media Environments
description: Collaborative planning and activation of media interfaces for stakeholders informed by multidisciplinary approaches. Prerequisite: MDIA_V 290. Restricted to BMS students with 3rd year standing or higher.

name: Current Topics in Medical Genetics Research
description: Critical discussion of current primary research literature in medical genetics.

name: Directed Studies
description: Advanced research undertaking topics of media studies, with the agreement and under the supervision, of a faculty member with relevant expertise. Prerequisite: Restricted to BMS students with approval from the Program Chair.

name: Immunogenetics
description: Molecular basis of lymphocyte development, activation and adhesion; immunogenetics and the major histocompatibility complex. Consult the Credit Exclusion list within the Faculty of Science section of the Calendar. Prerequisite: MICB 302 and one of BIOL 334, BIOL 335. A standing of B or better is recommended. Equivalency: MICB402

name: Emerging Media Practitioners
description: The roles and responsibilities of media producers as agents of transformation, with a focus on the student's own media decisions and artefacts. Prerequisite: MDIA_V 350. Restricted to BMS students with 4th year standing.

name: Human Genomics and Medical Genetics
description: Sequence and structure of the human genome. Human genetic evolution. Identification of genes affecting normal and pathological variation. Molecular mechanisms of genetic diseases and disorders. Medical applications of human genetics.

name: Directed Studies
description: A supervised individual program of study of a topic to be agreed upon by a member of faculty and the student. Permission of the appropriate supervisor and the department head is required.

name: Genetics and Cell Biology of Cancer
description: Molecular mechanisms of oncogenes and tumor suppressors in cancer biology, methods of and insights from studying cancer genomes, and current topics in cancer research. Prerequisite: BIOL 335 and one of BIOC 302, BIOC 303.

name: Capstone Media Projects
description: Advanced media works created in collaboration with community partners for public impact. Prerequisite: MDIA_V 350. Restricted to BMS students with 4th year standing.

name: Developmental Origin of Human Disorders
description: Genetic and epigenetic determinants of development from conception to birth. Topics include development of the neural tube, face, heart, endoderm, blastocyst, embryonic stem cells, gastrulation, genomic imprinting, placental complications, chromosomal abnormalities and prenatal diagnosis. Discussions based on published research articles. Prerequisite: One of BIOL 233, BIOL 234 and one of BIOL 331, BIOL 335. A standing of 'B' or higher recommended.

name: Special Topics
description: Selected topics in media studies. Not offered every year. Prerequisite: Restricted to students with 3rd year standing or higher.

name: Mammalian Developmental Genetics
description: Genetic determination of morphology and differentiation in human and other mammalian embryos. Recommended pre-requisite: BIOL 335.

name: Acid Rock Drainage
description: Lectures and seminars on topics of importance in acid rock drainage including fundamentals of ARD generation, prediction, prevention, control, treatment and monitoring for waste management and regulatory control in the mining industry. Credit will be granted for only one of MINE 540 or MINE 580.

name: Applied Underground Rock Mechanics
description: Study of design methods; underground engineering of openings, pillars and support. Emphasis on design with input being stress, structure and rock mass, employing analytical, empirical and numerical tools.

name: Mining Geostatistics
description: Basic geostatistical concepts. Applications of geostatistical techniques and stochastic simulation to orebody modelling and grade control.

name: Environmental Risk Assessments in Relation to Mining
description: Advanced topics related to mining environment selected in consultation with the instructor.

name: Advanced Immunogenetics
description: Cell-cell interaction, intracellular control mechanisms, analysis of complex physiological systems using transgenic animals and molecular approaches. Equivalency: MICB502

name: Genome Analysis
description: Investigation of genetic information as it is organized within genomes, genetic and physical map construction, sequencing technologies, gene identification, database accessing and integration, functional organization of genomes from contemporary, historic and evolutionary perspectives. Recommended pre-requisite: BIOL 234.

name: Energy from the Earth: Renewable Versus Conventional
description: Coal, oil, gas, uranium, hydro, wind, geothermal, and geosolar.

name: Treatment of Mineral Industry Effluents
description: Characteristics of mineral dispersions in gases and in water; dust suppression in mining and in mineral transport facilities; solid-liquid separations; removal of noxious chemicals; waste disposal systems. Credit will be granted for only one of MINE 533 or MINE 573. Prerequisite: Permission of instructor is required.

name: Mining and Society
description: Discussion of social, political and technical topics concerning mining-related activities. Credit will be granted for only one of MINE 555 or MINE 583.

name: Safety of Tailings Storage Facilities
description: Safety evaluation of tailings storage facilities as a system, including tailings transport and containment structures. Consequence classifications. Credible failure modes. Breach analyses. Risk management and reporting. Emergency planning. Critical controls. Change management. Governance frameworks. Prerequisite: Permission of instructor is required.

name: Modelling of Industrial Systems
description: Use of mathematical programming, network theory, queuing models and simulation to model service and production operations in industry. Use of models in decision-making.

name: Mining Environment Case Studies
description: Regulatory requirements for mine-mill environmental protection in design, operation and closure. Studies of environmental impact statements and closure plans. Credit will be granted for only one of MINE 544 or MINE 574.

name: Indigenous Peoples and Mining in Canada
description: Permission of the instructor is required.

name: Comprehensive Midwifery Theory and Practice
description: In-depth review of the theoretical principles and evidence basis for comprehensive midwifery care through tutorials and case reviews.

name: Clinical Clerkship
description: Students assume a primary care role in clinical placements in midwifery practices across the provinces. Demonstration of independent decision making and application of the full range of their academic knowledge to professional practice. A practicum under the supervision of a registered midwife. Pass/Fail.

name: Midwifery Self-Directed Course
description: Unique self-directed elective learning opportunities.

name: Industrial Expert Systems
description: The use of artificial intelligence to solve complex problems in industry. Topics include knowledge acquisition, knowledge representation, knowledge accumulation, and conflict resolution. Credit will be granted for only one of MINE 547 or MINE 578.

name: Maintenance Engineering
description: The analytical foundation for maintenance of industrial plant equipment and mobile equipment in various production environments. Reliability theory, sensing technology and theory, risk analysis, and operations research applied to maintenance management.

name: Mineral Resources Engineering II
description: The design, planning, and operation, and closure of mining operations, with a focus on mineral processing technologies, plant design, waste and tailings management, and the future of mining. Prerequisite: MINE 200.

name: Mineral Resources Engineering I
description: Introduction to the mining life cycle and the design, planning, operation, and closure of mining systems, with a focus on mining methods, mineral processing, community engagement, and social license to operate.

name: Mineralogy for Mining Engineering
description: Fundamentals of the rock and minerals formation. Exploring main techniques used to understand implications of mineralogy in mining and mineral processing.

name: Mine Economics and Finance
description: Mine valuation using discounted cash flow analysis and option pricing methods. Sources of mine finance and requirements. Sensitivity and risk assessment. Introduction to metals marketing, hedging and risk management.

name: Introduction to Mineral Processing
description: Overview; extracting a mineral or final product from an ore. Prerequisite: MINE 224.

name: Underground Mining and Design
description: Selection, design, and development of underground mining methods based upon physical, geological, economic, and environmental constraints. Underground excavation methods and equipment selection. Prerequisite: Third-year standing.

name: Introduction to Mining
description: Leading practices and technologies employed in the design, planning, and operation of mining systems. Life cycle of surface and underground mining systems.

name: Rock Fragmentation
description: Theory and practice of rock fragmentation by drilling and blasting; introduction to explosives and initiation systems; design of surface and underground blasts; machine excavation systems for tunneling and stoping; environmental impacts, safety, and risk assessment. Prerequisite: Third-year standing.

name: Mineralogy for Resources Engineering
description: Fundamentals of rock and minerals formation. Exploring main techniques used to understand implications of mineralogy in mining and mineral processing. Prerequisite: CHEM 154

name: Surface Mining and Design
description: Surface mining methods, calculation of pit limits, cutoff grades, break-even criteria, stripping ratios, ultimate pit depth and dimensions, and pit sequencing. Geotechnical inputs to surface mine design. Loading and hauling equipment, production rates, capacity and systems. Prerequisite: Third-year standing.

name: Seminar
description: Oral presentation of topics by instructor and guest lecturers.

name: Rock Engineering Fundamentals
description: The study of the mechanical and structural properties of rock materials at the laboratory and field scale, with reference to common mining, geological and civil engineering problems. Prerequisite: One of MECH 260, CIVL 230.

name: Seminar
description: Oral presentations of topics on mine safety, and mining engineering by industry practitioners, faculty and/or stake- and rights-holders.

name: Engineering Economics
description: Discrete and continuous cash flow models, discounted cash flow analysis, effects of depreciation and taxes, economic analysis of projects, sensitivity and risk analysis, financing and cost of capital.

name: Mine Ventilation and Occupational Health and Safety
description: Design and analysis for ventilation systems for mining. Topics such as ventilation design, ventilation surveys, thermodynamic aspects, psychrometry of air and air conditioning.

name: Strategic Issues in Mining
description: Strategic issues in an organization; types of organizations; personnel evaluations and job rating systems; impact of manpower planning on decision-making; union negotiations; public relations; dealing with the media; corporate responsibilities to society and employees.

name: Flotation
description: Theory and technology of flotation and ancillary processes.

name: Physical Mineral Processes
description: Mineral processing unit operations and sampling, crushing, grinding, screening, classification, gravity separation, magnetic separation, electrostatic separation, concentrate dewatering practices. Prerequisite: Third Year Standing.

name: Mine Project Valuation and Risk Assessment
description: Mineral economics and finance. Analytical tools and techniques used in the valuation of mining companies and the financial analysis and risk assessment methods.

name: Introduction to Risk Management for Mining and Large Industrial Projects
description: Risk management and its application to mining and large industrial projects, including risk analysis, treatment, and governance.

name: Mineral Process Control
description: Automatic control theory, PID control, Laplace and z-transforms, loop tuning, frequency response, stability analysis, control strategies in flotation, comminution, dewatering, reagent and bin/sump levels, automated load-haul-dump and drilling equipment, instrumentation and soft sensors.

name: Applied Geostatistics
description: Geostatistical analysis and simulation of spatiotemporal phenomena in natural and engineered systems with applications to mining problems.

name: Mine Waste Management
description: Basic geotechnical, hydrological, and water management aspects of mine waste management.

name: Processing Precious Metal Ores
description: Process alternatives and mineralogical considerations; physical and chemical recovery technologies; environmental protection; flowsheet studies.

name: Rock Engineering Design
description: The design of rock slopes and underground openings with respect to stress, structure and the rock mass. Stabilization and monitoring of rock movement.

name: Modelling and Simulation
description: Methods for determining the behaviour of large scale industrial systems and their application to the design and analysis of such systems.

name: Music Performance (Secondary)
description: Private instruction, vocal or instrumental.

name: Mineral Deposit Modelling
description: Types of mineral deposits. Exploration and sampling methods. Methods for data analysis and computer modelling of mineral deposits and their use in production planning and design.

name: Music Performance (Secondary)
description: Private instruction, vocal or instrumental.

name: Music Performance (Major)
description: Private instruction, vocal or instrumental.

name: Music Performance (Secondary)
description: Private instruction, vocal or instrumental.

name: Plant and Process Design
description: Design of unit operations in a mineral processing plant including crushing, grinding, classification, gravity separation, magnetic separation, flotation, thickening and filtration. Equipment selection and sizing, flowsheet design, circuit analysis and processing options.

name: Intensive Chamber Ensemble
description: Intensive coaching.

name: Readings in Orchestral Repertoire
description: Continuation of MUSC 506.

name: Music Performance (Major)
description: Private instruction, vocal or instrumental.

name: Music Performance (Major)
description: Private instruction, vocal or instrumental.

name: Intensive Specialized Chamber Ensemble
description: Intensive coaching.

name: Opera Repertoire I
description: A musico-dramatic study and analysis of representative works in the international operatic theatre from 1600 to the present, through musical, literary and graphic sources. Each sequential year of study, the student is expected to show increased facility in musical and dramatic analysis as well as a greater understanding of the works under examination. Open to students outside the B.Mus. program by permission of the instructor.

name: Composition
description: Further study for doctoral candidates in Composition.

name: Large Instrumental Ensemble (Lower Years)
description: Symphony Orchestra, Symphonic Wind Ensemble, or Concert Winds. May be taken twice for credit. Open to students by audition, with credit, as stipulated by their faculties.

name: Music Performance (Major)
description: Private instruction, vocal or instrumental. May be repeated for credit, in accordance with program requirements.

name: Music Performance (Major)
description: Private instruction, vocal or instrumental.

name: University Singers (Lower Years)
description: May be taken twice for credit. Open to students by audition, with credit, as stipulated by their faculties.

name: Music and Human Experience
description: A multi-disciplinary survey of music in selected world traditions and genres, connecting it to ideas of time, evolution, history, anthropology, philosophy, and contemporary globalised culture.

name: Seminar in Analytical Techniques
description: Not open to Master's students or to Ph.D. students in Music Theory. Prerequisite: One of MUSC_V 500, MUSC_V 410, MUSC_V 411, MUSC_V 412, MUSC_V 413.

name: Piano Repertoire I
description: Performance and discussion of the repertoire for string-keyboard instruments essential to the performer and teacher. Special attention to matters of structure, style, and performance practices. Required of piano performance majors and open to piano concentrators, space permitting. First term prerequisite to second term.

name: Early Music Ensemble (Lower Years)
description: Performance of early Western instrumental and vocal ensemble music. May be taken twice for credit. Open to students by audition, with credit, as stipulated by their faculties.

name: Class Voice
description: Group instruction in music performance. Required of all first-time secondary voice students. Restricted to B.Mus. students.

name: Advanced Orchestration and Arranging
description: Prerequisite: [MUSC509]

name: Collaborative Piano I
description: Skills and performance practice with primary emphasis on voice/piano partnership principles and repertoire. Strong sight-reading skills essential. For Piano majors; open to others by audition.

name: Class Woodwinds
description: Group instruction in music performance. Restricted to B.Mus. students.

name: University Chamber Orchestra (Lower Years)
description: May be taken twice for credit. Open to students by audition, with credit, as stipulated by their faculties.

name: Vocal Chamber Ensembles (Lower Years)
description: May be taken twice for credit. Open to students by audition, with credit, as stipulated by their faculties.

name: String Chamber Ensembles (Lower Years)
description: May be taken twice for credit. Open to students by audition, with credit, as stipulated by their faculties.

name: Advanced Studies in Modern Arabic Language and Cultures
description: Advanced-level Arabic written and oral language course focused on contemporary topics related to Arab and Arabic-speaking cultures. Recommended: Provide evidence of ACTFL Advanced High or CEFR C1.1 proficiency in Modern Standard Arabic or placement test with course instructor.

name: Aural Skills I
description: Sight singing; melodic and harmonic dictation; rhythm production; error detection; tuning; perception of harmony, form, and tonality; improvisation in set idioms.

name: Intermediate Modern Arabic II
description: Continued development of listening, speaking, reading and writing skills in both standard and spoken Arabic, and further exploration of various aspects of Arab culture. Recommended pre-requisite: ARBM 201 or placement approval and permission of the instructor

name: University Choral Union (Lower Years)
description: May be taken twice for credit. Open to students by audition, with credit, as stipulated by their faculties.

name: Introduction to the Theory of Music
description: Concepts of rhythm, pitch, timbre, and texture. Notation and aural recognition of rhythmic and pitch patterns. Basic principles of melody and form. Background in Western music theory or notation unnecessary.

name: University Chamber Strings (Lower Years)
description: May be taken twice for credit. Open to students by audition, with credit, as stipulated by their faculties.

name: Principles of Musical Form
description: Explain rhythmic, melodic, textural, and harmonic materials and processes of music, and how they create small-scale structures. Fluency with music notation advised.

name: Introduction to Diatonic Harmony
description: Triads, key and elementary harmony in Western music. Elements of musical form. Aural training and exercises in composition, modeled on historical styles. Not for credit in the B.Mus. Prerequisite: [MUSC103] or permission of the instructor.

name: History of Music I
description: An overview of Western music from antiquity through the Middle Ages and Renaissance, providing a framework for understanding musical styles and practices, and examining selected compositions in greater analytical and historical depth.

name: Diatonic Harmony and Voice Leading
description: Harmonic and linear functions of diatonic chords; common progressions and sequences; introduction to tonal hierarchy and prolongation; simple modulation. Compositional and analytical exercises. Prerequisite: One of MUSC 100, MUSC 110.

name: Class Piano I
description: Required of all first-time secondary piano students.

name: Aural Skills II
description: Continuation of MUSC 105. Restricted to B.Mus. students. Prerequisite: a score of 68% or higher in MUSC_V 105. Students may register for MUSC_V 106 prior to meeting the pre-requisite but will be required to withdraw if the pre-requisite is not met by the first day of class.

name: Introduction to Contemporary Art Music
description: Contemporary music repertoire, emphasizing music from the past fifty years.

name: Class Brasses and Percussion
description: Group instruction in music performance.

name: Composition I
description: An introduction to musical composition.

name: Intermediate Modern Arabic I
description: Continued development of listening, speaking, reading and writing skills in both standard and spoken Arabic, and further exploration of various aspects of Arab culture. Recommended pre-requisite: ARBM 102 or placement approval and permission of the instructor.

name: Introduction to Music Technology
description: Practical and theoretical training in technologies that support current artistic and academic practice, such as MIDI, podcasts/videocasts, websites, social media, and software for score notation, music education, and basic audio/video editing.

name: Special Topics in Mechanical Engineering
description: Lectures and readings on specialized topics of current interest in Mechanical Engineering.

name: Industrial Fluid Mechanics
description: Analysis of piping networks. Review of pumps, turbines and hydraulic motors. Flow measurement devices such as flow meters and transducers for measuring velocity and pressure. Multiphase flows. Introduction to turbulence, mixing and buoyancy driven flows.

name: Sensors and Actuators
description: Measurement of motion, stress, force, torque, temperature, flow and pressure; principles of sensors and signal conditioning methods; selection and sizing of actuators.

name: History of Music II
description: The development of Western music from circa 1600 to circa 1800. Prerequisite: MUSC 120. Or permission of the instructor

name: Engineering in Society and Technological Stewardship
description: Societal influences that affect engineering activities, including interactions between engineering and the economic, health, safety, legal, and cultural aspects of society; uncertainties in the prediction of such interactions; industrial policy; sustainable development; entrepreneurship; and environmental and technological stewardship.

name: Mechatronics System Instrumentation
description: Architecture of mechatronics devices; integration of mechanical, electronics, sensors, actuators, computer and real time software systems; PLC and PC based systems; discrete and continuous automation system design.

name: Air Pollution, Technology and Society
description: Causes and effects of air pollution in the context of technology and society. Topics include: impact of air pollutants on air quality and climate, atmospheric science, public policy, collective action, environmental justice, science communication, economic externalities, and ethical engineering design. Recommended pre-requisite: third-year standing.

name: Introduction to Microelectromechanical Systems
description: Fundamentals of MEMS (MicroElectroMechanical Systems). Microfabrication of MEMS with solid-state technology. LIGA and micro injection molding. Physics of MEMS. Operational principles of various MEMS devices.

name: Manufacturing Processes
description: Manufacturing characteristics of materials and their control. Metal forming processes, plastic deformations, rolling, forging, drawing, extrusion, sheet metal forming. Machining processes and machine tools, turning, milling, drilling, grinding. Metal fabrication, welding and casting. An introduction to process planning.

name: Professionalism and Ethics in Engineering
description: Professionalism, ethical frameworks, decolonization, equity, diversity, inclusion, law. Obligations of the engineer.

name: Mechanical Design
description: Design of shafts and welded joints. Fatigue and fracture considerations in design: failure types, failure under static and dynamic loading, fatigue failure, crack initiation, and propagation. Introduction to the FEM in mechanical design. Students can only receive credit for one of MECH 326 or MECH 426.

name: Environmental Microbiology Laboratory
description: Microbiological analysis of environmental samples using culture-dependent and culture-independent methods.

name: Engineering Economics
description: Discounted cash flows. Sources of funds, cost of capital. Effects of depreciation, taxes, inflation. Evaluation and comparison of economic models for engineering projects. Replacement decisions. Public project analysis. Risk analysis. Project control, inventory analysis, simulation. Recommended pre-requisite: third-year standing.

name: Mechatronic Product Design
description: Design of mechatronic systems for industrial and human-centric applications compliant structures; electronic circuits to interface with sensors and actuators; embedded systems; precision timing and control; data acquisition and processing; user interfaces; and product innovation.

name: Orthopaedic Biomechanics
description: Musculoskeletal anatomy. Muscle and joint loads. Muscle mechanics. Musculoskeletal dynamics. Gait. Tissue mechanics of tendon, ligament, articular cartilage, and bone. Biomaterials. Application examples in orthopaedics including joint replacement and fracture fixation. Credit will be granted for only one of MECH 435 or MECH 535. Students who have received credit for BMEG 230 or 330 cannot also receive credit for MECH 435.

name: Advanced Immunology
description: Molecular basis of lymphocyte development, activation and adhesion; immunogenetics and the major histocompatibility complex. Consult the credit exclusion list within the Faculty of Science section of the calendar.

name: Engineering Data Analysis
description: The use of probability and statistical methods for engineering applications.

name: Biofluids
description: Review of principles, Navier-Stokes equations, biorheology, circulatory biofluid mechanics, synovial fluid in joints, biofluid dynamics of the human brain, respiratory biofluid mechanics, flow and pressure measurement techniques in human body. Credit will be granted for only one of MECH 433 or MECH 533.

name: Topics in Molecular Virology
description: Presentations, library research, paper reviews, class discussions about current research in virology. Topics such as molecular targets in viral therapy; chronic viral infection; virus-host cell interaction.

name: Bioinformatics
description: Computational methods to analyze genome and protein sequences to derive structural and functional information. Related topics in functional genomics.

name: Industrial Microbiology and Biotechnology
description: Exploitation of microbial and animal cells for the industrial production of chemicals ranging from alcohol to therapeutic proteins. Genetic manipulation of cellular characteristics, fermentation methods, patenting and governmental approval processes.

name: Viral Infections in Humans.
description: Interactions between viruses and humans; pathogenesis; persistence and viral oncogenesis; virological diagnosis and treatment. (Consult the Credit Exclusion list within the Faculty of Science section of the Calendar.)

name: History of Popular Music
description: Genres of popular music from 1950 to the present and their changing aesthetic, social, cultural, and historical dimensions. Prior experience with music notation and terminology is not required.

name: Experimental Microbiology
description: Research in microbial physiology and molecular genetics. Guided and independent laboratory projects are developed.

name: Topics in Microbiome Research
description: Critical examination and discussion of contemporary research literature concerning the impact of host-associated microbiomes on host development, health and disease with a focus on humans. Priority given to students in Microbiology and Immunology specializations.

name: Music Appreciation
description: An introductory course for which previous musical background is helpful, but not required. Contents include a discussion of musical concepts, evolution of forms, style, and media and detailed study of selected works from the concert repertoire. Popular forms of music (jazz, folk, rock, etc.) not included.

name: The Guitar in History and Practice
description: Introduction to guitar performance and repertoire for non-majors. Lectures explore guitar repertoires from selected regions and eras. Students are expected to provide their own guitars.

name: Accompanying on the Harpsichord I
description: Basic techniques and styles of continuo playing. Open to keyboard players with no previous harpsichord experience.

name: World Music Cultures
description: Introduction to the principles of ethnomusicology and an examination of at least two contrasting musical traditions. May be repeated once for credit if different traditions are covered.

name: Topics in Immunological Research
description: Presentations, library research, paper reviews and class discussion on selected areas of advanced molecular and cellular immunological research.

name: Topics in Western Music
description: Study in one major genre of Western music (e.g., The Symphony, Women in Opera, History of the Song Cycle). No musical knowledge is required.

name: Directed Research
description: A library (3 credits) or laboratory (3 or 6 credits) project. Requires permission of the Undergraduate Advisor. The results are presented in a written report to be reviewed by oral examination.

name: Seminar in Microbiological Literature
description: Student seminars on selected papers from the microbiological literature.

name: Topics in Molecular Bacterial Pathogenesis
description: A lecture/discussion/library research course. Topics such as antibiotic resistance, pathogen genomics; host-pathogen interactions; evolution of pathogens; host responses to infection, invasive mechanisms, resistance mechanisms.

name: Music Appreciation, Twentieth-Century
description: Designed for students with little or no musical background.

name: Microbial Ecological Genomics
description: Intrinsic and extrinsic forces driving prokaryotic genome evolution. Gene transfer; microbial species concepts; community genome structure, function and dynamics; ecological impacts of microbial genome diversity. Emphasis on problem solving and experimental design.

name: Opera Theatre Techniques I
description: Performance techniques associated with the musical theatre of various historical periods. Basic dance. Most operatic excerpts will be in English.

name: An Introduction to Pulp and Papermaking
description: Overview of pulp and paper operations. Conversion of wood to fibre through mechanical or chemical pulping, processing of recycled fibre, the papermaking process and paper converting operations. Contemporary developments.

name: Workshop in World Rhythm
description: Theory and practice of selected rhythmic systems of world music cultures, focusing on West African drumming, and including other systems such as Indian Tala and Peking opera percussion. Prerequisite: MUSC 200.

name: Experimental Molecular Biology
description: A laboratory course with a choice of independent, supervised research projects. Students develop protocols to carry out investigation of selected molecular biology problems.

name: Computer Control of Mechatronics Systems
description: Block diagrams and transfer functions, continuous and discrete domain transformations, feedback control system characteristics, control design in both continuous and discrete domain, absolute and relative stability, laboratory examples of Mechatronic systems design. Credit will be granted for only one of MECH 467 or MECH 541. Credit cannot be obtained for both MECH 466 and MECH 467.

name: Advanced Bacterial Pathogenesis
description: Current and emerging themes in bacterial pathogenesis including cellular microbiology, bacterial cell biology processes and their role in virulence including secretion systems to deliver virulence factors and immune evasion strategies employed by pathogens. Development of antibiotics and resistance to antibiotics.

name: Energy Conversion Systems
description: Energy supply and demand. Energy conversion chain. Electrical power generation using thermal power plants, renewable energy, and fuel cells. Rankine cycle steam power. Brayton cycle gas turbine power plants, intercooling, reheat, and regeneration. Internal combustion engines. Exhaust gas after treatment. Combined and binary cycles. Nuclear power.

name: Aesthetics and Practice of Film Music
Keyboard Harmony and Transposition
description: Designed for the keyboard performance major and keyboard concentrator in General Studies.

name: Opera Workshop I
description: Participation in performances by the School. Open also to students outside Music without credit, after audition.

name: Cantonese Music
description: A history of musical genres with Cantonese lyrics from the nineteenth century to the present. Topics include music and text relationships, major singers, major genres (narrative songs, Cantonese opera, Cantopop). Credit will be granted for only one of MUSC_V 327 or ASIA_V 335. Equivalency: ASIA_V 335.

name: Aerospace Propulsion
description: Cycle analysis of jet engines, thermodynamic cycles, mechanics and thermodynamics of combustion, components and the performance characteristics of chemical rockets. The detailed analysis of operating characteristics of turbojet, turbofan, turboprop, afterburning, and ramjet propulsion systems.

name: Heating, Ventilating and Air Conditioning
description: Principles of air conditioning; psychometrics and refrigeration. Heat transfer through building materials. Estimation of heating and cooling loads including the use of current software. System design. Ground, air and water source heat pumps.

name: Music in Vancouver's Ethnic Communities
description: Examination of music within the ethnic context as found in the urban environment of Vancouver. The musics of several traditions (e.g., Chinese, Jewish, English folk) will be studied together with the social issues surrounding their preservation. For credit toward the B.Mus. and the B.A. in Music, but open to students not majoring in music.

name: Modern Control Engineering
description: Introduction to state space control methods for linear systems including modal control, controllability, observability, linear quadratic regulators, optimal control. Recommended co-requisite: MECH 366 or MECH 466.

name: Introduction to Computational Fluid Dynamics
description: Techniques for numerical solution of ordinary and partial differential equations, including an introduction to the finite difference, finite volume and finite element approaches. Simulation of laminar and turbulent flows, including common turbulent models. Validation techniques. Recommended pre-requisite: MECH 380.

name: Piano Pedagogy I: Theory and Studio Management
description: Basic principles of teaching piano. Business aspects of establishing and maintaining a music studio. For Piano Performance majors; open to other Bachelor of Music students by permission of the instructor.

name: Dynamic System Modelling
description: Modelling of mechanical, electrical, fluid, and thermal systems; analytical models; model representations such as linear and bond graphs; response analysis; digital simulation. Recommended pre-requisite: third-year standing.

name: Aerodynamics of Aircraft
description: Analysis of airfoils and wings. Potential flow, thin airfoil theory, lifting line analysis of wings. Predicting viscous drag. Numerical methods for analysis and design of airfoils and wings. Subsonic, transonic, supersonic, and hypersonic flow. Credit will be granted for only one of MECH_V 481 or MECH_V 581.

name: Experimental Thermofluids
description: Experimental uncertainty. Design of experiments. Test facilities. Temperature and pressure measurement techniques and instrumentation. Velocity and flow rate measurement techniques. Flow visualization. Case studies of industrial and research experimental practice. Credit will be granted for only one of MECH 489 or MECH 582.

name: Internal Combustion Engines
description: Analysis of spark and compression ignition engines. Calculation of fuel economy, power, and emission. Practical and regulatory considerations in engine design. Engine emission and control systems. Recommended pre-requisite: MECH 327. Credit will be granted for only one of MECH 478 or MECH 578.

name: Industrial Mixing
description: Fundamentals of mixing technology, and industrial mixing systems and equipment. Selection, design, monitor, and scale-up mixing systems for mining applications. Prerequisite: MATH 255 and one of MECH 280, CIVL 215.

name: Dewatering of Fine Tailings
description: Interparticle forces; DLVO theory of colloid stability; dispersion, coagulation, and flocculation phenomena; settling; thickening and consolidation processes; polymers in mineral processing; measurement techniques in tailings treatment; thickeners and principles of operation; industrial practice. Prerequisite: Third-year standing

name: Aircraft Design: Structures
description: Structural components of aircraft, introduction to the finite element method, bending and buckling of thin plates. Design of aircraft wing and fuselage structures, moments of inertia for complex shapes.

name: Aircraft Stability and Control
description: Aircraft performance, stability and control, loading and air worthiness. Detailed example.

name: Mine Water Management
description: Mine water management covering integrated water resource management, water balances, sources, water use optimization, water quality and treatment and long-term stewardship. Prerequisite: Third-year standing.

name: Advanced Process Mineralogy
description: Textural parameters, such as mineral liberation size and mineral associations in connection with the mineral processing techniques for mineral recovery. Prerequisite: MINE 331.

name: Introduction to Ship Design
description: This course introduces the ship design process from a Systems Engineering point of view. Topics include ship operational requirements, space and weight estimation, parametric design, optimization techniques, and the impacts of ship design on economics and the environment. Credit will be granted for only one of MECH_V 486 or NAME_V 581.

name: Indigenous Peoples and Mining in Canada
description: Historical context of Indigenous peoples of Canada interactions with the development of mineral resources. Current best practices and systems supporting effective engagement and involvement of Indigenous peoples in the development of mines and mineral resources. Prerequisite: Third-year standing.

name: Introduction to Ship Hydrodynamics
description: Ship terminology, lines plans, ship hydrostatics, transverse and longitudinal stability of ships, dimensional analysis, ship resistance prediction; ship propulsion methods, propeller selection and design. Recommended prerequisites: One of MECH 380 or CIVL 315, or enrollment in the NAME MEng or NAME MEL program.

name: Materials Handling
description: Knowledge and understanding of equipment used in mining operations, including diesel, electro-mechanical, hydraulic and pneumatic equipment as well as conveyors, load-haul-dump trucks and pumps. Prerequisite: Third-year standing.

name: Coal Preparation Technology
description: Thermal and metallurgical coals: objectives of their cleaning; coal washability and flotability fundamentals; coal preparation unit operations; performance characteristics of coal washing equipment; products dewatering; plant flowsheets. Prerequisite: MINE 331.

name: Cave Mining Systems: Design and Planning
description: Designs, planning, and leading practices are applied to underground mining systems reliant on induced and controlled rock mass caving. Prerequisite: MINE 303.

name: Urban Mining: Recovering Value From E-waste
description: Technological and social issues related to the recovery of value from e-waste seen through the eyes of engineers, social scientists and economists. Recovery of valuable minerals in the context of circular economy to provide sustainable solutions for our planet. Prerequisite: Third-year standing

name: Foundations of Microbiology
description: Prokaryotic diversity and the impact and applications of microbial metabolic, genetic, and growth processes in environmental contexts. Bacteria-human interactions in health and disease, mode of action of antibiotics and antibiotic resistance, virulence factors of bacteria, and host response to infection.

name: Fundamental Data Science in Microbiology and Immunology
description: Foundations in data science course that incorporates the use of biological data science tools to perform survey-level analysis of microbiology and immunology datasets.

name: Mining and The Environment
description: Environmental topics of importance to engineers practicing within the mining, metallurgical and related industries including technical practices, regulatory and public issues.

name: Heavy Oil Sand Mining and Processing
description: Life cycle of the production of Oil Sands resources, including mining, bitumen extraction, and reclamation. Prerequisite: MINE 310.

name: Basic Microbiology Laboratory
description: Procedures and principles associated with isolation, characterization and handling of microorganisms. Intended for students requiring a basic microbiology laboratory course.

name: Mine and Plant Engineering Design Feasibility Study
description: Mining Engineering design project from scope definition to final design and project feasibility. Based on a problem from industry and/or research. Prerequisite: All of MINE 302, MINE 303, MINE 310, MINE 331, MINE 333, MINE 350, MINE 396.

name: Directed Studies
description: Requires approval of the department head.

name: Seminar
description: Oral presentation of a technical nature. Use of closed circuit television for personal evaluation. Prerequisite: Fourth-year standing in Mining Engineering.

name: Maintenance Engineering
description: Analytical foundation for maintenance of industrial plant equipment and mobile equipment in various production environments; maintenance planning and management, life cycle analysis, reliability theory, total quality maintenance, condition monitoring. Prerequisite: Fourth-year standing.

name: Microbial Ecophysiology
description: Dynamics and control of prokaryotic cellular processes in response to the biotic and abiotic environment including metabolic interactions and metabolic cooperation between microorganisms.

name: Co-operative Work Placement II
description: Work experience. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-operative Education Program in the Biotechnology or Microbiology and Immunology specializations. Pass/Fail

name: Molecular Immunology and Virology Laboratory
description: Genetic manipulations of bacteria, introductory immunological and virological procedures, tissue culture. Restricted to students in Microbiology and Immunology specializations.

name: Data Science in Microbiology and Immunology Research
description: A team-based data science research experience in microbiology and immunology.

name: Midwifery Theory for Primary Care
description: Care of normal pregnancy, labour, birth, and puerperium with an emphasis on the intrapartum period and assessment and management skills. Includes a four-week intensive session in Vancouver, a series of online tutorials, and simulation and skills lab practice.

name: Analysis of Microbial Genes and Genomes
description: Genetic, molecular biological and bioinformatic approaches for the analysis of microbial genomes, gene structure-function and gene expression with emphasis on bacteria.

name: Evidence-Informed Midwifery
description: Principles of evidence-informed midwifery, what counts as evidence? Making sense of the evidence, applying the evidence in practice.

name: Immunology
description: Mechanisms of innate and adaptive immune responses. Hematopoiesis, development of T and B lymphocytes, leukocyte migration, antigen processing/presentation and the major histocompatibility complex, immune responses against pathogens, and diseases associated with aberrant immune responses.

name: Paradigms in Bacterial Pathogenesis
description: Mechanisms of bacterial pathogenesis including adherence, invasion, intracellular survival, toxins, host defenses and microbial evasion strategies, antibiotics, and vaccines. Introduction to experimental approaches used to study bacterial pathogens.

name: Food Microbiology Laboratory
description: Procedures and principles associated with isolation, enumeration, characterization and handling of microorganisms. Restricted to students registered in the Food Science program.

name: Primary Research Directed Studies
description: An original piece of scholarship that builds on knowledge and skills acquired from coursework and in consultation with faculty mentors. This self-directed course can be taken in year 1, 2, or 3 of the Program.

name: Molecular Microbiology Laboratory
description: Aseptic handling and characterization of microbes, growth properties, enzyme assays, protein analysis and plasmid isolation. Restricted to students in Microbiology and Immunology specializations.

name: Molecular Virology
description: Introduction to virus structure and replication. Detailed examination of selected viruses including polio, HIV and cancer-causing retroviruses. Development of vaccines and anti-viral drugs, the use of virus vectors to cure genetic diseases.

name: Professionalism in Community-based Care
description: Prepares students for interprofessional and community-based placements. Professionalism and principles of community health and healthcare in rural and remote, Indigenous communities, and global health contexts. Prerequisites: MIDW_V 305 and MIDW_V 320. Corequisite: MIDW_V 326

name: Midwifery Clinical Care - Abnormal and Unexpected Conditions
description: Clinical education for midwifery care of pregnancy, birth, and the puerperium with an emphasis on abnormal situations in pregnancy, labour and birth, and in newborns. Clinical practicum around the province. Pass/Fail.

name: Ethics in Maternity Care
description: Application of ethical theory in midwifery and health care management.

name: Introductory Immunology & Virology
description: Innate and adaptive immune responses to bacterial and viral pathogens, autoimmunity, allergies and graft rejection; virus structure, replication cycles, pathogenesis and vaccines; data analysis of foundational immunology and virology experiments.

name: Dialogue and Decisions: Advancing Person-Centred Care
description: Build knowledge and competencies to navigate complex human interactions around decisions in health care. Flexible, online course for health professional learners. Learning activities include small group, cross-profession discussions, best practice video exemplars, case-based and self-reflection exercises, and a simulation. This course is open to all health professions learners. For Midwifery students: Prerequisites: MIDW_V 305 and MIDW_V 320. Corequisite: MIDW_V 328.

name: Midwifery Theory for Antepartum, Postpartum and Newborn Care
description: Online situation-based learning tutorials occurring simultaneously with MIDW 200 clinical placement.

name: Midwifery Clinical Care - Variations of Normal
description: Clinical education experiences with the preventative and therapeutic midwifery care of pregnancy, birth, and the puerperium. Emphasis on the recognition and management of variations of normal and findings outside normal. A 10-week practicum in locations around the province. Pass/Fail.

name: Co-operative Work Placement I
description: Work experience. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-operative Education Program in the Biotechnology or Microbiology and Immunology specializations. Pass/Fail

name: Midwifery Primary Care Clinical
description: Clinical course focusing on consolidation of skills and knowledge of all aspects of midwifery care.

name: Introduction to Fluid Mechanics
description: Fluid properties; statics; kinematics, dynamics, energy, and momentum principles for control volumes; dimensional analysis and similarity; laminar and turbulent flow; pipe flow; principles of centrifugal pumps.

name: Midwifery Clinical Care - Intrapartum and Postpartum
description: Clinical education experiences with the preventative and therapeutic midwifery care of normal pregnancy, labour, birth, and puerperium with an emphasis on the intrapartum period and assessment and management skills. A clinical practicum in locations around the province. Pass/Fail.

name: Data Analysis and Mechanical Engineering Laboratories
description: The use of probability and statistical methods for engineering applications. Mechanics of materials, heat transfer, and fluid dynamics. Instrumentation, data acquisition, and data manipulation using modern computational tools.

name: Thermodynamics II
description: Air standard and vapor cycles; first and second law of cycles. Exergy. Gas mixtures. Energy conservation. Equilibrium. Reacting systems. Application to thermofluid systems such as power plants.

name: Theory for Advanced Midwifery Care
description: Theoretical principles for midwifery care of pregnancy, labour, birth, newborns, and the puerperium. Emphasis on assessment and management skills for abnormal situations. Includes a five-day intensive session in Vancouver, a series of online tutorials, and lab practice.

name: Midwifery Theory for Variations in Primary Care
description: Theoretical principles of care for pregnancy, birth, and the puerperium with an emphasis on the recognition and management of variations of normal and findings outside of normal. Consists of a one-week intensive time in Vancouver, during which emergency skills certification is acquired, and weekly web-based tutorials.

name: Interprofessional Placements in Perinatal Health
description: Eight weeks of rotation through different interprofessional clinical settings. Students develop inter-professional competencies, working with and learning the roles and scopes of various general practitioners and/or specialists in perinatal care. Pass/Fail. Prerequisites: MIDW_V 322, MIDW_V 326 and MIDW_V 328. Corequisite: MIDW_V 365

name: Engineering Analysis
description: Fourier series; auto- and cross-correlation; power spectra; discrete Fourier transform; boundary-value problems; numerical methods; partial differential equations; heat, wave, Laplace, Poisson, and wave equations. Applications to mechanical engineering and practical computing emphasized.

name: Introduction to Mechanics of Materials
description: Statically determinate frames and trusses; normal and shear stresses and strains; shear force and bending moment diagrams; theory of beam bending, torsion of circular rods; transformation of stress and strain in two and three dimensions, Mohr's circle; yield and ultimate failure criteria.

name: Mechanical Engineering Design Project
description: Applying the design process, making educated assumptions and decisions, and working in teams to provide a new mechanical design. Weekly lecture discussing product development and various factors affecting the design.

name: Data Analysis and Mechatronics Laboratories
description: The use of probability and statistical methods for engineering applications. Mechanics of materials and heat transfer. Instrumentation, data acquisition, and data manipulation using modern computational tools. Common mechanical devices. For students in the Mechatronics Option only.

name: Community Health Placement
description: A student-selected, four-week clinical or non-clinical placement in one of 4 settings: global community health, rural and remote community health, Indigenous community health, or a self-selected focus in community health. Pass/Fail. Prerequisites: MIDW_V 322, MIDW_V 326 and MIDW_V 328. Corequisite: MIDW_V 355

name: Machine Design
description: Selection of flexible drives, bearings, fluid power system components, and couplings. Design of shafts, bolted joints and power screws. Design and selection of gears, gear trains, and mechanisms. Recommended co-requisite: MECH 360.

name: Modelling of Mechatronic Systems
description: Modelling of mechanical, electrical, thermal, fluid elements and mixed mechatronic systems. Signal processing, signal conditioning. Sensors, data acquisition systems, actuators.

name: Engineering Measurements and Instrumentation
description: Industrial measurement needs including: architecture of electronic instrumentation systems; electrical representation of physical quantities; sensors and actuators; analog signal processing using linear and non-linear circuits; computer-based readout including programming for user-interface and data acquisition.

name: Fluid Dynamics
description: Review of principles, compressible flow, potential flow, simple laminar viscous flow, boundary layers, flow around bluff bodies.

name: Mechanics of Materials
description: Beam deflections, singularity functions; use of tabulated solutions; column buckling; Castigliano's theorem, statically indeterminate beams, bending of beams with asymmetric cross-sections, shear centre; principal stresses and stress invariants in three dimensions.

name: Materials for Mechanical Design
description: Selection of material properties for mechanical design. Metals and alloys, ceramics, polymers, composites and other hybrid materials.

name: Computational Methods for Mechanical Engineering
description: Computational methods for solving mechanical engineering problems. Numerical computation of linear and nonlinear algebraic equations; interpolation and extrapolation; numerical integration and differentiation; numerical solution of differential equations. Credit will be granted for only one of MECH 358 or MECH 359.

name: Introduction to Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery
Oral Medicine and Oral Diagnosis
description: Oral diagnosis, including orofacial pain and temporomandibular disorders.

name: Advanced Oral Radiology and Oral Radiography
Endodontics
description: Application of the basic principles of endodontics.

name: Oral Radiology
description: Radiographic techniques and radiological interpretation with emphasis on extraoral techniques.

name: Heat Transfer
description: Steady and transient conduction. Radiation heat transfer. Convective heat and mass transfer in pipes and from external surfaces. Design of heat exchangers.

name: Oral Medicine, Oral Diagnosis and Therapeutics
description: Assessment and treatment of advanced periodontal diseases.

name: History of Renaissance Music
description: Sacred and secular music, vocal and instrumental. Prerequisite: MUSC 120.

name: Directed Research in Oral Biology
description: An elective laboratory project taken with the permission of the appropriate supervisor and the department head.

name: University Chamber Orchestra (Upper Years)
description: May be taken twice for credit. Open to students by audition, with credit, as stipulated by their faculties. Restricted to students with 3rd year standing or above. Prerequisite: MUSC 151.

name: Romantic Music
description: Prerequisite: MUSC 220.

name: History of Music Since 1900
description: Prerequisite: [MUSC221]

name: Large Instrumental Ensemble (Upper Years)
description: Symphony Orchestra, Symphonic Wind Ensemble, or Concert Winds. May be taken twice for credit. Open to students by audition, with credit, as stipulated by their faculties. Restricted to students with 3rd year standing or above. Prerequisite: MUSC 150.

name: History of Medieval Music
description: Sacred and secular music, vocal and instrumental. Prerequisite: All of MUSC 120, MUSC 121.

name: History of Jazz
description: Jazz styles and their cultural contexts; the relationship of performers and audiences; issues of race and gender; non-Western influences. Prerequisite: MUSC 221.

name: Topics in Social and Environmental Planning to Foster Health of Populations
description: Characteristics of social and built environments for their impact on the health of populations.

name: Graduate Practicum in Nursing
description: Restricted to students in the Master of Health Leadership and Policy. Pass/Fail. Equivalency: NURS_V 579.

name: Classical Music
description: Prerequisite: MUSC 121.

name: Song Repertoire I
description: An exploration of the solo art song repertoire from 1600 to the Romantic period. Repertoire essential to the performer and teacher will be studied through live and recorded performance with special attention given to poetic content and musical style. Prerequisite: [MUSC221]

name: String Chamber Ensembles (Upper Years)
description: May be taken twice for credit. Open to students by audition, with credit, as stipulated by their faculties. Restricted to students with 3rd year standing or above. Prerequisite: MUSC 160.

name: Leadership in Knowledge Application and Translation
description: Prerequisite: NURS 580.

name: Baroque Music
description: Prerequisite: MUSC 121.

name: Wind and Percussion Chamber Ensembles (Upper Years)
description: May be taken twice for credit. Open to students by audition, with credit, as stipulated by their faculties. Restricted to students with 3rd year standing or above. Prerequisite: MUSC 162.

name: University Chamber Strings (Upper Years)
description: May be taken twice for credit. Open to students by audition, with credit, as stipulated by their faculties. Restricted to students with 3rd year standing or above. Prerequisite: MUSC 159.

name: Piano Chamber Ensembles (Upper Years)
description: May be taken twice for credit. Open to other students by audition, with credit, as stipulated by their faculties. Restricted to students with 3rd year standing or above. Prerequisite: MUSC 161.

name: History and Repertoire of the Guitar and Related Instruments
description: A chronological survey, from the Renaissance to the present day, of music for the guitar and related instruments and of the development of the instruments themselves. Instruments considered include Renaissance and Baroque lutes, the vihuela, and early types of guitar as well as the modern six-string guitar. Musical forms and genres, national schools and the works of principal composers of every period are explored and attention is given to national systems, continuo realization, historical ornamentation and pedagogical systems. Prerequisite: [MUSC221]

name: Master's Thesis
description: Corequisite: NURS 511.

name: The Philosophy of Evidence
description: Students not enrolled in the doctoral program require permission of instructor. Prerequisite: NURS 511.

name: Recreation and Tourism Planning
description: Principles and methods for planning urban and rural recreation and related tourism resources including analyzing recreation resources, applying policies and standards, developing park/recreation area management plans, and understanding benefits to human and community wellbeing and biodiversity.  Prerequisite: Third-year standing.

name: Graduate Practicum in Nursing
description: Equivalency: NURS 577.

name: Directed Studies in Nursing
description: Prerequisite: NURS 511.

name: Topics in Conservation Genetics
description: The genetics of small populations, inbreeding, extinction risks due to genetic versus demography factors, adaptation and climate change, and methods for assessing genetic diversity for conservation planning. Equivalency: ZOOL524

name: Seminar in Biological Conservation
description: Topics in conservation biology with application to current issues and particular reference to (but not limited to) forested ecosystems.

name: Conservation Policy
description: Examination of international and Canadian conservation agreements and policies as instruments of distributive justice. Application of contemporary theories of justice to conservation policy issues.

name: Ecological Restoration
description: Global overview of ecological restoration, examining perspectives and practices in diverse ecosystems worldwide. Causes of degradation, motivations for restoration (including cultural underpinnings), restoration objectives (biodiversity, ecosystem function, ecosystem services), restoration practices (and their evolution over time), challenges and lessons learnt.

name: Ethical and Professional Issues in NP Practice
Forest Conservation in Asia: Challenges and Opportunities
description: Key forest conservation issues in Asia, regional strategies, programs, and practices for restoration of critical landscapes, rehabilitation of terrestrial ecosystems and conservation of flagship species.

name: Primate Conservation in the Anthropocene
description: Modern-day threats facing primates and the wide range of conservation strategies being implemented globally to protect them. Prerequisite: Third year standing.

name: Science and Expertise in Global Environmental Governance
description: Structures of global environmental governance, how science and expertise shape the evaluation and incorporation (or not) of diverse forms of knowledge into decisions, failings of global environmental regimes and what can be done to support transformative change.

name: Social Science Research Methods and Design for Natural Resource Management
Advanced Ship Structures
description: Pressure hull design; finite element analysis applications; classification rules; ice and ice loads; dynamic loads including slamming, risk and reliability. Prerequisite: CIVL 435.

name: Human Wildlife Conflict
description: Evaluation of the impacts of human wildlife conflicts on wildlife populations; application of innovative methods to reduce human wildlife conflicts. Prerequisite: Third-year standing or higher. BIOL 230 or FRST 395 and APBI 315 or APBI 416 recommended. Equivalency: APBI495

name: Thesis or Special Project
description: An independent study or research project of a subject of special interest to the student under the supervision of a staff member.

name: Pursuing Innovative Solutions to Big Questions
description: Multidisciplinary approaches to solving pressing challenges in natural resources. Diversifying perspectives of natural resources and land stewardship. Skill-building in written and verbal communication, collaboration, and critical thinking.

name: Pathways in Natural Resources
description: Exploration of disciplines within natural resources, including majors in the B.Sc. in Natural Resources degree, potential career pathways, and post-graduate education options.

name: Music Performance (Secondary)
description: Private instruction, vocal or instrumental.

name: Music Performance (Major)
description: Private instruction, vocal or instrumental.

name: Music Performance (Secondary)
description: Private instruction, vocal or instrumental.

name: Forest Ecology
description: The structure and function of forest ecosystems, including: energetics; productivity; nutrient, carbon and water cycling; soils; the physical environment; population and community ecology; disturbance ecology; ecological succession; biological diversity and ecological resilience. Credit will be granted for only one of NRES_V 201 or FRST_V 201.  Corequisite: One of NRES_V 200, FRST_V 200. Equivalency: FRST_V 201

name: Special Topics in Naval Architecture and Marine Engineering
Topics in Ethnomusicology
description: Topics involving methodology and fieldwork in non-Western traditions. Topics will vary and students should consult the School as to areas of focus in any given term.

name: Forest Plant Biology II
description: The functional biology of trees and other forest plants in their environment, with an emphasis on gymnosperms. Credit will be granted for only one of NRES_V 210 or FRST_V 210.  Prerequisite: One of NRES_V 200, FRST_V 200. Equivalency: FRST_V 210

name: Scholarly Writing and Argumentation in Natural Resources
description: Communicating concepts of forestry and links to human and environmental activities through writing, elements of argumentation, evaluating evidence, and searching for and citing references to back up claims; small-class experience. Credit will be granted for only one of NRES 150 or FRST 150 or LFS 150.  Equivalency: FRST 150, LFS 150

name: Land One: First-year Integrative Seminar
description: Current issues and cases in Forestry and Land and Food Systems are examined with a focus on integration of first-year subjects and exposure to both First Nations and Western perspectives.  Equivalency: LFS 110, FRST 110.

name: Forest Plant Biology I
description: The structure, diversity and development of trees and other plants, with emphasis on the angiosperms. Credit will be granted for only one of NRES_V 200 or FRST_V 200.  Prerequisite: BIOL_V 121. Equivalency: FRST_V 200

name: Introduction to Ethnomusicology
description: Preliminary studies in the discipline of ethnomusicology, with an emphasis on history and orientations.

name: Seminar in Conducting and Repertoire I
description: Advanced study of conducting techniques and of representative major compositions and literature (earlier historical periods). Emphasis on knowledge and conducting skills that can communicate a thorough understanding of genre, idiom, form, texture, and style, in rehearsal and performance. Prerequisite: Restricted to M.Mus. Conducting (Choral, Orchestral, Wind) or permission of the instructor.

name: Seminar in Ethnomusicology
