description: Partial and directional derivatives; maxima and minima; Lagrange multipliers and second derivative test; multiple integrals and applications. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion List:https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/faculty-science/bachelor-science/credit-exclusion-lists
prerequisites: One of MATH 101, MATH 103, MATH 105, MATH 121, SCIE 001.

name: Calculus III
description: Analytic geometry in 2 and 3 dimensions, partial and directional derivatives, chain rule, maxima and minima, second derivative test, Lagrange multipliers, multiple integrals with applications. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion List:https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/faculty-science/bachelor-science/credit-exclusion-lists.
prerequisites: One of MATH 101, MATH 103, MATH 105, MATH 121, SCIE 001.

name: Advanced Calculus II
description: Parametrization of curves and surfaces; line and surface integrals; theorems of Green, Gauss, Stokes; applications to physics and/or introduction to differential forms. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion List:https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/faculty-science/bachelor-science/credit-exclusion-lists
prerequisites: MATH 226. Prerequisite grade requirement: 68% in MATH226.

name: Drug Metabolism and Toxicology
description: The biotransformation of drugs, pesticides, carcinogens and other foreign chemicals in animals and humans. The biochemical mechanisms responsible, particularly the cytochrome P-450 mono-oxygenases, will be emphasized. The formation of toxic reactive metabolites and their effects will be discussed. Enrolment restricted.

name: Basic Theory & Practice of Isothermal Titration Calorimetry
description: Isothermal titration calorimetry thermodynamic concepts and practical applications in measuring molecular interactions.

name: Pharmaceutical Research Techniques II
description: Immunological assays, capillary and gel electrophoresis, radioisotope techniques, PET, peptide analysis and receptor binding studies.

name: Topics in Pharmacology
description: Lectures and supervised studies in selected areas of pharmacology. Enrolment restricted.

name: Advanced Laboratory in Pharmacology
description: A laboratory course giving instruction in the methods and techniques used in pharmacological research. Registration limited.

name: Marvels of Mathematics
description: A variety of topics in mathematics, showcasing its beauty and utility. Intended for a general audience of students whose degrees have no mathematics requirements, but who may be curious about practical and recreational mathematics. Not for credit in the Faculty of Science. Students who obtain UBC credit for any other mathematics course cannot in the same or later years obtain credit for MATH 230.

name: Advanced Calculus I
description: Functions of several variables: limits, continuity, differentiability; implicit functions; Taylor's theorem; extrema; Lagrange multipliers; multiple integration, Fubini's theorem; improper integrals. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion List:https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/faculty-science/bachelor-science/credit-exclusion-lists
prerequisites: Either (a) a score of 68% or higher in MATH 121 or (b) a score of 80% or higher in one of MATH 101, MATH 103, MATH 105, SCIE 001.

name: Pharmaceutical Research Techniques I
description: Spectroscopic, GC, HPLC, LCMS and NMR analytical techniques for drug analysis, pharmacokinetics and metabolism.

name: Cardiovascular Pharmacology
description: A course composed of lectures, assigned readings and conferences dealing with aspects of drug actions and cardiovascular function. Topics include the role of adenylate cyclase in cardiac function, the role of calcium in myocardial contractility and the effect of drugs on myocardial and vascular function. Enrolment restricted. Given in alternate years.

name: Cell Culture and New Biomedical Approaches
description: Basic cell culture techniques and novel insights into alternative methods in biomedical research.

name: Central Nervous System Pharmacology
description: A course comprised of lectures, assigned readings and reports on selected topics dealing with drug actions in the central nervous system. Given in alternate years. Permission of instructor required.

name: Analytical Techniques and Basic Tests in Clinical Chemistry
description: Biochemistry tests in clinical medicine and the analytical chemistry techniques used to produce the results; pathophysiology of common clinical conditions. Prerequisites: PATH_V 308. Credit will be granted for either PATH_V 406 or PATH_V 413 and PATH_V 414.

name: Pharmacoepidemiology
description: Principles and applications of pharmacoepidemiology. Practical skills in designing, conducting, and appraising studies of medications in large populations. Prerequisite: Previous coursework in statistics or biostatistics.
prerequisites: Previous coursework in statistics or biostatistics

name: Specialized Tests in Clinical Chemistry
description: Biochemistry tests in clinical medicine; pathophysiology of common clinical conditions. Prerequisites: PATH_V 413. Credit will be granted for either PATH_V 406 or PATH_V 413 and PATH_V 414.

name: Immunopathology
description: Innate and adaptive immunity and how these host defense mechanisms are involved in both health and illness.

name: Clinical Toxicology
description: A theoretical and practical examination of analytical and pathophysiological aspects related to detection and management in medical laboratories. Credit will be granted for either PATH_V 407 or PATH_V 416 and PATH_V 418.

name: Viral Infections in Humans
description: Interactions between viruses and humans; pathogenesis; prompt virological diagnosis; rationale for antiviral chemotherapy and prophylaxis.  Equivalency: MICB407

name: Etiology of Diabesity, from Cell to Society
description: Advanced course on pathophysiology and patient care for obesity and diabetes focusing on healthcare quality improvement, patient safety and optimising outcomes. Equivalency: PHRM346

name: Introduction to Advanced Techniques in Pathology and Laboratory Medicine
description: Theoretical foundations and practical applications of advanced pathology and laboratory medicine techniques in both research and clinical settings.

name: Advanced Economic Evaluation in Health Care
description: Economic evaluation of health technologies, considering, in detail, the policy context for the use of economic evaluation. Prerequisite: SPPH 541. Or equivalent training. Equivalency: SPPH 549

name: Systemic Pathology
description: A series of Pathology discussions in conjunction with various clinical departments designed to illustrate the role of Pathology in the diagnosis and management of various diseases.

name: Clerkship in Laboratory Medicine and Infection Prevention and Control
description: May involve attendance at an approved institution and/or a project assigned by the instructor(s). Instructor permission required. Enrolment may be limited.

name: Clerkship in Anatomic Pathology
description: An elective course open to third-year medical students, designed to familiarize the student with Anatomic Pathology, including Surgical Pathology, Pediatric Pathology, Autopsy Pathology and Cytology. This elective may involve attendance at one or more affiliated hospitals. Registration requires consent of the Department and enrolment may be limited.

name: M.Sc. Seminar
description: Attendance at regular seminars throughout the session and presentation of one or more papers on selected topics.

name: Forensic Toxicology and Therapeutic Drug Monitoring
description: A theoretical and practical examination of analytical and pathophysiological aspects related to detection and management in medical laboratories. Credit will be granted for either PATH_V 407 or PATH_V 416 and PATH_V 418.

name: Human Bacterial Infections
description: Students acquire content relating to the virulence factors of the bacteria and the pathophysiology of the host while working through case scenarios on their own and in online groups. Students taking this course must be willing to engage in both self-directed and small-group learning.

name: Medical Laboratory Science: Directed Studies
description: Investigation of a specific topic in Medical Laboratory Science.

name: Introduction to Laboratory Medicine
description: An elective course open to first-year medical students who spend at least three consecutive hours each week in one of the affiliated hospitals of the Department of Pathology, Vancouver Hospital, under the joint supervision of a Senior Resident in Pathology and the Professional Staff of the following Divisions: anatomical pathology, clinical biochemistry, hematology, pediatric pathology. Enrolment is limited.

name: Basic Principles of Infection Prevention and Control
description: This course provides the basic principles to prevent the spread of microorganisms pathogenic to humans. It may be taken towards a Certificate in Infection Control.

name: Directed Studies
description: An elective in clinical infection control, medical microbiology or molecular biology.

name: Clinical Laboratory Hematology
description: Correlative seminars based on haematology case studies relating clinical features to laboratory investigations. Equivalency: MEDI452 (1970W)

name: Issues in Business and Professional Ethics
Philosophical Issues in the Foundations of Mathematics
Co-operative Work Placement III
description: Approved and supervised technical work experience in either industrial, public, or academic laboratory for a minimum of 14 weeks. Technical report required. Restricted to students admitted to the Coop Program in BMLSc. Prerequisite: PATH 399.

name: Co-operative Work Placement IV
description: Approved and supervised technical work experience in either industrial, public, or academic laboratory for a minimum of 14 weeks. Technical report required. Restricted to students admitted to the Coop Program in BMLSc. Prerequisite: PATH 498.

name: Basic Microbiology for Infection Control
description: The identification, clinical significance, and transmission of pathogenic organisms are presented. This course is available by correspondence or webCT. It may be taken towards fulfillment of the Certificate in Infection Control.

name: Basic Epidemiology for Infection Control
description: Epidemiology, study, design and analysis, and outbreak investigation as it applies to institutional infection control. Equivalency: SPPH 401

name: Clinical Laboratory Microbiology
description: Selected clinical laboratory exercises plus seminars to illustrate the diagnosis and management of patients with microbial infections. Elective course limited to third- and fourth-year medical students. Prerequisite: Departmental approval required.

name: Foundations of Human Histopathology
description: Microscopic anatomy of human tissues and organs in health and disease. Principles of histological analysis and applications in pathology.

name: Bacteriology, Mycology, Virology and Parasitology
description: All groups of microorganisms pathogenic for humans. Clinical features, pathogenesis and pathology, epidemiology, properties of the agents, immunology, laboratory diagnosis, therapy, preventative measures.

name: Principles of Antimicrobial Chemotherapy
description: Classification, structure and mode of action of antimicrobial agents. In-depth comparison of factors affecting the activity of antimicrobials in vivo and in vitro. Prerequisite: All of MICB 200, PATH 427.

name: Current Topics in Pathology Research
description: General principles of etiology, pathogenesis, disordered physiology, and anatomic pathology of common disease processes.

name: Introduction to the Pathogenesis of Human Disease
description: Current medical research; cardiovascular and pulmonary disease. Prerequisite: Permission of instructor.

name: Molecular and Cell Biology of Cancer
description: This course focuses on molecular and cell biology of cancer and consists of a series of lectures/reviews combined with discussions and presentations by students on the topics selected by the instructors. Emphasis will be on students' presentations and discussion.  Prerequisite: MEDG 421 is recommended. Course coordinator approval is required. Equivalency: MEDG521

name: Cooperative Work Placement I
description: Approved and supervised relevant work experience in an industrial, academic, or government setting for a minimum of 13 weeks, full-time. Normally taken in Summer Session after third year. Work term report required. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-op Program in Neuroscience. Prerequisite: Co-op workshops, and third-year standing in the neuroscience specialization.
prerequisites: third-year standing in the neuroscience specialization

name: Nutrition and Metabolic Aspects of Human Disease
description: Molecular effects of changes in nutrient status and metabolism on health. Prerequisite: Restricted to students registered in the Pathology Graduate Program or instructor approval required.

name: Pulmonary Pathophysiology
description: A review of current topics in pulmonary pathophysiology at an advanced level suitable for graduate students majoring in pathology, medicine, surgery or anesthesiology. Topics will include lung anatomy, ventilation, blood flow, gas and fluid exchange. Prerequisite: One of PHYL 301, PHYL 303, PHYL 400.

name: Your Position in the Neurosciences
description: Practices to promote equity, diversity, inclusion, and decolonization in the neurosciences, and exploration of one's positionality through historical and present-day neuroscience.  Prerequisites: One of BIOL_V 372, NSCI_V 201, PSYC_V 301, PSYC_V 304, PSYC_V 371.

name: Directed Studies in Neuroscience
description: Directed investigation of a neuroscience research question requiring a report of the findings. Prerequisite: At least a 70% average in the preceding 30 credits, permission of the supervisor, and permission of the director of the neuroscience specialization.
prerequisites: At least a 70% average in the preceding 30 credits
permission of the director of the neuroscience specialization

name: Neuroscience Capstone
description: A capstone course to provide students with a rigorous neuroscience research experience under the supervision of one or more faculty members. Integrated support and feedback is provided by peers and faculty.  Prerequisite: Restricted to students in the neuroscience specialization.
prerequisites: Restricted to students in the neuroscience specialization

name: Advanced Topics in Behavioural and Cognitive Neuroscience
description: Selected topics in Behavioural and Cognitive Neuroscience. May be taken more than once for credit with permission of the program. Prerequisite: Third-year standing in a Neuroscience specialization.
prerequisites: Third-year standing in a Neuroscience specialization

name: Cooperative Work Placement II
description: Approved and supervised relevant work experience in an industrial, academic, or government setting for a minimum of 13 weeks, full-time. Normally taken in Term 1 of the 4th Year Winter Session. Work term report required. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-op Program in Neuroscience. Prerequisite: NSCI 398.

name: Advanced Neurosurgery I
description: Selected topics in neurosurgery and the related basic sciences. Given in alternate years.

name: Cooperative Work Placement IV
description: Approved and supervised relevant work experience in an industrial, academic, or government setting for a minimum of 13 weeks, full-time. Normally taken in the Summer Session after 4th year. Work term report required. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-op Program in Neuroscience. Prerequisite: NSCI 498.

name: Advanced Neurosurgery II
description: The second year of the above program. Given in alternate years.

name: Topics in Neuroscience
description: Selected topics in a specific area within Neuroscience. May be taken more than once for credit with permission of the department.  Prerequisite: Third year standing in a Neuroscience specialization, and permission of an Advisor for the Undergraduate Program in Neuroscience.
prerequisites: Third year standing in a Neuroscience specialization
permission of an Advisor for the Undergraduate Program in Neuroscience

name: Cooperative Work Placement III
description: Approved and supervised relevant work experience in an industrial, academic, or government setting for a minimum of 13 weeks, full-time. Normally taken in Term 2 of the 4th Year Winter Session. Work term report required. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-op Program in Neuroscience. Prerequisite: NSCI 399.

name: Seminar
description: Attendance required of all M.Sc. candidates in the Department.

name: Advanced Neuroanatomy
description: Detailed coverage of neuroanatomy, with applications  Prerequisite: One of NSCI_V 200, PSYC_V 371, BIOL_V 371.

name: Advanced Topics in Cellular and Molecular Neuroscience
description: Selected topics in Cellular and Molecular Neuroscience. May be taken more than once for credit with permission of the program. Prerequisite: Third-year standing in a Neuroscience specialization.
prerequisites: Third-year standing in a Neuroscience specialization

name: Primary Care Pharmacy Practice
description: Strategies for leveraging opportunities and addressing barriers to effective pharmacist integration into multidisciplinary primary care teams and optimizing patient care. Co-requisite: PHRM 311.

name: Clinical Pharmacokinetics
description: Lectures and discussions of topics on the application of pharmacokinetic principles and the use of therapeutic drug level monitoring in clinical pharmacy practice.

name: Leadership Experience Applied to Pharmacy (LEAP)
description: Leadership skills in preparation for the practice of pharmacy in direct or non-direct patient care settings and contexts.

name: Renal Pharmacotherapeutics
description: Case-based approach to pathophysiology, pharmacology, clinical pharmacokinetics, and pharmacotherapy in nephrology with emphasis on the integration and application of fundamental principles to clinical situations in class. Prerequisite: Third-year standing.

name: Correlative Clinical Neurosurgery Rounds
description: Residents meet with radiology, neuropathology, and active staff members for discussion of problem cases. One and one-half hours weekly.

name: Neurosurgery Professors Conference
description: One one-hour session weekly with a member of the active staff, conducted at the bedside or in conference room. Cases reviewed with emphasis on the proper application of diagnostic methods and the indications for operative management.

name: Pharmacology of Drugs of Misuse and Abuse
description: Biological, pharmacological, and psychological aspects of drugs of misuse and abuse.

name: Pharmaceutical Care in Indigenous Health
description: Indigenous health in Canada and the role pharmacists' cultural humility and safety can play when collaborating with other health professionals and Indigenous communities to provide care and healing.

name: Precision Medicine
description: Precision medicine approaches in research and medical practice to mitigate drug toxicity and improve drug efficacy. Equivalency: PHAR 421.

name: Pharmacotherapy in Oncology
description: Common oncological diseases and their drug treatment.

name: Diabesity
description: Current issues in obesity and diabetes from pathophysiology to patient care, with a focus on healthcare quality improvement, patient safety, and optimizing outcomes. Prerequisite: Third-year standing. Equivalency: PHAR 546

name: Practical Applications of Pharmacoepidemiology & Health Economics
description: Principles and methods of collecting epidemiological and economic evidence used to assess the value of pharmaceuticals and services provided by pharmacists.

name: Seminar: Pharmacists in Practice III
description: Current and potential roles for pharmacists, and contemporary issues in pharmacy practice. Focus on the role of pharmacists as patient educators, researchers and collaborators in interprofessional teams. Prerequisite: One of PHRM 271, PHRM 272.

name: Pain Research and Therapy
description: Basic mechanisms and the clinical management of acute and chronic pain. Prerequisite: Third Year standing.

name: Pharmacy Practice in Acute and Critically Ill Patients
description: Pharmaceutical care concepts for managing acute and critically ill patients. Prerequisite: Third-year standing and a combined grade average of 70% in PHRM 211 and PHRM 212.

name: Applied Pharmacokinetics and Pharmacogenomics
description: Pharmacokinetic monitoring of drug therapy in common clinical situations with foundations for application to other drugs. Pharmacogenomics and personalized medicine principles and applications to practice. Pass/Fail.

name: Introductory Pharmacy Practice Experience - Outpatient III
description: Direct patient care activities in an outpatient setting. Building on existing pharmaceutical knowledge and problem solving ability. Increased involvement in diverse patient care situations. Pass/Fail. Prerequisite: One of PHRM 311, PHRM 312, PHRM 341, PHRM 351.

name: Practice Management and Leadership
description: Application of management and leadership principles and skills to pharmacy operations. Prerequisite: All of PHRM 271, PHRM 272.

name: Critical Appraisal of Pharmacotherapy Literature
description: Principles of clinical study design, focusing on randomized controlled trials, systematic reviews, epidemiologic studies (cohort, case-control), pharmacoeconomic analyses, clinical prediction rules, and guidelines. Pass/Fail.

name: Practice Management
description: Values, concepts, issues and responsibilities of individuals exercising leadership and management roles in pharmacy practice and health care settings. Pass/Fail.

name: Clinical Skills: Administration of Injections
description: Training for authorization to administer injections. Equivalency: PHRM 252.

name: Pharmacotherapeutics 7
description: Genitourinary disorders, reproductive health, endocrinology, and nephrology. Pass/Fail. Prerequisite: PHRM 461.

name: Pharmacotherapeutics 6
description: Gastroenterology and musculoskeletal disorders. Pass/Fail. Prerequisite: PHRM 461.

name: Pharmacotherapeutics 1
description: Therapeutic foundations. Pass/Fail.

name: Pharmacotherapeutics 8
description: Oncology, hematology, and toxicology. Pass/Fail. Prerequisite: PHRM 461.

name: Pharmacotherapeutics 4
description: Infectious diseases. Pass/Fail. Prerequisite: PHRM 461.

name: Seminar: Advanced Topics in Pharmacy Practice
description: Pharmacists in practice, emerging pharmacy practice issues and pharmacists as preceptors. Pass/Fail. Prerequisite: PHRM 371.

name: Directed Studies in Pharmacology
description: Advanced investigation of a specific topic in Pharmacology.

name: PharmD Seminar
description: Seminar course about current and potential roles for pharmacists. Students will also deliver an individual and a group seminar. Pass/Fail.

name: Co-operative Work Placement IV
description: Approved and supervised technical work experience in an industrial research setting for a minimum of 3.5 months. Normally taken during the summer after fourth year. Technical report required. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-operative Education Program in Pharmacology. Prerequisite: [PCTH498]

name: Patient Assessment Skills
description: Principles and practices of patient assessment, applied to the monitoring of drug efficacy and toxicity. Pass/Fail.

name: Pharmacotherapeutics 2
description: Respirology, dermatology, and ears, eyes, nose, and throat. Pass/Fail. Prerequisite: PHRM 461.

name: Structure-Activity Relationships in Pharmacology
description: Lectures, discussions and assigned reading on physicochemical approaches to drug design - the relationship between molecular structure and pharmacological activity in various representative classes of drugs. Given in odd-numbered and alternate years.

name: Molecular Aspects of Drug Action at the Membrane Level
description: Lectures, discussions and assigned reading on actions of drugs on ion channels, receptors and intracellular processes and the methodologies used including electrophysiology, fluorescence measurements, molecular neurobiology and microdialysis. Given in even-numbered and alternate years.

name: Pharmacotherapeutics 3
description: Cardiovascular disorders. Pass/Fail. Prerequisite: PHRM 461.

name: Pharmacotherapeutics 5
description: Neurology and psychiatry. Pass/Fail. Prerequisite: PHRM 461.

name: Pharmacology of Anesthesia
description: Pharmacology of drugs used in anesthesia. Conferences, assigned reading and laboratory exercises demonstrating the actions of drugs as currently applied in the practice of anesthesia. Prerequisite: Permission of the department head is required.

name: Systematic Pharmacology Laboratory
description: A series of demonstrated, group, and individual laboratory experiments designed to illustrate the concepts and hypotheses of pharmacology. The course is restricted to Honours students in Pharmacology, but may be taken by others with permission of the department head.  Prerequisite: All of PCTH 302, PCTH 303.

name: Co-operative Work Placement III
description: Approved and supervised technical work experience in an industrial research setting for a minimum of 3.5 months. Technical report required. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-operative Education Program in Pharmacology. Prerequisite: [PCTH399]

name: Seminar in Pharmacology or Therapeutics
description: To give students experience in the presentation of data and to enhance communication skills in the discussion of scientific topics. All students will present at least one seminar during their graduate work and would be expected to attend all seminars.

name: Honours Thesis
description: A research problem directed by a faculty member. Restricted to Honours Pharmacology students.

name: Drug Assay and Pharmacometrics
description: The techniques, including methods of statistical analysis, used to detect and measure the actions of endogenous or exogenous chemicals, using chemical assays and bioassays as appropriate. Enrolment limited to students in Pharmacology and others with permission of the department head.  Prerequisite: Either (a) PCTH 303 or (b) one of PCTH 300, PCTH 305; and one of BIOL 300, STAT 200.

name: Drugs and Intercellular Communication (including Neuropharmacology)
description: Lectures, discussions and assigned reading on the actions of drugs on the production, release and cellular effects of hormones and neurotransmitters. Given in odd-numbered and alternate years.

name: Directed Studies in Pharmacology
description: In special cases, with the approval of the department head, advanced courses may be arranged.

name: Experimental Design and Analysis in Pharmacology
description: A series of lectures, tutorials and exercises designed to improve student skills in the design and statistical analyses of pharmacological experiments.

name: Selected Topics
description: Thesis or essay.

name: Directed Studies in Clinical Pharmacy
description: Individual assignments involving library and clinical investigation of specific problems relating to drug utilization and information topics.

name: Directed Studies in Pharmaceutics and Biopharmaceutics
description: Individual assignments involving library and laboratory investigation of problems involved in the development of pharmaceutical dosage forms.

name: Community Service Learning II
description: Service learning activities with external community partner sites and members. Pass/Fail. Prerequisite: PHRM 171.

name: Medication Management IV
description: Modules and integration activities focusing on psychiatry, gastroenterology disorders, and oncology and palliative care. Prerequisite: All of PHRM_V 271, PHRM_V 272.

name: Introductory Pharmacy Practice Experience - Outpatient II
description: Prescription processing, drug distribution systems, and select patient care activities in real world outpatient environments. Focus on direct patient care activities. Pass/Fail. Prerequisite: All of PHRM 211, PHRM 212, PHRM 221, PHRM 231, PHRM 241, PHRM 251, PHRM 252, PHRM 261, PHRM 270.

name: Travel Health
description: Providing a consultative service to patients based on patient medical and travel history. Recommending and administering vaccinations according to guidelines. Making recommendations regarding oral medications needed for safe travel.

name: Directed Studies in Pharmacy Practice
description: Individual assignments involving library and field work investigations of problems associated with pharmacy practice.

name: Introductory Pharmacy Practice Experience - Inpatient and Health Authority-Based
description: Application of problem-solving skills to patient care activities in real world inpatient and/or health authority-based settings. Pass/Fail.

name: Directed Studies in Pharmacology
description: Individual assignments involving library and laboratory investigation of certain aspects of drug action.

name: Peer Teaching in Pharmacy Skills
description: Development and delivery of patient counselling role-playing activities.

name: Medication Management V
description: Modules and integration activities focusing on reproductive health, sexual health, and genitourinary disorders; special infectious diseases; and toxicology. Prerequisite: One of PHRM 271, PHRM 272.

name: Directed Studies in Pharmacy Education
description: Individual assignments involving library and scholarly inquiry related to pharmacy education.

name: Directed Studies in Epidemiology and Health Outcomes
description: Individual assignments involving scholarly inquiry related to epidemiology or health outcomes.

name: Study Design and Interpretation I
description: Principles of clinical study design, focusing on biostatistical foundations, randomized controlled trials, and systematic review of randomized controlled trials.

name: Foundations of Pharmacy
description: Scientific concepts and pharmacy practice principles. Role of the pharmacist, patient assessment skills, professional identity, communication skills, and an understanding of legal and ethical responsibilities.

name: Introductory Pharmacy Practice Experience - Outpatient I
description: Prescription processing, drug distribution systems, and select patient care activities in real world outpatient environments. Pass/Fail. Prerequisite: All of PHRM 100, PHRM 111, PHRM 131, PHRM 141, PHRM 161.

name: Nutrition for Pharmacists
description: Foundations of nutrition, nutrition for healthy individuals through the lifespan, and selected clinical applications of nutrition in pharmacy practice. Prerequisite: PHRM 171.

name: Indigenous Health and Cultural Safety
description: Overview of Indigenous health in Canada and the role a pharmacist can have in collaborating with Indigenous communities in providing culturally safe care and healing Prerequisite: PHRM 171.

name: Community Service Learning I
description: Service learning activities with external community partner sites and members. Pass/Fail. Not offered in 2023/24.

name: Institutional Practice Skills
description: Preparation for experiential learning in the hospital setting. Focuses on enhancing familiarity with the care environment and developing skills suited for students to apply to patient care during institutional experiential rotations. Prerequisite: PHRM 171.

name: Technology in Healthcare
description: Knowledge and skills related to the role and applications of technology in health care.

name: Fundamentals of Injury Biomechanics
description: Introduction to injury biomechanics. Anatomy. Impact experiments. Multi-body dynamic simulation and finite element analysis. Skull, face, brain, spine, eye, pelvis, abdomen, and extremity injury. Anthropomorphic test devices, seat belts, airbags, child restraints, and helmets. Recommended pre-requisites: MECH 224, or all of MECH 260 and BMEG 330. Credit will be granted for only one of MECH 436 or MECH 536.

name: Biomechanics Research
description: Seminar in Biomechanics research.

name: Medication Management III
description: Modules and integration activities focusing on nephrology, endocrinology, and neurology. Prerequisite: PHRM 211.

name: Seminar: Pharmacists in Practice II
description: Current and future roles for pharmacists and controversies in pharmacy practice, focusing on the roles and training opportunities for pharmacists in specialty areas of outpatient and inpatient practice. Prerequisite: PHRM 171.

name: Energy and Environment Capstone Design Project
description: A capstone course to provide students experience in the design/development of practical energy and environment devices. Projects are provided by local industry and engineering research laboratories. Credit will be granted for only one of MECH 453, MECH 454, MECH 455, MECH 456, MECH 457, MECH 458, MECH 459, or MECH 490. Prerequisite: All of MECH 325, MECH 327, MECH 328, MECH 360. and fourth-year standing in the Energy and Environment Option.

name: Medication Management I
description: Modules and integration activities focusing on: an introduction to infectious diseases; musculoskeletal disorders; dermatology; eyes, ears, nose, and throat disorders; and hematology. Prerequisite: PHRM 100.

name: Medication Management II
description: Modules and integration activities focusing on respirology and cardiovascular disorders. Corequisite: PHRM 231.

name: Study Design and Interpretation II
description: Principles of screening and diagnostic tests, clinical prediction rules, clinical practice guidelines, conflicts of interest, economic evaluation of therapeutics and medical technologies, harm-benefit analysis, and how to incorporate the best available evidence into practice. Corequisite: PHRM 211.

name: Aerospace Capstone Design Project
description: A capstone course to provide students experience in the design/development of practical mechanical and aerospace devices. Projects are provided by local industry and engineering research laboratories. Credit will be granted for only one of MECH 453, MECH 454, MECH 455, MECH 456, MECH 457, MECH 458, MECH 459, MECH 490. Prerequisite: All of MECH 327, MECH 328, MECH 360, MECH 426. and fourth-year standing in the Aerospace Option.

name: Fuel Cell Systems
description: Energy system architecture and electrochemical energy conversion: fuel cell thermodynamics and electrochemistry; Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cells (PMFCs) and Solid Oxide Fuel Cells (SOFCSs); hydrogen production, storage, and distribution. Recommended pre-requisites: MECH 327 and MECH 375. Credit will be granted for only one of MECH 445 or MECH 577. Prerequisite: Either (a) MECH 225 or (b) one of CHBE 241, ENPH 257 and one of CHBE 251, CIVL 215, MECH 280.

name: Seminar: Pharmacists in Practice I
description: Current and future roles for pharmacists and controversies in pharmacy practice.

name: Clinical Skills: Administration of Injections
description: Training for authorization to administer injections. Pass/Fail.

name: Naval Architecture and Marine Engineering Capstone Design Project
description: A capstone course to provide students experience in the design/development of practical naval architecture and marine engineering devices. Projects are provided by local industry and engineering research laboratories. Credit will be granted for only one of MECH 453, MECH 454, MECH 455, MECH 456, MECH 457, MECH 458, MECH 459, or MECH 490. Prerequisite: All of MECH 325, MECH 328, MECH 360, MECH 380. and fourth-year standing in the Naval Architecture and Marine Engineering Option.

name: Thermofluids Capstone Design Project
description: A capstone course to provide students experience in the design/development of practical mechanical and thermofluids devices. Projects are provided by local industry and engineering research laboratories. Credit will be granted for only one of MECH 453, MECH 454, MECH 455, MECH 456, MECH 457, MECH 458, MECH 459, MECH 490. Prerequisite: All of MECH 325, MECH 327, MECH 328, MECH 360. and fourth-year standing in the Thermofluids Option.

name: Mechatronics Capstone Design Project
description: A capstone design program designed to give students experience in the design/development of practical mechanical and mechatronics devices. Projects are provided by local industry and engineering research laboratories. Credit will be granted for only one of MECH 453, MECH 454, MECH 455, MECH 456, MECH 457, MECH 458, MECH 459, or MECH 490. Prerequisite: All of MECH 325, MECH 328, MECH 360 and fourth-year standing in the Mechatronics Option.

name: Flex Capstone Design Project
description: A capstone design project designed to give students experience in the design/development of practical mechanical devices. Projects are provided by local industry and engineering research laboratories. Credit will be granted for only one of MECH 453, MECH 454, MECH 455, MECH 456, MECH 457, MECH 458, MECH 459, or MECH 490. Prerequisite: All of MECH 325, MECH 328, MECH 360 and fourth-year standing in Mechanical Engineering.

name: Industrial Robotics
description: Definition and classification of industrial robotic devices. Selection and implementation issues. Workcell environments. Forward and inverse kinematics, dynamics, trajectory planning. Sensing and manipulation tasks. Control architectures. Recommended co-requisite: MECH 466 or MECH 467. Credit will be granted for only one of ELEC 442, EECE 571R, EECE 589, MECH 464 or MECH 563.

name: Advanced Mechanics of Materials
description: Mechanics of rubber, tissue, and gels at large viscoelastic deformation; large plastic deformations and damage of materials; mechanical characterization of materials (property extraction from mechanical tests); selected problems in linear elasticity. Prerequisite: MECH_V 360

name: Biomechanics and Medical Devices Capstone Design Project
description: A capstone design program designed to give students experience in the design and development of practical biomedical devices. Projects are provided by local industry and engineering research laboratories. For students in the Biomechanics and Medical Devices Option only. Credit will be granted for only one of MECH_V 453, MECH_V 454, MECH_V 455, MECH_V 456, MECH_V 457, MECH_V 458, MECH_V 459, or MECH_V 490. Prerequisite: All of MECH_V 325, MECH_V 328, MECH_V 360 and fourth-year standing in the Biomechanics and Medical Devices Option.

name: Mechanical Vibrations
description: Theory of vibration of mechanical systems. Undamped 1 degree of freedom vibration, forced vibrations and resonance, damping, multiple degree of freedom systems, mode shapes and orthogonality, continuous systems, vibration measuring instruments and frequency spectrum analysis. Prerequisite: One of MECH 224, MECH 260.

name: Music Performance (Concentration)
description: Private instruction, vocal or instrumental. Prerequisite: One of MUSC 271, MUSC 272, MUSC 281, MUSC 283, MUSC 291, MUSC 292, MUSC 293.

name: Music Performance (Concentration)
description: Private instruction, vocal or instrumental. Prerequisite: One of MUSC 271, MUSC 272, MUSC 281, MUSC 283, MUSC 291, MUSC 292, MUSC 293.

name: Music Performance (Major)
description: Private instruction, vocal or instrumental. Prerequisite: One of MUSC 271, MUSC 272, MUSC 281, MUSC 283, MUSC 291, MUSC 292, MUSC 293.

name: Finite Element Analysis
description: Theory and element selection. Virtual work and weighted residual formulation. Linear elastic analysis. Heat transfer analysis. Isoparametric elements. Development of computer programs for simple problems. Utilization of existing computer packages. Application to mechanical engineering problems. Credit will be granted for only one of MECH_V 462 or MECH_V 514. Prerequisite: MECH_V 360

name: Music Performance (Major)
description: Private instruction, vocal or instrumental. Prerequisite: One of MUSC 271, MUSC 272, MUSC 281, MUSC 283, MUSC 291, MUSC 292, MUSC 293.

name: Biologics
description: Biologics as a therapeutic; how biologics are developed as drugs; synthesis and unique properties of biologics as drugs. Prerequisite: All of PHAR 303, PHAR 306, PHAR 307.

name: Music Performance (Secondary)
description: Private instruction, vocal or instrumental. Prerequisite: One of MUSC 271, MUSC 272, MUSC 281, MUSC 283, MUSC 291, MUSC 292, MUSC 293.

name: Intensive Chamber Ensemble (Upper Years)
description: Intensive coaching in chamber ensemble for advanced players. Performance of works prepared is expected. May be taken twice for credit. Restricted to students with 3rd year standing or above. Corequisite: One of MUSC 350, MUSC 351, MUSC 359, MUSC 360, MUSC 361, MUSC 362, MUSC 366, MUSC 453, MUSC 456, MUSC 457, MUSC 463, MUSC 466. and permission of the instructor.

name: Selected Topics in Music
description: See School of Music schedule for description and prerequisites. Restricted to B. Mus. and B.A. in Music students.

name: Advanced Anesthetics and Analgesics
description: Advanced concepts in anesthetic and analgesic drugs, their uses and abuses. Prerequisite: PHAR 308.

name: Jazz Theory and Arranging
description: Jazz scales, chord relationships, substitutions, orchestration, listening, and score analysis. Restricted to B.Mus. and B.A. in Music students. Prerequisite: MUSC 200.

name: Music Performance (Concentration)
description: Private instruction, vocal or instrumental. Prerequisite: One of MUSC 271, MUSC 272, MUSC 281, MUSC 283, MUSC 291, MUSC 292, MUSC 293.

name: Music Performance (Secondary)
description: Private instruction, vocal or instrumental. Prerequisite: One of MUSC 271, MUSC 272, MUSC 281, MUSC 283, MUSC 291, MUSC 292, MUSC 293.

name: University Choral Union (Upper Years)
description: May be taken twice for credit. Open to students by audition, with credit, as stipulated by their faculties. Restricted to students with 3rd year standing or above. Prerequisite: MUSC 154.

name: Composition IV
description: Continuation of MUSC 307.

name: Statistical Methods for Pharmaceutical Outcomes Research
description: Basic principles of biostatistics and epidemiology. Application of epidemiologic and statistical knowledge in the area of health outcomes. Prerequisite: PHAR 305.

name: Financing and Therapeutics in the Canadian Health Care System
description: Foundation in Canadian health care delivery systems and policies, with a focus on pharmaceutical policy and on comparison with other types of health care systems.

name: Music Performance (Major)
description: Private instruction, vocal or instrumental. Prerequisite: One of MUSC 271, MUSC 272, MUSC 281, MUSC 283, MUSC 291, MUSC 292, MUSC 293.

name: Special Projects
description: For fourth-year students who receive permission of the Director of the School of Music to do advanced studies in their major field.

name: Pharmacoeconomics
description: Evidence evaluation skills and understanding the role of, and the methods and principles used in, health economics and economic evaluation in healthcare, with a focus on health technology assessment studies. Prerequisite: PHAR 305.

name: Automatic Control
description: Process and system characteristics; transient response; the closed loop; block diagrams and transfer functions; control actions; stability; Nyquist diagrams; Bode diagrams; root locus methods; frequency response; system compensation; nonlinear control systems; digital computer control. Laboratory experiments to support the lecture content. Recommended prerequisite: MECH_V 463. Credit cannot be obtained for both MECH_V 466 and MECH_V 467. Prerequisite: Either (a) all of MECH_V 220, MECH_V 221 or (b) MATH_V 255 and one of ELEC_V 201, ELEC_V 202, ELEC_V 204.

name: Precision Medicine
description: Precision medicine approaches in research and medical practice to mitigate drug toxicity and improve drug efficacy. Prerequisite: PHAR 203. Equivalency: PHRM 327.

name: Music Performance (Major)
description: Private instruction, vocal or instrumental. Prerequisite: One of MUSC 271, MUSC 272, MUSC 281, MUSC 283, MUSC 291, MUSC 292, MUSC 293.

name: Drug Structures in Medicinal Chemistry
description: Therapeutically important privileged scaffolds and functional groups, and selectivity achieved through different chemical modifications. Prerequisite: All of CHEM 233, PHAR 202.

name: Clinical Chemistry
description: Principles, practices and procedures of medical laboratory clinical chemistry. Prerequisite: CHEM 211.

name: Biomolecular Pharmaceutical Chemistry
description: Chemical principles and their application to drugs used to regulate enzyme activity.

name: Adverse Drug Reactions
description: Molecular and physiological basis of common adverse drug reactions (ADRs). ADRs in the context of current understanding of drug metabolism and pharmacogenetics. New approaches to prediction, detection and treatment.

name: Pharmaceutical Cases II
description: Advanced application and problem solving in the pharmaceutical sciences. Integration of knowledge and skills from multiple courses to problem solve authentic cases and problems of increasing complexity. Further development and practice of self-directed learning skills. Prerequisite: PHAR 370.

name: Toxicology
description: Biochemical, cellular, and molecular processes that govern toxicity elicited by drugs and environmental toxins at the molecular, cellular, tissue, and organ system levels. Adverse drug reactions and precision medicine approaches to mitigate drug toxicity. Prerequisite: PHAR 308.

name: Physical Therapy Foundations
description: Builds on prerequisite concepts in anatomy, physiology, and physics taken at undergraduate and high school level to apply basic theories and principles of anatomy, human physiology, pathophysiology, biomechanics, and physics to essential rehabilitation concepts.

name: Functional Foods
description: Functional food concepts related to efficacy and safety; examples of bioactive component-disease relationships; natural health products; approval of functional food and health claims; the importance of clinical studies in support of efficacy for health claims; market determinants of functional foods. Credit will be granted for only one of PHAR 431 or FNH 402. Prerequisite: PHAR 202, PHAR 203. Equivalency: FNH 402.

name: Advanced Pharmacokinetics
description: Polyexponential pharmacokinetics, pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic modeling, pharmacokinetic predictions, physiologically-based pharmacokinetic modeling and population-based pharmacokinetic modeling. Credit will be granted for only one of PHAR 433 or PHAR 502. Prerequisite: PHAR 302.

name: Philosophy of Social Science
description: Topics in the philosophy of science of special concern to the social sciences: the problem of objectivity, the use of models and evidence, causation and causal reasoning, formal methods, the status of social kinds and norms, scientific explanation, laws. Prerequisite: 9 credits at the 200-level or above from philosophy, anthropology, geography, economics, history, political science, psychology or sociology.

name: Topics in Science and Technology Studies
description: Advanced seminar on a theme or topic of interest to both STS and Philosophy.

name: Philosophy of Biology
description: Methodological, historical, philosophical and social science questions about biology. Prerequisite: Fourth-year standing in any degree program or 9 credits of philosophy.

name: Topics in Philosophy of Science
description: Topics such as probability and induction; foundations of measurement; theory construction. Recommended pre-requisite: PHIL_V 369.

name: Comparative Conceptions of the Self
description: Ways in which the 'self' has been portrayed in eastern and western religious traditions. Thinkers to be considered include Aristotle, Mencius, Freud, Xunzi (Hsün-tzu), Nietzche, and Zhuangzi (Chuang-tzu). Credit will be granted for only one of PHIL 470 or ASIA 470. Equivalency: ASIA 470

name: Directed Reading
description: Same as PHIL 486-9.

name: Space and Time
description: Such topics as: Are space and time continuous? Is motion always relative to another body? Does time flow? Is time irreversible? Recommended pre-requisites: PHIL 340 or 12 credits of mathematics or science.

name: Seminar for Majors in Philosophy
description: Selected problems in philosophy, with attention to methods of research. Check with the department for specific topics. Primarily for fourth-year Philosophy Major students, but also open to Philosophy Honours.

name: Quality Correlation in Nuclear Medicine
description: See RADI 713.

name: Persian Reading and Writing for Persian-Speaking Students
description: Reading and writing of standard Persian; lexical and syntactic differences between written and spoken Persian. Restricted to Persian heritage speakers with aural/oral knowledge but no reading/writing skills.

name: Basic Persian II
description: Continuation of PERS 100. Recommended pre-requisite: PERS 100.

name: Intermediate-High Persian II
description: Continuation of PERS 300. Recommended pre-requisite: PERS 300.

name: Basic Persian I
description: Basic vocabulary and the fundamentals of modern Persian grammar, structure, and pronunciation, as well as reading, writing, listening, and speaking.

name: Contemporary Iranian Cinema for Advanced Speakers of Persian
description: Iranian cultural norms, and sociopolitical information about Iranian society and history, as conveyed through Iranian cinema. Emphasis on speaking, writing, and vocabulary development of Persian language. Recommended pre-requisites: PERS 300, or native or proficient heritage speaker of Persian with permission of the instructor.

name: Topics in Classical Persian Language and Culture
description: Study of Classical Persian literary, fiction and non-fiction texts, including poetry, prose, and fables. Topics vary from section to section. Consulthttps://asia.ubc.ca/courses/for current offerings. This course is recommended for students with 6 credits of upper level PERS courses and placement approval. For more information on placement approval, please visit Placement Tests at:

name: Intermediate-High Persian I
description: Graded reading, writing, exposure to textual history, newspaper reading, and translation. Cultural materials presented as appropriate. Recommended pre-requisites: PERS 201 or Persian heritage speakers with basic reading/writing skills (no more than Grade 6 formal education in Iran).

name: Honours Tutorial
description: For students in fourth-year Honours.

name: Persian through Shahnameh for Advanced Speakers of Persian
description: Persian through Shahnameh, with a focus on speaking, reading, writing and vocabulary development. Emphasis on Iranian cultural norms, mentalities and values. Recommended pre-requisite: PERS 300 or native or proficient heritage speaker of Persian, with permission of the instructor.

name: Pharmaceutical Topics and Communication Seminar IV
description: Senior level skills and concepts for planning, delivering and critiquing a scientific seminar using extended topics in the pharmaceutical sciences and beyond. Prerequisite: PHAR 380.

name: Topics in Modern Persian Language, Literature and Culture
description: Study of modern Persian language through culturally rich and varied material such as satire, popular culture, songs, and modern poetry and prose. Topics vary from section to section. Consulthttps://asia.ubc.ca/courses/for current offerings. This course is recommended for students with 6 credits of upper level PERS courses and placement approval. For more information on placement approval, please visit Placement Tests at:

name: Intermediate-Low Persian I
description: Reading of simple texts with emphasis on reading and writing, conversation skills, grammar, and syntax. Recommended pre-requisite: one of PERS 101, PERS 104.

name: Research Project
description: Provides research experience equivalent to one full-time term of work on a defined research project in an area of pharmaceutical research. Prerequisite: PHAR_V 302, PHAR_V 303, PHAR_V 304, PHAR_V 305, PHAR_V 306, PHAR_V 307, PHAR_V 308, PHAR_V 370 and PHAR_V 380.

name: Intermediate-Low Persian II
description: Continuation of PERS 200. Recommended pre-requisite: PERS 200.

name: Pharmaceutical Topics and Communication Seminar I
description: Current topics in the Pharmaceutical Sciences and basic skills for a short presentation on a biological science topic.

name: Advanced Concepts in Pharmacokinetics
description: Models of linear and dose-dependent systems in pharmacokinetics including sustained release, volumes of distribution, drug clearance, metabolite kinetics, multiple dosing and computer modelling. Credit will be granted for only one of PHAR 502 or PHAR 433.

name: Persian Media
description: Reading, understanding and participating in contemporary registers of Persian Language as used in newspapers, radio/TV, as well as in online news and social media. Recommended pre-requisites: PERS 104, 201, or 3 credits of PERS at the 300 level, or permission of instructor.

name: Advanced Pharmaceutics I
description: A study of physical and chemical properties of pharmaceutical systems with emphasis on formulation and preparative aspects.

name: Honours Thesis
description: Research project and production of a thesis document in an area of pharmaceutical research according to national/international standards. Prerequisite: PHAR_V 485

name: Practicum
description: Provides practicum experience equivalent to one full-time term of work in a professional area of pharmaceutical research. Prerequisite: PHAR_V 302, PHAR_V 303, PHAR_V 304, PHAR_V 305, PHAR_V 306, PHAR_V 307, PHAR_V 308, PHAR_V 370 and PHAR_V 380.

name: Persian Short Story for Native and Heritage Speakers
description: Modern short stories from mid-19th century to present. Recommended pre-requisites: one of PERS 104, PERS 300, or Persian heritage speakers with strong reading/writing skills (High School). NOT eligible to students who have studied at the post-secondary level in Iran.

name: Directed Studies in Pharmaceutical Sciences
description: Individual assignments involving library and laboratory investigation in an area of pharmaceutical research. Prerequisite: PHAR 204.

name: Lipid-Based Drug Delivery
description: Advances in lipophilic drug delivery systems.

name: Introduction to Philosophy
description: Basic problems and methods of Philosophy. Topics such as the existence of God, the nature and scope of human knowledge, the relationship between mind and body, personal identity, free will, issues and problems in moral philosophy. Credit will be granted for only one of PHIL 100 and either or both PHIL 101 or PHIL 102.

name: Polymeric Drug and Protein Delivery
description: Advances in polymer-based drug delivery systems.

name: Nanomedicines
description: Nano-sized drug delivery systems and their interactions with biological systems.

name: Diagnostic Imaging and Radiopharmaceuticals
description: Radiation-related, optical, and other imaging methods (SPECT, PET, CT, MRI, microscopy, ultrasound) and their application in research.

name: Introduction to Philosophy II
description: Basic problems and methods of philosophy. Topics such as morality, personal identity, free will and determinism, and the meaning of life. Credit will be granted for only one of PHIL 100 or PHIL 102.

name: Greek Philosophy I: Socrates and Plato
description: The Pre-Socratics; Socrates; Sophists; Plato. Recommended as preparation for PHIL 310. Credit will only be granted for one of PHIL 211, CLST 211 or AMNE 235. Equivalency: CLST211, AMNE235

name: Happiness
description: What makes for deep, lasting happiness, joy, and wellbeing? Contemporary and classical works of philosophy and important debates in related fields such as psychology, economics, political theory, and sociology.

name: Enriched Symbolic Logic
description: Naïve set theory, relations and functions, recursion and induction; Propositional and predicate logic; Symbolizations, semantics, and formal proof theory; Metatheory for propositional logic. Recommended for students interested in pursuing upper-level courses in logic or formal philosophy. Credit will be granted for only one of PHIL 220 and PHIL 222.

name: Pharmacy Leadership Seminar
description: Corequisite: PHRM_V 520. Prerequisite: PHRM_V 523.

name: Symbolic Logic
description: Sentential and predicate logic. Translation from natural language; truth tables and interpretations; systems of natural deduction up to relational predicate logic with identity; alternative proof methods. Some sections may use computer-based materials and tests. Credit will be granted for only one of PHIL 220 and PHIL 222. Equivalency: PHIL 222

name: Advanced Pharmaceutics II
description: A study of problems in pharmaceutics with emphasis on biopharmaceutical aspects.

name: Basic Theory & Practice of Scanning Electron Microscopy and Dynamic Light Scattering
description: Sample preparation; standard & advanced imaging techniques; image interpretation & quantification, applications in pharmaceutical research.

name: Leadership in Pharmacy Education
description: Corequisite: PHRM_V 520. Prerequisite: PHRM_V 522.

name: Applied Omics Science for Drug Discovery and Development
description: General principles of genomics, proteomics, glycomics, and metabolomics; advanced functional omics techniques and their applications in pharmaceutical research.

name: Basic Theory and Practice of Liquid Chromatography - Mass Spectrometry in Pharmaceutical Research
description: Fundamental and practical knowledge and skills to run liquid chromatography tandem mass spectrometry.

name: Introduction to Ethics
description: Theories of obligation and value; moral reasoning; normative ethics, descriptive ethics and meta-ethics. Readings in classic and contemporary texts.

name: Introduction to Philosophy
description: Basic problems and methods of philosophy. Topics such as the nature and scope of human knowledge, the existence of God, and the relationship between mind and body. Credit will be granted for only one of PHIL 100 or PHIL 101.

name: Greek Philosophy II: Aristotle and After
description: Aristotle; selections from Hellenistic and Late Antique Philosophy. Recommended as preparation for PHIL 310. Credit will only be granted for one of PHIL 212, CLST 212 or AMNE 236. Equivalency: CLST212, AMNE236

name: Introduction to Scientific Reasoning
description: Historical and logical analysis of various types of scientific hypotheses and the data that support or undermine them. This course is restricted to students with fewer than 90 credits.

name: Introduction to Epistemology
description: Topics in epistemology such as skepticism, truth, justification, a priori and a posteriori knowledge. Readings from classic and contemporary texts.

name: Introduction to Critical Thinking
description: Tools for dealing with both everyday and more technical arguments and concepts. Analysis and resolution of confusions, ambiguities, and fallacies. This course is restricted to students with fewer than 90 credits.

name: Music Performance (Secondary)
description: Private instruction, vocal or instrumental. Prerequisite: One of MUSC 371, MUSC 372, MUSC 381, MUSC 382, MUSC 383, MUSC 391, MUSC 392, MUSC 393, MUSC 394.

name: Interdisciplinary Projects
description: Group projects and workshops with students majoring in other creative arts. Prerequisite: Permission of instructor. Credit will be granted for only one of MUSC_V 469 or THTR_V 469 or VISA_V 469 or CRWR_V 440. Equivalency: THTR_V 469, VISA_V 469, CRWR_V 440.

name: Music Performance (Major)
description: Private instruction, vocal or instrumental. Prerequisite: One of MUSC 371, MUSC 372, MUSC 381, MUSC 382, MUSC 383, MUSC 391, MUSC 392, MUSC 393, MUSC 394.

name: Music Performance (Concentration)
description: Private instruction, vocal or instrumental. Prerequisite: One of MUSC 371, MUSC 372, MUSC 381, MUSC 382, MUSC 383, MUSC 391, MUSC 392, MUSC 393, MUSC 394.

name: Music Performance (Secondary)
description: Private instruction, vocal or instrumental. Prerequisite: One of MUSC 371, MUSC 372, MUSC 381, MUSC 382, MUSC 383, MUSC 391, MUSC 392, MUSC 393, MUSC 394.

name: Contemporary Moral Issues
description: Moral issues such as life and death decisions, paternalism, markets, animal welfare, technology, and global justice.

name: World Music Ensembles (Upper Years)
description: Training on traditional instruments and their techniques, with emphasis on ensemble performance. Different sections focus on the music of different cultures, e.g., Bali, China, Ghana, Korea. May be taken twice for credit. Restricted to students with 3rd year standing or above. Prerequisite: MUSC 165.

name: Chamber Music Master Class
description: Enrolment by audition only.

name: Music Performance (Concentration)
description: Private instruction, vocal or instrumental. Prerequisite: One of MUSC 371, MUSC 372, MUSC 381, MUSC 382, MUSC 383, MUSC 391, MUSC 392, MUSC 393, MUSC 394.

name: Music Performance (Major)
description: Private instruction, vocal or instrumental. Prerequisite: One of MUSC 371, MUSC 372, MUSC 381, MUSC 382, MUSC 383, MUSC 391, MUSC 392, MUSC 393, MUSC 394.

name: Readings in Schenkerian Theory
description: Recommended pre-requisite: MUSC 410.

name: Music Performance (Concentration)
description: Private instruction, vocal or instrumental. Prerequisite: One of MUSC 371, MUSC 372, MUSC 381, MUSC 382, MUSC 383, MUSC 391, MUSC 392, MUSC 393, MUSC 394.

name: Advanced Musical Analysis
description: Recommended pre-requisite: one of MUSC 410, MUSC 411, MUSC 412, MUSC 413.

name: The Structure and Function of Music Theories
description: Recommended pre-requisites: one of MUSC 410, MUSC 411, MUSC 412, or permission of the instructor.

name: Pharmaceutical Research
description: Types of research scientists in Academia and Industry across the broad range of Pharmaceutical Science Disciplines. Prerequisite: PHAR_V 202.

name: Music Performance (Major)
description: Private instruction, vocal or instrumental. Prerequisite: One of MUSC 371, MUSC 372, MUSC 381, MUSC 382, MUSC 383, MUSC 391, MUSC 392, MUSC 393, MUSC 394.

name: Techniques in Molecular Biology and Pharmacology Theory and Laboratory
description: Theoretical and practical knowledge of the foundational techniques used in pharmaceutical research in both Academic Research and the Pharmaceutical and Biotechnology Industries. Prerequisite: All of CHEM_V 211, CHEM_V 233, CHEM_V 235, PHAR_V 203, PHAR_V 204, MICB_V 212, and STAT_V 200.

name: Medicinal Chemistry of High-Impact Pharmaceuticals in Major Diseases
description: Structure and mechanism of action of drugs used in the treatment of major chronic diseases: heart disease, cancer, lung disease, and diabetes. Prerequisite: All of CHEM 233, PHAR 202.

name: Biochemical Pharmacology
description: Biochemical pharmacology including fundamental aspects of enzymology, biochemistry, enzyme kinetics, drug metabolism and pharmacokinetics. Prerequisite: BIOL_V 112, BIOL_V 155, one of CHEM_V 111 or 121, CHEM_V 123, and one of MATH_V 100, MATH_V 120 or MATH_V 180.

name: Pharmaceutical Topics and Communication Seminar II
description: Current topics in the Pharmaceutical and Biotechnology Industry and intermediate level skills for a short presentation. Prerequisite: PHAR_V 180 and WRDS_V 150.

name: Drug Delivery Technologies and Personalized Medicine Theory and Laboratory
description: Theoretical and practical knowledge of biopharmaceuticals, pharmaceutics, formulations, nanomedicine, and precision medicine as they apply to pharmaceutical sciences. Prerequisite: PHAR_V 202

name: Clinical Epidemiology & Pharmaceutical Outcomes I
description: Population-level study designs and critical appraisal skills in evidence evaluation, with a special emphasis on evidence-based pharmacy practice.

name: Pharmacokinetics
description: Basic pharmacokinetic concepts: absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion. Evaluation of how drug physicochemistry, organism physiology, and pharmacogenetics affect pharmacokinetics. Prerequisite: PHAR_V 202.

name: Music Performance (Major)
description: Private instruction, vocal or instrumental. Prerequisite: One of MUSC 371, MUSC 372, MUSC 381, MUSC 382, MUSC 383, MUSC 391, MUSC 392, MUSC 393, MUSC 394.

name: Pharmaceutical Topics and Communication Seminar III
description: Preliminary skills and concepts for planning, delivering and critiquing a scientific presentation using selected topics in the pharmaceutical sciences. Prerequisite: PHAR 280.

name: Clinical Epidemiology & Pharmaceutical Outcomes II
description: Population-level study designs and their critical appraisal skills in evidence evaluation, with a special emphasis on evidence-based pharmacy practice and the practical application of population-level data analysis and interpretation. Prerequisite: PHAR 205.

name: Analytical Sciences Theory and Laboratory
description: Theoretical and practical knowledge of the analytical sciences commonly used in Academic Research as well as the Pharmaceutical and Biotechnology Industries. Prerequisite: PHAR_V 304

name: Nanomedicine
description: Advanced nanomedicine concepts for drug packaging, delivery, and efficacy. Prerequisite: PHAR 202.

name: Pharmaceutical Cases I
description: Application and problem solving in the pharmaceutical sciences. Integration of knowledge and skills from multiple courses to problem solve authentic cases and problems of increasing complexity. Development of self-directed learning skills. Prerequisite: PHAR_V 202, PHAR_V 203, PHAR_V 204, PHAR_V 205, and PHAR_V 280.

name: Systematic Pharmacology
description: General principles of pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetics: drug action on nervous, cardiovascular, GI and endocrine systems; beneficial and detrimental effects of drug action. Prerequisite: PHAR 202.

name: Topics in Pharmaceutics and Biopharmaceutics
description: A study of selected topics in the field of pharmaceutics and biopharmaceutics. Registration restricted. Permission of instructor required.

name: Theoretical Perspectives in Nursing: Special Topics in Complex and Urgent Health Challenges across Settings/Populations
description: Consolidation of fundamental theories, concepts, evidence, and competencies pertaining to nursing practice across the life-span and care context. Prerequisite: All of NURS 300, NURS 301, NURS 303, NURS 310, NURS 321, NURS 322, NURS 323, NURS 330, NURS 331, NURS 345, NURS 346, NURS 350, NURS 351, NURS 352, NURS 353, NURS 354, NURS 360, NURS 361, NURS 362, NURS 363, NURS 365, NURS 366, NURS 401. Corequisite: All of NURS 344, NURS 402.

name: Foundational Skills and Competencies for Clinical Practice V
description: Students are guided to consolidate skills and competencies for clinical practice through a variety of modalities and learning activities. Prerequisite: All of NURS 300, NURS 321, NURS 322, NURS 323, NURS 350, NURS 351, NURS 352, NURS 353, NURS 360, NURS 361, NURS 362, NURS 363, NURS 365, NURS 366, NURS 401. Corequisite: NURS 430.

name: Supplemental Guided Study
description: Supplemental guided study to integrate and consolidate professional nursing knowledge, skills and competencies. For Bachelor of Science Nursing students only. Pass/Fail.

name: Foundational Skills and Competencies for Clinical Practice IV
description: Students are prepared with the skills and competencies for clinical practice in simulated acute and community settings through a variety of modalities and learning activities. Prerequisite: All of NURS 300, NURS 321, NURS 322, NURS 323, NURS 330, NURS 352, NURS 360. Corequisite: Either (a) all of NURS 345, NURS 365, NURS 346, NURS 366 or (b) all of NURS 303, NURS 363, NURS 301, NURS 362.

name: Consolidated Practice Experience
description: Nursing practice to consolidate nursing knowledge, theory, evidence, and practice, and facilitate the transition to professional practice. Prerequisite: All of NURS 344, NURS 402, NURS 430.

name: Baltic Cultures and Literatures
description: Examination through literature of the historical, cultural, and ethnic elements that have made the Baltic area (Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania) the crossroads of northeastern Europe. Credit will be granted for only one of SCAN_V 413 or NORD_V 413. Equivalency: SCAN_V 413.

name: The World of the Sagas
description: Explore the medieval and early modern world of the Nordic region through the Icelandic sagas and their literary, cultural, and historical context. Credit will be granted for only one of SCAN_V 415 or NORD_V 415. Equivalency: SCAN_V 415.

name: Nursing Practice with Infants, Children, Youth and their Families: Practicum
description: Nursing practice to integrate and consolidate professional nursing knowledge, skills and competencies in the care of infants, children, youth and their families. Prerequisite: All of NURS 300, NURS 310, NURS 321, NURS 322, NURS 330, NURS 352. Corequisite: NURS 346 and one of NURS 323, NURS 401.

name: Topics in Northern European Cultural Studies
description: Selected topics for advanced study, such as activism, ethnicity, gender, identity, migration, sexuality, and justice across Northern Europe. Credit will be granted for only one of SCAN_V 414 or NORD_V 414. Equivalency: SCAN_V 414.

name: Human Sexual Health
description: Beliefs, behaviours, and expressions of human sexuality and the link to health for students from any program. How sexuality is discussed and practiced from various perspectives, and strategies to promote healthy sexual expression and sexual health.

name: Stress and Strategies to Promote Well Being
description: Introduction to foundational knowledge related to stress, stressors, resilience, social support, and strategies to foster physical, mental, emotional, and spiritual health. Open to all students interested in learning about managing and navigating the stressors of student life.

name: Diverse Perspectives on Aging
description: Examines aging experience from interdisciplinary, equity, diversity, inclusion and Indigeneity (EDI-I) (race, sex, gender, disability), and systems perspectives. Topics include older adult health and illness, age friendly communities, ageism and stigma, and end of life issues.

name: Health Impacts of Climate Change
description: Human health impacts of the current and projected environmental crisis; study of key concepts and ideas to prepare for the future to promote wellbeing of individuals, communities and populations.

name: Pharmacology and Therapeutics in Primary Care
Advanced Health Assessment Across the Life Span
Clinical Procedures in Primary Care Settings
Directed Studies
description: Advanced research undertaking topics of Nordic Studies, with the agreement and under the supervision, of a faculty member with relevant expertise. Restricted to Nordic Studies students with approval from the Director of Undergraduate Studies.

name: Theoretical and Professional Foundations for Nursing Practice
description: Introduction to knowledge fundamental to the discipline and practice of nursing.

name: Topics in Symbolic Logic
description: Formal semantics, proof theory, incompleteness and decidability, axiomatic set theory, independence results. Consult the Department as to which topics are offered in a given year.

name: Philosophy of History
description: Concepts of history and historical explanation, historical progress, purpose, necessity, law and causation. Hegel, Marx, Vico, Spengler, Pareto, Collingwood, Croce, and Toynbee, as well as contemporary figures. Students will be expected to have an adequate knowledge of ancient or modern history.

name: Foundational Skills and Competencies for Clinical Practice III
description: Skills and competencies for clinical practice across the lifespan and health care continuum through a variety of modalities and learning activities. Prerequisite: All of NURS 300, NURS 310, NURS 321, NURS 330, NURS 352, NURS 360. Corequisite: Either (a) all of NURS 345, NURS 365 or (b) all of NURS 346, NURS 366 or (c) all of NURS 303, NURS 363 or (d) all of NURS 301, NURS 362.

name: Philosophy of Mathematics
description: Logicism, formalism and constructivism, implications of metatheorems such as those of Gödel and Church, mathematical truth, mathematics and mental construction, mathematics and the physical world.

name: Basic Principles of Pharmacology for Nursing Practice
description: Basic principles of pharmacology and the basic structure and function of each body system will be explored to demonstrate how drug interactions occur within systems.

name: Foundational Skills and Competencies for Clinical Practice I
description: Skills and competencies for clinical practice using a variety of modalities and learning activities. Corequisite: All of NURS 300, NURS 310, NURS 330, NURS 352, NURS 360.

name: Topics in Twentieth-Century Philosophy
description: Intensive study of a major philosopher such as Wittgenstein, Russell, or Heidegger, or school, such as pragmatism or logical empiricism.

name: Foundational Skills and Competencies for Clinical Practice II
description: Clinical practice through a variety of modalities and learning activities in the laboratory environment. Prerequisite: All of NURS 300, NURS 310, NURS 321, NURS 330, NURS 352, NURS 360. Corequisite: All of NURS 331, NURS 361.

name: Topics in Social and Political Philosophy
description: Central concepts and problems in political life and thought including obligation, citizenship, representation, justice; equality; civil rights and liberty; disobedience.

name: Theoretical Perspectives in Nursing: People Living with Mental Health Challenges and Their Families
description: Theory informing a life course perspective on nursing practice with people living with mental health challenges and their families is introduced. Prerequisite: All of NURS 300, NURS 310, NURS 321, NURS 322, NURS 330, NURS 352, NURS 360. Corequisite: NURS 363 and one of NURS 323, NURS 401.

name: Topics in Ethical Theory
description: Classic or contemporary works in ethical theory.

name: Philosophy of Action
description: Explanation of human actions; the conditions of responsibility; freedom of the will; the domains of rational and moral appraisal; the category of action and the individuation of actions.

name: Topics in Metaphysics
description: Topics including ontology, universals and particulars, substance, determinism and indeterminism, identity over time, and theories of truth.

name: Topics in Epistemology
description: Analysis of the concept of knowledge; problems of justifying ordinary and basic empirical beliefs.

name: Philosophy of Perception
description: The contribution of the senses to knowledge of the external world; the nature of perception and its contribution to empirical knowledge.

name: Topics in 19th-Century Philosophy
description: Study of a major 19th-century philosopher such as Hegel, Mill or Nietzsche, or school, such as German Idealism.

name: Theoretical Perspectives in Nursing: Primary Health Care
description: Analysis and application of theories, concepts, evidence and competencies guiding professional nursing practice in the context of primary health care. Prerequisite: Five of NURS 300, NURS 310, NURS 321, NURS 322, NURS 330, NURS 352, NURS 360. Corequisite: NURS 362 and one of NURS 323, NURS 401.

name: Topics in Philosophy of Language
description: Advanced topics in the philosophy of language.

name: Drugs and Society
description: Introductory principles of drug action. Historical and present day medical and non-medical use of drugs.  Prerequisite: One of BIOL 12, BIOL 111, BIOL 112, BIOL 153, BIOL 155, SCIE 001. Second-year standing is required.

name: Topics in the Philosophy of Cognitive Science
description: Philosophical topics in the cognitive sciences, such as empiricism vs. nativism, consciousness, mental representation, cognitive architecture, language & thought, and situated cognition.

name: Philosophy of Mind
description: The nature of the mental and physical; the relation between minds and bodies; the character of psychological explanation.

name: Fundamentals of the Pharmaceutical Sciences Disciplines
Introduction to Pharmacology
description: Fundamental concepts of drug-receptor interactions in the context of autonomic, autacoid, and psychoactive pharmacology.  Prerequisite: All of CAPS 205, CAPS 206. or CAPS 301 as a co-requisite.

name: Introduction to Pharmacology
description: The concepts, language and techniques of scientific pharmacology. Intended primarily for Honours and Major students in Pharmacology.  Prerequisite: Either(a) all of BIOL 200, BIOL 201, CHEM 233, CHEM 235 or (b) all of BIOL 200, BIOL 201, CHEM 203, CHEM 204; and CHEM 211 and one of CHEM 205, CHEM 201. Permission of the undergraduate advisor is required.

name: Research in the Pharmaceutical Sciences: Principles and Methods
Rational Basis of Drug Therapy
description: The principles and applications underlying the action and disposition of therapeutic agents (including alternative medicines) in the body. Use of drugs as tools in experimental research.  Prerequisite: One of BIOL 201, BIOC 202, BIOC 203, BIOC 300.

name: Introductory Pharmacology Laboratory
description: A series of experimental demonstrations and individual laboratory experiments illustrating the basic principles of pharmacology.  Corequisite: One of PCTH 300, PCTH 301.

name: Co-operative Work Placement I
description: Approved and supervised technical work experience in an industrial research setting for a minimum of 3.5 months. Technical report required. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-operative Education Program in Pharmacology. Prerequisite: One of PCTH 300, PCTH 303.

name: Topics in Continental Philosophy
description: A study of European philosophers from amongst Husserl, Heidegger, Habermas, Foucault, Derrida, Lacan, Levinas, and others.

name: Co-operative Work Placement II
description: Approved and supervised technical work experience in an industrial research setting for a minimum of 3.5 months. Technical report required. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-operative Education Program in Pharmacology. Prerequisite: [PCTH398]

name: Systematic Pharmacology
description: Lectures and discussions in scientific pharmacology, with a concentration on the scientific aspects of the pharmacology of neurohumoral transmission; mathematics of pharmacology; cardiovascular, respiratory and clinical pharmacology; and to a lesser extent on the pharmacology of various organs and tissues.  Prerequisite: Either (a) PCTH 303 or (b) one of PCTH 300, PCTH 305.

name: Basic Human Pharmacology
description: Lectures and assigned reading on the effects, mechanisms of action, absorption, distribution, fate and excretion of major classes of therapeutic agents. Indications for the use of particular drugs will be discussed in terms of risk versus benefit for the individual and for society.  Prerequisite: One of BIOL 201, BIOC 202, BIOC 203. Corequisite: CAPS 301.

name: Bio-Medical Ethics
description: Moral problems arising in the health sciences, especially in medicine but also in biology, psychology, and social work. Topics include abortion, death and euthanasia, genetic engineering, behaviour modification, compulsory treatment, experimentation with human beings and animals, and the relationship between professionals and their patients, subjects or clients. No philosophical background is required.

name: Ethics for the Sciences
