description: Economic strengths and weaknesses of current arrangements, and the prospects and objectives of various proposals for reform.

name: Operations and Logistics
description: The application of management tools and principles to production and allocation problems.

name: Economic Evaluation
description: Maximizing health benefits from health care budgets.

name: Information Technology for Management
description: The role of IT in health care management, the importance of effective IT in a health care setting, and the strategic uses of IT.

name: Buddhism in China
description: History, thought and practices of Chinese Buddhism from its beginnings until the twentieth century. Equivalency: ASIA382

name: Mystical Traditions: Jewish and Christian
description: Methodology, textual study and scholarly analysis of selected texts from these traditions.

name: Health Care Priority Setting
description: Application of priority setting and resource allocation methods to improve health from the perspective of the policy maker, health professional, and patient.

name: Health Information Systems
description: Information systems in planning and management of health care services provided through single-purpose units, comprehensive clinics and hospitals. Emphasis on computerized systems.

name: Indigenous Health and Cultural Safety
description: Core concepts of Indigenous-specific racism and human rights, cultural safety and how this relates to the practice of health administrators.

name: Program Planning and Evaluation
description: Basic concepts and principles underlying program planning and evaluation in health services.

name: Design and Measurement 2
description: Clinical Epidemiology, trials and the evaluation of diagnostic tools and therapeutic interventions.

name: Application of Statistics in Management
description: Data analysis and statistical inference. Applications in assessment of the legitimacy and significance of reports.

name: Intermediate Experimental Physics II
description: Thermodynamics experiments, modern physics experiments and use of computers in data analysis.

name: Design and Measurement 1
description: Basic concepts and methods in Epidemiology.

name: Co-operative Work Placement II
description: Approved and supervised technical work experience in an industrial research setting for a minimum of 3.5 months. Normally taken during the summer following the second year. Technical report required. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-operative Education Program in Physics. Prerequisite: [PHYS298]

name: Co-operative Work Placement I
description: Approved and supervised technical work experience in an industrial research setting for a minimum of 3.5 months. Normally taken during the winter term of the second year. Technical report required. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-operative Education Program in Physics. Prerequisite: PHYS 200.

name: Introduction to Biophysics
description: Physical principles involved in biological systems at the microscopic and molecular scales. Diffusion, low Reynolds number dynamics, the physicist's view of biomolecular structure, models of molecular motors and membranes.

name: Introduction to Quantum Mechanics
description: Principles and applications of quantum mechanics, wave mechanics, the Schroedinger equation, expectation values, Hermitian operators, commuting observables, one-dimensional systems, harmonic oscillators, angular momentum, three-dimensional systems.

name: Advanced Mechanics
description: Variational calculus, Lagrangian dynamics, rigid body motion including free and forced precession, Hamiltonian mechanics, Poisson brackets, canonical coordinates, Hamilton-Jacobi theory, action angle variables. Introduction to dynamical chaos: determinism, Lyapunov exponents.

name: Introduction to Modern Physics
description: Wave-particle duality of matter, special relativity, processes in atomic, nuclear and solid state, and introduction to quantum mechanical devices and techniques.

name: Electricity and Magnetism
description: Maxwell's equations and their applications, electrical fields and potentials of static charge distributions, current, fields of moving charges, magnetic fields, electromagnetic induction.

name: Electrical Laboratory
description: Selected experiments in electromagnetism and electronics; computer data acquisition; advanced data analysis and simulation.

name: Fluids
description: Kinetic theory: Diffusion, viscosity and sound waves. Introduction to hydrodynamics: Laminar flow, capillary and gravity waves, convection and turbulence. Dimensional analysis.

name: Introduction to Mathematical Physics
description: The application of ordinary and partial differential equations to physical problems; boundary and initial value problems associated with heat, wave and Laplace equations. Fourier analysis; expansions in Bessel and Legendre functions. Credit will be granted for only one of PHYS 312 and MATH 316.

name: Quantum Physics of Materials
description: Crystal structure, elasticity and phonons, elementary electronic transport, defects, alloys, liquid crystals and polymers.

name: Major Project, Part II
description: Prerequisite: RHSC 587. Permission of the project coordinator is also required.

name: Introduction to Religions in Asia
description: A survey of religious traditions of Asia, including communities, professionals, practices and beliefs of small-scale and large-scale societies. Approaches and theories drawn from the field of religious studies. Equivalency: ASIA110

name: Leadership in Rehabilitation
description: Leadership approaches, styles and research evidence applied to clinical rehabilitation contexts; Role and critique of emotional intelligence in effective personal leadership practices. Prerequisite: RHSC 501.

name: Machine Learning for Physics and Astronomy Data Analysis
description: Fundamental principles and applications of data-centric research techniques in Physics and Astronomy. Topics include algorithms for data structuring, dimensionality reduction, linear regression and classification, artificial neural nets, convolutional neural nets, unsupervised learning.

name: Doctoral Dissertation
description: Pass/Fail.

name: Death and Afterlife in Western Religious Tradition
description: A survey of traditional attitudes toward death and beliefs regarding human existence after death in Western religions.

name: Jews and Christians
description: Aspects of Jewish-Christian relations from the beginnings of Christianity to the present day. Emphasis on the study of Christian and Jewish texts in translation.

name: Experimental Acoustics
description: Experimental techniques of acoustics: data acquisition hardware and software, microphones, loudspeakers, noise, vibration and modal analysis.

name: Electronics Laboratory
description: A project-oriented lab introducing the design and construction of microprocessor-controlled devices.

name: Jews and Judaism in Canada
description: The history of the Jewish community in Canada, from New France to the present. Emphasis on the relationship between immigration and religious transformation, Jewish-Christian relations, the development of community structures.

name: Intermediate Punjabi I
description: Study of the grammar and introduction to Punjabi literature. Recommended pre-requisite: PUNJ 101.

name: Prophetic Figures in the Christian Tradition
description: Examined in their historical context and in terms of their continuing significance. Selection will vary from year to year, but may include Augustine, Thomas Aquinas, Martin Luther, and Teresa of Avila.

name: History of Christian Thought
description: Selected topics with special emphasis on doctrinal change and development, orthodoxy and heresy, tradition and authority, and Church and State in the Patristic, Medieval, Reformation, and Modern periods.

name: Jewish Literature in Translation
description: A survey of Jewish literature in medieval and modern times.

name: Classical Islam
description: The history and culture, values, and achievements of Islamic societies from 700-1500; the interconnections between power, politics, gender, and the arts in Islamic societies. This course is highly recommended as a basis for all 300- and 400-level Islamic Studies courses.

name: Modern Islam
description: The history and culture, values, and socio-political movements of the Islamic world from 1500 to the modern day; the interconnections between power, politics, gender, and the arts in modern Islamic societies. This course is highly recommended as a basis for all 300- and 400-level Islamic Studies courses.

name: Introductory Punjabi
description: Spoken and written Punjabi. Students who have taken Punjabi 11 in high school cannot take PUNJ 102 for credit.

name: Introduction to Asian Religions
description: The religions of India, China, and Japan in their interactions and cultural contexts, including Hinduism, Buddhism, Jainism, Sikhism, Taoism, Confucianism, and Shinto.

name: Intermediate Punjabi II
description: Continuation of PUNJ 201. Recommended pre-requisite: PUNJ 201.

name: History of Christianity II (15th C. C.E. - present)
description: The history of Christianity from the Reformation to the present day. Provides an historical overview of Christian thought and its institutions and significant people during the rise of the Reformation in various locales of Europe and beyond (Germany, France, Great Britain, Switzerland, and Scandinavia).

name: Intermediate Punjabi
description: Study of the grammar and introduction to Punjabi literature. Recommended pre-requisites: one of PUNJ 101, PUNJ 102.

name: Jewish Responses to Catastrophe
description: Topics include the destruction of the Second Temple, the Crusades, the expulsions from Spain and Portugal, and the Holocaust. A study of texts in translation.

name: Waris Shah's Hir
description: A detailed study of Waris Shah's poetic narration of the story of Hir. Emphasis is on reading and written expression. Analytical writing in English and Punjabi required. Recommended pre-requisite: PUNJ 300.

name: Applied Developmental Psychology
description: Applications of theories and research in developmental psychology to contemporary social issues; topics may include daycare, child abuse, divorce and remarriage, substance abuse, sexuality. Strongly recommended: PSYC 102 and one of PSYC 216, 217, or 277. Restricted to students with second-year standing or higher.

name: Clinical Nuclear Medicine
description: Daily discussions of the clinical applications of nuclear medicine. See PATH 730.

name: The Punjabi Novel (Advanced Punjabi)
description: Study of the modern Punjabi novel to deepen understanding and use of Punjabi, and strengthen analysis in English and Punjabi. Recommended pre-requisite: PUNJ 300.

name: Introduction to the Gurmukhi Script
description: The writing system of Punjabi for those with some background in the spoken language. May be taken at the same time as PUNJ 200.

name: Devotional Literature in Punjabi
description: Emphasis is on reading and written expression. Analytical writing in English and Punjabi required. Recommended pre-requisite: PUNJ 300.

name: Clinical Investigation or Research
description: Each resident is encouraged to complete an investigative project in each of the four years in Radiology, under the supervision of a faculty member, for possible presentation at an annual department meeting. Average 80 hours each year.

name: Memory: Historical, Clinical and Cognitive Perspectives
description: Classical and contemporary metaphors for memory and their impact on theory development. Strongly recommended: PSYC 101 and one of PSYC 216, 217, or 277. Restricted to students with second-year standing or higher.

name: Psychology of Sex Differences
description: Theory and research on gender development and the influence of sex and/or gender on cognition, emotion, motivation, social behaviour, and health. Strongly recommended: PSYC 101, 102 and PSYC 216, 217, or 277. Restricted to students with second-year standing or higher.

name: Introductory Punjabi II
description: Continuation of PUNJ 100. Students who have taken Punjabi 11 in high school cannot take PUNJ 101 for credit. Recommended pre-requisite: PUNJ 100.

name: Punjabi Theatre
description: Punjabi-language theatre, with emphasis on Canadian forms. Reading, writing, and performance of plays; examination of history of Punjabi theatre. Recommended pre-requisite: PUNJ 300.

name: Advanced Punjabi
description: Advanced grammar and conversation. Major genres of Punjabi literature. Recommended pre-requisites: one of PUNJ 200, PUNJ 202.

name: Childhood and Adolescence
description: Human development from the preschool period through adolescence. Strongly recommended: PSYC 102 and one of PSYC 216, 217, or 277. Restricted to students with second-year standing or higher.

name: Adulthood and Aging
description: Issues, theories, and psychological research regarding adulthood and the aging process. Strongly recommended: PSYC 102 and one of PSYC 216, 217, or 277. Restricted to students with second-year standing or higher.

name: Modern Punjabi Literature
description: Popular and literary works in modern Punjabi, with a focus on short stories and poetry. Emphasis on reading, writing, and vocabulary development. Recommended pre-requisite: PUNJ 300.

name: Forensic Psychology
description: The application of psychological theory and research to legal issues and the criminal justice system. Strongly recommended: PSYC 102 and one of PSYC 216, 217, or 277. Restricted to students with second-year standing or higher.

name: Memory II
description: Organic amnesia; remembering childhood events; the self and memory; and the problem of distinguishing genuine from simulated forgetting. Prerequisite: [PSYC333]

name: Gambling and Decision Making
description: The psychology of gambling behaviour, with emphasis on relevant work from judgment and decision-making, the cognitive neuroscience of choice, and clinical perspectives on disordered gambling. Strongly recommended: PSYC 101 and one of PSYC 216, 217, or 277. Restricted to students with second-year standing or higher.

name: Socialization: Media Content and Effects
description: Examines human development in the context of the socializing role of media. Strongly recommended: PSYC 102 and one of PSYC 216, 217, or 277. Restricted to students with second-year standing or higher.

name: Oral Histories in Punjabi
description: Develops students' oral expression and listening comprehension in Punjabi through Community Based Learning. Students engage in oral history collection in the Punjabi-speaking community and develop short video or sound projects. Analytical reading and writing required. Recommended pre-requisite: PUNJ 300.

name: The Psychology of Language II
description: Language and thought; deriving psychological principles from language universals; the psychology of literacy, dyslexia, multilingualism, and natural language processing. Prerequisite: [PSYC336]

name: Evolutionary Psychology
description: Theory and research on the evolution of the human mind, with emphasis on implications for cognition and behaviour in contemporary environments. Strongly recommended: PSYC 102 and one of PSYC 216, 217, or 277. Restricted to students with second-year standing or higher.

name: The Psychology of Language I
description: Psychological abilities underlying human language; language processing, lexical representation, and principles of online conversation; animal versus human communication. Strongly recommended: PSYC 101 and one of PSYC 216, 217, or 277. Restricted to students with second-year standing or higher.

name: Psychological Aspects of Human Sexuality
description: Human sexuality from a biopsychological, behavioural, and psychosocial perspective. Strongly recommended: PSYC 101, 102 and one of PSYC 216, 217, or 277. Restricted to students with second-year standing or higher.

name: Directed Studies in Psychology
description: Directed investigation of a research problem, requiring a written report of the findings. Requires the supervising faculty member's permission. See the Department's website for more information. Restricted to Majors in Psychology or Cognitive Systems with second-year standing or higher.

name: Language Contact and Multilingualism in the Romance-speaking World
description: A sociolinguistic examination of diverse multilingual contexts that characterise the Romance-speaking world.

name: Afterlife of the Text: Rewritings and Adaptations
description: How stories travel across media and across national and linguistic boundaries in the Romance-speaking world. Dialogue between different versions and inter-media translations. Questions of authorship and reception.

name: Short Fiction in Romance Literatures
description: A study of the genres of the novella and the short story within and across Romance cultures.

name: Introduction to Romance Language Cinema
description: Overview of the history, aesthetics and characteristics of films in French, Italian, Spanish, and/or Portuguese. Credit will be granted for only one of RMST 234 or RMST 305. Equivalency: RMST 234.

name: Theatre and Poetry of the Romance World
description: Theatre and poetry of the Romance-speaking world from the Middle Ages to the present day from a comparative perspective.

name: Honours Seminar
description: Orientation to psychological research, with special emphasis on ongoing research within the department; effective presentation of research findings, oral and written; critical evaluation of research. Requires a research project. Restricted to students in Honours Psychology. Prerequisite: All of PSYC 217, PSYC 218.

name: Special Topics in Romance Studies
description: Study of Romance literatures, cultures, languages, or communities. Topics vary from section to section. Consult Department for current offerings.

name: French Literature since the Revolution
description: French literature through reading and analysis of translated works.

name: French Cultural Identities
description: Aspects of French culture through a set of key concepts that weave across French history, politics, and social structures. Credit will be granted for only one of RMST 325 or FREN 380.

name: French Literature from the Middle Ages to the Revolution
description: French literature through reading and analysis of translated works. Credit will be granted for only one of RMST_V 321 or MDVL_V 301. Equivalency: MDVL_V 301.

name: Italian Literature and Culture of the Medieval and Early Modern Period
description: A thematic approach to Italian literary works from the origins to the end of the sixteenth century considered in a broad cultural context. Credit will be granted for only one of ITAL _V 303 or RMST _V 341. Equivalency: ITAL_V 303

name: Myths, Legends and Tales in Romance Literatures and Cultures
description: Study of foundational narratives shared by Romance literatures and cultures from a comparative perspective.

name: Quebecois Literature and Culture
description: Study of the historical, political and cultural contexts that influenced the development of literature and culture in Quebec. Credit will be granted for only one of RMST 324 or FREN 280.

name: Biostatistics
description: Data collection, numeric and graphic summarization, and elementary statistical analysis. Examples primarily from health sciences.

name: Italian Food Cultures
description: Analyses of Italian or Italian-style foodways and the role they play in articulating larger cultural issues. Credit can only be applied for one of ITAL_V 380, ITST_V 380, or RMST_V 340. Equivalency: ITAL_V 380 or ITST_V 380.

name: Francophone Indigenous Literatures in Dialogue
description: Comparative studies of literature and visual culture from British Columbia and Quebec.

name: Ethics and Ethical Decision Making in Health Care
description: Ethical dilemmas in the health care setting. Understanding how Ethical features of the system may contribute to or perpetuate some of these problems.

name: Strategic Management
description: Management of multi-faceted organizations; weighting functions, understanding industry and organization-specific effects.

name: Selected Topics
description: Current and emerging trends and issues.

name: Quality of Health Care
description: Current concepts, methods, and applications in health care quality assessment and improvement.

name: Social Determinants of Health
description: Foundations of population health. An overview of research on determinants of health, with an emphasis on the social determinants of health.

name: The French Enlightenment
description: A study of the cultural and intellectual dimensions of the Enlightenment period in France.

name: Research Project
description: Completion of a bounded project within a health agency and under individual faculty supervision. Honours/Pass/Fail.

name: Directed Studies
description: Opportunity to focus on a selected topic under faculty supervision.

name: Leadership and Management Skills
description: A comprehensive understanding of what it takes to be a credible leader in the health economy. Concepts of leadership through a number of lenses and perspectives, using case studies, group activities and individual assignments.

name: Working in Global Health
description: Planning/preparing for work in global health, with attention to health inequities and determinants internationally and domestically, the pursuit of partnerships to address this, power imbalances and ethical principles for carrying out this work. Health Science background not essential.

name: Understanding the Sociocultural Determinants of the Health of Populations
description: The idea of "population health," and the implementation and evaluation of programs or policies to improve health. Open to all students.

name: Introduction to Politics
description: Political issues and case studies, drawn from Canadian and international contexts, will be used to introduce students to central debates and concepts of politics and political analysis.

name: Learning Polish: Intermediate II
description: Continuation of POLS 201. Find out more athttps://cenes.ubc.ca/courses/. Credit will be granted for only one of POLS 202 or POLS 300.

name: Introduction to Twentieth-Century Polish Literature
description: Readings and discussion of selected works of representative writers. Find out more athttps://cenes.ubc.ca/courses/

name: Understanding the Sociocultural Determinants of the Health of Populations
description: The idea of "population health," and the implementation and evaluation of programs or policies to improve health. Open to all students.

name: Environmental Impacts on Human Health
description: Harmful environmental exposures in water, air, food; aspects of environment that are beneficial for health; environmental justice; emerging environmental health threats; how epidemiology and risk assessment inform public health policy and practice.

name: Canadian Political Ideas
description: Political theories and ideologies in Canada. Prerequisite: All of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 110, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or higher.

name: Topics in Health Informatics for Health/Life Sciences Students
description: Basic literacy in health informatics. Innovative approaches to healthcare implementation, access to care, and data utilization.

name: Federalism in Canada
description: Theory and practice of Canadian federalism, its relationship to public policy, cultural pluralism, social stresses, and role of the courts.​ Prerequisite: All of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 110, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or higher.

name: British Columbia Government and Politics
description: An examination of political history, party politics, and public policy in British Columbia.​ Prerequisite: Two of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 110, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or higher.

name: Introduction to Canadian Politics
description: Canadian governments, politics, and public policy. How policies emerge from politics contested through the interaction of institutions (Constitution, Parliament, federalism, elections, and the courts) and actors (individuals, parties, interest groups, nations). Insights are applied to explain current events and controversies.

name: Public Administration
description: The structure and organization of the administrative branch of government in theory and practice. Administrative powers and policy-making in the modern state. Examples of the administrative processes are drawn from Canada and other countries. Prerequisite: All of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 110, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or higher.

name: Quebec Government and Politics
description: The nature of politics and the conduct of government in contemporary Quebec. The course is open to students from fields other than political science. Prerequisite: All of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 110, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or higher.

name: Introduction to Political Systems Around the World
description: Compares political systems around the world. Investigates why some countries are democracies and others are dictatorships; how different countries resolve political conflict; how institutions and culture affect the use of power and collective choices. Prerequisite: POLI_V 100. Or second-year standing or higher.

name: Introduction to Global Politics
description: Examines key themes and issues in the study of political interaction between states and non-state actors, including international security, armed conflict and conflict management, global governance and international institutions, the world economy, poverty and inequality, and climate change. Prerequisite: POLI_V 100. Or second-year standing or higher.

name: Doctoral Seminar on Resources and Environment
description: Environment and resource management goals and issues.

name: Investigating Politics: An Introduction to Scientific Political Analysis
description: The logic, challenges, and major strategies of empirical political research. Core research tasks including: asking answerable questions, defining concepts, formulating hypotheses, gathering evidence, measuring variables, constructing comparisons, drawing causal inferences, and reporting findings.

name: Currents of Political Thought
description: A critical introduction to some major ideologies and traditions of Western political thought that examines their philosophical origins as well as their implications for political life. Prerequisite: POLI_V 100. Or second-year standing or higher.

name: Introduction to Romance Cultures
description: Explore the diverse cultures of France, Spain, Italy, Latin America and the Romance-speaking world from a comparative perspective.

name: Local Government and Politics in Canada
description: Local and regional political institutions and public policies in Canada, with particular attention to those of Vancouver and other British Columbia localities. Prerequisite: Two of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 110, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or higher.

name: Canadian Political Parties
description: The organization and operation of party politics and the systems of party competition in Canada. The focus is on national-level politics. Prerequisite: All of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 110, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or higher.

name: Introduction to Italian Culture II: From the Modern to the Post-Colonial Age
description: The debate around nation vs. empire vs. republic, from the Napoleonic age to our days, as captured in Italy's microcosm, condensing and often anticipating issues that have later become global. Credit can only be applied for one of ITAL_V 232, ITST_V 232 or RMST_V 242. Equivalency: ITAL_V 232 or ITST_V 232.

name: Introduction to Literatures and Cultures of the Romance World II: Modern to Post-Modern
description: An introduction to the main themes that shaped the Romance World in the age of the nation state, imperialism, colonization, and decolonization.

name: Paris
description: A cultural history of Paris surveyed through selected works of literature, cinema and art.

name: Made in Italy
description: Where do Italy's glamour, lifestyle, traditions come from? This course introduces Italy's multifaceted ways of being and the cultural creations of the peninsula in their context. Credit can only be applied for one of ITAL_V 110, ITST_V 110, or RMST_V 140. Equivalency: ITAL_V 110 or ITST_V 110.

name: Introduction to Italian Culture I: From the Middle Ages to the Early Modern Period
description: The shift from the Medieval to the Early Modern worldview, explored through some of the major representatives of the verbal and visual arts, from Dante to Machiavelli, from Giotto to Leonardo. Credit can only be applied for one of ITAL_V 231, ITST_V 231 or RMST_V 241. Equivalency: ITAL_V 231 or ITST_V 231.

name: Prose Fiction and Non-Fiction of the Romance World
description: Fiction and non-fiction of the Romance-speaking world from the Middle Ages to the present day from a comparative perspective.

name: Introduction to the Analysis of Portuguese and Brazilian Cultures
description: Critical analysis of different cultural genres, including music, film and visual art through the study of selected Portuguese and Brazilian texts. Credit will be granted for only one of PORT 222 or RMST 260. Equivalency: PORT 222.

name: Revolution!
description: Concepts, theories, and practice of protest, revolt, and revolution in the Hispanic world, highlighting the intersection of politics and culture through novels, poetry, letters, diaries, and/or historical accounts of specific revolutionary uprisings. Credit will be granted for only one of SPAN_V 280 or RMST _V 280. Equivalency: SPAN_V 280.

name: Introduction to Literatures and Cultures of the Romance World I: Medieval to Early Modern
description: An introduction to the main themes that shaped the Romance World as its different national identities emerged in the Mediterranean sphere.

name: Introduction to Hispanic Cultures
description: Cultural texts from Latin America and Spain. Examines their broad cultural and transnational impact on the Romance-speaking world of past and present.

name: History of the Romance Languages
description: Development of the Romance language family from its origins in Latin to contemporary varieties. Emphasis on French, Italian, Portuguese and Spanish. Prerequisite: A beginners' knowledge (A1) in at least of one of the Romance languages is highly recommended.

name: Introduction to Italian Cinema
description: A thematic course surveying major classics of Italian cinema, emphasizing their historical, political, social, philosophical and technical contexts. Credit can only be applied for one of ITAL_V 234, ITST_V 234 or RMST_V 250. Equivalency: ITAL_V 234 or ITST_V 234.

name: Theories of Canadian and International Social Development
Foundation MSW Integrative Seminar
description: Development of professional judgment, critical reflection, and integration of theory, practice, research and policy.

name: Advanced Analysis of Culture and Race in Social Work Practice
Experimental Physics
description: A laboratory course with a wide choice of experiments for fourth year Honours and Major students. Topics include solid state, nuclear, classical, quantum, electromagnetic and low temperature physics. For six credits, two weekly laboratory periods and completion of a project in second term are required. Prerequisite: One of PHYS 309, PHYS 319.

name: Computational Physics
description: Scientific programming applied to problems in physics. Fundamentals of numerical analysis for continuum problems. Solution of linear and non-linear algebraic systems, ordinary differential equations and stochastic problems. Prerequisite: One of PHYS 312, MATH 257, MATH 316 and one of PHYS 210, EOSC 211, CPSC 110, CPSC 103, APSC 160.

name: Social Work Practice in the Field of Aging
Radiation Biophysics
description: Physical and chemical interactions of ionizing radiations and their biological effects at the cellular, tissue and whole-animal levels.  Prerequisite: One of PHYS 102, PHYS 108, PHYS 118, PHYS 153, PHYS 158, SCIE 001. and third year standing in Science or Applied Science.

name: Optics
description: Principles and applications of optical physics. Interference, diffraction, coherence, polarization, Fresnel relations, optical coatings, waves in dielectric media, Gaussian beams, waveguides, optical cavities, lasers, fibre optics, and Fourier optics. Prerequisite: One of PHYS 301, PHYS 354 and one of MATH 215, MATH 255.

name: Theoretical Foundations of Social Work in the Health Field
Advanced Social Work Practice: Mental Health
Quantum Physics
description: Fundamentals of atomic, nuclear, particle, and condensed matter physics. Prerequisite: MATH 215 and one of CHEM 312, PHYS 200.

name: Introduction to General Relativity
description: Physical consequences of Einstein's equations, including the principle of equivalence, curved space-time, geodesics, the Schwarzschild solution, deflection of light, black holes, and gravitational radiation. Prerequisite: One of MATH 217, MATH 227, MATH 317 and one of MATH 215, MATH 255. PHYS 301 and one of PHYS 206, PHYS 306 are recommended.

name: Communities and Social Development: Debates, Approaches and Fields of Practice
Social Work Practice with Individuals and Couples
Physics of Biocellular Structure and Machinery
description: Molecular structure and architecture of biological cells, interactions of molecules in aqueous solution and at interfaces, physical properties of polymers and surfactants, mechanisms of cell membranes and cytoplasmic structures, thermodynamics of molecular machines and mechanical enzymes. Credit can not be given for both PHYS_V 437 and 537. Prerequisite: One of PHYS_V 313, PHYS_V 403, PHYS_V 455, CHEM_V 304.

name: Advanced Topics in Physics
description: Directed studies available to students in Honours Physics with approval from the Head of the Department.

name: Quantum Mechanics
description: Postulates of quantum mechanics, expectation values, hermitian operators, commuting observables, applications to one-dimensional systems, harmonic oscillators, angular momentum, applications in three dimensions, hydrogen atom, time dependent perturbations. Credit will be granted for only one of PHYS 304, 450 or CHEM 312. Prerequisite: One of PHYS 200, PHYS 250.

name: Statistical Mechanics
description: Introduction to quantum statistical mechanics and its application to systems of varying complexity from the simple ideal gas to the degenerate gas. Quantum fluids, phase transitions and simulation methods will also be introduced. Credit will be granted for only one of PHYS 403 or PHYS 455. Prerequisite: One of PHYS 257, PHYS 203, PHYS 313 and one of PHYS 304, PHYS 450.

name: Applied Optics
description: Basic applications of lasers, geometrical optics, fibre optics, diffraction, and Fourier optics. Prerequisite: All of PHYS_V 250, PHYS_V 354.

name: Honours Thesis
description: A research project, undertaken under the direction of a faculty member, culminating in a thesis.

name: Physics Demonstrations
description: The students will prepare, under the supervision of a faculty member, a demonstration or series of demonstrations intended to illustrate physical principles to diverse audiences. Intended for third- or fourth-year Physics Majors and Math/Science Education students.

name: Applied Electromagnetic Theory
description: Wave propagation and related phenomena in dielectrics, conductors and plasmas. Wave guides, radiation, antennae, special relativity. Prerequisite: One of PHYS_V 301, PHYS_V 354.

name: Zoological Physics
description: Animal systems viewed from a physicist's perspective. Topics include sensory systems, energy budgets, locomotion, internal flows, physical advantages of grouping. Prerequisite: One of PHYS 101, PHYS 106, PHYS 107, PHYS 117, PHYS 131, PHYS 157, SCIE 001. BIOL 325 is recommended. Equivalency: BIOL438

name: Social Work Practice with the Family
Qualitative Methods in Social Work Research
Advanced Integrative Seminar
description: Advanced development of professional judgment, critical reflection, and integration of theory, practice, research, policy.

name: Seminar in Social Work Practice Theory
Quantitative Methods in Social Work Research
Directed Field Studies in Social Work II
Seminar in Methodological Issues in Social Welfare
Orthopaedic Clinical Reasoning and Skills
description: Restricted to students in the Graduate Certificate in Orthopaedic Manipulative Physical Therapy program. Prerequisite: RHSC 501. Corequisite: PHTH 581.

name: Introductory Physics
description: Kinematics, force, energy, momentum, use of graphs and vectors in physics; thermal energy, heat transfer, Earth's energy balance; electricity. Students with credit for Physics 12 may not obtain credit for this course unless they took AP, IB, or A-level Physics and were offered advanced credit for PHYS 100.  Prerequisite: Not open to students with credit for PHYS 12. Principles of Mathematics 12 or Pre-calculus 12 is required; Physics 11 is required for first-year students, strongly recommended for others.

name: Clinical Decision Making V
description: Pass/fail.

name: Electricity, Light and Radiation
description: Introduction to optics, electricity and magnetism, electric circuits, radioactivity, including biological applications.  Prerequisite: One of PHYS_V 101, PHYS_V 107. Corequisite: One of MATH_V 101, MATH_V 103, MATH_V 105, MATH_V 121.

name: Enriched Physics II
description: Electricity and magnetism, electrical circuits, induction, electromagnetic waves, Maxwell's equations and applications.  Prerequisite: Either (a) one of PHYS_V 106, PHYS_V 107 or (b) a score of 85% or higher in one of PHYS_V 101, PHYS_V 117, PHYS_V 131. Corequisite: One of MATH_V 101, MATH_V 103, MATH_V 105, MATH_V 121.

name: Enriched Physics 1
description: Classical mechanics including conservation laws, angular momentum of rigid bodies and simple harmonic motion, wave phenomena, with an introduction to special relativity, quantum mechanics, nuclear physics, statistical mechanics and solid state physics.  Prerequisite: Either (a) a score of 85% or higher in all of PHYS 12, MATH 12 or (b) a score of 85% or higher in all of PHYS 12, PREC 12 or (c) a score of 85% or higher in all of PHYS 12, CALC 12 or (d) a score of 85% or higher in PHYS 100. MATH 12 = Principles of Mathematics 12; PREC 12 = Pre-Calculus 12; CALC 12 = Calculus 12; PHYS 12 = Physics 12. Corequisite: One of MATH_V 100, MATH_V 102, MATH_V 104, MATH_V 120, MATH_V 180, MATH_V 184.

name: Public Health, Transportation, and the Built Environment
description: Health issues associated with transportation and the built environment; design of urban form for non-motorized transportation for the improvement of personal and environmental health; factors that impact transportation choices; applying findings from research to specific transportation planning processes and projects. Credit will be granted for only one of PLAN 579 or SPPH 571. Equivalency: PLAN579

name: Dynamics and Waves
description: Kinematics including curvilinear motion. Forces and Newton's laws of motion. Work-energy theorem, conservation of energy. Conservation of momentum, collisions. Torque, rotational dynamics, angular momentum. Oscillations and waves.  Prerequisite: One of PHYS 12, PHYS 100. Corequisite: One of MATH 100, MATH 102, MATH 104, MATH 110, MATH 120, MATH 180, MATH 184.

name: Enriched Physics 1 (lecture)
description: Classical mechanics including conservation laws, angular momentum of rigid bodies and simple harmonic motion, wave phenomena, with an introduction to special relativity, quantum mechanics, nuclear physics, statistical mechanics and solid state physics.  Prerequisite: Either (a) a score more than 85% in all of PHYS 12, MATH 12 or (b) a score more than 85% in all of PHYS 12, PREC 12 or (c) a score more than 85% in all of PHYS 12, CALC 12 or (d) a score more than 85% in PHYS 100. PHYS 12 = Physics 12; MATH 12 = Principles of Mathematics 12; PREC 12 = Pre-Calculus 12; CALC 12 = Calculus 12. Corequisite: One of MATH 100, MATH 102, MATH 104, MATH 120, MATH 180, MATH 184.

name: Evidence and Theory in Musculoskeletal Physical Therapy
description: Restricted to students in the Graduate Certificate in Orthopaedic Musculoskeletal Physical Therapy program. Prerequisite: RHSC 501. Corequisite: PHTH 580.

name: Enriched Experimental Physics
description: A laboratory course accompanying PHYS 108 with emphasis on data collection and analysis and experimental techniques.  Prerequisite: PHYS 107. Corequisite: One of PHYS 108, PHYS 118.

name: Current Issues in Public Health Practice
Energy and Waves
description: Fluids, harmonic oscillator, travelling waves, standing waves, sound, and interference of light waves, including diffraction.  Prerequisite: One of PHYS 12, PHYS 100. Corequisite: One of MATH 100, MATH 102, MATH 104, MATH 110, MATH 120, MATH 180, MATH 184.

name: Introduction to Indigenous Health Research Ethics
description: Principles and regulatory requirements related to conducting health research with Indigenous communities.

name: Selected Topics
description: By seminar and directed readings, certain topics of current interest are explored in depth.

name: Occupational and Environmental Hygiene Project
description: Applied project on approved topic based on practicum: requires a written and oral report.

name: Introduction to Quantitative and Qualitative Research Methods in Indigenous Health Research
description: Qualitative, quantitative and mixed methods research as applied to Indigenous public health priorities.

name: Special Topics in Hispanic Studies
description: Study of Hispanic literatures, cultures, languages, or communities. Topics vary from section to section. Consult Department for current offerings. Recommended for students in 3rd year or above. Restricted to students with 2nd year standing or above.

name: Topics in Nineteenth-century Italian Literature and Culture
description: Italian literature of the 19th century in its intellectual, socio-political, and cultural context. Credit will be granted for only one of ITST _V 418 or ITAL _V 408 or RMST _V 458. Equivalency: ITST _V 418 or ITAL _V 408

name: Topics in Modern and Contemporary Italian Literature and Culture
description: Italian literature of the 20th century in its intellectual, socio-political and cultural context. Credit will be granted for only one of RMST _V 459, ITST _V 419 or ITAL_V 409. Recommended pre-requisite: Second-year standing or higher. Equivalency: ITST_V 419 or ITAL_V 409.

name: M.P.H. Capstone
description: Restricted to students in the Master of Public Health. Prerequisites: All of SPPH_V 521, SPPH_V 500, SPPH_V 502, SPPH_V 503.

name: M.Sc. Thesis
description: Pass/Fail.

name: Collecting, Analyzing and Using Public Health Data in Indigenous Communities
description: Applied biostatistics, epidemiology and data management addressing public health priorities and clinical research in Indigenous communities.

name: Mental Health Care and Delivery in Indigenous Communities
description: Approaches to mental health and resilience concepts and strength based interventions with Indigenous communities.

name: Studies in Portuguese and Brazilian Culture
description: Selected topics. Please see the Department website for current course offering information. Credit will be granted for only one of PORT_V 405 or RMST_V 460. Recommended: Second-year standing or higher. Equivalency: PORT_V 405.

name: Indigenous Health Policy in Canada
description: Indigenous health policy and history in Canada through four substantive areas: economics and financing; need and demand; ethics, rights and law; quality and effectiveness.

name: Environmental Health and Indigenous Communities
description: Environmental risk factors faced by Indigenous communities in land, air and water.

name: Interdisciplinary Approach to Understanding the Health of Indigenous Peoples
description: Indigenous health through core public health disciplines and interdisciplinary approaches.

name: Studies in Romance Languages and Cultures
Social Determinants of Indigenous Health
description: Survey of impacts of land and resources, housing, education, criminal justice systems, child apprehension and other determinants on the health of Indigenous peoples in Canada.

name: Research Intensive Seminar in Romance Studies
Learning Russian 4
description: Continuation of RUSS_V 201. Find out more athttps://cenes.ubc.ca/courses/Credit will be granted for only one of RUSS_V 202 or RUSS_V 200.

name: Learning Russian 5
description: Continuation of RUSS_V 202. Find out more athttps://cenes.ubc.ca/courses/Credit will be granted for only one of RUSS_V 301 or RUSS_V 300.

name: Learning Russian 3
description: Continuation of RUSS_V 102. Find out more athttps://cenes.ubc.ca/courses/Credit will be granted for only one of RUSS_V 201 or RUSS _V 200.

name: Korean Government and Politics
description: An introduction to the politics of Korea. The evolution of Korean politics from authoritarian rule to democratic transition, focusing on present and future political, economic and social issues. Prerequisite: All of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or higher.

name: Gender and Politics
description: Relations between gender and political processes and institutions, including the impact of globalization and economic development. Prerequisite: All of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or higher.

name: The U.S. Presidency in Comparative Perspective
description: Executive leadership of the U.S. presidency in comparison to the leadership of other Anglo-American systems, including the U.K., Canada, and Australia. Prerequisite: All of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or higher.

name: Comparative Federalism
description: An empirical and normative analysis of federalism as a way of structuring political life in industrialized democracies, investigating explanations for the design, persistence and operation of federal systems. Prerequisite: All of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or higher.

name: Learning Russian 2
description: Continuation of RUSS _V 101. Find out more athttps://cenes.ubc.ca/courses/. Credit will be granted for only one of RUSS_V 102 or RUSS _V 100.

name: Politics and Development
description: The relationship between political institutions and economic growth. How governments shape economic policy and development aid. Prerequisite: All of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or higher.

name: Comparative Democratization
description: Literatures and theories on regime democratization around the world; the roles of political, economic, social, and international factors in encouraging or impeding democratization. Prerequisite: All of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or higher.

name: Associations and the State in Comparative Perspective
description: How organised groups (civil society organizations, NGOs, interest groups) interact with governments in a variety of countries. Prerequisite: All of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or higher.

name: Issues in Comparative Politics
description: An examination of a major issue in comparative politics (e.g., the media, gender, nationalism, ethnic conflict). Topics will vary from year to year. Prerequisite: All of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or higher.

name: Politics and Government of Latin America
description: A comparative examination of democracy and authoritarianism in Latin America: populism, corporatism, bureaucratic authoritarianism, transitions from authoritarianism, and contemporary debates on the quality and diversity of democratic institutions. Prerequisite: All of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or higher.

name: Japanese Political Economy
description: Issues in contemporary Japanese political economy, including industrial policy, the Keiretsu groupings, the main-bank system, trends toward deregulation, and business-labour relations. Prerequisite: All of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or higher.

name: Learning Russian 1
description: Introduction to the language for beginners. Ability to enjoy communicating in everyday situations and cultural contexts. Find out more athttps://cenes.ubc.ca/courses/Credit will be granted for only one of RUSS_V 101 or RUSS _V 100.

name: History of Political Ideas
description: An introduction to the political ideas of leading political philosophers from Ancient Greece to the 19th century. Prerequisite: All of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or above.

name: Russian Conversation Practice 1
description: Emphasis on the study of oral communication skills and strategies. Find out more athttps://cenes.ubc.ca/courses/Credit will be granted for only one of RUSS_V 208 or RUSS_V 215. Equivalency: RUSS_V 215.

name: Learning Russian 6
description: Continuation of RUSS_V 301. Find out more athttps://cenes.ubc.ca/courses/Credit will be granted for only one of RUSS_V 302 or RUSS_V 300.

name: Social and Political Thought
description: An examination of some of the major concepts in political philosophy such as justice, equality, rights, obligation, liberty in the context of both classical and contemporary political thought. Prerequisite: All of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or higher.

name: Theories of State and Society
description: Classical origins of contemporary theories of the state, market, and civil society, focused on the relationship between social order, politics, and democracy. Readings from Smith, Tocqueville, Weber, and contemporary sources. Prerequisite: All of POLI_V 100, POLI_V 101, POLI_V 240. Or third-year standing or higher.

name: Control of Communicable Disease
description: Epidemiology of viral, bacterial and parasitic infections with emphasis on the control of these infections in human populations. Immunization programs will be stressed. Prerequisite: Either (a) SPPH 400 or (b) SPPH 521; and SPPH 502.

name: Modern Political Theory: Analysis of a Selected Theorist
description: A detailed examination of an acknowledged masterpiece of modern political theory. The text and attendant literature vary from year to year. Consult the departmental website. Prerequisite: All of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or higher.

name: Statistics for Health Research
description: Planned collection, numeric and graphic summarization, elementary statistical analysis of data. Examples from health sciences illustrate standard techniques for parametric and nonparametric hypothesis testing; regression and correlation; contingency tables. Also randomization, "blindfolding" and other specifically biomedical topics in statistics. Credit will be granted for only one of SPPH 400 or SPPH 521.

name: Core Biological Concepts of Public Health Practice
description: Cell biology, microbiology, molecular science, genetics, physiology, and evolution.

name: Contemporary Political Theory
description: Topics may include freedom, colonialism, capitalism, Critical Theory and ideology, power and knowledge, social justice, rationalism, gender and identity politics, and the political. Prerequisite: All of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or higher.

name: Topics in Environmental Health
description: Role of air, water, food and solid waste as sources of human health risks; global environmental health issues; sustainability.

name: Issues and Concepts in Public Health
description: History of public health research and practice; occupational and environmental health; health services and systems; social and lifecourse determinants of health; and population health and emerging trends.

name: Major Essay
description: Required for all M.H.Sc. students. Pass/Fail.

name: Social Determinants of Health
description: Foundational thinking giving rise to the concept of population health. Overview of the current state of research.

name: Rural and Remote Health
description: Issues and solutions to delivery of health services to underserved rural populations. Prerequisite: Either (a) SPPH_V 400 or (b) SPPH_V 521; and SPPH_V 502. Corequisite: SPPH_V 500

name: Leadership in Public Health
description: Organizational structure; engaging others in an organization; inter-organizational networking; building coalitions; identification of opportunities to bring change to organizations through knowledge development, management, synthesis, and implementation.

name: Global Health and Human Security
description: Global threats to human health stemming from conflict, poverty, and environmental degradation.

name: Epidemiology of Occupational and Environmental Health
description: Design and analysis of etiologic research in occupational health. Prerequisite: SPPH 502. or permission of the instructor.

name: Environmental Health Risk Assessment and Communication
Toxicology and Public Health
description: Mechanism of action of commonly encountered occupational toxic agents; relevance of laboratory and epidemiological evidence. Prerequisite: Permission of instructor.

name: Behavioural and Neuroscientific Research Methods
description: Research methods used in the neurosciences. Credit will be granted for only one of PSYC_V 217 or PSYC_V 277. Restricted to students in one of NSCI Major, BSc COGS Major (Cognition and Brain stream).

name: Health Care Systems Analysis
description: Theory, concepts, measurement, and practical skills using administrative data for analysis of health care systems.

name: Occupational Health and Illness Processes
description: Occupational diseases; research, historical perspectives, and surveillance.

name: Analysis of Behavioural and Neuroscientific Data
description: Statistical methods for use in the neurosciences. Credit will be granted for only one of: PSYC_V 218, PSYC_V 278, BIOL_V 300, COMM_V 291, ECON_V 325, ECON_V 327, EPSE_V 482, FRST_V 231, GEOG_V 374, KIN_V 371, POLI_V 380, SOCI_V 328, STAT_V 200, STAT_V 203. Restricted to students in one of NSCI Major, BSc COGS Major (Cognition and Brain stream).Prerequisite: One of PSYC 217, PSYC 277.

name: Infancy
description: Human cognition, perception, motor, social, emotional needs, brain development and their interactions from birth until the emergence of language. Strongly recommended: PSYC 101, 102, and one of PSYC 216, PSYC 217, or 277. Restricted to students with second-year standing or higher.

name: Principles of Animal Behaviour
description: Behavioural neuroscience; behavioural genetics; social systems; mating and parental strategies; instinct and learning; evolution of human behaviour. Credit will be given for only one of BIOL 310 or PSYC 306. Strongly recommended: PSYC 101, and one of PSYC 216, 217, or 277. Restricted to students with second-year standing or higher.

name: Cognitive Processes
description: Contribution of cognitive processes to perception, attention, and memory; cognitive development, language, thinking, and creativity. Strongly recommended: PSYC 101 and one of PSYC 216, 217, or 277. Restricted to students with second-year standing or higher.

name: Brain and Behaviour
description: The neurobiological bases of behaviour; brain processes involved in perception, motivation, emotion, psychopathology, learning and memory. A maximum of 6 credits can be granted for either PSYC 304 or PSYC 370 and 371. Strongly recommended: PSYC 101 and one of PSYC 216, PSYC 217, PSYC 277. Restricted to all Arts and Science students with second-year standing or higher, excluding those in the B.Sc. Behavioural Neuroscience or B.Sc. Neuroscience specializations.

name: Tests and Measurements
description: Theory and practice of psychological measurement, statistical models for items and tests, assessment of test reliability and validity, factor analysis, scoring. Restricted to students with second-year standing or higher. Prerequisite: One of PSYC 218, PSYC 278.

name: Psychology of Sport
description: Psychological theory, research, and skills training related to sport performance, exercise motivation, and adherence. Credit will be granted for only one of PSYC 311 and KIN 150 and 231. Strongly recommended: PSYC 101 and one of PSYC 216, 217, or 277. Restricted to students with second-year standing or higher.

name: Introduction to Psychopathology and Clinical Science
description: The definition, history, and scope of mental illness; emphasis on the psychological factors that control its origins, maintenance, and modification. Restricted to students with second-year standing or higher. Strongly recommended: PSYC_V 101, 102, and one of PSYC_V 216, 217, or 227.

name: Cultural Psychology
description: Cultural influences on human thought and behaviour; interactions of culture and self; multicultural experiences; intercultural relations; methodological issues. Strongly recommended: PSYC 102, and one of PSYC 216, 217, or 277. Restricted to students with second-year standing or higher.

name: Cross-National Comparisons in the Social Sciences
description: Credit will be granted for only one of SOCI 511 or IAR 511. Credit will be granted for only one of SOCI 511 or IAR 511. Equivalency: IAR 511

name: Social Psychology
description: Theory and research of individual social behaviour; social motivation; attitudes; group interaction; socialization; prejudice. Strongly recommended: PSYC 102, and one of PSYC 216, 217, or 277. Restricted to students with second-year standing or higher.

name: Brain Dysfunction and Recovery
description: Cognitive and behavioral impairments resulting from brain dysfunction. Focus on the efficacy of various intervention approaches. Strongly recommended: PSYC 101, 102, and one of PSYC 216, PSYC 217, or 277. Credit will be granted for only one of PSYC 301 or NSCI 302. Restricted to students with second-year standing or higher.

name: Italian Fascism in Interdisciplinary Perspective
description: The cultural, literary, philosophical roots of Fascism and its evolution: its policies in literature, sports, cinema, architecture, racial legislation, and colonial adventures. Credit will be granted for only one of ITAL_V 345, ITST_V 345 or RMST_V 345. Equivalency: ITAL_V 345, ITST_V 345

name: Personality Psychology
description: Theory and research on individual differences in motivation, emotion, and social behaviour. Strongly recommended: PSYC 102, and one of PSYC 216, 217, or 277. Restricted to students with second-year standing or higher.

name: Seminar in Work, Industry and Technology
Masterpieces of the Novella in Italian Literature
description: A study of the genre of the novella as an expression of social and political contexts within and across cultures from its inception in feudal times to the post-modern age. Credit will be granted for only one of ITAL_V 333, ITST_V 333 or RMST_V 343. Equivalency: ITST_V 333 or ITAL_V 333

name: History of Psychology
description: The principal trends of psychological explanation and events in the history of psychology from the earliest times to the present. Strongly recommended: PSYC 101 and one of PSYC 216, 217, or 277. Restricted to Psychology Major or Psychology Honours students.

name: Cultural Exchange between Modern Italy and China
description: Key moments and texts about intercultural exchange between Italy and China since the beginning of the twentieth century in their social, historical, and political contexts. Credit can only be applied for one of ITAL_V 377, ITST_V 377 or RMST_V 344. Equivalency: ITAL_V 377 or ITST_V 377.

name: Health Psychology
description: Health-related behaviours such as smoking and drug use; effects of stressful events on health; methods for coping with stress; impact of chronic illness on the family; social support systems. Strongly recommended: PSYC 102 and one of PSYC 216, 217, or 277. Restricted to students with second-year standing or higher.

name: Analyzing Quantitative Data in Sociology
description: Prerequisite: SOCI 502 is a prerequisite for Sociology graduate students. A background in material such as that covered in SOCI 502 is highly recommended for all others.

name: Colonial and Postcolonial Italy
description: Italian colonialism in the twentieth century and postcolonial legacy in recent decades through media, literary, and cinematic texts. Credit can only be applied for one of ITAL_V 378, ITST_V 378 or RMST_V 346. Equivalency: ITAL_V 378 or ITST_V 378

name: Gender and Sexuality in Italian Cinema
description: Gender and sexuality in Italian cinema within the country's historical, sociopolitical, and cultural milieus. Credit can only be applied for one of ITAL_V 379, ITST_V 379 or RMST_V 347. Equivalency: ITAL_V 379 or ITST_V 379.

name: Italian Cinema: Neorealism
description: A survey of the major classics of post-WWII Italian Neorealism in cinema emphasizing their historical, political, social, philosophical and technical contexts. Credit will be granted for only one of ITAL _V 385, ITST _V 385, or RMST _V 355. Equivalency: ITAL _V 385 or ITST _V 385

name: Special Topics in Italian Studies
description: Study of Italian literatures, cultures, languages, or communities. Topics vary from section to section. Consult Department for current offerings.

name: Italian Literature and Culture of the Modern and Contemporary Age
description: The development of modern and contemporary Italian literature and culture against the background of social and historical events. Credit will be granted for only one of ITAL_V 304 or RMST_V 342. Equivalency: ITAL_V 304.

name: Qualitative Data Analysis in Sociology
description: Prerequisite: SOCI 503.

name: Brazilian and Portuguese Cultures
description: Examines materials from a variety of cultural genres, including Lusophone cultural manifestations such as fado, futebol, samba, cuisine, telenovelas and more.

name: The Brazilian Amazon
description: Examines the complexity and diversity of the Brazilian Amazon, engaging in a variety of topics of interdisciplinary nature, with focus on the peoples, literatures and cultures of this region, and through the use of various genres.

name: Studies in Portuguese and Brazilian Literature
description: Selected topics. Please see the Department website for current course offering information. Credit will be granted for only one of PORT_V 392 or RMST_V 361. Equivalency: PORT_V 392.

name: The Global Renaissance:  Hispanic Cross-Cultural Contacts
description: Early modern (ca. 1400-1700) literature and culture. Exploration of Spain's Mediterranean, Transatlantic and Transpacific cross-cultural contacts.

name: Scientific Basis for Epidemiological Thinking
description: The course will provide a framework for students to use epidemiological and other scientific evidence to make decisions about causation and to recommend policy actions.

name: Hopscotch: Topics in Hispanic Literature
description: Spain and Latin America's contributions to global culture through popular Hispanic literature in translation. Credit will be granted for only one of SPAN _V 312 or RMST _V 372. Equivalency: SPAN_V 312.

name: Quantitative Research Methods
description: Major quantitative research designs, measurement reliability and validity, common data sources used, internal and external validity, research proposals, and peer review.

name: M.Sc. Research Seminar
description: SPPH 507 in conjunction with SPPH 607 is a required course for students in the M.Sc. program. Students present and discuss their research and other topics of interest.

name: Genetic Epidemiology
description: Human genetics and genomics, behavioural, social, and environmental factors in modifying or influencing genetics in the manifestation of disease. Prerequisite: SPPH 502

name: Masterpieces in Hispanic Literature
description: Literary texts from Spain and the Hispanic world. Examines their broad cultural and transnational impact on the Romance-speaking world of yesterday and today.

name: The Design and Analysis of Clinical Trials
description: Ethical considerations, intention-to-treat versus efficacy trials, principles of sampling and exclusion, methods of allocation and techniques of randomization, parallel versus cross over design, monitoring treatment outcomes, adverse effects, stopping rules, analytic techniques and data interpretation, and logistical issues in the management of clinical trials. Prerequisite: One of SPPH 502, SPPH 513.

name: Survey Methods in Health Measurement
description: Concepts and techniques of measurement in epidemiological research. Topics covered include validity, reliability and misclassification, scale design and the construction of questionnaires and indices for both health outcomes and exposures. Prerequisite: One of SPPH 400, SPPH 521.

name: Mapping Gendered Spaces in Hispanic Literature and Culture
description: Examines selected topics in gender and sexuality in diverse time periods, geographical contexts, and literary genres in Spain and Latin America.

name: M.P.H. Practicum
description: Applied epidemiology and biostatistics in a field setting. Pass/Fail.

name: Cancer Control and Epidemiology
description: Collection and analysis of epidemiological data on cancer; genetic, occupational, and other risk factors; analytic techniques; cancer control, prevention, screening, early detection, and policy issues. Prerequisite: SPPH 502. or equivalent.

name: Clinical Epidemiology
description: Principles and methods of epidemiology are applied to clinical problems. Evaluation and design of laboratory and clinical tests and of therapeutic interventions. Prerequisite: Either (a) SPPH 400 or (b) SPPH 521; and SPPH 502.

name: Clinical Research methods for Surgical Procedures
Pharmacoepidemiology
description: Principles and applications of pharmacoepidemiology. Practical skills in designing, conducting, and appraising studies of medications in large populations. Credit will be granted for only one of SPPH 551 or PHAR 561. Prerequisite: Previous coursework in statistics or biostatistics.

name: Surveillance and Monitoring in Public Health
description: Prerequisite: Either (a) SPPH 400 or (b) SPPH 521; and SPPH 502.

name: Decision Analysis in Health Care
description: Methods and application of decision analysis to improve health from the perspective of the policy maker, health professional, and patient. Prerequisite: Either (a) SPPH 400 or (b) SPPH 521; and SPPH 502.

name: Qualitative Methods in Health Research Design
description: Purposes, context, procedures, and relationships within qualitative health research and methodologies.

name: Foundations of Public Health Computing
description: Data gathering, cleaning, analysis, and visualization to produce key results using statistical software. Prerequisite: Either (a) SPPH 400 or (b) SPPH 521; and SPPH 502.

name: Public Health Approaches to Substance Use and Addictions
description: Critical examination of strategies regarding addictive behaviours, substance use and related problems, in the context of a multi-disciplinary approach.

name: Chemical and Biological Hazard Measurement
description: Industrial hygiene and environmental exposure monitoring, methods, and instrumentation, and theory. Laboratories demonstrate workplace sampling and analysis techniques. [2-3] Prerequisite: SPPH 535.

name: Principles and Practices of Injury Prevention
description: Injury epidemiology; surveillance; development, implementation, and evaluation techniques of preventive strategies; determinants of health; social marketing; injury policy; evidence-based prevention strategies; utilization of injury datasets.

name: Methods for Systematic Reviews in Health Research
Occupational Hygiene Practice
description: Application of occupational hygiene principles using field investigations, critical appraisal of results, and communication with labour and management. [2-3] Prerequisite: SPPH 562. Corequisite: SPPH 563.

name: Science and Risk Communication for Public Health
description: Theory and practice of risk communication in public health, basic principles underlying effective science communication with peers, the media, and the public.

name: Technical Aspects of Occupational Hygiene Hazard Controls
description: Industrial ventilation, heating and air conditioning systems, respiratory protection, chemical protective clothing. Prerequisite: SPPH 535.

name: Ergonomics
description: Human factors in workplace design, anthropometry, work physiology.

name: Mathematical Modelling of Communicable Diseases
description: Application of mathematical models in understanding communicable disease dynamics and control; interpretation of model outcomes; modelling methods and their applications.

name: Quantitative Methods for the Assessment and Analysis of Exposure Data
description: Determinants of exposure, sampling strategies.

name: Major Essay
description: Required for Master of Health Administration (M.H.A.) non-thesis program.

name: Addiction and Mental Health
description: Severe addiction and mental illness and the systemic context in which they occur.

name: Industrial and Environmental Acoustics and Vibration
description: Fundamentals of acoustics and vibrations, physiologic effects, measurement, instrumentation, interpretation of data, industrial standards, and control. For students in Occupational and Environmental Hygiene; other graduate students may enrol with permission of the instructor.

name: Global Indigenous Politics
description: The political dynamics of Indigenous peoples' politics on the global level; the legal and practical realities of colonization as a global Indigenous experience; current global Indigenous political issues and avenues of Indigenous resistance. Prerequisite: All of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or higher.

name: Advanced Topics in Occupational and Environmental Health
description: Recommended: SPPH 567 or an equivalent statistics or quantitative course is recommended. Prerequisite: All of SPPH 502, SPPH 535. Corequisite: SPPH 522.

name: Canadian Perspectives on Human Rights
description: Key issues in the theory and practice of human rights in Canada. Topics will vary from year to year. Prerequisite: All of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 110, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or higher.

name: Occupational Safety Programs and Systems
description: Safety management; systems analysis; accident investigation; collection of accident data; fault trees; total loss control.

name: Chinese Politics and Development
description: The course will explore various aspects of Chinese politics and the dynamics of China's development since 1949. Topics include: the Cultural Revolution, political reform and protest, and economic reform policies and their consequences. Prerequisite: All of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or higher.

name: Japanese Government and Politics
description: Introduction to modern Japanese politics and public policy from various theoretical and comparative perspectives. Prerequisite: Two of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 110, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or higher.

name: Threats to Contemporary Democracies
description: Domestic and international challenges to democracy, and innovative democratic responses to populism, polarization, globalization and disinformation. Prerequisite: Two of POLI_V 100, POLI_V 101, POLI_V 110, POLI_V 240. Or third-year standing or higher.

name: Government and Politics of the United States of America
description: The distinctive political system of the U.S. Covers all major institutions and processes, focusing on contemporary issues. Comparisons with the Canadian system. Sources of political failure and possible reform. Prerequisite: All of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or higher.

name: Topics in Comparative Politics
description: Topics will vary from year to year. Consult the departmental website. Prerequisite: All of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or higher.

name: Social Policy and Program Planning in the Health Field
Child and Family: Policy and Practice
European Politics: Selected Cases
description: The politics and government of one or more European countries: political development, institutional structure, party politics, and policy-making. The specific country or countries will vary by section. Prerequisite: All of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or higher.

name: Communist and Post-Communist Politics
description: An examination of the origins, development, and demise of Communist political systems, as well as the nature of post-Communist politics, with special emphasis on the Soviet Union and its successor states. Prerequisite: All of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or higher.

name: The Strategy of Politics
description: Uses game theory to show how politicians strike bargains, outmanoeuvre opponents, and manipulate institutional rules. Prerequisite: Two of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 110, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or higher.

name: Political Psychology
description: How psychology explains political behavior, exploring personality, cognition, emotion, and social influence in political identity, media effects, leadership, conflict, and decision-making. Prerequisite: Two of POLI_V 100, POLI_V 101, POLI_V 110, POLI_V 240. Or third-year standing or higher.

name: Southeast Asian Government and Politics
description: The political systems of contemporary Southeast Asia. Prerequisite: All of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or higher.

name: Advanced Data Analysis in Social Work
Topics in Canadian Politics
description: An important topic in Canadian politics and public policies. Possible topics include elections, media, and gender and identity. Topics vary year to year; seehttp://www.politics.ubc.ca/courses. Prerequisite: Two of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 110, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or higher.

name: South Asian Government and Politics
description: Comparative analysis of politics and government in India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, and Sri Lanka. Imperial legacies and nationalist movements; political institution-building amidst socio-cultural diversity; parties and interest groups; elections and leadership crises; military intervention; ethnic and class conflicts; foreign policy. Prerequisite: All of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or higher.

name: European Integration
description: Post-1945 integration of Europe, comparison of national politics and attitudes to integration, and the history and institutions of the European Union. Prerequisite: All of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or higher.

name: Social Work Doctoral Seminar
description: Critical examination of research, teaching, proposal writing and publication.

name: Social Theory, Ideology and Ethics
description: Critical analysis of major social theories, differentiating competing approaches to understanding human behaviour; social theory, social ideology, and social ethics.

name: Inequality and Social Change
description: Inequality, institutions, social structure and social change. Credit will be granted for only one of SOCI 102 or SOCI 100.

name: Social Interaction and Culture
description: Culture, identity, social interaction, relationships and socialization. Credit will be granted for only one of SOCI 101 or SOCI 100.

name: Global Population Dynamics
description: Core processes that influence world population patterns and trends.

name: Ethnicity
description: An introduction to the study of the relations between ethnic groups and of the interplay between ethnicity and other social factors.

name: The Caribbean: Frontiers of the Romance World
description: Literature and culture from the island of Hispaniola (Haiti, Dominican Republic) and the French Caribbean from a comparative perspective.

name: Canadian Social Structure
description: Descriptive and analytic survey of such features as demographic characteristics, class structure, ethnicity, and regional variation in Canadian society as a basis for understanding current social issues.

name: Sociology of Family
description: An introduction to contemporary family forms and relations.

name: Introduction to Sociology
description: Introduction to problems in the analysis of social structures and processes. Basic sociological concepts will be introduced and their application demonstrated in various areas of sociology. Credit will be granted for only one of SOCI 100 or both SOCI 101, SOCI 102.

name: Barcelona
description: An introduction to the city of Barcelona from a cultural studies perspective including the study of its art, literature, architecture, and social practices.

name: Research Methods
description: Introduction to research designs and methodologies. Prerequisite: One of SOCI 100, SOCI 101, SOCI 102, SOCI 200.

name: Studies in Romance Languages and Literature
description: Study of a literary or cultural topic that extends beyond just one of the Romance Languages. Consult the Department for this year's offerings. Recommended: Second-year standing or higher.

name: Special Topics Abroad
description: Study of Romance language literature, history, culture, or communities in an authentic context. Topics and locations may vary. Consult Department for current offerings.

name: Dante Alighieri's Divine Comedy
description: A close reading of Dante's masterpiece, along with excerpts from some of his other works: Vita Nuova, Convivio, Monarchia, Epistles. Credit will be granted for only one of RMST  453, ITST  413 or ITAL  403. Equivalency: ITST  413 or ITAL  403.

name: Special Topics in Francophone Studies
description: Study of Francophone literatures, cultures, languages, or communities. Topics vary from section to section. Consult Department for current offerings. Recommended for students in 3rd year or above. Restricted to students with 2nd year standing or above.

name: Romance Linguistics
description: Vocabulary, phonetics, phonology, morphology, syntax, and sociolinguistics of spoken and written Romance languages. Credit will be granted for only one of RMST 400 or RMST 468. Prerequisite: 2nd year standing. A beginners knowledge (CFER A1) in at least one of the Romance languages is highly recommended.

name: Italian Cinema and Its Cultural Background
description: Films with English subtitles. Course content will vary. Credit will be granted for only one of RMST  452, ITST  432 or ITAL  430. Equivalency: ITAL 430 or ITST 432.

name: Topics in the Italian Literature and Culture of the Middle Ages
description: Italian literature of the Middle Ages in its intellectual, socio-political and cultural context. Dante and his contemporaries and/or immediate followers (may include Petrarch and Boccaccio). Credit will be granted for only one of RMST  454, ITST  414 or ITAL  404. Equivalency: ITST  414 or ITAL  404.

name: Perinatal Epidemiology
description: Indicators of maternal/newborn well-being across population subgroups, changing trends in obstetrical intervention, perinatal morbidity, and the analysis of perinatal data. Prerequisite: Either (a) SPPH 400 or (b) SPPH 521; and SPPH 502. Corequisite: SPPH 500 Equivalency: OBST 507

name: Application of Ethical Theories in the Practice of Public Health
Classics of Eighteenth-Century Italian Literature and Culture
description: Classics of the Italian literature of the age of the Enlightenment in its intellectual, socio-political, and cultural context. Credit will be granted for only one of ITST  417 or ITAL  407 or RMST  457. Equivalency: ITST  417 or ITAL  407

name: Genre Adaptations in the Hispanic World
